 Hunter Method 

The Hunter method aligns axles with each other, without reference to 
chassis or frame. Computerized alignment systems use sensors containing 
calibrated devices and microprocessors attached to individual wheels with 
lines connecting one adapter to the others to measure tandem axle alignment 
angles. The thrust angle is determined for the rear rear drive axle to measure 
perpendicularity (squareness) to the frame. Thrust angle is the resultant 
direction of travel for an axle due to the relative toe setting for the wheel 
at both ends of the axle. An acceptable thrust angle on Hunter alignment 
equipment is within ±0.12 degrees on the rear rear drive 
axle.

Depending on the alignment condition which exists, axle position 
adjustments may be made by adding or removing shims as necessary.

For either Bee Line or Hunter methods, a trammel gauge or other 
suitable device can be used to set the forward rear drive axle parallel to the 
rear rear drive axle. Measure from rear rear drive axle centers to forward 
rear drive axle centers on both sides. If these measurements differ by more 
than 3 mm (1/8 inch), reposition the forward rear drive axle so that B 1 
 = B 2 .

[FIGURE: F45971B.gif]

ADJUSTMENTS

Vehicle Lean Correction

 CAUTION: Frame twisting should not be attempted to correct vehicle lean because 
it can cause frame damage. 

Before attempting any correction, the cause for excessive lean must be 
determined. The following measurements must be made without payload on the 
vehicle and with all vehicle fluid levels at full.

Place the vehicle on a flat surface, fill all tires to the recommended 
inflation pressures. Measure and record the ride height (ride height is the 
perpendicular distance between the top of the axle and the bottom of the frame 
rail). Measure and record the distance between the lower flange of the bumper 
ends and ground for both the left side and right side of the vehicle.

Corrections should not be attempted on vehicles with a bumper-to-ground 
right-to-left height variation of 25.4 mm (1 inch) or less. Corrections should 
not be made if the ride height variation is 12.7 mm (1/2 inch or less).

If a front spring spacer is needed to correct a vehicle lean condition, 
use the following procedure.

Raise the vehicle by the frame until the tire comes off the ground and 
place a jack stand under the frame to retain that height. 

Raise the axle slightly with a jack to remove the weight from the 
spring. 

Remove the U-bolt nuts and the U-bolts. 

Lower the axle slightly to allow enough clearance between the bottom of 
the spring and the top of the axle so the spacer can be installed. 

 NOTE: If a spacer 25.4 mm (1 inch) thick or less is in place, remove the 
spacer on the opposite side to eliminate the lean condition. 

Install the spacer between the spring and axle, making sure the 
locating pin is facing down.

[FIGURE: F7727B.gif]

Raise the axle to the spring and reinstall the applicable U-bolts with 
hardened flatwashers and attaching nuts. Refer to the following chart.

The steering wheel stop bolt does not normally require adjustment. To

ADJUSTMENTS

Drive Axle Adjustments 

Misalignment of Hendrickson walking beam suspensions must be checked. 
Although no single point for alignment adjustment is currently provided, frame 
attachment brackets, axle attachments and spring-to-saddle location are all 
items to be checked. 

Four-spring suspension alignment can be corrected by adding or removing 
alignment shims at the radius rod attachment point on the spring hanger 
brackets.

Correct a misalignment condition through the following procedures: 

Loosen the frame bracket attaching bolts and the spring-to-saddle bolts 
to allow freedom of movement. 

 CAUTION: Do not attempt to move the off-axle hanger brackets with respect to the 
axle housing. The welds at this interface are critical to the structural 
integrity of the axle housing. If axle misalignment cannot be corrected by 
this procedure and is determined to be caused by the off-axle brackets, review 
the condition with the service manager and contact the axle manufacturer's 
representative. 

Move the axles until square to frame (within 5 mm [
3/16 inch]) and parallel to each other (within 3 mm [1/8 
inch]).

Retighten all fasteners to original torque specifications.

 NOTE: The following steps should be performed after all service has been 
completed and all suspension fasteners have been tightened to specified torque 
values. 

Begin alignment by checking rear rear drive axle first. Use a trammel 
bar or its equivalent to measure from straightedge to centerline of rear rear 
drive axle on both sides of vehicle (Ll and Lr in the illustration). If both 
sides measure within 5 mm (3/16 inch) of each other, alignment of rear rear 
drive axle is acceptable.

[FIGURE: F37051A.gif]

If Ll and Lr differ by more than 5 mm (3/16 inch), adjust rear rear 
drive axle by loosening up torque rod bar pin lock nuts on center spring 
hanger and add drop-in shims. Torque rod bar pin must always be mounted 
adjacent to forward face of spring hanger legs. No more than four shims can be 
used (1/4 inch maximum total thickness). Snug torque rod bar pin lock nuts, 
but do not tighten to specification yet.

[FIGURE: F3706F.gif]

With rear rear drive axle properly aligned, check forward rear drive

trammel bar. If the forward rear drive axle spacing measurements (Sl and Sr in 
the illustration in Step 1) differ by more than 3 mm (1/8 inch), make 
adjustments at forward spring hangers in a similar manner. Snug torque rod bar 
pin lock nuts.

[FIGURE: F3707B.gif]

Following alignment of both axles, move vehicle back and forth several 
times prior to removing straightedge from frame, and recheck alignment to 
confirm adjustments. Tighten torque rod bar pin lock nuts to specified torque.

SPECIFICATIONS

SPECIFICATIONS

 Tire Zone Description 

Specified wheelcuts and turning diameters are based on the tire zone 
concept. Tire zones are determined by the combination of tire and rim. Any 
tire by itself does not fall into a particular zone and, in fact, the same 
tire can be in more than one zone. Only a tire and rim combination uniquely 
determines the tire zone.

The main reason for using the tire zones is to take advantage of 
greater wheel offsets on certain rims, which allows increased wheelcuts and, 
therefore, tighter turning diameters.

To determine wheel turn angle, first determine the tire zone for the 
rim/tire combination installed on the vehicle using the tables below and then 
use the corresponding column in the Front Wheel Turn Angle Specifications 
chart that follows the tire zone tables.

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Suspension 

The front suspension consists of the following major components:

axle

leaf springs

shock absorbers 

stabilizer bar

The front axle is available in 9K, 12K and 13K capacities on the 
CF-8000. The CFT-8000 is equipped with either a 12K or 13K capacity front axle.

When servicing the front axle, wheel hubs or suspension, replace any 
component that is damaged or out of specification. All major axle and 
suspension components are heat treated and, therefore cannot be bent, twisted, 
welded, heated or reconditioned without experiencing a strength and/or fatigue 
life reduction.

Following are examples of specific prohibited operations:

hot or cold bending or twisting of I-beam, tie rod assemblies, 
spindles, steering arms or tie rod arms for any reason

welding of, or to, steering arms, tie rod arms, I-beams, steering 
spindles, spindle pins or tie rod assemblies

the redrilling or reboring of I-beam spindle pin holes for a bushing

milling or machining of any component

spray welding of bearing diameters or other machined surfaces

the redrilling or reboring of draw key holes

relocation or removal of tie rod clamps

================================================================================
PAGE 2914
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 04-01: Suspension and Wheel Hubs, Front

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Components

Spindle

Provides steering pivot point. The spindle pivots on a pin installed 
through the end of the axle. Bushings provide bearing surface between spindle 
and pin. The front wheel and brake drum are mounted on the spindle. Opposed, 
tapered roller bearings are installed in the brake drum hub to support the 
weight of the vehicle on the spindle.

Shock absorber

Hydraulic, direct-acting type. Provides continuous damping effect 
under compression and extension. Connected to frame and bracket located below 
the leaf spring. Rubber bushings are used to isolate the shock absorbers from 
their attaching points.

Leaf spring

Multi-leaf, semi-elliptic springs are used to support the front of the 
vehicle. The leaf spring is an over-the-axle installation with U-bolts used to 
attach spring to the axle. The spring is attached to the frame through a 
single pivot and bracket at the front, and a shackle and bracket arrangement 
at the rear.

Stabilizer bar

Links the left and right suspension to reduce body roll and suspension 
movement. The ends of the stabilizer are attached to spring bracket through 
rubber insulators. Links with ball-type joints at each end attach the 
stabilizer bar to the frame.

Axle

I-beam, non-driving type axle is attached to the frame through leaf 
springs and stabilizer bar. Spindle pin and camber angles are built into axle 
and are not adjustable.

================================================================================
PAGE 2915
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 04-01: Suspension and Wheel Hubs, Front

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Component Replacement

Shock absorbers must be replaced as an assembly. They are not 
serviceable. It is not necessary to replace shock absorbers in pairs. Replace 
only the worn or damaged shock absorber.

Leaf springs can be replaced individually. Bushings in spring eyes and 
spring pins are serviceable as separate components.

Spindle assembly can be replaced as an assembly. Since spindle pin 
bushings are serviceable items, if spindle pin bushings are worn, it is not 
necessary to replace the spindle assembly.

Stabilizer bar, links and bushings can be replaced as separate 
components.

Spring, shock and stabilizer mounting brackets are serviceable as 
separate components.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fasteners, Suspension

 CAUTION: All front suspension fasteners are important retaining parts in that 
they affect the performance of vital parts and systems and result in major 
service expense. Any part must be replaced with one of the same part number or 
with an exact equivalent part if replacement becomes necessary. Do not use a 
replacement part of lower quality or substitute design. Torque values must be 
used as specified during assembly to ensure proper retention of suspension 
parts. 

Never attempt to heat, quench or straighten any front suspension part. 
Replace with a new part.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Shock Absorber 

The hydraulic shock absorbers are of the direct double-acting type. 
They provide a continuous damping effect both under compression and extension. 
These shock absorbers are telescopic in design, with rubber bushings at the 
mounting points for quiet operation. The shock absorbers are sealed and 
nonadjustable and must be replaced as complete assemblies.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Wheel Bearing and Wheel Hub

 CAUTION: Wheel seals on front axles must be replaced any time the axle 
lubricants on that axle are changed from the factory-installed mineral lube to 
synthetic lube or vice versa. 

Each front wheel and tire assembly is bolted to its respective front 
hub and brake drum assembly. Two opposed tapered roller bearings are installed 
in each hub. A wheel seal is installed at the inner end of the hub to prevent 
lubricant from leaking into the drum. The entire assembly is retained to its 
spindle by an adjusting nut and cotter pin.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Wheel Spindle

 Removal 

Loosen front wheel hub bolt nuts. Raise front of vehicle and remove 
wheel. 

Remove hub and drum and wheel bearing from spindle. 

Remove retaining bolts and brake backing plate. To prevent damage to 
brake hose, hang backing plate from frame. 

Remove cotter pin and retaining nut from steering linkage drag link and 
connecting rod.

Disconnect drag link from steering spindle arm and connecting rod from 
steering arm.

Remove nut from upper and lower lock pins.

Remove lock pins using brass drift and hammer. Strike threaded end of 
pin. Note direction of threaded ends before removing lock pins.

If spindle is to be replaced, remove spindle and steering arms.

Remove the upper and lower spindle pin cap assemblies.

 CAUTION: Do not heat axle to loosen spindle pin. Heat can weaken axle. 

Drive spindle pin out of spindle and axle.

Remove spindle assembly thrust bearing and end play shim.

 Installation 

Place spindle in position on axle. Insert spindle pin thrust bearing 
between bottom of axle and spindle.

Pack thrust bearing and coat all mating surfaces of spindle and axle 
parts with Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B prior to assembly. On all axles, thrust 
bearing must be installed with retainer lip facing down. The shim is placed 
between the top of axle and the spindle. Axle-to-spindle clearance of 
0.076-0.254 mm (0.003-0.010 inch) must be maintained on all axles.

Line up notches in spindle pin with spindle pin holes in axle. Using a 
brass drift, drive spindle pin through axle until notches and holes in spindle 
are aligned.

 NOTE: Do not install both lock pins from the same side of the axle. 

Install lower (longer) lock pin and seat by striking prior to 
installing nut. Install upper (shorter) lock pin and seat by striking prior to 
installing nut. Install nuts on lock pins and tighten to 68-95 Nm
 (50-70 lb-ft).

Install the upper and lower cap assemblies. Tighten to 50-70 Nm
 (37-51 lb-ft). 

If necessary, install spindle and steering arms. Use new cotter pins 
and tighten retaining nuts to specified torque.

Install brake backing plate on spindle. 

Lubricate spindle bushings until lubricant is visible at 
spindle-to-axle area. 

Install hub and drum assembly and wheel. Adjust wheel bearings as 
described in Wheel Bearings, Front , in the Adjustments portion of this 
section. 

Check and adjust toe-in. Refer to Section 04-00 .

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Wheel Seal and Bearings 

 CAUTION: Sodium-base grease is not compatible with lithium-base grease and 
should not be intermixed. Therefore, do not lubricate front and/or rear wheel 
bearings without first determining the type of original wheel bearing 
lubricant. Mixing incompatible bearing lubricants could result in premature 
lubricant breakdown. 

 CAUTION: If bearing adjustment does not eliminate looseness or rough and noisy 
operation, the hub and bearings should be cleaned, inspected, and repacked or 
filled to the full mark on the hub cap with specified lubricant. If the 
bearing cups or the cone and roller assemblies are worn or damaged, they must 
be replaced. 

 CAUTION: Wheel seals on front axles must be replaced any time the axle 
lubricants are changed from the factory-installed mineral lube to synthetic 
lube or vice versa. 

 NOTE: Wheel bearing lubricant, used with a grease-type seal, is a 
lithium-base grease, Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B. 

 NOTE: Front wheel bearing lubricant for oil-filled hubs is Motorcraft SAE 90 
Premium Rear Axle Lubricant C6AZ-19580-E or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESW-M2C105-A.

The basic design of the hub bearings is the same in all hubs, but minor 
differences in size exist between the various models. 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Impact Slide Hammer

T50T-100-A

Seal Replacer

T73T-1190-B

Driver Handle

T80T-4000-W

 Removal 

Raise the vehicle until the tires clear the floor and install safety 
stands to support the front axle.

Remove the hub cap and gasket from the hub. 

Remove the cotter pin, adjusting nut and flatwasher from the spindle. 

Inspect the condition of the spindle and nut threads to ensure a free 
turning nut when reassembling. 

Remove the outer bearing cone and roller assembly. Using a Rotunda 
Wheel Dolly 014-00030 or equivalent to support the hub and drum assembly, pull 
the hub and drum/rotor assembly off the spindle. 

 CAUTION: Be careful not to damage bearing cone cage. 

Remove inner bearing cone and wheel seal using Impact Slide Hammer 
T50T-100-A and Seal Remover TOOL-1175-AC or equivalent.

[FIGURE: F7553B.gif]

 Installation 

Remove all traces of old lubricant from the bearings, hubs and axle 
spindle. Inspect bearing cups for pitting, spalling or unusual wear. If either 
cup is worn or damaged, remove both cups. It is recommended that bearings and 
cups be replaced in sets. If cups are worn or damaged, install the inner and 
outer bearing cups in the hub with an appropriate bearing cup driver tool. 
Check for proper seating of new bearing cups by trying to insert a 0.038-mm 
(0.0015-inch) feeler gauge between bottom face of cup and wheel hub seat. You 
should not be able to insert feeler gauge.

[FIGURE: F31301A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not spin the bearings dry with compressed air. 

Clean the inner and outer bearing cone and roller assemblies with 
solvent and dry thoroughly. 

Inspect bearing cones and rollers for pitting, spalling or unusual 
wear. Closely inspect rollers for end wear and flat or rough spots. Replace 
all worn or damaged assemblies. It is recommended that bearings and cups be 
replaced in sets. 

Cover the spindle with a clean cloth and brush all loose dust and dirt 
from the brake assembly. Remove the cloth from the spindle carefully to 
prevent dirt falling on the spindle. 

Remove all burrs from the shoulder of the spindle and seal bore in the 
hub with emery cloth. Remove any nicks or scratches from the seal bore or 
spindle with emery cloth.

Scratches in the hub seal bore may be too deep to be dressed out by 
light polishing with an emery cloth. In this case, apply a thin layer of 
non-hardening sealer such as Silicone Rubber D6AZ-19562-AA or -BA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M5G92-A or ESE-M4G195-A to the 
colored outside diameter of the new seal prior to installation.

If bearing lubricant is oil, dip inner and outer bearing in SAE 90 
Premium Rear Axle Lubricant C6AZ-19580-E or equivalent lubricant meeting Ford 
specification ESW-M2C105-A. If bearing lubricant is grease, proceed with 
following:

Pack the inside of the hub with lithium-base wheel bearing grease such 
as Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESA-M1C75-B. Fill the hub until the grease is flush with the 
inside diameters of both bearing cups. 

Pack the bearing cone and roller assemblies with wheel bearing grease. 
Use a bearing packer for this operation. If a packer is not available, work as 
much lubricant as possible between the rollers and cages. Lubricate the cup 
surfaces with grease. 

Place the inner bearing cone and roller assembly in the inner cup and 
install the wheel seal using Seal Replacer T73T-1190-B and Driver Handle 
T80T-4000-W. Make sure the seal is fully bottomed in the hub.

[FIGURE: F7554A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Bushing, Spindle 

 Removal 

On a spindle with bronze or low friction (Garlock) bushings, press 
bushing out of spindle with a tool that is slightly smaller than spindle bore. 

[FIGURE: F14541B.gif]

Clean spindle bores thoroughly and make certain lubricating holes (if 
so equipped) are not plugged. 

 Installation 

Position a new bushing in spindle bore with the lubricating hole in 
line with lubricating fitting and open end of oil groove toward axle. Press 
bronze bushing into spindle with a driver that pilots in bushing. 

Press the bushing until there is 3.4-4.1 mm (0.133-0.161 inch) between 
the bottom of the bushing and the bottom of the top bore.

[FIGURE: F9372A.gif]

[FIGURE: F14531B.gif]

Turn the spindle over and install remaining bushing in same manner. 

Ream bronze or low friction (Garlock) bushings 0.025-0.076 mm 
(0.001-0.003 inch) larger than diameter of a new spindle pin. 

[FIGURE: F56401A.gif]

Clean all metal shavings from bronze bushings after reaming. Coat 
bushing and pin with lubricant prior to assembly.

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Bushing, Spring Eye and Shackle

 Removal 

 CAUTION: Special care should be taken when pressing out old bushings and 
pressing in new bushings to make sure spring eyes are not gouged or otherwise 
damaged. 

Press bushing out of spring with a tool that is slightly smaller than 
spring bore.

Clean bores thoroughly.

 Installation 

Position a new bushing in spring bore. Press bushing into spring with a 
driver that pilots in bushing.

[FIGURE: F9161A.gif]

Because the spring eye is not perfectly round, minor distortion of the 
bushing inner diameter can occur as the bushing is installed. Therefore, 
reaming might be required. 

[FIGURE: F4667C.gif]

Do not ream the solid bronze bushing after installation in the shackle 
bracket unless the inner diameter is less than 25.45 mm (1.002 inches). No 
distortion should have occurred because it was pressed into a machined hole. 
After reaming, clean and coat the bushing and pin with Motorcraft Premium 
Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M1C75-B prior to assembly.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Axle, Front

 Removal 

Loosen wheel retaining nuts.

Raise and support vehicle at frame rails.

Remove wheels.

Remove hub and brake drum assemblies.

Remove retaining bolts and brake backing plate. To prevent damage to 
brake hose, hang backing plate from frame.

Disconnect drag link from steering spindle arm.

Support axle on suitable jack.

Remove U-bolt attaching nuts.

Lower axle and remove from vehicle.

 Installation 

Position axle in vehicle and install U-bolt retaining nuts. Tighten 
5/8-inch nuts to 204-277 Nm (150-205 lb-ft). Tighten 3/4-inch 
nuts to 299-406 Nm (220-300 lb-ft).

Connect drag link. Use new cotter pin and tighten attaching nut to 
149-203 Nm (110-150 lb-ft).

Install brake backing plate. With air brakes, tighten attaching nuts to 
299-406 Nm (220-300 lb-ft) torque. With hydraulic brakes, 
tighten attaching nuts to 204-277 Nm (150-205 lb-ft) torque.

Install hub and drum assembly. Adjust wheel bearings. Refer to Wheel 
Bearings, Front , in the portion of this section.

Install wheels and lower vehicle. Tighten wheel attaching nuts to 
specification as listed at end of Section 04-04 .

ADJUSTMENTS

Wheel Bearings, Front

 CAUTION: Wheel seals on front axles must be replaced any time the axle 
lubricants are changed from the factory-installed mineral lube to synthetic 
lube or vice versa. 

 CAUTION: If bearings are adjusted too tightly, they will overheat and wear 
rapidly. An adjustment that is excessively loose can cause pounding and 
contribute to uneven tire wear, steering difficulties and inefficient brakes. 
Check bearing adjustment at regular inspection intervals. 

Wheel bearings are adjustable to correct for bearing and shoulder wear 
of the spindle. Satisfactory operation and long life of bearings depend on 
proper adjustment and correct lubrication. If bearings are adjusted too 
tightly, they will overheat and wear rapidly. An adjustment that is 
excessively loose can cause pounding and contribute to uneven tire wear, 
steering difficulties and inefficient brakes. The bearing adjustment should be 
checked at regular inspection intervals.

Periodically check the oil level on oil-lubricated front axle bearings. 
Keep oil level between ADD and FULL marks shown on the hub cap. Do not 
overfill. Overfilling can result in oil on brake linings. 

[FIGURE: F2633D.gif]

Front hub assemblies and bearings must be cleaned, inspected and 
lubricated whenever the hub assemblies are removed or at the mileage/time 
periods indicated in the maintenance schedule. 

New hub seals should be installed when the hub is removed. A damaged or 
worn seal may permit bearing lubricant to reach the brake linings, resulting 
in ineffective brake operation and necessitating premature replacement of 
linings.

To check the wheel bearing adjustment, raise the front of the vehicle. 
Then, grasp the tire at the sides and alternately push inward and pull outward 
on the tire. If any looseness is felt, adjust the front wheel bearings. 

Remove the hub cap and gasket from the hub.

Remove the cotter pin.

While rotating wheel, tighten adjusting nut to 108-162 Nm
 (80-120 lb-ft) to seat bearings. 

Back off adjusting nut until loose. 

Finger-tighten adjusting nut. Final bearing adjustment must provide 
0.000-0.125 mm (0.000-0.005 inch) end play. The final adjustment must not 
result in a preloaded bearing.

If cotter pin hole lines up with a slot in the nut, insert and secure a 
new cotter pin. If it does not, advance adjusting nut to align a slot with 
first available cotter pin hole and insert and secure new cotter pin. Do not 
advance nut to align hole with slot in nut.

Install gasket and grease or oil hub cap and adjust the brakes.

[FIGURE: F4637D.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Suspension 

Semi-elliptic, multi-leaf rear springs are used on all Cargo vehicles 
with single rear axle. The suspension is mounted to the frame side rails and 
held in place on the axles by four U-bolts. 

The front and rear ends of the springs are mounted on the frame side 
rails by a spring hanger bracket and a radius leaf.

================================================================================
PAGE 2933
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 04-02A: Suspension, Rear

1997 Cargo with Single Rear Axles Workshop Manual

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Suspension, Rear

 Inspection and Verification 

Verify vehicle operator's original concern by road testing to duplicate 
the concern.

 Symptom Chart — Rear Suspension 

 REAR SUSPENSION 

Condition

Possible Source

Action

Rear Leaf Spring Squeaks

Loose attachments at the front or rear spring eyes.

TIGHTEN rear spring front and rear retaining bolts and rear shackle to 
specifications listed at the end of this section.

Individual leaf springs rubbing against each other or leaf ends sliding.

RAISE vehicle so rear axle hangs freely. REMOVE spring clips if 
necessary to allow leaves to spread. Make sure area is clean and dry. 
LUBRICATE tip of each leaf with Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B. REINSTALL spring clips. 
TIGHTEN to 68-95 Nm (50-70 lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Spring

 Removal 

Raise vehicle frame until weight is off rear springs with wheels still 
touching floor. 

Support axle and remove nuts and washers from U-bolts and drive U-bolts 
out of spring seat cap. Remove auxiliary spring and spacer. 

Support spring and remove front radius leaf eye pin. The pin is held in 
place by lock bolts. Remove front rebound pin which is held in place by a 
cotter pin. 

Remove rear rebound pin, which is held in place by a cotter pin, and 
remove spring.

 Installation 

Position spring in rear bracket and install rebound pin and cotter pin. 

Position spring in front bracket. Install rebound pin and secure with a 
cotter pin. 

Using a C-clamp or jack, force front eye of spring up into bracket 
until eye is aligned with holes in bracket. Install lower radius leaf eye pin 
through front bracket and spring eye. Align pin grooves with locking bolt 
holes in bracket and install locking bolts, nuts and washers. Tighten to 
specifications listed at end of this section. 

Position spring seat and wedge (if so equipped) between axle and 
spring. Install auxiliary spring and spacer. Place U-bolt pad on top of spring 
assembly at center bolt. Put U-bolt over spring assembly and axle. 

Install spring cap on U-bolt. Install nuts and washers on U-bolts. 

Lower vehicle to floor and tighten U-bolts to specifications listed at 
the end of this section.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Wheel Bearings and Seals, Rear

Chicago Rawhide unitized wheel seals are standard items on all rear 
axles. The unitized wheel seal combines the function of a wear sleeve and the 
seal in one self-contained unit with the seal and sleeve surface inside. The 
unitized design provides maximum protection for the sealing surface during 
installation and operation. The tools required for unitized seal installation 
are only available from C.R. Industries. 

Stemco two-piece seals are available as regular production options. The 
seal consists of a lip-type oil seal and a wiper sleeve. The seal is installed 
in the wheel hub and the wiper sleeve is installed on the axle tube housing. 
When the hub is installed, a seal is formed between the wear sleeve and seal 
lip. The tools required for Stemco seal installation are only available from 
the Stemco warehouse. Refer to Specifications at the end of this section for 
service tool availability.

New wheel seals must be installed whenever the hub is removed. A 
damaged or worn seal can permit bearing lubricant to reach the brake linings, 
resulting in ineffective brake operation which requires premature replacement 
of linings.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Wheel Hubs 

 Removal 

Raise the rear wheels off the floor and place safety stands under the 
rear axle housing so the axle is parallel with the floor. Back off the rear 
brake adjustment. Refer to the appropriate section in Group 06 for procedure. 

Remove the axle shaft stud nuts and lockwashers. 

If tapered dowels are installed in the axle shaft flange, place a drift 
in the center of the flange and strike it sharply to loosen the dowels.

[FIGURE: E73621A.gif]

Remove the axle shaft. 

Remove lock nut, lockwasher, and adjusting nut.

[FIGURE: E7473C.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

4254

Lock Nut

2

1124

Lockwasher (Design for 21K, 23K, 40K, 46K Rear Axles)

3

4254

Adjusting Nut (21K, 23K, 40K, 46K Rear Axles)

4

4255

Adjusting Nut (17.5K, 19K, 34K Rear Axles)

5

1124

Lockwasher (Design for 13K, 15K, 17.5K, 34K Rear Axles)

Using Rotunda Wheel Dolly 014-00030 or equivalent, raise the wheel so 
that all wheel weight is removed from the wheel bearings.

[FIGURE: E69531A.gif]

Remove the outer bearing cone. Pull the wheel straight out and away 
from the axle.

 CAUTION: Do not use a chisel to cut through the wear sleeve as damage to the 
spindle could occur. 

If the old seal is a two-piece design, remove the old wear sleeve by 
striking the ring surface several times with a ball peen hammer. 

[FIGURE: E43491A.gif]

Thoroughly clean the spindle.

With a piece of hard wood that will just clear the outer bearing cup, 
or a brass drift, carefully drive the inner bearing cone and inner seal out of 
the wheel hub. 

Clean all the old grease or axle lubricant out of the wheel hub. 

Inspect the bearing races and rollers for pitting, galling, and erratic 
wear patterns. Inspect the rollers for end wear.

[FIGURE: E67831A.gif]

If the bearing cups are to be replaced, refer to Bearing 
Cup Replacement (Aluminum Hubs) in the Removal and Installation portion of this 
section for procedure. 

 Installation 

If bearing cups are removed, install new bearing cups using the 
appropriate bearing cup replacer. Refer to Bearing Cup Replacement (Aluminum 
Hubs) in the Removal and Installation portion of this section. 

Check for proper seating of the new bearing cups by trying to insert a 
0.038-mm (0.0015-inch) feeler gauge between the bottom of the cup and the 
wheel hub seat. You should not be able to insert the feeler gauge. 

Dip the inner and outer bearing cones in differential oil or pack with 
Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent lubricant meeting Ford 
specification ESA-M1C75-B. 

Place the inner bearing cone and roller assembly in the wheel hub. 
Install a new wheel seal as described under Hub Seal, Rear, 
Two-Piece , or Hub Seal, Rear, 
Unitized , in the Removal and Installation portion of this section. 

Apply a light film of lithium-base grease such as Premium Long-Life 
Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent lubricant meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M1C75-B to the axle spindle. Position a seal protector tool over the axle 
spindle threads. 

With the hub centered on the axle spindle, carefully slide hub assembly 
straight (to avoid seal damage) onto the axle housing spindle. Then remove the 
seal protector from the axle spindle. 

Fill the wheel cavity with rear axle lube before installing the outer 
bearing. 

[FIGURE: E44261A.gif]

Install the outer wheel bearing and start the bearing adjuster nut. 
Remove the wheel jack. 

Adjust the wheel bearings. 

Install the axle shaft, a new gasket, lockwashers and axle shaft 
retaining nuts. Tighten the nuts to specifications listed at the end of this 
section.

Adjust the brakes. 

Check the rear axle lube level and add oil, if required. 

Remove the safety stands and lower the vehicle.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Bearing Cup Replacement (Aluminum Hubs)

 WARNING: DO NOT USE OXY-ACETYLENE OR SIMILAR EQUIPMENT TO HEAT THE HUB. THIS CAN 
CAUSE OVERHEATING IN LOCALIZED AREAS WHICH WILL RESULT IN LOSS OF STRENGTH 
THAT CAN CAUSE FAILURE OF THE HUB ASSEMBLY AND ULTIMATELY LOSS OF VEHICLE 
CONTROL. 

Remove the wheel bearings.

Thoroughly clean and degrease the hub with a nonflammable solvent. 

Heat the hub evenly throughout in an oven to 79°-96°
C (175°-205°F). 

 WARNING: REPLACE DAMAGED HUBS. USING A DAMAGED HUB ON A VEHICLE CAN RESULT IN 
HUB FAILURE AND ULTIMATELY IN LOSS OF VEHICLE CONTROL. 

 CAUTION: Take care to avoid damage to the bearing cup bore and shoulder. 

 NOTE: Variations in tolerances of materials and oven temperatures may allow 
bearing to drop in and out easily. 

Remove the hub from the oven and quickly press out the bearing cup. 

Heat the hub evenly again, as in Step 3. 

 CAUTION: Take care to avoid damage to the bearing cup and shoulder. 

Remove the hub from the oven and quickly press in the new bearing cup. 
Make sure the cup is properly aligned and fully seated. 

[FIGURE: E1739E.gif]

Check for proper seating of the new bearing cups by trying to insert a 
0.038-mm (0.0015-inch) feeler gauge between the bottom of the cup and the 
wheel hub seat. You should not be able to insert the feeler gauge. 

Install the wheel bearings.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Hub Seal, Rear, Unitized 

 Removal 

With a piece of hard wood that will just clear the outer bearing cup, 
or a brass drift, carefully drive the inner bearing cone and inner seal out of 
the wheel hub. 

Remove and discard the old seal. If a wear sleeve is in place on the 
spindle, carefully remove the wear sleeve and discard. Unitized seals will 
leak if installed over a wear sleeve. Thoroughly clean all grease and dirt 
from the spindle, spindle threads, seal bore and wheel cavity. 

Remove all burrs from the shoulder of the spindle and seal bore in the 
hub with emery cloth. Remove any nicks or scratches from the seal bore or 
spindle with emery cloth. 

Scratches in the hub seal bore might be too deep to be dressed out by 
light polishing with an emery cloth. In this case, apply a thin layer of 
nonhardening sealer such as Silicone Rubber D6AZ-19562-AA or -BA or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESB-M4G92-A or ESE-M4G195-A to the colored outside 
diameter of the new seal prior to installation. 

 Installation 

Dip the inner and outer bearing cones in differential oil or pack with 
grease such as Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B before installation. 

Position the inner bearing cone in the bearing cup. 

Seat smaller outside diameter of seal in the recess of the tool 
adapter. Use green tool with seal E1HT-1175-AA. Use red tool with seal 
E1HT-1175-B. 

Insert centering plug of tool in bore of inner bearing cone. The plug 
prevents cocking of the seal in the bore. 

Hold the tool handle firmly and strike until the sound of the impact 
changes to a ringing as the seal bottoms out. Use a 4-5 pound hammer and hold 
the tool firmly to avoid bouncing and unseating of the seal from the tool. 
After seal is bottomed in the bore, check for freedom of movement by manually 
moving interior rubber component of seal backwards and forward. A slight 
movement indicates damage-free installation. 

[FIGURE: E43501A.gif]

================================================================================
PAGE 2940
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 04-02B: Wheel Bearings and Seals, Rear

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Hub Seal, Rear, Two-Piece 

 Removal 

Remove and discard the old oil retainer. 

 WARNING: DO NOT USE A CHISEL TO CUT THROUGH THE WEAR SLEEVE AS DAMAGE TO THE 
SPINDLE COULD OCCUR. 

Remove the old wear sleeve by striking the ring surface several times 
with a ball peen hammer. 

 Installation 

Thoroughly clean the axle spindle with a wire brush. Remove all burrs 
with an emery cloth. 

If the spindle shoulder is scored or pitted, apply a thin coat of 
nonhardening sealant such as Silicone Rubber D6AZ-19562-AA or -BA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESB-M4G92-A or ESE-M4G195-A. 

Using suitable tool, install the wiper sleeve on the axle housing. Do 
not use heat on the wiper sleeve to facilitate installation.

[FIGURE: E1928F.gif]

After bottoming, rotate the tool while applying several light hammer 
blows to ensure that the seal ring is flush and square with the face of the 
shoulder. The sleeves are designed with flanges to eliminate the possibility 
of installing them backwards. 

Remove all burrs and protrusions from the seal area of the wheel hub. 

Dip the inner and outer bearing cones in differential oil or pack with 
grease such as Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent lubricant 
meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B before installation. 

Position the inner bearing cone in the bearing cup. 

Pack grease such as Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent 
lubricant meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B between the spring and seal 
lip to prevent the spring from dislocating when the seal is installed.

Position the seal in the hub bore and drive it squarely into position 
using the correct tool. The seal must be evenly bottomed.

ADJUSTMENTS

Wheel Bearings, 17.5K and 19K Rear Axles 

Tighten the adjusting nut to 237 Nm (175 lb-ft) while 
rotating the wheel to seat the bearings. 

Back off the adjusting nut one-quarter turn. 

Install the lockwasher. Advance the adjusting nut if necessary to align 
the dowel pin in the nut with the hole in the lockwasher. 

Install the lock nut and tighten to 237 Nm (175 
lb-ft). The wheel assembly must rotate freely and with an end play of 
0.000-0.125 mm (0.000-0.005 inch). Do not preload the bearings.

[FIGURE: E73631A.gif]

ADJUSTMENTS

Wheel Bearings, 21K, 23K, 40K Rear Axles 

Tighten the adjusting nut to 237 Nm (175 lb-ft) while 
rotating the wheel to seat the bearings. 

Back off (loosen) the adjusting nut one quarter turn. Install the 
tabbed lockwasher so that the pre-bent arms fit over either the point or flat 
of the inner nut. If necessary, advance the adjusting nut to align the 
pre-bent tabs with the flat on the adjusting nut. 

Install the lock nut and tighten to 237 Nm (175 
lb-ft). The wheel assembly must rotate freely and with an end play of 
0.000-0.125 mm (0.000-0.005 inch). Do not preload the bearings. Bend a minimum 
of two of the tabs on the lockwasher outboard over the flats of the locknut.

Section 04-02C: Suspension, Rear, Hendrickson RTE2-Series Tandem Axle

1997 CFT-8000 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Suspension

The Hendrickson RTE2-400 tandem suspension is available for CFT-8000 
Series vehicles. 

The prefix letters RT indicate the type of suspension. The prefix 
letter E stands for extended leaf springs, which provide a two-stage spring 
action offering a superior ride whether empty or loaded. The prefix number 2 
indicates the latest, most updated, lightweight version of this suspension. 

The suffix numeral 400 indicates the rated 40,000-pound capacity of the 
suspension.

 RTE2-Series Suspension 

The RTE2 steel leaf suspension has conventional stacked leaf springs. 
Equalizing beams and the below-axle load design absorb strain, twist and road 
shock. 

RTE2-Series suspensions attach the leaf spring to the equalizing beam 
with bolts and a spring top pad. The equalizing beam design distributes the 
load equally between the axles.

================================================================================
PAGE 2946
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 04-02C: Suspension, Rear, Hendrickson RTE2-Series Tandem Axle

1997 CFT-8000 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Leaf Springs, Extended

The extended leaf suspension consists of conventional stacked leaf 
springs with the top two leaves extended to the rear. A two-stage spring 
action on the tandem suspension is created when the top spring leaves come 
into contact with a second, inner hanger. When the vehicle is empty, the 
spring weight is carried by the rearmost hanger and most of the spring 
deflection is through the top two leaves. As the load increases, the inner 
hanger comes in contact with the spring. At contact, the effective spring 
length is reduced, increasing the spring rate.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Spring

 Removal 

Raise the rear of the vehicle and position blocks under the frame 
behind the rear axle. 

Remove the wheels, brake drum and hub from the forward rear axle. 

Position a jack under the front end of the equalizing beam. 

Remove the caps from the lower side of the saddle. 

Remove the spring pin lock bolts from the spring front hanger. 

Remove the lube fitting and spring eye pin. 

Remove rebound bolt at the rear hanger.

Lower the spring and saddle and remove the spring from the equalizing 
beam.

Remove the spring top pad retaining bolts and nuts. Loosen the 
setscrews and remove the saddle and spring top pad from the spring. 

 Installation 

Position the saddle on the leaf spring assembly and install the top pad 
on the leaf spring. 

 NOTE: Lubricate the threads of all bolts with SAE-20 oil. 

Install the four top pad bolts and nuts. Alternately and evenly tighten 
the nuts until snug to hold the assembly in place (top view in the following 
illustration).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Spring Eye Pin 

 Removal 

Raise the vehicle frame until the load is removed from the spring eye 
pin. Place safety stands under the frame and support the weight at the axle 
with a floor jack.

Remove the spring pin lock bolts from the spring front hanger. 

Remove the lubrication fitting from the spring eye pin and remove the 
spring eye pin from the spring and spring hanger. 

 Installation 

Align the spring eye with the hanger and install the pin.

Install the spring pin lock bolts and retaining nuts. Tighten the nuts 
102-142 Nm (75-105 lb-ft).

with Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent lubricant 
meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B. 

Remove the floor jack and safety stands. Lower the vehicle.

 Removal

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Equalizing Beam 

 Removal 

Block the front wheels and both tandem axles to prevent the vehicle 
from moving. 

Exhaust the air from the air brake system. Mark and disconnect all air 
lines to the rear axles. Plug all lines to prevent the entry of dirt. Unlock 
all mechanically set safety brakes on the tandem axles. Refer to Section 06-08E or Section 06-08F .

 CAUTION: The axle is free to pivot on the beam ends. Use necessary blocking to 
prevent damage to the interaxle driveshaft, power divider and differential 
carriers. 

Remove the U-bolts and nuts and disconnect the driveshaft from the 
forward/rear tandem axle. 

Remove the bolts retaining the torque rods to the axle bracket ends and 
disconnect the torque rods.

Remove the nuts and washers from the saddle studs and remove the saddle 
caps. If a stud is removed along with a nut during saddle cap removal, remove 
the nut from the stud. Clean the stud threads and install the stud in the 
saddle with an appropriate stud installation tool. 

Raise the rear of the vehicle with an overhead hoist or A frame, and 
roll the tandem axles and equalizing beams out as an assembly. Support the 
frame with safety stands of an appropriate capacity. 

Apply penetrating oil to the threads of the bolts and lock nuts that 
connect the bar pin bushing to the axle bracket.

 WARNING: ALWAYS PLACE AN APPROPRIATE SUPPORT UNDER THE END OF THE EQUALIZING 
BEAM ASSEMBLY. THE BEAM CAN DROP UPON REMOVAL OF THE BAR PIN BUSHING RETAINING 
BOLTS. 

Remove the bolts and nuts retaining the bar pin bushing to the axle 
brackets.

[FIGURE: F8904B.gif]

Item

—

(Part of 5001)

 WARNING: DO NOT REUSE THE FASTENERS. AFTER ALL FASTENERS ARE REMOVED, DISCARD 
THEM. 

Remove the bar pin end attaching bolts and nuts on the opposite end of 
the equalizing beam.

With both ends of the equalizing beam removed, pull the beam off the 
crosstube.

Inspect the mounting surfaces of the axle brackets for gouges, cracks 
or excessive wear. Any cracks detected near the top of the axle bracket legs 
require replacement of the axle bracket. If any one of these conditions 
exists, contact the axle manufacturer for instructions.

The dimension between the inside surfaces of the axle bracket must be 
57-58 mm (2.263-2.313 inches).

[FIGURE: F8905B.gif]

 Installation 

Coat the connection holes in the axle bracket legs with an appropriate 
anti-seize compound. 

On equalizing beams with rubber center bushings, insert the crosstube 
into the center bushing inner sleeve of both equalizing beam rubber center 
bushings. On equalizing beams with bronze center bushings, apply Motorcraft 
Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M1C75-B to the bushing and inner sleeve.

Coat the inner and outer surfaces of the rubber end bushings with an 
appropriate anti-seize compound. 

Install the equalizing beams onto the crosstube. Position the two beams 
and crosstube under the drive axle assembly. 

 WARNING: WHEN USING THE SHIM STYLE BAR PIN BUSHING, A SHIM MUST BE INSTALLED AT 
EACH BOLT LOCATION. THE SAME PART NUMBER SHIM IN THE SAME ORIENTATION MUST BE 
USED AT BOTH BOLT LOCATIONS ON ANY ONE BUSHING ASSEMBLY. DO NOT INSTALL OR 
STACK MORE THAN ONE SHIM AT EACH BOLT LOCATION. USE GENUINE HENDRICKSON SHIMS. 
DO NOT USE STANDARD WASHERS. FAILURE TO FOLLOW THIS WARNING CAN RESULT IN THE 
FRACTURE OF EITHER THE BRACKET OR BAR PIN, WHICH COULD RESULT IN THE LOSS OF 
VEHICLE CONTROL AND POSSIBLE PERSONAL INJURY OR PROPERTY DAMAGE. 

 CAUTION: Once the retaining nuts are removed, they must be replaced. The nuts 
incorporate a self-locking feature that is damaged upon removal. 

Raise the beam end into the axle bracket and support it with a jack. If 
the axle pinion angle causes difficulty in assembly, disconnect the upper 
torque rod and rotate the axle so the bar pin slips into the bracket. Minor 
alignment adjustments to the inner metal of the bushing can be made with OTC 
tooling or an open end wrench.

Disconnect the longitudinal torque rods and assemble the bolts, washers 
and lock nuts. Do not tighten the nuts at this time.

With the equalizing beams attached to the axles, roll them under the 
center of the saddle, making sure that the center bushing of each equalizing 
beam is lined up with the center of the saddle legs. Lower the frame and 
center saddles on the equalizing beam center bushings. Install the saddle 
caps, washers and new nuts. Do not tighten the nuts at this time.

Connect the torque rods to the axle brackets and frame brackets. 
Install lock nuts and tighten to 204-277 Nm (150-205 lb-ft).

Tighten the equalizing beam end nuts to 611-813 Nm 
(450-600 lb-ft).

With the vehicle weight on the center bushings, evenly tighten the 
saddle cap lock nuts to maintain an even gap between the saddle cap and saddle 
during tightening to avoid distortion of saddle caps.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Beam End Bushing, Equalizing

 Removal 

Remove the equalizing beam.

Remove the confinement washer from one end of the bushing for pushing 
tool clearance. If required, use a chisel where the washer has been staked to 
the inner casting of the bushing.

[FIGURE: F8907A.gif]

Cut the protruding rubber on the same end of the beam end as shown. 
This permits the pushing tool to contact the outer metal of the bushing.

[FIGURE: F3529B.gif]

 WARNING: WHEN REMOVING AND INSTALLING BUSHINGS IN AN EQUALIZING BEAM, FOLLOW THE 
PROCEDURES DESCRIBED IN THIS SECTION. DO NOT USE A TORCH TO REMOVE THE BUSHING 
OUTER METAL PRESSED IN THE BEAM. WELDING, TORCHING OR ATTACHING MATERIAL TO 
THE EQUALIZING BEAM MUST NEVER BE PERFORMED. ALL EQUALIZING BEAMS (ALUMINUM 
AND STEEL) ARE HEAT TREATED FOR STRENGTH AND SERVICE LIFE. THE USE OF HEAT CAN 
ADVERSELY AFFECT THE STRENGTH OF THE BEAMS. AFTER REMOVING THE EQUALIZING BEAM 
BUSHINGS, THOROUGHLY INSPECT THE BEAM BORES. IF THE BEAM BORES ARE DAMAGED, 
REPLACE WITH A NEW EQUALIZING BEAM. 

 NOTE: If OTC tooling is to be used to remove the bushings, follow the 
instructions provided with the OTC tooling.

If OTC tooling is not used, fabricate a piece of steel tubing 101.6 mm 
(4 inches) long and 108 mm (4-1/4 inches) OD with 12.7 mm (1/2-inch) wall 
thickness to press out the bushing. The press should have a capacity of at 
least 72,570 kg (80 tons).

[FIGURE: F3531C.gif]

 Installation 

Inspect the bushing bores for nicks and burrs. Remove any nicks or 
burrs with emery cloth. 

Coat the bushing bore with Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C 
or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B. 

Clean the outer sleeve of the bushing with emery cloth to remove the 
phosphate coating that acts as a rust preventative. 

 NOTE: If OTC tooling is used, follow the instructions provided with the OTC 
tooling.

A shop-made installation tool can be fabricated using a 127 mm (5-inch) 
steel tube with a 127 mm (5-inch) OD and 12.7 mm (1/2-inch) wall thickness. 
The installation tool must be split in half, then bolted or clamped together 
to compress the rubber to allow contact with the bushing outer metal.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Bushing, Center, Bronze, Beam Installed 

 Removal 

Block the front wheels to prevent the vehicle from moving. 

Remove the nuts retaining the saddle caps to the saddle. Remove the 
saddle caps. 

Raise the rear of the frame until the saddle cap studs clear the 
equalizing beam assembly. 

If required, remove and replace the lube fitting in the equalizing beam 
assembly. 

Remove the thrust washers and center sleeves from the equalizing beams. 
Remove the crosstube from the beam center bushing bore. 

Remove the bushings using Bushing Remover Tool Set 1745 and adapters as 
shown in the illustration under Bushing, Center, Bronze, Beam Removed. 

 Installation 

 NOTE: Do not install a bronze center bushing in an aluminum equalizing beam.

Position the bronze center bushing in the bore so the lubricant groove 
lies along the vertical centerline of the equalizing beam. 

Press the bronze bushing and seals into the bore. 

Coat the bushing inside diameter and the center sleeve with Motorcraft 
Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent lubricant meeting Ford 
specification ESA-M1C75-B. 

 NOTE: When installing thrust washers on the center sleeves, install washers 
until the gap is less than one washer. 

Install two thrust washers (total four) on the inboard side of each 
bronze bushing. Install the crosstube and center sleeves. Install two thrust 
washers (total four) on the outboard side of each bronze bushing. 

Install the lube fitting in the equalizing beam. 

Lower the frame until the saddle is in position over the equalizing 
beam and crosstube assembly. 

 NOTE: The weight of the vehicle must be on the suspension (axle in operating 
position) when the saddle cap retaining nuts are tightened.

Install the saddle caps. Install the washers and nuts on the studs and 
tighten the nuts to 306-372 Nm (225-275 lb-ft).

Pressure lubricate both center bushings with Motorcraft Premium 
Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent lubricant meeting Ford 
specification ESA-M1C75-B.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Bushing, Center, Rubber, Beam Removed 

 Removal 

Remove the equalizing beam. 

Inspect the area surrounding the bushing outer metal for signs of 
mushrooming. Remove all signs of mushrooming with a chisel or disc sander.

 WARNING: WHEN REMOVING AND INSTALLING BUSHINGS IN EQUALIZING BEAMS, FOLLOW 
PROCEDURES DESCRIBED IN THIS SECTION. DO NOT USE A TORCH TO REMOVE THE BUSHING 
OUTER METAL PRESSED IN THE BEAM. WELDING, TORCHING OR ATTACHING MATERIAL TO 
THE EQUALIZING BEAM MUST NEVER BE PERFORMED. ALL EQUALIZING BEAMS (ALUMINUM 
AND STEEL) ARE HEAT TREATED FOR STRENGTH AND SERVICE LIFE. THE USE OF HEAT CAN 
ADVERSELY AFFECT THE STRENGTH OF THE BEAM. AFTER REMOVING THE EQUALIZING BEAM 
BUSHINGS, THOROUGHLY INSPECT THE BEAM BORES. IF TORCH UNDERCUTTING IS FOUND, 
REPLACE WITH A NEW EQUALIZING BEAM. 

 CAUTION: When pressing the bushing out, make sure the equalizing beam is 
securely supported at the center bore area on the press bed to avoid bending 
the equalizing beam. 

Remove the rubber bushing with OTC tool set Y-849 and adapter Y-861. If 
the tool set is not available, use a press of at least 45,000 kg (50-ton) 
capacity. Press the bushing out with a piece of tubing with a 117 mm (4-5/8 
inch) OD and a 178 mm (7-inch) length.

 Installation 

Inspect the bushing bore for nicks and burrs. Remove any nicks and 
burrs with emery cloth. 

Clean the outer steel sleeve of the rubber bushing with emery cloth to 
remove the phosphate coating that acts as a rust preventative. 

Apply a coating of Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or 
equivalent lubricant meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B around the bushing 
outer sleeve. 

Position the bushing in the bore and install using a press of at least 
45,000 kg (50-ton) capacity. Press the bushing in with OTC tool 302026. If 
tool is not available, press the bushing in place with a piece of tubing with 
a 117 mm (4-5/8 inch) OD and a length of 178 mm (7 inches).

Install the equalizing beam.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Bushing, Center, Rubber, Beam Installed

 Removal 

Block the front wheels to prevent movement of the vehicle. 

Remove the nuts retaining the saddle caps to the saddle and remove the

 CAUTION: DO NOT USE A TORCH TO REMOVE THE WELDED PLUG; THE EQUALIZING BEAM CAN

beams.

Remove the crosstube. 

Inspect the inside face of the equalizing beam center hub. If the 
bushing outer sleeve is excessively worn, and the edge is "mushroomed" over 
the inner face of the equalizing beam hub remove the mushroomed surface with a 
chisel or disc sander. 

 WARNING: WHEN REMOVING AND INSTALLING BUSHINGS IN EQUALIZING BEAMS, FOLLOW 
PROCEDURES DESCRIBED IN THIS SECTION. DO NOT USE A TORCH TO REMOVE THE BUSHING 
OUTER METAL PRESSED IN THE BEAM. WELDING, TORCHING OR ATTACHING MATERIAL TO 
THE EQUALIZING BEAM MUST NEVER BE PERFORMED. ALL EQUALIZING BEAMS (ALUMINUM 
AND STEEL) ARE HEAT TREATED FOR STRENGTH AND SERVICE LIFT. THE USE OF HEAT CAN 
ADVERSELY AFFECT THE STRENGTH OF A BEAM. AFTER REMOVING THE EQUALIZING BEAM 
BUSHINGS, THOROUGHLY INSPECT THE BEAM BORES. IF THE BEAM BORES ARE DAMAGED, 
REPLACE WITH A NEW EQUALIZING BEAM.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Torque Rod, Straddle (Longitudinal) Mount 

 Removal 

Position a jack under the differential carrier housing to prevent the 
axle from tipping. 

Remove the two retaining nuts and the two bolts that retain the torque 
rod to the axle, and rotate arm clear of housing. 

Remove the two nuts that retain the torque rod and bracket to the frame 
crossmember, and remove torque rod and bracket from vehicle. 

Inspect the torque rod and bushings for visual damage and bushing wear. 
If metal-to-metal contact exists between torque arm housing and torque rod 
pin, if rubber seems excessively worn, or if looseness is encountered between 
pin and bushing, replace torque rod assembly. If unusually damaged (cracks in 
weld or parent metal or rod bent such that ends are not parallel with each 
other), replace the torque rod assembly. 

 Installation 

If original axle angle settings are to be retained, install torque rod 
and bracket to frame crossmember with original shims in place and tighten nuts 
to 204-277 Nm (150-205 lb-ft). Go to Step 3.

Install torque rod and bracket assembly to frame crossmember on top of 
original spacers. Assemble nuts loosely onto bracket retaining bolts. Assemble 
torque rod to axle and tighten to 204-277 Nm (150-205 lb-ft). 

Set new angles by adding or subtracting spacer(s) to original spacer 
pack under the torque arm frame bracket. (Remove the jack under the axle 
housing during this procedure, if necessary.) When the desired axle angle is 
attained, reset the jack under housing (if removed).

Assemble the spacers properly under the torque rod bracket and tighten 
the nuts to 204-277 Nm (150-205 lb-ft). 

Install the torque rod to axle by rotating torque arm into position and 
installing nuts, bolts and washers. Place a washer under the bolt head and 
nut. Tighten the nuts to 204-277 Nm (150-205 lb-ft). 

Remove the jack from under the differential carrier housing.

Suspension

The Hendrickson E4-400 (40,000-pound capacity) tandem suspension is a

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Spring 

 Removal 

Chock axle wheels. 

 WARNING: DO NOT USE A CUTTING TORCH TO REMOVE ANY FASTENERS. DO NOT USE A 
CUTTING TORCH TO REMOVE THE BUSHINGS FROM THE EQUALIZING BEAM ASSEMBLY. THE 
USE OF HEAT ON SUSPENSION COMPONENTS WILL ADVERSELY AFFECT THE STRENGTH OF 
THESE PARTS. A COMPONENT DAMAGED IN THIS MANNER CAN CAUSE THE LOSS OF VEHICLE 
CONTROL AND POSSIBLE PERSONAL INJURY OR PROPERTY DAMAGE. 

Straighten keeper tabs on bolt retainer plate and loosen both upper and 
lower shackle bolts. 

Remove rebound bolt, rebound roller, lock nut, washers and spacer from 
end spring hanger. 

Raise rear of frame far enough to remove load from spring. 

Remove U-bolt lock nuts and washers. 

Remove U-bolts, bottom cap and top pad. 

 WARNING: DO NOT REUSE SHACKLE BOLT RETAINER PLATE. 

Remove both shackle bolts (raise frame, if necessary, for bolts to 
clear tires). Discard shackle bolt retainer plate.

Remove spring assembly. 

 Installation 

Position shackle on eye of new or serviced spring assembly as shown in 
the following illustration. Hook must go through opening provided in shackle. 
Threaded bosses must be positioned toward vehicle frame.

[FIGURE: F37081D.gif]

Assemble one shackle bolt with new retainer plate through upper shackle 
hole and spring eye.

Position spring on spring seat with spring center bolt piloting into 
countersunk hole in spring seat while aligning lower shackle legs over 
equalizing beam end bushing. 

Assemble other shackle bolt through retainer plate and lower shackle 
hole and equalizing beam end bushing. Hand-tighten shackle bolt. 

Assemble top pad, U-bolts, bottom cap, washers and lock nuts. 

Lower frame so that end spring hanger engages spring. 

Tighten U-bolt lock nuts to specified torque. Rap top of U-bolts and 
retighten to 360-480 Nm (266-354 lb-ft).

Tighten shackle bolts to 406-542 Nm (300-400 lb-ft) 
and bend both keeper tabs at each bolt. 

Assemble rebound bolt, rebound roller, spacer, washers and lock nut in 
end spring hanger. Tighten lock nut to 102-142 Nm (75-105 
lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Beam End Bushing, Equalizing

 Removal 

 WARNING: DO NOT USE A CUTTING TORCH TO REMOVE ANY FASTENERS. DO NOT USE A 
CUTTING TORCH TO REMOVE THE BUSHINGS FROM THE EQUALIZING BEAM ASSEMBLY. THE 
USE OF HEAT ON SUSPENSION COMPONENTS WILL ADVERSELY AFFECT THE STRENGTH OF 
THESE PARTS. A COMPONENT DAMAGED IN THIS MANNER CAN CAUSE LOSS OF VEHICLE 
CONTROL AND POSSIBLE PERSONAL INJURY OR PROPERTY DAMAGE. 

[FIGURE: F3709C.gif]

Chock wheels or rear drive axle, and support rear of frame. 

Remove torque rod bar pin lock nuts, bolts, washers and any shims from 
the center spring hanger. Note the number of shims at each location. These 
must be reinstalled in the same manner to avoid affecting alignment. 

 WARNING: DO NOT REUSE SHACKLE BOLT RETAINER PLATES. 

Straighten all keeper tabs on shackle bolt retainer plates and remove 
all shackle bolts. Discard shackle bolt retainer plates. 

Reinstall upper shackle bolts through spring eyes with new shackle bolt 
retainer plates. Do not tighten. 

Remove center spring hanger to equalizing beam lock nut, washers and 
bolt. 

Lower frame so that equalizing beam ends drop clear of shackles. 

Slide equalizing beam forward and down, out of center spring hanger. 
Note that there are thrust washers between the beam and the hanger (one on 
each side of each beam). 

 WARNING: DO NOT USE HEAT OR A CUTTING TORCH TO REMOVE THE BUSHING OUTER METALS 
THAT ARE PRESSED IN THE BEAM. THE USE OF HEAT WILL ADVERSELY AFFECT THE 
STRENGTH OF THE BEAM. 

 CAUTION: Make sure the beam is securely supported at the bore area on the press 
bed for safety and to avoid bending the equalizing beam. 

Press out old bushings. Use a vertical shop press with a capacity of at 
least 15 tons. For end bushing removal, use a 102-mm (4-inch) long piece of 
2-1/4-inch outside diameter x 1/4-inch wall steel tubing. For center bushing 
removal, use a 127-mm (5-inch) long piece of 2-5/8-inch outside diameter x 
1/4-inch wall steel tubing.

Clean bores of equalizing beam with emery cloth to remove any nicks or 
metal buildup from bushing removal. 

Clean outer metals of new bushings with emery cloth to remove phosphate 
coating which acts as a rust preventative. Apply a thin coat of grease on the 
outer metal of bushings. 

 CAUTION: Make sure the beam is securely supported at the bore area on the press 
bed for safety and to avoid bending the equalizing beam. 

Press in new bushings. For end bushing installation, use a 76-mm 
(3-inch) piece of 2-1/2-inch outside diameter x 1/4-inch wall steel tubing. 
For center bushing installation, use a 76-mm (3-inch) long piece of 2-3/4-inch 
outside diameter x 1/4-inch long steel tubing. Center all bushings in beam. 
The pushing tool must contact only the outer metals of the bushings.

Remove any remaining grease from ends of rubber bushings. End faces of 
rubber bushings must be clean and dry before assembling beam with shackles and 
center spring hanger. 

 Installation 

Position equalizing beam with thrust washers in center spring hanger. 
The inside diameter of the thrust washers must be on the outside diameter of 
the beam center bushing inner metal. There must be one thrust washer on each 
side of each beam. Assemble bolt, washers and lock nut. With equalizing beam 
parallel to frame as viewed from the side of the vehicle, tighten lock nut to 
543-671 Nm (400-495 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: F3710D.gif]

Raise frame until equalizing beam ends align with lower shackle bolt

Assemble lower shackle bolts and tighten both upper and lower shackle

against shackle bolt heads. 

Position bar pin end of torque rod at forward face of spring hanger

during disassembly. Tighten lock nuts to 204-277 Nm (150-205 
lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Torque Rod 

 Removal 

Chock wheels of drive axles. 

 WARNING: DO NOT USE A CUTTING TORCH TO REMOVE ANY FASTENERS. THE USE OF HEAT ON 
SUSPENSION COMPONENTS WILL ADVERSELY AFFECT THE STRENGTH OF THESE PARTS. A 
COMPONENT DAMAGED IN THIS MANNER CAN CAUSE THE LOSS OF VEHICLE CONTROL AND 
POSSIBLE PERSONAL INJURY OR PROPERTY DAMAGE. 

Remove bar pin lock nuts and washers at axle end of torque rod. 

Loosen rebound bolt in spring hanger from which torque rod is being 
removed. 

Remove bar pin lock nuts, bolts, washers and any alignment shims at 
spring hanger ends of torque rods. Note the number of shims at each location. 
These must be installed in the same manner to avoid affecting alignment. 

 Installation 

 NOTE: The torque rod can be installed in one way only. Be sure to read the 
directional instructions on the rod before installation. 

Position axle end of new torque rod on axle cap studs and assemble 
washers and lock nuts. Hand-tighten lock nuts. 

 NOTE: For the center spring hanger, the equalizing beam center bolt must be 
tightened before the rear torque rod is installed. 

Position forward bar pin end of new torque rod at forward face of 
spring hanger legs and assemble bolts, washers, lock nuts and any alignment 
shims that were removed.

Tighten the lock nuts to 204-277 Nm (150-205 lb-ft). 

Tighten rebound bolt lock nut to 102-142 Nm (75-105 
lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Bushing, Torque Rod

 Removal 

 WARNING: DO NOT USE HEAT OR A CUTTING TORCH TO REMOVE THE BUSHINGS FROM THE 
TORQUE ROD. THE USE OF HEAT WILL ADVERSELY AFFECT THE STRENGTH OF THE TORQUE 
ROD. 

Use a press with a minimum capacity of 10 tons. 

 CAUTION: Make sure the torque rod is securely supported on the press bed. 

Support the torque rod on a piece of 6-mm (1/4-inch) wall steel tubing 
that is 127 mm (5 inches) long with an inside diameter of 50.8 mm (2.0 inches).

Push directly on the bar pin to remove bushing from the torque rod. 

 Installation 

Clean and inspect the inside diameter of the ends of the torque rod. 
Use emery cloth to remove any nicks and small scratches from the bore. 

 CAUTION: Do not use a petroleum or soap base lubricant. 

Lubricate the inside diameter of the torque rod and the new bushing 
with a vegetable base oil such as cooking oil or lard.

 CAUTION: Make sure the torque rod is securely supported on the press bed. 

Support the torque rod on the piece of steel tubing used during 
removal. Make sure the bore of the torque rod is centered in the tube.

Put the bushing in the bore of the torque rod so the mounting flat of 
the bar pin is positioned as shown in the following illustrations.

 Front Torque Rod Bushing Installation 

[FIGURE: F6434A.gif]

 Rear Torque Rod Bushing Installation 

[FIGURE: F6435A.gif]

Press the bushing into the torque rod so the bushing extends 4.763 mm 
(3/16 inch) on the opposite side of the torque rod. 

Turn the torque rod over and press on the bar pin so the bushing is 
centered in the torque rod bore.

ADJUSTMENTS

Alignment 

 Tandem Suspension 

The following procedure should be performed after all service has been 
completed and all suspension fasteners have been tightened to specified torque 
values. 

Place vehicle on a level floor area. Move it back and forth several 
times slowly and without using brakes to free and center all suspension 
joints. In this condition, equalizing beams must be essentially level. 

Chock front wheels and make sure vehicle brakes are released. 

Using C-clamps, securely clamp a 9-foot piece of straight bar stock or 
angle iron across frame as shown in the following illustration. Select a 
location as far forward of forward drive axle as possible where vehicle 
components will not interfere. On some vehicles, lower frame flange might be 
preferred. Otherwise use upper frame flange. 

Accurately square straightedge to frame using a carpenter's square. 

Begin alignment by checking rear drive axle first. Use a trammel bar or 
its equivalent to measure from straightedge to centerline of rear drive axle 
on both sides of vehicle as shown in the following illustration, Ll and Lr. If 
both sides measure within 5 mm (3/16 inch) of each other, alignment of rear 
drive axle is acceptable.

[FIGURE: F37051A.gif]

If Ll and Lr differ by more than 5 mm (3/16 inch), adjust rear drive 
axle by loosening up torque rod bar pin lock nuts on center spring hanger and 
add drop-in shims as shown in the following illustration. Torque rod bar pin 
must always be mounted adjacent to forward face of spring hanger legs. No more 
than four shims may be used (6.35 mm [1/4 inch] maximum 
total thickness). Snug torque rod bar pin lock nuts but do not tighten to 
specification.

[FIGURE: F3706F.gif]

With rear drive axle properly aligned, front drive axle alignment can 
be checked by measuring forward from rear drive axle center using a trammel 
bar. Adjust pointers on trammel bar to pilot into center-drilled holes in axle 
shafts. If the forward drive axle spacing measurements (Sl and Sr) differ by

similar manner. Snug torque rod bar pin lock nuts.

[FIGURE: F3707B.gif]

Following alignment of both axles, move vehicle back and forth several 
times prior to removing straightedge from frame, and recheck alignment to 
confirm adjustments. Tighten torque rod bar pin lock nuts to 204-277 Nm
 (150-205 lb-ft).
