 Disassembly 

Lay shift bar housing on workbench. Remove all capscrews and retainers.

[FIGURE: C7355B.gif]

Remove 1st-reverse yoke assembly.

[FIGURE: C73561A.gif]

Remove 2nd-3rd yoke assembly and interlock pin.

[FIGURE: C73571A.gif]

Remove 4th-5th yoke assembly.

[FIGURE: C73581A.gif]

If yoke replacement is required, remove yoke by driving the roll pin 
through the yoke and rail. If the yoke pad inserts are to be replaced, remove 
worn pad from shift fork, install new pad and bend tabs over top and bottom of 
fork. 

 NOTE: Remove interlock and detent balls before removing springs. 

Remove interlock balls, detent balls and springs.

[FIGURE: C73591A.gif]

 WARNING: THE SNAP RING AND RETAINER WASHER ARE UNDER SPRING PRESSURE. 

If the removal of the reverse plunger is necessary, secure the shift 
bar in a hand press. Depress the retainer washer and spring and remove the 
snap ring.

Remove the retainer washer.

Remove the inner and outer springs.

Remove the washer and the reverse plunger.

 Assembly 

If reverse plunger was removed, install reverse plunger and washer in 
reverse shift block.

 WARNING: THE SNAP RING AND RETAINER WASHER WILL BE UNDER PRESSURE WHEN INSTALLED. 

Install outer and inner springs.

Place the shift bar in a hand press. Depress retainer washer and spring 
and install the snap ring.

 NOTE: Balls and springs can be used interchangeably. 

Install interlock balls, detent balls and springs in the following 
sequence:

Position three balls into reverse light switch bore and install 
1st-reverse detent spring and ball. 

Position two balls in adjacent cross bore and install 2nd-3rd detent 
spring and ball. 

Position two balls in adjacent cross bore and install 4th-5th detent 
spring and ball.

 NOTE: All yoke assemblies must be installed in the neutral position. 

Position 1st-reverse yoke in housing.

[FIGURE: C73601A.gif]

Install interlock pin in 2nd-3rd yoke assembly and install in housing. 
Position yoke in housing as shown in the illustration.

[FIGURE: C73611A.gif]

Position 4th-5th yoke assembly in housing as shown in the illustration.

[FIGURE: C7362B.gif]

 NOTE: If a new housing is being used in the assembly, the bores for the 
retainer capscrews are not tapped. The capscrews that are used are 
thread-forming and can be reused on a new housing. 

 NOTE: Support yokes in the proper position while installing retainers. 

Install front retainer over shift bars. Coat threads of retainer

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Mainshaft 

 Disassembly 

Install mainshaft assembly in a soft-jawed vise or use wood blocks to 
prevent damage. Position mainshaft in vise with the front of the shaft facing 
up. Remove the 4th-5th synchronizer and cups.

[FIGURE: C7366B.gif]

Use a suitable puller such as 2-Jaw Puller D80L-1002-L or equivalent 
mounted behind the 4th-5th shift hub and remove the hub and bearing.

[FIGURE: C12472A.gif]

Remove 4th gear, bearings and spacer from mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C73681A.gif]

Remove snap ring, thrust washer and locating ball from 3rd gear.

[FIGURE: C73691A.gif]

Remove 3rd gear, bearings and spacer.

[FIGURE: C73701A.gif]

Remove 2nd-3rd speed synchronizer and cups.

[FIGURE: C7371C.gif]

Remove snap ring and 2nd-3rd shift hub.

[FIGURE: C7372C.gif]

Remove 2nd gear, bearings and spacer from mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C7383C.gif]

Remove snap ring, thrust washer and locating ball from mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C7374C.gif]

Remove 1st gear, bearings and spacer from mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C7375C.gif]

Remove mainshaft sliding clutch gear.

[FIGURE: C7376C.gif]

Reposition mainshaft in vise with the rear of the shaft facing up.

[FIGURE: C73771A.gif]

Using 2-Jaw Puller D80L-1002-L or equivalent, remove the reverse gear, 
washer and rear bearing.

[FIGURE: C12473A.gif]

Remove reverse gear bearings and spacer from mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C73791A.gif]

 Assembly 

 NOTE: All parts must be lubricated with recommended transmission lubricant 
when reassembling. No part should be reassembled dry. Refer to Recommended 
Lubricants chart under the Transmission Oil Drain and Refill 
Procedure in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

Install mainshaft in vise equipped with wood or brass jaws, rear of 
mainshaft facing up. Lubricate reverse gear bearings, and install with spacer 
between bearings.

Install reverse gear with clutching teeth of gear down.

[FIGURE: C73801A.gif]

Install reverse gear washer. Washer can be installed either way.

[FIGURE: C73811A.gif]

Using a sleeve-type bearing driver, install rear bearing.

[FIGURE: C73821A.gif]

Reposition mainshaft in vise with front of mainshaft facing up. 
Lubricate friction surface, and install mainshaft sliding clutch gear.

[FIGURE: C7376C.gif]

Lubricate and install 1st gear bearings and spacer. Install 1st gear, 
clutching teeth facing down.

[FIGURE: C7375C.gif]

Install locating ball and thrust washer. Washer can be installed either 
way. Install snap ring.

[FIGURE: C7374C.gif]

Lubricate and install 2nd gear bearings and spacer. Install 2nd gear, 
clutching teeth facing up.

[FIGURE: C7383C.gif]

Install 2nd-3rd shift hub with stepped face of hub facing up. Install 
snap ring in groove of mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C7372C.gif]

Lubricate friction surface, and install 2nd-3rd speed synchronizer and 
cups.

[FIGURE: C7371C.gif]

Lubricate and install 3rd gear bearings and spacer. Install 3rd gear, 
clutching teeth facing down.

[FIGURE: C73701A.gif]

Install locating ball and thrust washer. Washer can be installed either 
way. Install snap ring.

[FIGURE: C73691A.gif]

Lubricate and install 4th gear bearings and spacer. Install 4th gear, 
clutching teeth facing up.

[FIGURE: C73681A.gif]

Install 4th-5th shift hub with shouldered end of hub facing down.

[FIGURE: C7384B.gif]

Install synchronizer cup. Lubricate friction surface, and install 
4th-5th speed synchronizer assembly and synchronizer cup.

[FIGURE: C7366B.gif]

Using a suitable sleeve-type driver, install main drive gear bearing. 

[FIGURE: C7386B.gif]

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Countershaft 

 Disassembly 

Position 2-Jaw Puller D80L-1002-L or equivalent behind rear 
countershaft bearing and remove bearing.

[FIGURE: C12474A.gif]

Position countershaft in vise with the front of the shaft facing up. 
Position puller jaws into notches behind the front countershaft bearing and 
remove bearing.

[FIGURE: C73881A.gif]

Remove drive gear retaining snap ring from front of shaft. 

Using the rear face of the drive gear as a base, press it from the 
countershaft using Rotunda 25-Ton Capacity General Purpose Press 014-00085 or 
equivalent.

[FIGURE: C73891A.gif]

Remove the drive gear locating key and spacer from the shaft.

[FIGURE: C73901A.gif]

Using the rear face of the 4th gear as a base, press it from the 
countershaft. Remove the 4th gear locating key from the shaft.

[FIGURE: C73911A.gif]

 NOTE: Be sure that the 4th speed gear key has been removed before removing 
3rd gear from countershaft. 

Using the rear face of the 3rd speed gear as a base, press it from the 
countershaft.

[FIGURE: C73921A.gif]

Using the rear face of the 2nd speed gear as a base, press it from the 
countershaft.

[FIGURE: C73931A.gif]

 Assembly 

Press 2nd speed gear on countershaft, long hub of gear to front of 
shaft (i.e., pointing down in the press).

[FIGURE: C73941A.gif]

Press 3rd speed gear on countershaft, long hub of gear to rear of shaft 
(i.e., pointing up in the press).

[FIGURE: C73951A.gif]

 CAUTION: Make sure that keyway in gear is aligned with key in shaft before 
pressing gear on. Serious damage will result if key and keyway are not 
aligned. 

Install 4th and 5th drive gear keys on countershaft. Align keyway of 
4th speed gear to key on shaft. Press 4th speed gear on, long hub of gear to 
front of shaft (i.e., pointing down in the press).

[FIGURE: DC0278A.gif]

Remove 5th drive gear key from countershaft and install spacer. 

[FIGURE: C73971A.gif]

Reinstall key and align keyway of 5th drive gear with key on 
countershaft. Press 5th drive gear on shaft, long hub of gear to rear of 
shaft. 

Install snap ring in groove at front of countershaft.

Install front countershaft bearing with a suitable sleeve-type driver.

[FIGURE: C73981A.gif]

Install rear countershaft bearing with a suitable sleeve-type driver.

[FIGURE: C73991A.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Identification 

[FIGURE: C12536A.gif]

The transmissions have six forward speeds and one reverse speed. All 
gears are helical cut and have the following ratios:

1st 9.01:1 

2nd 5.27:1 

3rd 3.22:1 

4th 2.04:1 

5th 1.36:1 

6th 1.00:1 

Reverse 8.63:1 

Countershaft end play is controlled by shims located in the 
countershaft rear bearing cap. Mainshaft end play is controlled by shims 
located in the mainshaft rear bearing cover. The shift forks are single-piece 
forged and are equipped with bronze wear pads that can be replaced.

PAGE 3372
================================================================================

Section 07-03D: Transmission, Manual, Eaton FS-5306A and FS-6306A Six-Speed

1997 CF-8000, CFT-8000 Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Power Flow 

 NOTE: The numbers in these steps correspond to the numbers in the following 
Transmission Power Flow Cross Section View illustration.

The transmission transfers torque from the engine to the driveshaft 
through the following route: 

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the input shaft and 
drive gear. 

The input shaft drive gear transfers torque to the countershaft drive 
gear.

The countershaft drive gear turns the countershaft and all countershaft 
gears. 

Torque from the countershaft gear is transferred to the mainshaft gear 
that is currently engaged. 

The external clutching teeth of the engaged mainshaft gear transfer 
torque to the mainshaft through the synchronizer assembly. 

The mainshaft transfers torque directly to the driveshaft through the 
rear yoke. 

 Transmission Power Flow Cross Section View 

[FIGURE: C9996C.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Transmission Oil Drain and Refill Procedure

 CAUTION: The use of mild EP gear oil or multi-purpose gear oil is not 
recommended, but if these gear oils are used, be sure to adhere to the 
following limitations. 

 CAUTION: Do not use mild EP gear oil or multi-purpose gear oil when operating 
temperatures are above 110°C (230°F). Many 
of these gear oils, particularly 85W140, break down above 110°
C (230°F) and coat seals, bearings, and gears with deposits 
that can cause premature failures. If these deposits are observed (especially 
a coating on seal areas causing oil leakage), change to Eaton Roadranger®
 CD50 transmission fluid, heavy-duty engine oil, or mineral 
gear oil to ensure maximum component life and to maintain your warranty with 
Eaton. Refer to Operating Temperatures in this section. 

 CAUTION: Additives and friction modifiers are not recommended for use in Eaton 
Fuller transmissions. 

Proper lubrication procedures are the key to a good all-around 
maintenance program. If the oil is not doing its job, or if the oil level is 
ignored, all the maintenance procedures in the world are not going to keep the 
transmission running or ensure long transmission life.

Eaton Fuller transmissions are designed so that the internal parts 
operate in an oil circulating bath by the motion of the gears and shafts.

All parts are amply lubricated if the following procedures are closely 
followed:

Maintain oil level. Inspect regularly.

Change oil regularly.

Use the correct grade and type of oil.

Buy from a reputable dealer.

 LUBRICATION CHANGE AND INSPECTION

Eaton Roadranger® CD50 Transmission Fluid

 HIGHWAY USE 

Every 16 093 km (10,000 miles)

Check fluid level. Check for leaks.

Every 402 325 km (250,000 miles)

Change transmission fluid.

 OFF-HIGHWAY USE 

Every 40 hours

Inspect fluid level. Check for leaks.

Every 500 hours

Change transmission fluid where severe dirt conditions exist.

Every 1,000 hours

Change transmission fluid. (Normal off-highway use.)

 HIGHWAY USE — Heavy-Duty Engine Lubricant or Mineral 
Gear Lubricant 

First 4 828 to 8 047 km (3,000 to 5,000 miles)

Factory fill initial drain.

Every 16 093 km (10,000 miles)

Inspect lubricant level. Check for leaks.

Every 80 465 km (50,000 miles)

Change transmission lubricant.

 OFF-HIGHWAY USE 

First 30 hours

Change transmission lubricant on new units.

Every 40 hours

Inspect lubricant level. Check for leaks.

Every 500 hours

Change transmission lubricant where severe dirt conditions exist.

Every 1,000 hours

Change transmission lubricant. (Normal off-highway use.)

 Proper Oil Level 

Make sure oil is level with the filler opening. Because you can reach 
oil with your finger does not mean oil is at proper level. An oil level of 
25.4 mm (one inch) is equal to approximately 3.7 liters (one gallon) of oil.

[FIGURE: C11745A.gif]

 Draining Oil 

Drain transmission while oil is warm. To drain oil remove the drain 
plug at case bottom. Clean the drain plug before reinstalling.

 Refilling 

 CAUTION: When adding oil, do not mix types and brands of oil because of possible 
incompatibility. 

Clean case around filler plug and remove plug from case side. Fill the 
transmission to the level of the filler opening. If the transmission has two 
filler openings, fill to the level of both openings.

The exact amount of oil depends on the transmission inclination and 
model. Do not overfill when refilling the oil. Overfilling causes the oil to 
be forced out of the case through the front bearing cover. 

 Proper Lubrication Levels as Related to Transmission Installation Angles 

If the transmission operating angle is more than 12 degrees, improper 
lubrication can occur. The operating angle is the transmission mounting angle 
in the chassis plus the percent of upgrade (expressed in degrees).

The chart below illustrates the safe percent of upgrade on which the 
transmission can be used with various chassis mounting angles. For example, if 
you have a four-degree transmission mounting angle, then eight degrees (or 14 
percent of grade) is equal to the limit of 12 degrees. If you have a 
zero-degree mounting angle, the transmission can be operated on a 12-degree 
(21 percent) grade.

Anytime the transmission operating angle or 12 degrees is exceeded for 
an extended period of time, the transmission should be equipped with an oil 
pump or cooler kit to make sure transmission is properly lubricated.

Note on the chart the effect low oil levels can have on safe operating 
angles. Allowing the oil level to fall one-half inch below the filler plug 
hole reduces the degree of grade by approximately three degrees (5.5 percent). 
Proper lubrication levels are essential.

[FIGURE: C11746A.gif]

 Operating Temperatures 

 With Eaton Roadranger® CD50 Transmission Fluid, 
Heavy-Duty Engine Oil and Mineral Oil 

The transmission should not be operated consistently at temperatures 
above 120°C (250°F). However, intermittent 
operating temperatures to 149°C (300°F) will 
not harm the transmission. Operating temperatures above 120°C 
(250°F) increase the lubricant's rate of oxidation and 
shorten its effective life. When the average operating temperature is above 120°
C (250°F), the transmission may require 
more frequent oil changes or external cooling.

The following conditions in any combination can cause operating 
temperatures of over 120°C (250°F).

operating consistently at slow speeds

high ambient temperatures

restricted airflow around transmission

exhaust system too close to transmission

high horsepower, overdrive operation

External oil coolers are available to reduce operating temperatures 
when the above conditions are encountered.

Transmission oil coolers are recommended with the following engines:

350 HP and above with overdrive transmissions

Transmission oil coolers are required with the following engines:

399 HP and above with overdrive transmissions and GCW's over 40,824 kg 
(90,000 lb).

399 HP and above and 1898 Nm (1400 lb-ft) or greater 
torque

450 HP and above

 With EP or Multipurpose Gear Oil 

Mild EP gear oil and multipurpose gear oil are not recommended when 
lubricant operating temperatures are above 110°C (230°
F). In addition, transmission oil coolers are not 
recommended with these gear oils, since the oil cooler materials may be 
attacked by these gear oils. The lower temperature limit and oil cooler 
restriction with these gear oils generally limit their success to milder 
applications.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Transmission 

 Removal 

Tilt cab. 

Disconnect battery(s). 

Disconnect speedometer sensor and backup lamp switch.

[FIGURE: C5263D.gif]

Remove control rod ball joint-to-remote shift lever retaining nut and 
bolt. Remove rod bracket-to-remote shift lever control top retaining bolts. 
Remove lower ball joint and rod bracket.

[FIGURE: C5264C.gif]

Position a suitable drain pan under transmission. Remove drain plug and 
drain the transmission oil. Reinstall drain plug and tighten to 61-75 Nm
 (45-55 lb-ft). 

Remove driveshaft. Refer to Section 05-01 . 

Disconnect clutch linkage. Refer to Section 08-02 .

Disconnect and remove fuel lines and bracketry as required. Refer to 
 Section 10-01 .

Position Rotunda Heavy-Duty Truck Transmission Jack 164-R3510 or 
equivalent under the transmission.

Fabricate two guide pins from standard bolts as shown.

[FIGURE: C52661A.gif]

Remove two lower screws and washers retaining the transmission to the 
clutch housing. Install the two fabricated guide pins into the lower holes. 
Remove the two upper screws and washers retaining the transmission to the 
clutch housing.

Remove transmission from the clutch housing. Refer to Section 08-01 .

Lower transmission from vehicle.

 Installation 

If removed, reinstall the two fabricated guide pins into lower holes of 
clutch housing.

Using Rotunda Heavy-Duty Truck Transmission Jack 164-R3510 or 
equivalent, raise and align transmission to the clutch housing. Install 
transmission to the clutch housing. Refer to Section 08-01 . 

Install two upper transmission-to-clutch housing retaining screws and 
washers and tighten to 197-210 Nm (145-155 lb-ft).

Remove fabricated guide pins. Install two lower transmission-to-clutch 
housing retaining screws and washers and tighten to 197-210 Nm
 (145-155 lb-ft).

Install and connect fuel lines and bracketry as required. Refer to 
 Section 10-01 .

Connect clutch linkage. Refer to Section 08-02 .

Install driveshaft. Refer to Section 05-01 .

Install lower ball joint and rod bracket to remote shift lever control 
top. Install and tighten retaining bolts to 27-39 Nm (20-29 
lb-ft).

Install control rod ball joint to remote shift lever. Install and 
tighten retaining bolt and nut to 9.6-13 Nm (85-115 lb-in).

Connect speedometer sensor and backup lamp switch.

Fill transmission with the appropriate type and quantity oil. Refer to Specifications 
.

Connect battery(s).

Lower cab.

 Disassembly 

Position shift lever in neutral. Remove four capscrews retaining remote 
shift lever control top to shift bar housing. Jar housing lightly to break the 
gasket seal. Remove remote shift lever control top and gasket. Remove backup 
lamp switch.

Remove capscrews and separate shift bar housing and gasket from case. 

[FIGURE: C71651A.gif]

Lock the transmission by engaging two mainshaft gears.

[FIGURE: C71351B.gif]

Remove the yoke nut and the yoke or flange.

[FIGURE: C71361B.gif]

Remove six capscrews and tap the input shaft bearing cover with a 
rubber mallet to separate the cover from the case. Remove the cover. 

[FIGURE: C7138B.gif]

If necessary, remove the oil seal from the input shaft bearing cover. 
Refer to Input Shaft Bearing Cover in 
the Disassembly and Assembly portion of this section. 

Remove the input shaft assembly from the transmission case.

[FIGURE: C71591A.gif]

Remove the four nuts and lockwashers that hold the mainshaft rear 
bearing cover to the transmission case. Insert screwdrivers into the notches 
on either side of the mainshaft rear bearing cover and gently separate the 
cover from the transmission case.

[FIGURE: C71391A.gif]

Remove shims (if they did not come off when mainshaft rear bearing 
cover was removed) and speedometer rotor.

[FIGURE: C71401A.gif]

Wrap a sling around the 3rd-4th synchronizer. Using Rotunda Hand Chain 
Hoist 164-R1713 or equivalent, remove mainshaft assembly from case. 

[FIGURE: C71581A.gif]

 NOTE: Countershaft may slide rearward and out of bearing bore. 

Remove the four capscrews and remove the countershaft rear bearing cap, 
shims and bearing cup from the transmission case.

[FIGURE: C7141B.gif]

Using Impact Slide Hammer D79P-100-A or equivalent, remove reverse 
idler gear shaft. Remove locating ball once it is exposed.

[FIGURE: C7143C.gif]

Remove reverse idler gear, bearings, spacer and thrust washers.

[FIGURE: C71441A.gif]

Move countershaft assembly to the rear and lift it from the case. 

[FIGURE: C71451A.gif]

If countershaft front bearing cup is to be replaced, use a suitable 
driver and bearing cup remover to drive the bore plug through the front of the 
transmission case and drive the bearing cup toward the rear of the 
transmission case.

[FIGURE: C71461A.gif]

 Assembly 

If removed, install snap ring, countershaft front bearing cup (from 
inside of case) and bore plug, using a suitable driver. Coat outer diameter of 
bore with Gasket and Trim Adhesive D7AZ-19B508-B or equivalent meeting Ford 
specifications ESE-M2G52-A and ESR-M11P17-A before installing.

[FIGURE: C71471A.gif]

Turn transmission case onto end with the rear of the transmission 
facing up. Stand countershaft assembly into front bearing cup.

[FIGURE: C71481A.gif]

Use Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESA-M1C75-B on reverse idler thrust washers to hold them in 
place. Position tang of washers in groove of housing.

[FIGURE: C7149B.gif]

Install bearings and spacer in reverse idler gear.

[FIGURE: C71501A.gif]

Position reverse idler gear in transmission case with long hub of gear 
toward the front of the case (i.e., pointing down).

[FIGURE: C7151B.gif]

Insert reverse idler gear shaft through transmission case, bearings, 
spacer and thrust washers. Line up notch in shaft with notch in case. Install 
locating ball and drive the shaft into position.

[FIGURE: C7152B.gif]

Coat outer diameter of countershaft rear bearing cup with Gasket and 
Trim Adhesive D7AZ-19B508-B or equivalent meeting Ford specifications 
ESE-M2G52-A and ESR-M11P17-A. Install countershaft rear bearing cup into case.

[FIGURE: C71531A.gif]

Temporarily install new shims over countershaft rear bearing cup.

Install the countershaft rear bearing cap and capscrews. Tighten the 
capscrews to 47-54 Nm (35-40 lb-ft).

Rotate countershaft to seat the bearings. Position Dial 
Indicator/Magnetic Base D78P-4201-B or equivalent on the shoulder of one of 
the countershaft gears. Lift countershaft to measure end play. End play must 
be between 0.15-0.25 mm (0.006-0.010 in.). Add shims for less end play or 
remove shims for more end play. Once end play is correct, remove rear bearing 
cap, and apply a light coat of Gasket and Trim Adhesive D7AZ-19B508-B or 
equivalent meeting Ford specifications ESR-M11P17-A and ESE-M2G52-A to both 
sides of shims and to the rear bearing cap and reinstall them. 

[FIGURE: C7155D.gif]

Coat threads of capscrews with Pipe Sealant with Teflon®
 D8AZ-19554-A or equivalent meeting Ford specifications 
WSK-M2G350-AZ and ESR-M18P7-A and torque to 47-54 Nm (35-40 
lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12970A.gif]

Place transmission in a horizontal position. Shift 3rd-4th mainshaft 
synchronizer into 4th gear.

[FIGURE: C71571A.gif]

Place a sling around the 3rd-4th synchronizer assembly. Using Rotunda 
Hand Chain Hoist 164-R1713 or equivalent, carefully lower the assembly into 
the transmission case.

[FIGURE: C71581A.gif]

Align clutching teeth on main drive gear with teeth in 5th speed 
synchronizer cup. Install input shaft into aligned teeth.

[FIGURE: C71591A.gif]

If removed, install input shaft oil seal and bearing cup into input 
shaft bearing cover. Refer to Input Shaft Bearing Cover in the Disassembly and 
Assembly portion of this section for procedure. 

 NOTE: Top of input shaft bearing cover is marked for proper installation. 

Install input shaft bearing cover and ga

 Disassembly 

Lay shift bar housing on workbench. Slide 5th-6th yoke into 5th 
position and remove all capscrews and shift bar retainers.

[FIGURE: C7178B.gif]

Remove reverse yoke assembly.

[FIGURE: C71791A.gif]

Remove 1st-2nd yoke assembly and interlock pin.

[FIGURE: C71801A.gif]

Remove 3rd-4th yoke assembly and interlock pin.

[FIGURE: C71811A.gif]

Remove 5th-6th yoke assembly.

[FIGURE: C71821A.gif]

If yoke replacement is required, yokes can be removed by driving the 
roll pin through the yoke and bar. If the yoke pad inserts are to be replaced, 
remove worn pad from shift yoke, install new pad and bend tabs over top and 
bottom of fork. 

Remove interlock balls, detent balls and springs.

[FIGURE: C71831A.gif]

 WARNING: THE SNAP RING AND RETAINER WASHER ARE UNDER SPRING PRESSURE. 

If the removal of the reverse plunger is necessary, secure the shift 
bar in a hand press. Depress the retainer washer and spring and remove the 
snap ring.

Remove the retainer washer. 

Remove the inner and outer springs.

Remove the washer and the reverse plunger.

 Assembly 

If reverse plunger was removed, install reverse plunger in reverse 
shift block.

 WARNING: THE SNAP RING AND RETAINER WASHER WILL BE UNDER PRESSURE WHEN INSTALLED. 

Install washer, outer and inner springs.

Place the shift block in a hand press. Depress retainer washer and 
spring and install the snap ring.

 NOTE: Balls and springs can be used interchangeably. 

Install balls and springs in the following sequence:

Position three balls into reverse light switch bore and install reverse 
detent spring and ball.

Position two balls in adjacent cross bore and install 1st-2nd detent 
spring and ball.

Position two balls in adjacent cross bore and install 3rd-4th detent 
spring and ball.

Position two balls in adjacent cross bore and install 5th-6th detent 
spring and ball.

[FIGURE: C74101A.gif]

 NOTE: All yoke assemblies must be installed in the neutral position. 

Position reverse yoke assembly in housing.

[FIGURE: C71871A.gif]

Install interlock pin in 1st-2nd yoke assembly and install assembly in 
housing.

[FIGURE: C71881A.gif]

Install interlock pin in 3rd-4th yoke assembly and install assembly in 
housing.

[FIGURE: C71891A.gif]

Position 5th-6th yoke assembly in housing.

[FIGURE: C71901A.gif]

 NOTE: If a new shift bar housing is being used in the assembly, the bores for 
the shift bar retainer capscrews are not tapped. The capscrews that are used 
are thread-forming and can be reused on a new housing. 

 NOTE: Support yoke in the proper position while installing retainers. 

Install front retainer over shift bars. Coat threads of retainer 
capscrews with Pipe Sealant with Teflon® D8AZ-19554-A or 
equivalent meeting Ford specifications WSK-M2G350-AZ and ESR-M18P7-A. Install 
and tighten capscrews to 27-34 Nm (20-25 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C7191B.gif]

Position shift yokes as shown and install center retainer. Coat threads 
of retainer capscrews with Pipe Sealant with Teflon® 
D8AZ-19554-A or equivalent meeting Ford specifications WSK-M2G350-A2 and 
ESR-M18P7-A. Install and tighten capscrews to 27-34 Nm (20-25 
lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C7192B.gif]

Position rear retainer over shift bars. Coat threads of retainer 
capscrews with Pipe Sealant with Teflon® D8AZ-19554-A or 
equivalent meeting Ford specifications WSK-M2G350-AZ and ESR-M18P7-A. Install 
and tighten capscrews to 27-34 Nm (20-25 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C7193B.gif]

Make sure interlocking system is working — can't shift 
into two gears at the same time.

[FIGURE: C7194C.gif]

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Mainshaft 

 Disassembly 

Install mainshaft assembly in a soft-jawed vise or use wood blocks to 
prevent damage. Position mainshaft in vise with the front of the shaft facing 
up. Remove the 5th-6th synchronizer and cups.

[FIGURE: C71971A.gif]

Use a Bearing Pulling Attachment D79L-4621-A or equivalent, mounted 
behind the 5th-6th shift hub and remove the hub and bearing.

[FIGURE: C7198D.gif]

Remove 5th gear and bearings from mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C71991A.gif]

Remove snap ring, thrust washer and locating ball from 4th gear.

[FIGURE: C72001A.gif]

Remove 4th gear and bearings.

[FIGURE: C72011A.gif]

Remove 3rd-4th speed synchronizer and cups.

[FIGURE: C7202B.gif]

Remove snap ring and 3rd-4th shift hub.

[FIGURE: C72031A.gif]

Remove 3rd gear and bearings from mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C72041A.gif]

Remove snap ring, thrust washer and locating ball from mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C72051A.gif]

Remove 2nd gear and bearings from mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C72061A.gif]

Remove 1st-2nd speed synchronizer and cups.

[FIGURE: C7207B.gif]

Reposition mainshaft in vise with the rear of the shaft facing up.

[FIGURE: C72081A.gif]

Using a suitable puller, remove the reverse gear, spacer and rear 
bearing.

[FIGURE: C7209C.gif]

Remove reverse gear bearings and reverse gear sliding clutch.

[FIGURE: C72101A.gif]

Remove snap ring and clutch hub.

Remove 1st gear.

[FIGURE: C7213B.gif]

Remove bearings.

[FIGURE: C7212B.gif]

 Assembly 

 NOTE: All parts must be lubricated with recommended transmission lubricant 
when reassembling. No part should be reassembled dry. Refer to Recommended 
Lubricants chart under the Transmission 
Oil Drain and Refill Procedure in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

Install mainshaft in vise equipped with wood or brass jaws, rear of 
mainshaft facing up. Lubricate 1st gear bearings, and install the bearings.

[FIGURE: C7212B.gif]

Install mainshaft 1st gear with clutching teeth of gear down.

[FIGURE: C7213B.gif]

Install reverse gear shift hub with notched teeth down. Install snap 
ring.

[FIGURE: C7214C.gif]

Install reverse gear sliding clutch with stepped shoulder down.

[FIGURE: C7216B.gif]

Lubricate reverse gear bearings, and install on reverse gear race.

[FIGURE: C72171A.gif]

Install reverse gear with clutching teeth facing down.

[FIGURE: C7218B.gif]

Install reverse gear washer. Washer can be installed either way.

[FIGURE: C72191A.gif]

Using a sleeve-type bearing driver, install rear mainshaft bearing.

[FIGURE: C72201A.gif]

Reposition mainshaft in vise with front of mainshaft facing up. 
Lubricate friction surface, and install 1st-2nd speed synchronizer and cups.

[FIGURE: C7207B.gif]

Lubricate and install 2nd gear bearings. Install 2nd gear, clutching 
teeth facing down.

[FIGURE: C72061A.gif]

Install locating ball and washer. Washer can be installed either way. 
Install snap ring.

[FIGURE: C72051A.gif]

Lubricate and install 3rd gear bearings. Install 3rd gear, clutching 
teeth facing up.

[FIGURE: C72041A.gif]

Install 3rd-4th shift hub with stepped face of hub facing up. Install 
snap ring in groove of mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C7223C.gif]

Lubricate friction surface, and install 3rd-4th speed synchronizer and 
synchronizer cups.

[FIGURE: C7202B.gif]

Lubricate and install 4th gear bearings. Install 4th gear, clutching 
teeth facing down.

[FIGURE: C7224B.gif]

Install locating ball and washer. Washer can be installed either way. 
Install snap ring.

[FIGURE: C72251A.gif]

Lubricate and install 5th gear bearings. Install 5th gear, clutching 
teeth facing up.

[FIGURE: C7226B.gif]

Install 5th-6th shift hub with flat surface facing up.

[FIGURE: C7227C.gif]

Install synchronizer cup. Lubricate friction surface, and install 
5th-6th speed synchronizer assembly and synchronizer cup.

[FIGURE: C7228B.gif]

Using a suitable sleeve-type driver, install front mainshaft bearing. 

[FIGURE: C72291A.gif]

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Countershaft 

 Disassembly 

Position a suitable puller behind rear countershaft bearing and remove 
bearing.

[FIGURE: C72301A.gif]

Position countershaft in vise with the front of the shaft facing up. 
Position puller jaws into notches behind the front countershaft bearing and 
remove bearing.

[FIGURE: C72311A.gif]

Remove drive gear retaining snap ring from front of shaft. 

Using the rear face of the drive gear as a base, press it from the 
countershaft with Rotunda 25-Ton Capacity General Purpose Press 014-00085 or 
equivalent. Remove the drive gear locating key from the shaft.

[FIGURE: C7232B.gif]

Using the rear face of the 5th gear as a base, press it from the 
countershaft. Remove the 5th gear locating key from the shaft.

[FIGURE: C72331A.gif]

 NOTE: Be sure that 5th and 6th gear keys have been removed before removing 
4th gear from countershaft. 

Using the rear face of the 4th gear as a base, press it from the 
countershaft.

[FIGURE: C7234B.gif]

Using the rear face of the 3rd gear as a base, press 3rd gear from the 
countershaft.

[FIGURE: C72351A.gif]

 Assembly 

Press 3rd gear on countershaft, splined end of gear hub to front of 
shaft (i.e., pointing down in the press).

[FIGURE: C72361A.gif]

Press 4th gear on countershaft, long hub of gear to rear of shaft 
(i.e., pointing up in the press).

[FIGURE: C72371A.gif]

Install 5th and 6th gear keys on countershaft. Align keyway of 5th gear 
to key on shaft. Press 5th gear on long hub of gear to front of shaft (i.e., 
pointing down in the press).

[FIGURE: C7239B.gif]

Align keyway of drive gear to key on countershaft. Press drive gear on, 
long hub of gear to rear of shaft. 

[FIGURE: C7238B.gif]

Install snap ring in groove at front of countershaft.

Install front countershaft bearing with a suitable sleeve-type driver.

[FIGURE: C72401A.gif]

Install rear countershaft bearing with a suitable sleeve-type driver.

[FIGURE: C72411A.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Identification

[FIGURE: C9144B.gif]

The Eaton RT-7608LL transmission features a twin countershaft. 

Engine torque is split between the two countershafts, reducing tooth 
pressures on mainshaft and countershaft gears. This enables a reduction in 
gear, shaft and bearing size while maintaining a high torque capacity. 

Floating mainshaft gears are held in radial position by rotation of 
countershaft gears. Axial position is maintained by washers. This provides 
equal tooth-loading on mainshaft gears and eliminates the need for sleeves and 
bushings. 

Gears are clutched to the mainshaft by short sliding clutch gears on 
the mainshaft, which engage internal splines in gear hubs. Sliding clutch 
gears, with conical clutching teeth, provide short and easy shifts.

The transmission has a deep reduction gear, eight forward speeds and 
two reverse speeds with gear ratios as follows:

Deep Reduction LO LO 18.81:1

LO 12.31:1

1st 8.24:1

2nd 6.07:1

3rd 4.51:1

4th 3.32:1

5th 2.48:1

6th 1.83:1

7th 1.36:1

8th 1.00:1

Reverse LO LO 17.87:1

Reverse LO 11.69:1

Reverse HI 3.52:1

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Power Flow, Front Section

The transmission transfers torque from the engine to the driveshaft 
through the following route.

 NOTE: The numbers in these steps correspond to the numbers shown in the 
following Front and Auxiliary Sections Power Flow illustration.

Torque from the engine is transferred to the transmission's input shaft. 

Splines of input shaft engage internal splines in hub of main drive 
gear. 

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears. 

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to engaged mainshaft gear. 
The cross section view illustrates 1st speed gear engagement. 

Internal clutching teeth in hub of engaged mainshaft gear transfer 
torque to mainshaft through sliding clutch. 

Mainshaft transfers torque directly to the auxiliary drive gear.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Power Flow, Auxiliary Section

 Deep Reduction 

 NOTE: The numbers in these steps correspond to the numbers shown in the 
following Front and Auxiliary Sections Power Flow illustration.

Torque from the engine is transferred to the transmission's input shaft.

Splines of input shaft engage internal splines in hub of main drive gear.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to engaged mainshaft gear. 
The cross section view illustrates 1st speed gear engagement.

Internal clutching teeth in hub of engaged mainshaft gear transfer 
torque to mainshaft through sliding clutch.

Mainshaft transfers torque directly to the auxiliary drive gear.

The auxiliary drive gear splits torque between the two auxiliary 
countershaft drive gears. 

Torque is delivered along both auxiliary countershafts to the engaged 
deep reduction gear on output shaft.

Torque is transferred to output shaft through sliding clutch.

Output shaft delivers torque to driveline as DEEP REDUCTION or LO LO.

 Power Flow, Front and Auxiliary Sections 

[FIGURE: D9293B.gif]

 LO Range 

 NOTE: The numbers in these steps correspond to the numbers shown in the 
following Auxiliary Section LO Range Power Flow illustration.

Torque from the engine is transferred to the transmission's input shaft.

Splines of input shaft engage internal splines in hub of main drive gear.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to engaged mainshaft gear. 
The cross section view illustrates 1st speed gear engagement.

Internal clutching teeth in hub of engaged mainshaft gear transfer 
torque to mainshaft through sliding clutch.

Mainshaft transfers torque directly to the auxiliary drive gear.

The auxiliary drive gear splits torque between the two auxiliary 
countershaft drive gears. 

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to engaged LO range gear 
on range mainshaft or output shaft.

Torque is transferred to range mainshaft or output shaft through 
sliding clutch. 

Torque is delivered to driveline as LO range LO.

 Power Flow, Auxiliary Section, LO Range 

[FIGURE: D9294B.gif]

 HI Range 

The numbers in these steps correspond to the numbers shown in the 
following Auxiliary Section HI Range Power Flow illustration.

Torque from the engine is transferred to the transmission's input shaft.

Splines of input shaft engage internal splines in hub of main drive gear.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to engaged mainshaft gear. 
The cross section view illustrates 1st speed gear engagement.

Internal clutching teeth in hub of engaged mainshaft gear transfer 
torque to mainshaft through sliding clutch.

Mainshaft transfers torque directly to the auxiliary drive gear.

The auxiliary drive gear transfers torque directly to the range 
mainshaft or output shaft through engaged sliding clutch. 

Torque is delivered through range mainshaft and output shaft to 
driveline as HI range 5th gear.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Transmission Oil Drain and Refill Procedure

 CAUTION: The use of mild EP gear oil or multipurpose gear oil is not 
recommended, but if these gear oils are used, be sure to adhere to the 
following limitations. 

 CAUTION: Do not use mild EP gear oil or multipurpose gear oil when operating 
temperatures are above 110°C (230°F). Many 
of these gear oils, particularly 85W140, break down above 110°
C (230°F) and coat seals, bearings, and gears with deposits 
that can cause premature failures. If these deposits are observed (especially 
a coating on seal areas causing oil leakage), change to Eaton Roadranger®
 CD50 transmission fluid, heavy-duty engine oil, or mineral 
gear oil to ensure maximum component life and to maintain your warranty with 
Eaton. Refer to Operating Temperatures in this section. 

 CAUTION: Additives and friction modifiers are not recommended for use in Eaton 
Fuller transmissions. 

Proper lubrication procedures are the key to a good all-around 
maintenance program. If the oil is not doing its job, or if the oil level is 
ignored, all the maintenance procedures in the world are not going to keep the 
transmission running or ensure long transmission life.

Eaton Fuller transmissions are designed so that the internal parts 
operate in an oil circulating bath by the motion of the gears and shafts.

All parts are amply lubricated if these procedures are closely followed:

Maintain oil level. Inspect regularly.

Change oil regularly.

Use the correct grade and type of oil.

Buy from a reputable dealer.

 LUBRICATION CHANGE AND INSPECTION

Eaton Roadranger® CD50 Transmission Fluid

 HIGHWAY USE 

Every 16 093 km (10,000 miles)

Check fluid level. Check for leaks.

Every 402 325 km (250,000 miles)

Change transmission fluid.

 OFF-HIGHWAY USE 

Every 40 hours

Inspect fluid level. Check for leaks.

Every 500 hours

Change transmission fluid where severe dirt conditions exist.

Every 1,000 hours

Change transmission fluid. (Normal off-highway use.)

 HIGHWAY USE — Heavy-Duty Engine Lubricant or Mineral 
Gear Lubricant 

First 4 828 to 8 047 km (3,000 to 5,000 miles)

Factory fill initial drain.

Every 16 093 km (10,000 miles)

Inspect lubricant level. Check for leaks.

Every 80 465 km (50,000 miles)

Change transmission lubricant.

 OFF-HIGHWAY USE 

First 30 hours

Change transmission lubricant on new units.

Every 40 hours

Inspect lubricant level. Check for leaks.

Every 500 hours

Change transmission lubricant where severe dirt conditions exist.

Every 1,000 hours

Change transmission lubricant. (Normal off-highway use.)

 Proper Oil Level 

Make sure oil is level with the filler opening. Because you can reach 
oil with your finger does not mean oil is at proper level. An oil level of 
25.4 mm (one inch) is equal to approximately 3.7 liters (one gallon) of oil.

[FIGURE: C11745A.gif]

 Draining Oil 

Drain transmission while oil is warm. To drain oil remove the drain 
plug at case bottom. Clean the drain plug before reinstalling.

 Refilling 

 CAUTION: When adding oil, do not mix types and brands of oil because of possible 
incompatibility. 

Clean case around filler plug and remove plug from case side. Fill the 
transmission to the level of the filler opening. If the transmission has two 
filler openings, fill to the level of both openings.

The exact amount of oil depends on the transmission inclination and 
model. Do not overfill — this causes oil to be forced out of 
the case through the front bearing cover.

 Proper Lubrication Levels as Related to Transmission Installation Angles 

If the transmission operating angle is more than 12 degrees, improper 
lubrication can occur. The operating angle is the transmission mounting angle 
in the chassis plus the percent of upgrade (expressed in degrees).

The chart below illustrates the safe percent of upgrade on which the 
transmission can be used with various chassis mounting angles. For example: if 
you have a four-degree transmission mounting angle, then eight degrees (or 14 
percent of grade) is equal to the limit of 12 degrees. If you have a 
zero-degree mounting angle, the transmission can be operated on a 12-degree 
(21 percent) grade.

Any time the transmission operating angle of 12 degrees is exceeded for 
an extended period of time, the transmission should be equipped with an oil 
pump or cooler kit to make sure transmission is properly lubricated.

Note on the chart the effect low oil levels can have on safe operating 
angles. Allowing the oil level to fall one half inch below the filler plug 
hole reduces the degree of grade by approximately three degrees (5.5 percent). 
Proper lubrication levels are essential.

[FIGURE: C11746A.gif]

 Operating Temperatures 

 With Eaton Roadranger® CD50 Transmission Fluid, 
Heavy-Duty Engine Oil and Mineral Oil 

The transmission should not be operated consistently at temperatures 
above 120°C (250°F). However, intermittent 
operating temperatures to 149°C (300°F) will 
not harm the transmission. Operating temperatures above 120°C 
(250°F) increase the lubricant's rate of oxidation and 
shorten its effective life. When the average operating temperature is above 120°
C (250°F), the transmission may require 
more frequent oil changes or external cooling.

The following conditions in any combination can cause operating 
temperatures of over 120°C (250°F).

operating consistently at slow speeds

high ambient temperatures

restricted airflow around transmission

exhaust system too close to transmission

high horsepower, overdrive operation

External oil coolers are available to reduce operating temperatures 
when the above conditions are encountered.

Transmission oil coolers are recommended with the following engines:

350 HP and above with overdrive transmissions

Transmission oil coolers are required with the following engines:

399 HP and above with overdrive transmissions and GCW's over 40824 kg 
(90,000 lb)

399 HP and above and 1898 Nm (1400 lb-ft) or greater 
torque

450 HP and above

 With EP or Multipurpose Gear Oil 

Mild EP gear oil and multipurpose gear oil are not recommended when 
lubricant operating temperatures are above 110°C (230°
F). In addition, transmission oil coolers are not 
recommended with these gear oils, since the oil cooler materials may be 
attacked by these gear oils. The lower temperature limit and oil cooler 
restriction with these gear oils generally limit their success to milder 
applications.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Transmission

 Removal 

Tilt cab.

Drain air system and disconnect air lines at Roadranger®
 valve and position out of way. Refer to Section 07-06A .

Drain transmission oil.

Disconnect shift linkage and position out of way. Refer to Section 07-06B .

Disconnect wiring connectors.

Raise vehicle on hoist.

Disconnect and remove fuel lines and bracketry as required. Refer to 
 Section 10-01 .

Remove exhaust system as required. 

Remove driveshaft assembly. Refer to Section 05-01 .

Disconnect air lines at transmission. Refer to Section 07-06A .

If so equipped, disconnect low oil level indicator sensor.

Disconnect clutch linkage. Refer to Section 08-02 .

Remove clutch housing cover.

Position Rotunda Heavy-Duty Truck Transmission Jack 164-R3510 or 
equivalent under the transmission and install jack.

Remove transmission clutch housing-to-engine retaining bolts and raise 
transmission slightly with jack.

Remove top engine support bracket retaining nut and insulators.

Remove both jam nuts and insulators.

Lower transmission from vehicle.

 Installation 

Use transmission jack to lift transmission into place.

Install insulator retainer assembly.

 NOTE: For installing and aligning clutch discs, plates, flywheel and shafts, 
refer to Section 08-01 .

Install and align clutch assembly and install clutch housing-to-engine 
retaining bolts.

Position rear engine support bracket on transmission. Install 
insulators and tighten jam nut to 203-278 Nm (150-205 lb-ft). 
Tighten remaining jam nut finger-tight and apply two additional turns.

Install insulators and top rear engine support bracket retaining nut. 
Tighten nut to 203-278 Nm (150-205 lb-ft).

Remove transmission jack.

Install clutch housing cover.

Connect clutch linkage. Refer to Section 08-02 .

Install fuel lines and bracketry. Refer to Section 10-01 .

If so equipped, connect low oil level indicator sensor.

Connect air lines to transmission. Refer to Section 07-06A .

Install exhaust system if removed. 

Install driveshaft assembly. Refer to Section 05-01 .

Lower vehicle.

Reconnect all wiring connectors.

Connect shift linkage. Refer to Section 07-06B .

Connect air lines to Roadranger® valve. Refer to 
 Section 07-06A .

Refill transmission with appropriate type and quantity of oil. Refer to Transmission Oil Drain and Refill Procedure 
 in the Removal and Installation 
portion of this section.

Lower cab.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Companion Flange, Clutch Housing and Auxiliary Section, Removal

Lock transmission by engaging two mainshaft gears with the mainshaft 
sliding clutches. Use a large breaker bar to turn the nut from the output 
shaft. Remove washer.

[FIGURE: C8903B.gif]

Pull yoke straight to the rear and off output shaft.

 NOTE: For models so equipped, remove the clutch release mechanism and clutch 
brake assembly. 

Remove the two capscrews, then the six nuts and lockwashers from studs 
that secure the clutch housing to transmission case.

[FIGURE: C9233B.gif]

Jar clutch housing with rubber mallet to break gasket seal and pull 
from transmission case. Remove gasket.

[FIGURE: C12943A.gif]

 NOTE: There are three capscrew lengths. Note each location.

Remove the fifteen retaining capscrews holding the auxiliary section to 
the transmission case.

[FIGURE: C10924A.gif]

Insert three puller screws in the tapped holes of housing flange. 
Tighten evenly to move auxiliary section to the rear and just far enough from 
front section to break gasket seal.

[FIGURE: C10925A.gif]

Remove puller screws and attach a chain hoist, such as Rotunda Hand 
Chain Hoist 164-R1713 or equivalent, to auxiliary section. Move the assembly 
to the rear until free of front section and remove gasket.

Input Shaft

 Special Procedure for Changing Input Shaft 

Some cases of service can require replacement of the input shaft 
because of clutch wear on the splines. In these instances, the input shaft can 
be removed without disassembling the transmission other than removing the 
shifting bar housing. Removal of the clutch housing is optional.

Remove the shift bar housing from transmission case. Refer to Shift Bar 
Housing in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

 NOTE: To prevent lubricant leakage during shipment, a small rubber lip seal 
is installed on the transmission input shaft under the front cover. This seal 
should be removed and discarded during transmission service. 

Remove the retaining capscrews, front bearing cover and gasket. If 
necessary, service the oil seal of model covers so equipped.

Remove the bearing retainer snap ring from shaft groove. 

Push down on the input shaft to cock the bearing in the bore. Drive the 
input shaft toward the transmission rear through the bearing as far as 
possible. Pull the input shaft forward to expose the bearing. 

Use pry bars or screwdrivers to complete removal of the bearing. 

Remove the spacer and the snap ring. 

Pull the input shaft forward and out of the drive gear and case. 

 Installation 

If necessary, replace the bushing in the input shaft pocket. Install 
input shaft into drive gear.

Install the snap ring in the snap ring groove inside the drive gear. 

Install the spacer on the input shaft. 

Install the bearing on the input shaft. 

Install the bearing retainer snap ring. 

Install the front bearing cover and gasket. Make sure to align the oil 
return hole in the case with the hole in the cover. Lightly oil capscrew 
threads. Then, install and tighten capscrews to 47-61 Nm 
(35-45 lb-ft).

Install the shift bar housing. Refer to Shift Bar Housing , Installation 
in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Output Shaft and Rear Bearing Assemblies, Installation 

Remount the output shaft in vise with threaded-end up and secure on

[FIGURE: C9326B.gif]

Install the splined spacer on output shaft with large diameter splines 
down.

[FIGURE: C9327B.gif]

Mark any two adjacent teeth on deep reduction gear and repeat the 
procedure for the two adjacent teeth directly opposite the first set marked. A 
highly visible color of toolmakers' dye is recommended for making timing marks.

[FIGURE: C93281A.gif]

If previously removed, install the snap ring in deep reduction gear. 
Install the deep reduction gear on output shaft, clutching teeth down and 
engaged with spline of spacer.

[FIGURE: C9329B.gif]

step down.

[FIGURE: C9330B.gif]

 NOTE: Do not heat bearing above 136°C (275°
F). If possible, use heat lamps as source. 

Heat the front bearing cone and install on output shaft against washer, 
with bearing taper up.

[FIGURE: C9332B.gif]

Install the bearing inner spacer on output shaft against front bearing 
cone. 

[FIGURE: C9333B.gif]

Place the front bearing cup in housing bore, taper to the inside, and 
use a soft bar to start cup into bore.

[FIGURE: C9334B.gif]

Stack the bearing outer spacer and rear bearing cup on top of the front 
bearing cup in proper sequence. Use a soft bar or a flanged driver to move all 
three parts evenly into housing bore until lip of rear bearing cup seats on 
housing.

[FIGURE: C9335B.gif]

 NOTE: Do not heat bearing above 136°C (275°
F).

Install the auxiliary housing over end of output shaft assembly. Heat 
the rear bearing cone and install on shaft, taper down and inside bearing cup.

[FIGURE: C93361A.gif]

Remount assembly upright in vise and secure. Install the deep reduction 
sliding clutch on output shaft, internal splines toward gear and engaged with 
splines of shaft.

[FIGURE: C9260C.gif]

Install snap ring in groove of range mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C9259B.gif]

If previously removed, install the oil seal in rear bearing cover. Seal 
should be installed so the spring is to the front of cover.

[FIGURE: C9337B.gif]

 NOTE: Because the collar becomes distorted when compressed, do not reuse old 
nylon collar.

Position gasket on cover mounting surface and install the rear bearing 
cover on auxiliary housing. Use the nylon collar and brass washer with

Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification WSK-M2G315-AA to capscrew threads. Then, install and 
tighten capscrews to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Countershaft Bearings, Upper, Removal

 NOTE: If front bearing snap ring groove cannot be exposed (due to variances 
in thickness of case), use punch between hub of countershaft drive gear and 
inner race of bearing to move the bearing forward on shaft. 

Remove the right countershaft snap ring, in rear bearing bore of case. 

[FIGURE: C9284C.gif]

Using soft bar and maul against rear of countershaft, move the assembly 
forward as far as possible until snap ring groove in front bearing is exposed.

Install the snap ring that was removed from the rear bearing bore in 
exposed snap ring groove.

[FIGURE: C9285C.gif]

Using a soft bar and maul, drive the countershaft assembly to the rear 
as far as possible. This will move the front bearing forward on countershaft. 

 NOTE: The following procedure may have to be repeated several times to unseat 
the front bearing. 

From the rear of case, use a soft bar and maul to drive the 
countershaft forward to unseat the front bearing from case bore.

Use a puller or pry bars to remove the front countershaft bearing.

[FIGURE: C9286C.gif]

 NOTE: Removal procedures will damage the bearings. Removal should not be 
attempted unless replacement of the bearings is planned. 

Block the countershaft and use a maul and punch from inside the case, 
to drive the rear countershaft bearing from the case bore and countershaft.

[FIGURE: C92871A.gif]

Using inside jaw pullers or impact puller, remove the auxiliary 
countershaft front bearing from left reverse idler gear bore.

[FIGURE: C9288B.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Mainshaft Assembly

 Removal 

 CAUTION: After performing the following step, please note that the drive gear is 
free and can fall from shaft. 

Block the right countershaft assembly against case wall. Slide drive 
gear to the rear and engage with sliding clutch splines. Using a hook around 
the 1st/2nd speed sliding clutch, tilt front of mainshaft up and lift the 
assembly from case.

[FIGURE: C93901A.gif]

[FIGURE: C93951A.gif]

[FIGURE: C9396B.gif]

[FIGURE: C93971A.gif]

[FIGURE: C93981A.gif]

 Assembly 

Place mainshaft in a vise, equipped with brass jaws or wood blocks, 
pilot end down. Keep keyway in mainshaft clear for insertion of mainshaft key.

[FIGURE: C94011A.gif]

 NOTE: Each mainshaft gear is held in position by locking a tolerance washer 
to the mainshaft with a mainshaft key. There is one tolerance washer for each 
gear. Tolerance washers for reverse, LO, 1st, and 2nd gears are the same 
diameter, the 3rd gear tolerance washer is a smaller diameter. Refer to 
Selective Tolerance Washers chart in the Specifications portion of this 
section for tolerance washer thickness dimensions. 

Install reverse gear tolerance washer in groove near the rear of 
mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C94021A.gif]

 NOTE: Make sure mainshaft key is positioned with the word TOP to the outside. 
Procedure of rotating tolerance washer will be followed each time a tolerance 
washer is installed on mainshaft. 

Rotate the tolerance washer in groove of mainshaft to align the splines 
of washer with splines of mainshaft. Install mainshaft key in keyway to lock 
washer in place.

[FIGURE: C9403B.gif]

Install reverse gear on the tolerance washer with clutching teeth 
facing down.

[FIGURE: C94041A.gif]

Install auxiliary drive gear on mainshaft with clutching teeth facing up.

[FIGURE: C94051A.gif]

Install snap ring in groove at rear of mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C9406B.gif]

Insert two screwdrivers between the hub of reverse gear and the 
auxiliary drive gear. Apply slight downward pressure on screwdriver handles to 
spread gears evenly apart. Making sure the gear hubs are parallel, insert a 
feeler gauge between hubs. Correct axial clearance should be from 0.127-0.305 
mm (0.005-0.012 inch). If the clearance is less than the minimum 0.127-mm 
(0.005-inch) tolerance, the tolerance washer in reverse gear should be 
replaced by a thinner tolerance washer. This will increase the axial clearance 
between gears. If the clearance checked is greater than the maximum 0.305-mm 
(0.012-inch) tolerance, a thicker tolerance washer should be installed in 
reverse gear. This would decrease the axial clearance between the gears.

[FIGURE: C94071A.gif]

After proper reverse gear clearance has been set, remove the snap ring 
from rear of mainshaft, remove auxiliary drive gear and the reverse gear from 
mainshaft. The tolerance washer and key remain on the mainshaft. 

Reposition mainshaft in a vise as shown, pilot end up, so that the 
keyway is accessible.

[FIGURE: C94081A.gif]

Install the LO/reverse speed sliding clutch on mainshaft, against 
reverse gear tolerance washer. Align slot in sliding clutch with key on 
mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C94091A.gif]

Remove mainshaft key from mainshaft. Install LO gear tolerance washer 
on mainshaft LO gear location and reinstall the mainshaft key to lock 
tolerance washer to shaft.

[FIGURE: C94101A.gif]

Install LO gear on mainshaft, clutching teeth down, and engage with 
external splines of washer.

[FIGURE: C94111A.gif]

Install 1st gear on mainshaft, clutching teeth up.

[FIGURE: C94121A.gif]

 CAUTION: Caution should be used to prevent the mainshaft gears from dropping to 
the bottom of the mainshaft. 

Remove the mainshaft key from keyway. Install 1st gear tolerance washer 
on mainshaft and into hub of 1st gear.

[FIGURE: C94131A.gif]

Install mainshaft key in keyway to lock tolerance washer to shaft.

[FIGURE: C9414B.gif]

Check axial clearances and make adjustments, if necessary, between the 
LO and 1st gears, as described in Step 7.

[FIGURE: C94151A.gif]

Install the 1st/2nd speed sliding clutch, aligning slot in sliding 
clutch with key; engage with 1st gear.

[FIGURE: C94161A.gif]

Remove mainshaft key and install 2nd gear tolerance washer at 2nd gear 
location. Install mainshaft key. Reposition key so that it rests on mainshaft 
groove shoulder.

[FIGURE: C94171A.gif]

Install the 2nd gear on mainshaft, and engage with external splines of 
tolerance washer, clutching teeth down.

[FIGURE: C94181A.gif]

Install the 3rd gear on mainshaft, clutching teeth up.

[FIGURE: C94191A.gif]

Install tolerance washer in the bore of 3rd gear.

[FIGURE: C94201A.gif]

Install snap ring in snap ring groove. This will hold 3rd gear in 
position on mainshaft. Check axial clearance and make adjustments, if 
necessary, between 2nd and 3rd gears, as described in Step 7.

[FIGURE: C12956A.gif]

Install the 3rd/4th speed sliding clutch on mainshaft with FRONT up. 
Align slot in sliding clutch with key, and engage clutch with 3rd gear.

[FIGURE: C94221A.gif]

Mark timing teeth on drive (4th) gear, with a highly visible color of 
toolmakers' dye. 

Mark two adjacent teeth on drive gear. 

Mark two adjacent teeth on drive gear which are directly opposite the 
first set marked. There should be the same number of teeth between markings on 
each side of gear.

[FIGURE: C94231A.gif]

Install the drive (4th) gear on mainshaft-clutching teeth facing down.

[FIGURE: C93901A.gif]

Remove mainshaft assembly from vise, and install the reverse gear on 
mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C94241A.gif]

[FIGURE: C8922B.gif]

Repeat the procedure when installing the bearings on right

[FIGURE: C8923B.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Case Assemblies, Installation 

Place the mainshaft assembly into position in case.

[FIGURE: C93031A.gif]

If previously removed, install bushing in pocket of input shaft as shown.

[FIGURE: C9279B.gif]

Mesh the marked tooth of left countershaft drive gear with either set 
of two marked teeth on main drive gear. Install input shaft through bore of 
case and onto mainshaft. This will prevent the mainshaft assembly from 
dropping to the bottom of the case.

[FIGURE: C9304C.gif]

Align and install rear case gasket plate on alignment pins.

[FIGURE: C10852A.gif]

Partially install the auxiliary drive gear bearing in the case rear 
bore. Install the bearing retainer plates. Tighten capscrews until seated 
against auxiliary drive gear.

[FIGURE: C10853A.gif]

Completely seat auxiliary drive gear and tighten capscrews to 47-61 Nm
 (35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12959A.gif]

Bend the lock tangs on the retaining plates to secure capscrews.

[FIGURE: C10855A.gif]

Move mainshaft assembly to the rear to expose snap ring groove on rear 
of mainshaft and install snap ring.

[FIGURE: C9308B.gif]

Install snap ring in snap ring groove inside drive gear.

[FIGURE: C9309B.gif]

Install drive gear spacer on input shaft, chamfered side to front.

[FIGURE: C9310B.gif]

Install drive gear bearing on input shaft and into case bore.

[FIGURE: C93111A.gif]

Install the bearing retainer snap ring.

[FIGURE: C9274B.gif]

Install the front bearing cover and gasket, making sure to align oil 
return hole in the case with hole in cover. Apply Threadlock®
 and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
WSK-M2G315-A5 to capscrew threads. Then install and tighten capscrews to 47-61 Nm
 (35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12960A.gif]

Engage the 3rd/4th speed sliding clutch into 3rd gear. This will 
prevent the drive (4th) gear from dropping far enough to cause a possible 
timing error.

[FIGURE: C93131A.gif]

Mesh the marked timing tooth of the right countershaft drive gear with 
the two marked timing teeth of the main drive gear, making sure the left 
countershaft remains in time.

[FIGURE: C93141A.gif]

Hold the countershaft in position and partially install the front and 
rear countershaft bearings in case bores and on countershaft.

[FIGURE: C12961A.gif]

 NOTE: Do not shift the transmission into two gears at the same time. This 
will prevent the transmission from rotating. 

Shift the mainshaft sliding clutches into all the gear positions with a 
screwdriver. A clutch that cannot be shifted into a gear indicates that the 
gearset is out of time. The right countershaft bearings would then need to be 
removed and the countershaft retimed with the mainshaft. The front box is 
properly timed if the sliding clutches can be shifted into all the mainshaft 
gears.

[FIGURE: C93161A.gif]

Use a flanged bearing driver to complete seating both front and rear 
countershaft bearings. 

Install snap ring into groove in rear bore of case.

[FIGURE: C9317C.gif]

 NOTE: Since the upper and lower reverse idler gear assemblies are identical, 
reassembly and installation of the upper reverse idler gear assembly should be 
performed at this time.

Position reverse idler bearing gear and washer in case, washer to front 
of reverse idler gear case.

[FIGURE: C9318B.gif]

 NOTE: Reverse idler gear must be in mesh, before idler shaft can be inserted.

Install idler shaft through idler gear and washer and into case bore. 
Seat using installer.

[FIGURE: C93191A.gif]

Making sure that the reverse idler shaft is seated in bore of support 
boss and forward as far as possible, install the washer and stop nut on front 
of shaft. Tighten nut to 68-81 Nm (50-60 lb-ft). Install plug 
in reverse idler shaft.

[FIGURE: C12962A.gif]

Install the auxiliary countershaft front bearing into the reverse idler 
gear case bore.

[FIGURE: C93211A.gif]

DESCRIPTION

Identification 

[FIGURE: C10055B.gif]

The Fuller RT-6609A series transmission features a twin countershaft. 

The twin countershaft design, which splits torque evenly between the 
two countershafts, provides a high torque capacity-to-weight ratio. Because of 
torque splitting, each gear set carries only half of the load, greatly 
reducing the face width of each gear. 

The design employs a floating gear. The mainshaft gears, when not 
engaged, float between the countershaft gears, eliminating the need for gear 
sleeves and bushings. All gears are constant mesh with spur-type teeth. 

The RT-6609A transmission has five low range speeds, four high range 
speeds and two reverse speeds with gear ratios as follows:

LO Range

LO 12.72:1

1st 8.61:1

2nd 6.27:1

3rd 4.66:1

4th 3.42:1

HI Range

5th 2.52:1

6th 1.83:1

7th 1.36:1

8th 1.00:1

Reverse

LO 12.08:1

HI 3.53:1

================================================================================
PAGE 3430
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 07-03J: Transmission, Manual, Fuller RT-6609A

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION

Power Flow, Front Section: LO Range Direct

The transmission transfers torque from the engine to the driveshaft to 
the vehicle's rear wheels through the following route.

 NOTE: The numbers in these steps correspond to the numbers in the following 
illustration. 

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the transmission's 
input shaft. 

Input shaft splines engage internal splines of main drive gear. 

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears. 

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to the engaged mainshaft 
gear. The following cross-section views illustrate a 1st/6th speed gear 
engagement. 

Internal clutching teeth in engaged mainshaft gear hub transfers torque 
to mainshaft through the sliding clutch. 

Mainshaft transfers torque directly to the auxiliary drive gear.

Power Flow, Auxiliary Section

 NOTE: The numbers in these steps correspond to the numbers in the following 
illustration.

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the transmission's 
input shaft.

Input shaft splines engage internal splines of main drive gear.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to the engaged mainshaft 
gear. The following cross-section views illustrate a 1st/6th speed gear 
engagement.

Internal clutching teeth in engaged mainshaft gear hub transfers torque 
to mainshaft through the sliding clutch.

Mainshaft transfers torque directly to the auxiliary drive gear.

The auxiliary drive gear splits torque between the two auxiliary 
countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both auxiliary countershafts to engaged gear 
on the output shaft.

Torque is transferred to the output shaft through the sliding clutch.

Output shaft delivers torque to driveline.

 LO Range 

 NOTE: The numbers in these steps correspond to the numbers in the following 
illustration.

Power (torque) from the engine is transferred to the transmission's 
input shaft.

Input shaft splines engage internal splines of main drive gear.

Torque is split between the two countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to the engaged mainshaft

Mainshaft transfers torque directly to the auxiliary drive gear.

The auxiliary drive gear splits torque between the two auxiliary 
countershaft drive gears.

Torque is delivered along both countershafts to engaged LO range gear 
on the range mainshaft or output shaft.

Torque is transferred to the range mainshaft or output shaft through 
the sliding clutch.

Torque is delivered to the driveline as LO range 1st, or 1st gear.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Transmission Oil Drain and Refill Procedure

 CAUTION: The use of mild EP gear oil or multi-purpose gear oil is not 
recommended, but if these gear oils are used, be sure to adhere to the 
following limitations. 

 CAUTION: Do not use mild EP gear oil or multi-purpose gear oil when operating 
temperatures are above 110°C (230°F). Many 
of these gear oils, particularly 85W140, break down above 110°
C (230°F) and coat seals, bearings, and gears with deposits 
that can cause premature failures. If these deposits are observed (especially 
a coating on seal areas causing oil leakage), change to Eaton Roadranger®
 CD50 transmission fluid, heavy-duty engine oil or mineral 
gear oil to ensure maximum component life and to maintain your warranty with 
Eaton. Refer to Operating Temperatures in this section. 

 CAUTION: Additives and friction modifiers are not recommended for use in Eaton 
Fuller transmissions. 

Proper lubrication procedures are the key to a good all-around 
maintenance program. If the oil is not doing its job, or if the oil level is 
ignored, all the maintenance procedures in the world are not going to keep the 
transmission running or ensure long transmission life.

Eaton Fuller transmissions are designed so that the internal parts 
operate in an oil circulating bath by the motion of the gears and shafts.

All parts are amply lubricated if these procedures are closely followed:

Maintain oil level. Inspect regularly.

Change oil regularly.

Use the correct grade and type of oil.

Buy from a reputable dealer.

 LUBRICATION CHANGE AND INSPECTION

Eaton Roadranger® CD50 Transmission Fluid

 HIGHWAY USE 

Every 16 093 km (10,000 miles)

Check fluid level. Check for leaks.

Every 402 325 km (250,000 miles)

Change transmission fluid.

 OFF-HIGHWAY USE 

Every 40 hours

Inspect fluid level. Check for leaks.

Every 500 hours

Change transmission fluid where severe dirt conditions exist.

Every 1,000 hours

Change transmission fluid. (Normal off-highway use.)

 HIGHWAY USE — Heavy-Duty Engine Lubricant or Mineral 
Gear Lubricant 

First 4 828 to 8 047 km (3,000 to 5,000 miles)

Factory fill initial drain.

Every 16 093 km (10,000 miles)

Inspect lubricant level. Check for leaks.

Every 80 465 km (50,000 miles)

Change transmission lubricant.

 OFF-HIGHWAY USE 

First 30 hours

Change transmission lubricant on new units.

Every 40 hours

Inspect lubricant level. Check for leaks.

Every 500 hours

Change transmission lubricant where severe dirt conditions exist.

Every 1,000 hours

Change transmission lubricant. (Normal off-highway use.)

 Proper Oil Level 

Make sure oil is level with the filler opening. Because you can reach 
oil with your finger does not mean oil is at proper level. An oil level of 
25.4 mm (one inch) is about 3.7 liters (one gallon) of oil.

[FIGURE: C11745A.gif]

 Draining Oil 

Drain transmission while oil is warm. To drain oil, remove the drain 
plug at case bottom. Clean the drain plug before reinstalling.

 Refilling 

 CAUTION: When adding oil, do not mix types and brands of oil because of possible 
incompatibility. 

Clean case around filler plug and remove plug from case side. Fill the 
transmission to the level of the filler opening. If the transmission has two 
filler openings, fill to the level of both openings.

The exact amount of oil depends on the transmission inclination and 
model. Do not overfill — this causes oil to be forced out of 
the case through the front bearing cover.

 Proper Lubrication Levels as Related to Transmission Installation Angles 

If the transmission operating angle is more than 12 degrees, improper 
lubrication can occur. The operating angle is the transmission mounting angle 
in the chassis plus the percent of upgrade (expressed in degrees).

The chart below illustrates the safe percent of upgrade on which the 
transmission can be used with various chassis mounting angles. For example: if 
you have a four-degree transmission mounting angle, then eight degrees (or 14 
percent of grade) is equal to the limit of 12 degrees. If you have a 
zero-degree mounting angle, the transmission can be operated on a 12-degree 
(21 percent) grade.

Any time the transmission operating angle of 12 degrees is exceeded for 
an extended period of time the transmission should be equipped with an oil 
pump or cooler kit to make sure transmission is properly lubricated.

Note on the chart the effect low oil levels can have on safe operating 
angles. Allowing the oil level to fall one-half inch below the filler plug 
hole reduces the degree of grade by approximately three degrees (5.5 percent). 
Proper lubrication levels are essential.

[FIGURE: C11746A.gif]

 Operating Temperatures 

 With Eaton Roadranger® CD50 Transmission Fluid, 
Heavy-Duty Engine Oil and Mineral Oil 

The transmission should not be operated consistently at temperatures 
above 120°C (250°F). However, intermittent 
operating temperatures to 149°C (300°F) will 
not harm the transmission. Operating temperatures above 120°C 
(250°F) increase the lubricant's rate of oxidation and 
shorten its effective life. When the average operating temperature is above 120°
C (250°F), the transmission may require 
more frequent oil changes or external cooling.

The following conditions in any combination can cause operating 
temperatures of over 120°C (250°F).

operating consistently at slow speeds

high ambient temperatures

restricted airflow around transmission

exhaust system too close to transmission

high horsepower, overdrive operation

External oil coolers are available to reduce operating temperatures 
when the above conditions are encountered.

Transmission Oil Coolers are recommended with the following engines:

350 HP and above with overdrive transmissions

Transmission Oil Coolers are required with the following engines:

399 HP and above with overdrive transmissions and GCW's over 40 824 kg 
(90,000 lb).

399 HP and above and 1898 Nm (1400 lb-ft) or greater 
torque

450 HP and above

 With EP or Multipurpose Gear Oil 

Mild EP gear oil and multipurpose gear oil are not recommended when 
lubricant operating temperatures are above 110°C (230°
F). In addition, transmission oil coolers are not 
recommended with these gear oils, since the oil cooler materials may be 
attacked by these gear oils. The lower temperature limit and oil cooler 
restriction with these gear oils generally limit their success to milder 
applications.
