REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Transmission

 Removal 

Tilt cab.

Drain air system and disconnect air lines at Roadranger®
 valve and position out of way. Refer to Section 07-06A .

Drain transmission oil.

Disconnect shift linkage and position out of way. Refer to Section 07-06B .

Disconnect wiring connectors.

Raise vehicle on hoist.

Disconnect and remove fuel lines and bracketry as required. Refer to 
 Section 10-01 .

Remove exhaust system as required.

Remove driveshaft assembly. Refer to Section 05-01 .

Disconnect air lines at transmission. Refer to Section 07-06A .

If so equipped, disconnect low oil level indicator sensor.

Disconnect clutch linkage. Refer to Section 08-02 .

Remove clutch housing cover.

Position Rotunda Heavy-Duty Truck Transmission Jack 164-R3510 or 
equivalent under the transmission and install jack.

Remove transmission clutch housing-to-engine retaining bolts and raise 
transmission slightly with jack.

Remove top engine support to bracket retaining nut and insulators.

Remove both jam nuts and insulators.

Lower transmission from vehicle.

 Installation 

Use transmission jack to lift transmission into place.

Install insulator retainer assembly.

 NOTE: For installing and aligning clutch discs, plates, flywheel and shafts, 
refer to Section 08-01 .

Install and align clutch assembly and install clutch housing-to-engine 
retaining bolts.

Position rear engine support bracket on transmission. Install 
insulators and tighten jam nut to 203-278 Nm (150-205 lb-ft). 
Tighten remaining jam nut finger-tight and apply two additional turns.

Install insulators and top rear engine support bracket retaining nut. 
Tighten nut to 203-278 Nm (150-205 lb-ft).

Remove transmission jack.

Install clutch housing cover.

Connect clutch linkage. Refer to Section 08-02 .

Install fuel lines and bracketry. Refer to Section 10-01 .

If so equipped, connect low oil level indicator sensor.

Connect air lines to transmission. Refer to Section 07-06A .

Install exhaust system, if removed.

Install driveshaft assembly. Refer to Section 05-01 .

Lower vehicle.

Reconnect all wiring connectors.

Connect shift linkage. Refer to Section 07-06B .

Connect air lines to Roadranger® valve. Refer to 
 Section 07-06A .

Refill transmission with appropriate type and quantity of oil. Refer to Transmission Oil Drain and Refill Procedure 
 in the Removal and Installation 
portion of this section.

Lower cab.

 Removal

break the gasket seal. Lift the shift bar housing from the transmission case.

[FIGURE: C100641A.gif]

 Installation

Position the shift bar housing gasket on the transmission case.

[FIGURE: C100651A.gif]

Install the shift bar housing assembly on the transmission case, 
fitting the shift yokes into the corresponding sliding clutch slots. Lightly 
oil threads of capscrews. Then, install and tighten capscrews to 47-61 Nm
 (35-45 lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Output Yoke, Auxiliary Section and Clutch Housing 

 Removal 

Lock the transmission by engaging the two mainshaft gears with the 
mainshaft sliding clutches.

[FIGURE: C100571A.gif]

Use a large breaker bar to turn the nut from the output shaft. Pull the 
yoke straight to the rear and off the output shaft.

Remove the six nuts with lockwashers that hold the clutch housing to 
the transmission case.

[FIGURE: C100581A.gif]

Remove the two capscrews that hold the clutch housing to the 
transmission case.

[FIGURE: C100591A.gif]

Jar the clutch housing with a rubber mallet to break the gasket seal. 
Pull the clutch housing from the transmission case and remove the gasket.

 NOTE: There are three capscrew lengths. Note their locations. 

Remove the 15 capscrews that hold the auxiliary section to the 
transmission case.

[FIGURE: C100601A.gif]

Insert three capscrews in the housing flange tapped holes. Tighten 
evenly to move the auxiliary section back; leave a space wide enough to attach 
a chain hoist.

[FIGURE: C100611A.gif]

Remove the puller capscrews and attach a chain hoist to the auxiliary 
section. Pull the auxiliary section off and remove the gasket.

[FIGURE: C100621A.gif]

 Installation 

 NOTE: Make sure the synchronizer is in neutral, and the auxiliary front 
countershaft bearings are installed in the front case. 

Position a new gasket on the auxiliary housing. Attach a chain hoist to 
the auxiliary section. Move the assembly evenly into the front case rear, 
piloting it on the dowel pins. As the assembly is moved forward, the 
countershaft drive gears will mesh with the auxiliary drive gear. 

 NOTE: There are three capscrew lengths. Make sure the capscrews are in their 
proper locations. 

Lightly oil threads of capscrews. Then, install the 15 capscrews in the 
auxiliary housing flange and tighten to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

Position the corresponding new gasket on the clutch housing mounting 
surface. Install the clutch housing on the case front, piloting on the six 
studs and the front bearing cover.

[FIGURE: C100631A.gif]

Install the six nuts with lockwashers. Tighten to 244-271 Nm
 (180-200 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12973A.gif]

Lightly oil threads of capscrews. Then, install and tighten the 
capscrews to 108-136 Nm (80-100 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12974A.gif]

Install the yoke on the output shaft splines and move it into the rear 
bearing cover. 

Lock the transmission by engaging two mainshaft gears with their 
sliding clutches. 

Lightly oil output shaft threads. Then, install the nut on the output 
shaft. Tighten the nut to 542-610 Nm (400-450 lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Input Shaft 

 Special Procedure for Changing Input Shaft 

Some cases of service can require replacement of the input shaft 
because of clutch wear on the splines. In these instances the input shaft can 
be removed without disassembling the transmission other than removing the 
shift bar housing. Removal of the clutch housing is optional.

[FIGURE: C10066C.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

7025

Bearing

2

7A059

Spacer

3

7017

Input Shaft

4

7005

Case

5

7064

Snap Ring

7

—

Bushing (Part of 7017)

 Removal 

Remove shift bar housing from the transmission case. Refer to Shift Bar 
Housing in the Removal and Installation portion of this section. 

Remove the retaining capscrews, front bearing cover and gasket. Service 
the oil seal of model covers so equipped. 

Remove the bearing retaining snap ring from the shaft groove. 

Push down on the input shaft to cock the bearing in the bore. Drive the 
input shaft toward the transmission rear through the bearing as far as 
possible. Pull the input shaft forward to expose the bearing. 

Use pry bars or screwdrivers to complete removal of the bearing. 

Remove the spacer and the snap ring. 

Pull the input shaft forward and out of the drive (4th) gear and case. 

 Installation 

If necessary, replace the bushing in the input shaft pocket. Install 
input shaft into drive (4th) gear.

Install the snap ring in the snap ring groove inside the drive (4th) 
gear. 

Install the spacer on the input shaft. 

Install the bearing on the input shaft. 

Install the bearing retainer snap ring. 

Install the front bearing cover and gasket. Make sure to align the oil 
return hole in the case with the hole in the cover. Lightly oil capscrew 
threads. Then, install and tighten capscrews to 47-61 Nm 
(35-45 lb-ft).

Install the shift bar housing. Refer to Shift Bar Housing in the 
Removal and Installation portion of this section.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Auxiliary Section 

 Bearing Cover, Rear, Removal 

Remove the capscrews and the rear bearing cover and gasket.

[FIGURE: C100671A.gif]

If necessary, remove the oil seal from the rear bearing cover.

[FIGURE: C100681A.gif]

Remove the speedometer rotor or replacement spacer from the output shaft.

[FIGURE: C100691A.gif]

Remove the washer from the output shaft.

 Auxiliary Countershafts, Removal 

Use a soft bar and maul to drive the countershafts forward through the 
countershaft bearings and remove them from the auxiliary housing.

[FIGURE: C100701A.gif]

Remove the countershaft bearings from the auxiliary case bearing bores.

[FIGURE: C100711A.gif]

 NOTE: The vise should be equipped with soft jaws or wood blocks to prevent 
damage to the countershaft. 

If necessary, secure assembly in a vise and remove the auxiliary 
countershaft front bearing race from the countershaft with a jaw puller and 
clamp.

If necessary, secure assembly in a vise and remove the auxiliary 
countershaft rear bearing race. 

 Range Cylinder Assembly, Synchronizer Assembly, LO Range Gear and 
Output Shaft, Disassembly 

Secure the auxiliary housing in a vise. Remove the capscrews and the 
range cylinder cover and gasket.

[FIGURE: C100721A.gif]

Remove the yoke bar nut and washer.

[FIGURE: C100731A.gif]

 NOTE: Do not damage the piston. 

Push range yoke bar to the transmission rear. Use a screwdriver to 
remove the piston.

[FIGURE: C100741A.gif]

Remove the copper gasket from the yoke bar.

 NOTE: This step will damage the bearing and should not be attempted unless 
bearing replacement is planned. 

Use pullers and a clamp to remove the bearing from the output shaft 
front.

Move the synchronizer assembly, shift yoke and yoke bar forward and out 
of the housing assembly.

[FIGURE: C100751A.gif]

Remove the yoke bar and shift yoke from the synchronizer assembly. Cut 
the lockwire and remove the two lock screws. Remove the shift yoke from the 
yoke bar.

[FIGURE: C100771A.gif]

[FIGURE: C100761A.gif]

Remove the dust seal and air port extension from the range cylinder 
housing top.

[FIGURE: C100781A.gif]

Remove the cylinder housing. If necessary, remove the O-ring from the 
small bore in the cylinder.

[FIGURE: C100791A.gif]

 LO Range Gear and Output Shaft, Removal 

 NOTE: When applying force to the output shaft rear, do not damage threads. 

Using a soft bar and maul, drive or press against the output shaft rear 
to move assembly forward and out of the rear bearing.

Remove the rear washer and LO range gear from the shaft rear.

[FIGURE: C100801A.gif]

Remove the spline washer from the LO range gear hub.

[FIGURE: C100811A.gif]

Move the output shaft rear bearing to the rear and out of the housing.

 Synchronizer 

 Disassembly 

Place the larger LO range synchronizer ring on the bench. Cover the 
assembly with a shop towel to prevent losing the three springs released from 
the HI range synchronizer at the pin locations. Pull the HI range synchronizer 
from the blocker pins.

[FIGURE: C100821A.gif]

Remove the synchronizer springs from the HI range synchronizer ring bore.

[FIGURE: C100831A.gif]

Removing the sliding clutch from the synchronizer LO range pins.

[FIGURE: C100841A.gif]

 Assembly 

 NOTE: Pins on the LO range synchronizer must be lined up with the chamfered 
holes on the sliding clutch bottom. 

Place the larger LO range synchronizer ring race down on the bench with 
the pins up. Place the sliding clutch, recessed side up, on the pins of the LO 
range synchronizer.

[FIGURE: C100851A.gif]

Install the three springs in the HI range synchronizer ring bore. 

Place the HI range synchronizer ring, seating springs against the pins. 

Apply downward pressure to the HI range synchronizer ring while 
twisting counterclockwise to compress the springs and fully seat the ring on 
the LO range synchronizer blocker pins.

[FIGURE: C100861A.gif]

 LO Range Gear and Output Shaft, Assembly 

 NOTE: Make sure the magnetic discs are installed in the auxiliary housing. 

 NOTE: Mark timing teeth on the LO range gear. A highly visible color of 
toolmaker's dye is recommended. 

Mark any two adjacent gear teeth. Then mark two adjacent teeth which 
are directly opposite the first set marked. There should be the same number of 
teeth between the markings on each gear side.

[FIGURE: C100871A.gif]

Place splined washer on the output shaft, with shoulder facing up as 
shown.

[FIGURE: C100881A.gif]

Install the LO range gear over the output shaft rear and against 
shoulder of splined washer.

[FIGURE: C100891A.gif]

Install the LO range gear rear washer on the output shaft and against 
gear, with the chamfer side facing up.

[FIGURE: C100901A.gif]

Stand the output shaft on end with the shaft rear facing up. Place the 
auxiliary housing over the shaft so the output shaft extends through the rear 
bore.

[FIGURE: C100911A.gif]

 NOTE: Do not heat the bearing above 135°C (275°
F). 

Using a heat lamp or hot plate and oil, heat the output shaft rear 
bearing and install on the output shaft. Seat the bearing securely on the 
shaft and in the bore.

[FIGURE: C100921A.gif]

Install the bearing in the housing bore with the appropriate driver.

[FIGURE: C100931A.gif]

 Range Cylinder, Assembly 

If removed, install the O-ring in the cylinder small bore slot. 
Lubricate the O-ring with Silicone Lubricant COAZ-19553-AA or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESR-M13P4-A. 

Install the range cylinder in the housing with the cylinder air port 
aligned with the air port in the auxiliary housing.

[FIGURE: C100941A.gif]

Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to air port extension 
threads. Install the dust seal and air port extension through housing and into 
the air cylinder bore.

[FIGURE: C100781A.gif]

 Range Cylinder Assemblies and Synchronizer, Installation 

Place the shift yoke on the yoke bar, long hub toward the bar front. 
Align slots in the yoke bar and install the two lock screws. Tighten lock 
screws to 68-88 Nm (50-65 lb-ft) and secure with lockwire.

[FIGURE: C12975A.gif]

Place the yoke in the sliding clutch slot; threaded end of the yoke bar 
toward the larger LO range synchronizer. Place the entire assembly in the 
auxiliary housing, engaging the sliding clutch splines with the output shaft. 
Insert the yoke bar through the cylinder bore.

[FIGURE: C100751A.gif]

Install the copper gasket on the yoke bar threaded end.

[FIGURE: C100741A.gif]

Install the O-ring on the piston outer diameters. Apply a light coat of 
Silicone Lubricant COAZ-19553-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESR-M13P4-A to the O-ring.

[FIGURE: C100951A.gif]

Install the piston on the yoke bar and against the copper gasket, 
piston flat side out.

[FIGURE: C100961A.gif]

Install the lockwasher and nut on the yoke bar and tighten to 81-95 Nm
 (60-70 lb-ft). 

[FIGURE: C12976A.gif]

Install the gasket and cylinder cover with the HI range port to the 
right. Lightly oil threads of capscrews. Then, install and tighten the four 
capscrews to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12977A.gif]

 Auxiliary Countershafts 

 Assembly 

Install the bearing inner race on the countershaft front.

[FIGURE: C100971A.gif]

Install the bearing inner race on the countershaft rear.

[FIGURE: C100981A.gif]

 NOTE: Countershaft gear teeth must be marked for timing the auxiliary 
section. Mark with a highly visible color of toolmakers' dye. 

Mark the tooth on the countershaft gear which is stamped with an O.

[FIGURE: C100991A.gif]

 Installation 

Seat the outer races of the countershaft rear bearing only partially in 
the housing bores, just far enough to stay in place.

[FIGURE: C101001A.gif]

 NOTE: Time the countershaft gear with the LO range gear. As the countershaft 
is installed, mesh the marked LO range gear tooth on each countershaft between 
each set of marked gear teeth on the LO range gear. 

Place the countershaft into position in the auxiliary housing, 
inserting the inner race into the partially installed rear bearing. 

[FIGURE: C101011A.gif]

With the countershaft in position, complete the installation of the 
countershaft rear bearings on the shaft and into the case bore. Seat securely. 

Install the washer, flat side to the rear, on the output shaft and 
against the bearing. 

Install the speedometer rotor or replacement spacer on the output shaft. 

 NOTE: Use the proper seal driver to install the seal. 

If previously removed, install the oil seal in the rear bearing cover, 
with seal lip to the rear.

Install the rear bearing cover with the speedometer bore up and to the 
left. Apply Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 to capscrew threads. Then, 
install and tighten the capscrews to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12978A.gif]

Install the bearing on the output shaft front, with chamfered side to 
race rear.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Front Section 

 Input Shaft, Removal 

Remove the four capscrews retaining the front bearing cover. Remove the 
bearing cover and gasket.

[FIGURE: C101021A.gif]

Remove the bearing retaining snap ring from the shaft groove.

[FIGURE: C101031A.gif]

Push down on the input shaft to cock the bearing in the bore. Drive the 
input shaft toward the transmission rear, through the bearing as far as 
possible. Pull the input shaft forward to expose the bearing. 

Use pry bars to complete the bearing removal.

[FIGURE: C101041A.gif]

Remove the spacer from the input shaft. 

Remove the snap ring from the groove inside the drive (4th) gear.

[FIGURE: C101051A.gif]

Pull the input shaft forward and out of the drive (4th) gear and case. 

Check the bushing in the input shaft pocket, replace if worn.

[FIGURE: C101061A.gif]

 Auxiliary Drive Gear 

 Removal 

Straighten the lock tangs. Remove the four capscrews and two bearing 
retainers from the case.

[FIGURE: C101071A.gif]

Remove the snap ring from the mainshaft rear, located inside the 
auxiliary drive gear bore.

[FIGURE: C101081A.gif]

With two screwdrivers, pry the auxiliary drive gear off the mainshaft.

[FIGURE: C101091A.gif]

 Disassembly 

Remove the snap ring from the auxiliary drive gear. 

Press or use a driver to remove the bearing from the auxiliary drive 
gear. 

 Assembly 

Press the bearing on the auxiliary drive gear. 

Install the bearing retaining snap ring in the auxiliary drive gear 
shoulder groove. 

 Upper Countershaft Bearings, Removal 

Remove the upper countershaft snap ring from the case rear bearing bore.

[FIGURE: C101101A.gif]

Use a soft bar and maul against the countershaft rear and move the 
countershaft assembly forward as far as possible until the snap ring groove in 
the front bearing is exposed. 

Install the snap ring removed from the rear bearing bore, in the 
exposed snap ring groove.

[FIGURE: C101111A.gif]

 NOTE: Steps four and five may have to be repeated several times to unseat the 
front bearing. 

Use a soft bar and maul to drive the countershaft assembly to the rear 
as far as possible. This will move the front bearing forward on the 
countershaft. 

From the case rear, use a soft bar and maul to drive the countershaft 
forward to unseat the front bearing from the case bore.

Use puller or pry bars to remove the front countershaft bearing. 

 NOTE: Removal procedure damages the bearings. Removal should not be attempted 
unless bearing replacement is planned. 

Block the countershaft and use a maul and punch from inside the case to 
drive the rear countershaft bearing from the case bore and countershaft.

[FIGURE: C101121A.gif]

 Upper Reverse Idler Gear Assembly, Removal 

Use inside jaw pullers or an impact puller and remove the auxiliary 
countershaft front bearing from the left reverse idler gear bore. 

Remove the plug from the reverse idler gear shaft rear.

[FIGURE: C101131A.gif]

Use a socket wrench and remove the stop nut from the reverse idler gear 
shaft front. Remove the washer.

[FIGURE: C101141A.gif]

Use an impact puller with a 1/2-inch 13-threaded end to remove the 
reverse idler gear shaft from the case bore.

[FIGURE: C101151A.gif]

As the reverse idler gear shaft is moved to the rear, remove the thrust 
washer and reverse idler gear from the case. 

If necessary, remove the bearing from the reverse idler gear bore.

[FIGURE: C101161A.gif]

 Mainshaft Assembly 

 Removal 

 CAUTION: After performing this step, note that the drive gear will be free and 
can fall from the shaft. 

Block the right countershaft assembly against the case wall. Slide the 
drive gear to the rear and engage with the sliding clutch splines. Use a hook 
around 1st/2nd sliding clutch. Tilt the mainshaft front up and lift the 
assembly from the case.

[FIGURE: C101171A.gif]

 Disassembly 

Secure the mainshaft, with drive (4th) gear up, in a vise. Remove the 
drive (4th) gear and the 3rd/4th speed sliding clutch.

[FIGURE: C101181A.gif]

Remove 3rd gear hub snap ring from the mainshaft groove.

[FIGURE: C101191A.gif]

Remove tolerance washer and 3rd gear.

[FIGURE: C101201A.gif]

Remove 2nd gear and tolerance washer.

[FIGURE: C101211A.gif]

Remove 1st/2nd speed sliding clutch.

[FIGURE: C101221A.gif]

Remove mainshaft key from mainshaft keyway.

[FIGURE: C101231A.gif]

Remove tolerance washer and 1st gear.

[FIGURE: C101241A.gif]

Remove LO speed gear and tolerance washer.

[FIGURE: C101251A.gif]

Remove LO/reverse speed sliding clutch.

[FIGURE: C101261A.gif]

Remove tolerance washer and reverse gear.

[FIGURE: C101271A.gif]

 Assembly 

 NOTE: If previously removed, install the corresponding snap rings in the 
inside diameter of the mainshaft gears. 

Secure the mainshaft in a vise equipped with brass jaws or wood blocks, 
shaft pilot-end down. If previously removed, install the roll pin in the 
keyway. 

Install the reverse gear tolerance washer in the groove near the 
mainshaft rear.

[FIGURE: C101281A.gif]

 NOTE: Make sure the mainshaft key is positioned with the word TOP to the 
outside. 

Rotate the tolerance washer in the mainshaft groove to align the washer 
splines with the mainshaft splines. Install the mainshaft key in keyway to 
lock the washer in place.

[FIGURE: C101291A.gif]

Install the reverse gear on the tolerance washer with clutching teeth 
facing down.

[FIGURE: C101301A.gif]

Install the auxiliary drive gear on the mainshaft with clutching teeth 
facing up.

[FIGURE: C101311A.gif]

Install the snap ring in the mainshaft rear groove.

[FIGURE: C101321A.gif]

Insert two screwdrivers between the reverse gear hub and the auxiliary 
drive gear. Apply slight downward pressure on the screwdriver handles to 
spread the gears evenly apart. Make sure the gear hubs are parallel. Insert a 
feeler gauge between the hubs. The gap must be between 0.127-0.305 mm 
(0.005-0.012 inch). If the clearance is less than the minimum 0.127-mm 
(0.005-inch) tolerance, the tolerance washer in the reverse gear should be 
replaced by a thinner tolerance washer. This increases the axial clearance 
between gears. If the clearance checked is greater than the maximum 0.305-mm 
(0.012-inch) tolerance, a thicker tolerance washer should be installed in the 
reverse gear. This would decrease the axial clearance between the gears.

[FIGURE: C101331A.gif]

Washers are available in the following thicknesses to obtain the 
correct limits. Select the appropriate washer and as required.

After proper reverse gear clearance has been set, remove the snap ring 
from the mainshaft rear. Remove the auxiliary drive gear and the reverse gear 
from the mainshaft. The tolerance washer and key remain on the mainshaft. 

Reposition the mainshaft with the reverse gear minus its snap ring in 
the vise, with pilot end up, and the keyway accessible. 

Install the LO/reverse speed sliding clutch on the mainshaft, against 
the reverse gear tolerance washer. Align sliding clutch slot with mainshaft key.

[FIGURE: C101341A.gif]

Remove the mainshaft key. Install LO speed gear tolerance washer on the 
mainshaft. Install the key to lock the tolerance washer to the shaft. 

Install LO speed gear on the mainshaft, clutching teeth down and 
engaged with the washer external splines.

[FIGURE: C101351A.gif]

Install 1st gear on the mainshaft, clutching teeth up.

[FIGURE: C101361A.gif]

 CAUTION: When the key is removed, the mainshaft gears can drop to the bottom. 

Remove the mainshaft key from the keyway. Install 1st gear tolerance 
washer on the mainshaft and into 1st gear hub.

[FIGURE: C101371A.gif]

Install the mainshaft key to lock the tolerance washer to the shaft.

[FIGURE: C101381A.gif]

Check axial clearances and make adjustments if necessary. 

Install the 1st/2nd speed sliding clutch, aligning sliding clutch slot 
with key; engage with 1st gear.

[FIGURE: C101391A.gif]

 NOTE: Pull the mainshaft key up slightly to fit in keyway. 

Move the mainshaft key upward and install 2nd gear tolerance washer. 
Install mainshaft key.

[FIGURE: C101401A.gif]

Reposition the key so it rests on the mainshaft grooved shoulder. 

Install the 2nd gear on the mainshaft with clutching teeth down. Engage 
gear with the tolerance washer external splines. 

Install the 3rd gear on the mainshaft with clutching teeth up.

[FIGURE: C101411A.gif]

Install a tolerance washer in the 3rd gear bore. 

Install the snap ring in the snap ring groove.

[FIGURE: C101421A.gif]

Check axial clearance and make adjustments if necessary. 

Install the 3rd/4th speed sliding clutch on the mainshaft. Align 
sliding clutch slot with key and engage clutch with 3rd gear.

[FIGURE: C101431A.gif]

 NOTE: Mark timing teeth on drive (4th) gear with a highly visible color of 
toolmakers' dye. 

Mark two adjacent teeth on the (4th) drive gear. Then mark two adjacent 
teeth which are directly opposite the first set marked. There should be the 
same numb

Subassemblies 

 Remote Shift Tower

 Shift Bar Housing 

 Disassembly 

 NOTE: During disassembly, lay all parts on a clean bench in the order of 
removal to facilitate reassembly. Shift bars not being removed must be kept in 
the neutral position or interlock parts will lock bars. 

Remove the two capscrews and remove the detent spring cover from 
housing top. Remove the three tension springs installed under the cover.

[FIGURE: C101811A.gif]

Tilt the assembly and remove the three detent balls from the housing 
bores.

[FIGURE: C101821A.gif]

Secure the assembly in a vise with the air valve actuating shaft up. 
The housing front will be to the right.

[FIGURE: C101831A.gif]

 NOTE: When removing the shift bars, start with the upper shift bar, move all 
the bars to the right and out the rear boss bore. Cut the lockwire and remove 
the lock screws from each bar just before their removal. 

Move the LO/reverse shift bar to the right and out of housing, removing 
the shift yoke from bar.

[FIGURE: C101841A.gif]

Move the 1st/2nd shift bar to the right and out of housing, removing 
shift yoke from bar. As the neutral notch in bar clears the front web, remove 
the interlock pin from the neutral notch bore.

[FIGURE: C101851A.gif]

[FIGURE: C101861A.gif]

Remove the air valve actuating shaft from rear web.

[FIGURE: C101871A.gif]

Move the 3rd/4th shift bar to the right and out of housing, removing 
shift yoke from bar. As yoke is removed, remove the two interlock balls from 
front web.

[FIGURE: C101881A.gif]

If necessary, remove the plug, spring and reverse plunger stop from 
bore in LO/reverse shift yoke.

[FIGURE: C101891A.gif]

 Assembly 

If previously removed, place plunger stop in LO/reverse shift yoke and 
install spring in bore of yoke and onto shank of plunger. Install the plug and 
tighten to compress spring. 

Back the plug out 1-1/2 turns and stake plug through the small hole in 
yoke.

[FIGURE: C101901A.gif]

 NOTE: Keep bar in neutral position during installation. Do not exceed the 
recommended torque rating for yoke lock screws as overtightening can distort 
shift bars. 

Place the housing in a vise with the front of housing to the right as 
shown. Install the 3rd/4th shift bar in bottom bore with detent notches to the 
front. Install yoke and lock screw and tighten to 47-61 Nm 
(35-45 lb-ft). Secure with lockwire.

[FIGURE: C12980A.gif]

Install interlock ball in front web vertical bore.

[FIGURE: C101921A.gif]

Install air valve actuating shaft in rear web vertical bore.

[FIGURE: C101931A.gif]

Install the 1st/2nd shift bar in center bore, and install shift yoke on 
bar; insert interlock pin in detent notch. Install lock screw and tighten to 
47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft). Secure with lockwire.

[FIGURE: C101941A.gif]

Install interlock ball in front web vertical bore.

[FIGURE: C101951A.gif]

Install LO/reverse shift bar in upper bore, detent notches to the 
front. Install yoke on bar, fork to the rear. Install lock screw and tighten 
to 47-61 Nm (35-45 lb-ft). Secure with lockwire.

[FIGURE: C101961A.gif]

Remove assembly from vise and install the three detent balls, one in 
each bore in housing top. Keep yokes in neutral.

[FIGURE: C101971A.gif]

Install the three tension springs, one in each bore, in housing top.

[FIGURE: C101981A.gif]

Install the detent spring cover. Lightly oil threads of capscrews. 
Then, install and tighten the two capscrews to 47-61 Nm 
(35-45 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: C12982A.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Shift Selectors

Vehicle manufacturers may choose different types of shift selectors for 
their equipment. The shift selector in an Allison-equipped vehicle will be 
similar to one of those shown on this page.

[FIGURE: D13161A.gif]

 Push-Button Shifter 

The push-button shift selector has reverse, neutral, drive, up and down 
arrows, a mode button, and a digital display. When a range button has been 
pressed, a tone will sound, the SELECT indicator will display the chosen 
operation (if the ECU determines the shift is acceptable), and the 
transmission will shift to the starting range as indicated on the monitor 
display. In DRIVE, selection of a specific gear can be accomplished by 
pressing the up or down arrow buttons. Conditions resulting in the DO NOT 
SHIFT light located on the instrument panel will disable the pad and no tones 
will be heard.

 Shift Lever Selector 

The lever selector is an electro-mechanical control. The pattern of 
positions can vary according to the shift selector installed. Positions R, N, 
and D are selected by pressing a hold override button and choosing the desired 
gear. It is possible to move between forward drive positions without pressing 
the hold override button. A mode button (a dash-mounted switch can be used) is 
located on lever and push-button shift selectors to activate a second shift 
schedule or specialized function when desirable. The mode being utilized is 
identified above the mode button. The display will indicate MODE ON for most 
programmed functions.

 Mode Button 

This feature is located on the shift lever and push-button shifters and 
can be used to activate a second shift schedule (this is typically programmed 
for "economy," which will enable the transmission to shift at a lower engine 
rpm to conserve fuel).

 Display Mode 

A display mode button is included on the lever selector to allow access 
to diagnostic code information. The capability is included on the push-button 
selector by pressing the up and down arrow buttons at the same time.

This button is included on the shift lever selector to allow access to 
diagnostic code information. The capability is included on the push-button 
selector by pressing the up and down arrow buttons at the same time.

 Allison MD3060 and MD3560 

With an Allison MD-equipped vehicle, selecting the right moment to 
upshift or downshift during the changing road and traffic conditions is not 
necessary. The Allison MD does it for you. However, knowledge of the gear 
ranges and when to select them will make vehicle control and driving even 
easier.

 WARNING: THESE TRANSMISSIONS HAVE NO PARK POSITION. BEFORE LEAVING THE DRIVER 
SEAT EVEN MOMENTARILY, WHETHER THE ENGINE IS RUNNING OR SHUT OFF, ALWAYS SHIFT 
INTO N (NEUTRAL) AND SET THE PARKING BRAKE OR EMERGENCY BRAKE. ALWAYS USE 
WHEEL CHOCKS. UNEXPECTED AND POSSIBLY SUDDEN VEHICLE MOVEMENT CAN OCCUR IF 
THESE PRECAUTIONS ARE NOT TAKEN. 

 NOTE: The vehicle must be completely stopped before shifting from forward to 
reverse or from reverse to forward. The select indicator will display R and 
the Monitor will display R when reverse is attained.

The MD3060 and MD3560 automatics are six-speed transmissions that have 
five forward driving ranges, as described below. These transmissions are 
electronically controlled and are available with a push-button or shift lever 
shifter.

Reverse: The vehicle must be completely stopped before shifting from 
forward to reverse or from reverse to forward. The select indicator will 
display R and the monitor will display R when reverse is attained.

Neutral: Place the transmission in neutral before starting the engine. 
The engine will not start in any other gear (if it does, the neutral start 
circuit must be serviced immediately). Neutral is also used during stationary 
operation of the power takeoff (if so equipped).

 WARNING: DO NOT ALLOW THE VEHICLE TO COAST IN NEUTRAL. TRANSMISSION BRAKING IS 
NOT AVAILABLE IN NEUTRAL. THIS PRACTICE CAN RESULT IN TRANSMISSION DAMAGE. 

Drive: The vehicle will attain first gear when drive is selected, and 
as the speed increases, the transmission will automatically upshift through 
each gear. As the vehicle slows down, the transmission will automatically 
downshift.

5-2: Occasionally, the road conditions, load, or traffic conditions 
will make it desirable to restrict the automatic shifting to a lower gear. 
These positions also provide progressively greater engine braking for going 
down grades (the lower the gear, the greater the braking effect).

First gear: Use this gear when pulling through mud and deep snow, when 
maneuvering in tight spaces, or while driving up or down grades. Low gear 
provides the vehicle with its maximum driving power and maximum engine braking 
power.

 NOTE: The MD3060 and MD3560 transmissions incorporate a hold feature to 
prohibit upshifting above the gear selected during normal driving. For 
downhill operation, the transmission may upshift above the highest gear 
selected when the engine governed speed is exceeded, and damaging the engine 
is a possibility.

 NOTE: In case of engine shutdown (i.e., running out of fuel) while the 
transmission is in gear, the transmission will remain in gear until the 
ignition key is turned to the OFF position. After the ignition key has been 
turned to the OFF position, the transmission will automatically shift to 
neutral and the monitor on the shift pad will display NEUTRAL when the 
ignition key is in the ON position. If the vehicle is equipped with a shift 
lever shifter, the transmission will return to neutral (when the ignition key 
is turned to OFF) but the engine cannot be restarted until the shift lever has 
moved to the NEUTRAL position.

Power takeoff operation: The PTO drive gear on these transmissions is 
engine-driven and provides direct engine power. The power takeoff can be 
operated when the vehicle is moving or stopped.

The PTO gear is in constant mesh with the drive gear in the converter 
housing. A friction clutch or constant drive is used to transmit power to the 
PTO output.

DO NOT SHIFT: If this light illuminates (accompanied by eight seconds 
of short beeps from the shift selector) while the vehicle is in operation, it 
indicates the ECU has detected the transmission operating parameters have been 
exceeded and the shifts are being restricted (i.e., upshifts and downshifts 
may be restricted). Also, the SELECT digit on the shifter display will be 
blank. A diagnostic code will be recorded in the ECU if this happens. The 
transmission will continue to operate in order to seek service assistance. If 
the vehicle is equipped with a push-button shifter, it will not operate. If 
equipped with a shift lever and the lever is moved, a continuous alarm will 
sound until the original shift lever position is restored.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Throttle Linkage Check 

 NOTE: Whenever the throttle linkage has been adjusted, adjust the throttle 
modulator linkage. 

When the throttle linkage is properly adjusted, maximum engine 
performance starting and accelerating a heavily loaded truck is obtained 
automatically. The driver need only press the accelerator pedal to the WOT 
position and hold it there. With the accelerator pedal held at the WOT 
position, the transmission will stay in the starting gear until engine 
crankshaft speed approaches the engine governed speed (maximum engine 
performance), then it will shift into the next higher gear. The automatic, 
full throttle (at detent) shifting just under governed speed will continue 
until the highest gear or desired road speed is reached.

Diagnostic Codes, MD-Series

The following is a list of some of the most common diagnostic codes. 
For a complete listing accompanied by service information, see the Allison 
MD-Series Troubleshooting Manual.

The diagnostic codes are broken down into a two-digit main code and a 
two-digit sub-code.

 CODES 13/12 AND 13/23

Main Code

Sub-Code

Description

13

12

Battery voltage to electronic control unit (ECU) is too low.

13

23

Battery voltage to the ECU is too high.

If the condition is intermittent, closely inspect the vehicle wiring 
for transmission system power and grounds. Check for loose, dirty or painted 
connections. Check the vehicle interface module (VIM) for loose, incorrect or 
overheating relays or fuses. Check for wires that are chafed and touching 
other components.

 CODES 21/12 AND 21/23

Main Code

Sub-Code

Description

21

12

Throttle position sensor failed low.

21

23

Throttle position sensor failed high.

This code indicates the throttle position sensor has been released or 
pulled by its linkage into an error zone, a fault with the sensor or the 
wiring to the sensor of the ECU. Perform Pinpoint Test A .

 NOTE: Main Code 21 in conjunction with Main Code 33 indicates the potential 
loss of common ground between the throttle and temperature sensors.

 CODES 24/12 AND 24/23

Main Code

Sub-Code

Description

24

12

Oil temperature cold.

24

23

Oil temperature hot.

This code indicates the ECU has detected a high or low temperature in 
the transmission sump. All shifts are inhibited when Code 24/12 is set. No 
upshifts are allowed above a calibration range when code 24/23 is set. All 
inhibits are cleared when the temperature conditions are normal.

Should the hot oil code appear (24/23), shift the transmission to 
neutral and accelerate the engine to 1200-1500 rpm to allow the transmission 
to return to normal temperature 71-104°C (160-220°
F) before operation can take place. Check the transmission 
oil level.

 CODES 33/12 AND 33/23

Main Code

Sub-Code

Description

33

12

Oil temperature sensor low.

33

23

Oil temperature sensor high.

This code indicates the ECU has diagnosed a fault with the sump 
temperature sensor or associated circuitry. This indicates the sensor failed 
showing abnormally high or low temperature readings.

 CODES 35/00 AND 35/16

Main Code

Sub-Code

Description

00

Power interruption (this would occur only after the power has been
restored). During power interruption, the DO NOT SHIFT light will illuminate
but the transmission will shift.

35

Power interruption at the same time the ECU is recording a critical code.

This code indicates the ECU has detected a complete power loss before 
the ignition was turned off.

Air is supplied to the system at the air supply port by the vehicle's 
air system. The air filter removes foreign matter from the air, and then 
allows it to pass through the air regulator where the pressure is adjusted for 
396-431 kPa (58-63 psi). From there, the air passes through the 1/4-inch

supply air line to the supply ports of the range valve and the slave valve. 
Depending upon the position of the knob on the range valve, air will pass 
through either the low range air line or the high range air line to the range 
shift cylinder.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Slave Valve, Preselection 

An air valve shaft protruding from the shift bar housing prevents the 
actuating piston in the slave valve from moving while the gearshift lever is 
in a gear position and releases the piston when the lever is moved to or 
through neutral.

[FIGURE: C9523B.gif]

================================================================================
PAGE 3455
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 07-06A: Shift Controls, Manual Transmission, Air

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Range Cylinder 

In low range, air pressure is supplied from the slave valve to the low 
range air port in the range cylinder. This air pressure forces the range 
cylinder piston to the rear, engaging the low range gearing. Air pressure on 
the back of the piston and in the high range air line is exhausted out the 
slave valve. 

In high range, air pressure is supplied from the slave valve to the 
high range air port of the range cylinder cover. This air pressure forces the 
range cylinder piston forward, engaging the high range gearing. The air 
pressure that was on the front side of the piston and in the low range air 
line during low range operation is exhausted out the slave valve.

[FIGURE: C95241A.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Roadranger® Valve A-5010 

Constant air pressure is supplied from the slave valve to the S port of 
the Roadranger® valve. In low range (range lever down), air 
passes through the lever and out the P port of the Roadranger®
 valve. This air returns to the slave valve end port or P port depending on 
the type of slave valve used. In high range (control lever up) the lever 
prevents the air from passing through the Roadranger® valve. 
Air pressure that was in the outlet line is exhausted out the bottom of the 
Roadranger® valve.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Intermediate Shift Cylinder 

Constant, regulated air is channeled through the cover to the front 
side of shift piston. Air is always on the side of piston. 

The shift piston is moved by removing or applying air (from constant 
supply) to the backside of piston. This piston area is larger and can overcome 
the area of front side of piston. The removal or application of air on 
backside of piston is controlled by the insert valve in cylinder cover; this 
valve in turn is controlled by the Roadranger® valve.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Deep Reduction Air System

 Roadranger® Valve A-5015 

In addition to the various components of the range shift air system, 
the deep reduction air system utilizes a reduction cylinder and a Roadranger®
 valve A-5015. 

Constant air from the air filter/regulator assembly is supplied to the 
Roadranger® valve A-5015. Air is supplied to the built-in 
deep reduction valve only while in low range from tee fitting at the low range 
or L port of slave valve. The insert valve is installed in the cylinder cover 
to provide the proper airflow needed to move the reduction piston in the 
cylinder. 

With the deep reduction button in the rearward position, the SP port of 
Roadranger® valve is closed and no air is supplied to the 
center port of cylinder cover. 

While in low range, the button can be moved forward to operate in deep 
reduction. The SP port of valve is opened when deep reduction selection is 
made, supplying air to the center port of cylinder cover. 

While in high range, the mechanical interlock of the Roadranger®
 valve prevents movement of deep reduction button to the 
forward position.

4

—

Retaining Nut (Part of 7306)

5

—

Bottom Exhaust Port (Part of 7306)

Travel of the small insert valve piston is only 0.794 mm (0.031 inch). 
As shown in the illustrations below, when no air is applied to the top side of 
valve piston, constant air supplied from the air filter/regulator passes 
freely through the insert valve and to the backside of cylinder piston, moving 
the yoke bar forward to disengage deep reduction gearing (low range and high 
range). When air is applied to the top side of valve piston through the signal 
line, the piston moves down to cut off air supplied to the backside of 
cylinder piston. This air is exhausted out the bottom port of the cover when 
constant air supplied from the regulator is directed to the front side of 
cylinder piston, moving the yoke bar rearward to engage deep reduction gearing 
(deep reduction).

 Component Tests 

 Air Filter 

The air filter contains a replaceable filter element that can be 
removed by turning out the end cap. This element must be cleaned or replaced 
at each oil change, or more often under high humidity conditions. 

 Air Regulator 

With normal vehicle air pressure and the gear shift lever in neutral, 
check the breather port on the side of the regulator. There should be no air 
leaking from the port. If there is a steady leak of air from this port, this 
indicates a damaged regulator that must be replaced. 

Cut off the vehicle air pressure and install an air gauge in the output 
port of the regulator. Bring the vehicle air pressure back to normal. 
Regulated air pressure range is 396-430 kPa (57-62 psi). 

 Slave Valve, Poppet-Type (19470) 

The poppet-type slave valve (19470) is a nonserviceable valve. If the 
valve is damaged, the complete assembly must be replaced. Perform the 
following preliminary checks prior to valve replacement.

Check air fittings and air lines between the slave valve and range 
valve for restrictions. A restriction in the line between the outlet port of 
the range valve and the P port of slave valve can cause a constant air leak 
out the exhaust port of the slave valve. 

Check the torque of the four 1/4-inch slave valve mounting capscrews. 
Tighten to 11 Nm (97 lb-in) and determine if the valve 
functions properly. If the capscrews are not tightened correctly an air leak 
between the slave valve and the transmission case could result. 

If retightening the four slave valve capscrews eliminates the air 
leaks, remove the valve from the transmission and tighten the three No. 10 
Phillips head base plate screws on the back of the valve to 61 Nm
 (45 lb-ft). If the four slave valve retaining capscrews 
are equipped with star washers, install flatwashers under the star washers to 
prevent them from fretting into the valve. Reinstall the valve and tighten 
capscrews to 11 Nm (97 lb-in). 

If the valve continues to leak after the above checks have been made, 
the valve should be replaced.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Roadranger® Valve 

 Removal 

Drain the air from the system. 

Remove the screws in the side of the shift handle skirt, and slide the 
skirt down on the shifter shaft. 

[FIGURE: C91471A.gif]

 NOTE: If you experience difficulty removing the air line from the fitting, a 
slight impact to the tool used on the release sleeve helps remove the secured 
line. 

Remove the air line fittings from under the valve. 

The release sleeve must be pressed to remove the air line. A 5/32-inch 
open-end wrench or equivalent can be used to press the sleeve. 

To remove the air line, apply pressure evenly to both sides of the 
release sleeve and pull the tubing from the fitting. 

Loosen the lock nut and unscrew the valve from the shifter shaft.

[FIGURE: C9149B.gif]

 Installation 

Install the shift control valve on the shifter shaft and tighten the 
lock nut. 

Install the air lines to the valve. 

The air line cut end must be smooth and square. Use a plastic tubing 
cutter or sharp razor knife. Do not use diagonal cutters; they deform the 
tubing. If the air line end is deformed or burred, the internal O-ring can be 
damaged, which causes leaks. 

To install the air line, insert the cut tubing into the fitting. Make 
sure the tubing is seated fully (approximately 3/4-inch). Give a slight tug to 
make sure the air line is secured.

 NOTE: Before installing capscrews, coat the threads with Threadlock®
 and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification WSK-M2G315-A5.

Slide the skirt into place and tighten the retaining screws.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Slave Valve, Piston-Type (A-5000) 

 Disassembly 

Disconnect all air lines. Turn out the four capscrews and remove the 
slave valve from the transmission. 

Turn out the three capscrews and remove the side cap. 

Remove the seal from the piston and remove the O-ring from the seal. 

Remove the spring from the piston. 

Turn out the end cap from the valve body and remove the piston from the 
bore. 

Remove the U-seal from the piston. 

Remove the nylon plug from the piston and remove the O-ring from the 
plug. 

Remove the snap ring from the bore in front of the valve body. 

Remove plug, spring, washer and U-seal from valve body bore. Remove 
O-ring from plug. 

Lubricate all O-rings and U-seals with silicone lubricant and 
reassemble the slave valve. 

 Assembly 

Perform disassembly procedures in reverse order. When reinstalling the 
end cap, do not use more than 54 Nm (40 lb-ft) of torque. 
Overtightening can result in binding the piston in the valve bore.

 Disassembly 

 NOTE: For shift lever, bracket and fork disassembly, follow Steps 1-4. For 
U-joint disassembly, refer to Steps 5-7. 

To disassemble shift lever from bracket, remove the nut and washer 
retaining the bracket fork to bracket. Remove shift fork and shift lever 
assembly. 

[FIGURE: C11448C.gif]

Tighten to 43-50 Nm (32-37 Lb-Ft)

To disassemble the bracket fork from the shift lever, drill a hole in 
one of the bearing caps. Insert a punch in this hole. 

[FIGURE: C11449A.gif]

Drive the pin and opposite bearing assembly from pivot fork bore. 
Remove pin and bearing cap assembly. Discard bearing cap and thrust washer.

[FIGURE: C11450B.gif]

Remove the drilled bearing cap by placing an appropriate size punch on 
bearing inner surface. Drive bearing cap out of fork. Discard bearing cap and 
remaining thrust washer.

[FIGURE: C11474A.gif]

 NOTE: Rings might fly as they come off.

Place yoke assembly on workbench and remove snap rings. Using a drift 
punch and hammer, carefully position punch behind end of ring and strike 
gently. 

[FIGURE: C11465A.gif]

 NOTE: If ears of the yoke bend inward under pressure, tap ears lightly with a 
hammer while continuing to apply pressure. 

Install snap ring in the groove. Make sure the ring is completely 
seated in the groove. Repeat for opposite snap ring. Remove from vise. 

[FIGURE: C11466A.gif]

Place the shifter rod yoke over the cross and install the bearings. 
Refer to Steps 5 and 6. 

[FIGURE: C11467A.gif]

 Assembly 

Lubricate all internal components (pins, O-rings, washers, and 
bearings) with Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B. 

If bracket fork was serviced, refer to Steps 3-4. If U-joint was 
serviced, refer to Steps 5-12. 

[FIGURE: C11468A.gif]

Align bracket fork with pin hole in shift lever. Insert new knurled pin 
into the shift lever through the bracket fork. Make certain to align the 
knurls on the pin with the knurls in the shift lever. Align the pin 3.8 mm 
(0.15 inches) from both ends of the bracket fork, within 0.25 mm (0.010 
inches). Insert a wave washer on both ends of the pin. 

 NOTE: If no support is used on the bracket fork arms during the bearing cap 
press operation, spring-back of the bracket fork arms occurs. Spring-back can 
cause bearing caps to be improperly aligned, which can cause loose shifting 
for the vehicle operator. 

Drive bearing caps over pin ends. Make sure to press on bearing cap 
while maintaining bracket fork arm separation. 

[FIGURE: C11469A.gif]

Remove bearings from the U-joint kit and carefully place the cross in 
the shift lever yoke ears.

Put a dab of grease in each bearing cup to ensure adequate lubrication.

Put a bearing in each yoke ear and, being careful not to dislodge any 
of the needle bearings, push bearing slowly into the yoke using the cross to 
align the bearing. When the bearings are in place, position the assembly in 
the vise as shown.

Tighten the jaws pressing the bearings into the yoke. Do not use force. 
Remove the yoke form the vise and check to see if you dislodged any needles.

With bearings properly started, use slight effort to press the bearings 
in place. 

[FIGURE: C11470A.gif]

Position shifter rod yoke in a vise to support shift lever yoke as 
shown. Do not tighten vise against shifter rod yoke. Drive down on the shifter 
rod yoke with a plastic or brass hammer until the bearing comes out of the 
yoke. Be careful not to damage the yoke by using heavy impact. 

[FIGURE: C11471A.gif]

Adjust vise to provide a seat for the exposed trunnions and remove 
U-joint from yoke. Use light force only. 

[FIGURE: C11472A.gif]

Assembly is now complete. Remove from vise. Relieve assembly stresses 
by holding the yoke in position shown, and strike sharply on each yoke ear 
with a hammer. The assembly should work freely without binding. If not, repeat 
a single blow for each yoke ear. 

[FIGURE: C11473A.gif]

Once the bracket fork and U-joint are assembled, place the bracket fork 
in the bracket. Install nut and washer onto assembly. Tighten the nut to 43-50 Nm
 (32-37 lb-ft). 

Check for proper operation. There should be no binding or interference.

Section 08-00: Clutch System, Service

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Clutch System

The purpose of the clutch is to transfer power from the engine to the 
drivetrain. It connects and disconnects a manually operated transmission and 
the remainder of the drivetrain from the engine. This permits starting and 
stopping the vehicle, shifting and changing speeds that correspond to the 
engine speed through gear reductions for both forward and reverse directions.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Symptom Charts — Clutch Diagnosis

The following symptom routines can be used as an aid in clutch 
diagnosis. 

 NOTE: A light chatter or shudder in the vehicle when engaging the clutch at 
light throttle may be a normal occurrence. This condition may be more 
pronounced in heavily loaded vehicles. Drivetrain function and durability are 
not affected by this chatter condition. Drivetrain components, particularly 
clutches, should not be replaced or rebuilt in attempts to eliminate this 
condition. 

 CLUTCH DIAGNOSIS 

Condition

Possible Source

Action

Clutch Brake Not Functioning Properly During Shifting in Low and 
Reverse (Non-Synchronized Transmission)

Clutch adjustment.

READJUST for proper clutch brake squeeze. REFER to Clutch Release 
Bearing Adjustment in the Adjustments portion of this section for procedures.

Worn Clutch Brake Facing (Non-Synchronized Transmission)

Clutch pedal linkage misadjusted.

READJUST. REFER to Clutch Release Bearing Adjustment in the Adjustments 
 portion of this section for procedure. 

Clutch brake contacted every time operator changes gears.

REPLACE broken clutch brake. 

Used as an upshifting clutch brake.

Do not use for upshifting.

Broken Clutch Brake Tang (Non-Synchronized Transmission)

Clutch brake contacted every time operator changes gears.

REPLACE broken clutch brake. 

Clutch pedal misadjusted.

READJUST. REFER to Clutch Release Bearing Adjustment in the Adjustments 
portion of this section for procedure. 

Using the clutch brake to hold vehicle on a hill.

ADVISE operator to avoid abuse. 

Use of clutch brake for upshifting.

Do not use for upshifting.

Clutch Brake Internal (Wave) Washer Broken (Non-Synchronized 
Transmission)

Clutch brake contacted every time operator changes gears.

REPLACE broken clutch brake. READJUST linkage for proper clutch brake 
squeeze. REFER to Clutch Release Bearing Adjustment in the Adjustments 
 portion of this section for procedure. 

Clutch Brake Comes Apart at the External Crimp or Internal Tang Ring 
(Non-Synchronized Transmission)

Clutch brake linkage misadjusted.

REPLACE broken clutch brake. INSPECT transmission input bearing cover 
and clutch release bearing back plate. If the surface that the clutch brake 
contacts is deeply scored or grooved, REPLACE the transmission bearing cover 
or clutch release bearing and sleeve assembly. READJUST. REFER to Clutch 
Release Bearing Adjustment in the Adjustments portion of this section for 
procedure. 

Clutch brake contacted every time operator changes gears. 

Clutch brake is only used to shift into first or reverse.

Damaged material. 

REPLACE material.

Noisy Clutch

Clutch release bearing dry or damaged.

LUBRICATE bearing with Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K 
or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B, or REPLACE.

Flywheel pilot bearing dry or damaged.

GO to Pinpoint Test H .

Clutch release bearing housing striking cover assembly.

ADJUST clutch. CHECK for wear on cross-shafts, clutch housing bushings 
and release levers.

Clutch Dragging

Clutch disc distorted or warped.

STRAIGHTEN disc to within 0.381 mm (0.015 inch) total indicator 
reading. REPLACE disc if this cannot be done. GO to Pinpoint Test C .

Splines worn on transmission input shaft.

REPLACE input shaft and CHECK clutch disc hubs for excessive wear. If 
worn, REPLACE disc. CHECK flywheel housing alignment of engine and 
transmission. Make sure disc hub slides freely on input shaft splines. 

Flywheel pilot bearing fitting too tightly in flywheel or on end of 
transmission input shaft.

FREE pilot bearing to a light push. FIT in flywheel and on input shaft 
pilot. If bearing is rough, REPLACE. 

Facings gummed with oil or grease.

REPLACE facings or entire driven disc assembly. Cleaning not 
recommended. 

Damaged clutch release bearing.

REPLACE bearing. 

Clutch release shaft projecting through release yoke.

RELOCATE release shaft so it does not project. 

Inadequate bearing release travel.

BLEED the hydraulic control system. 

Clutch Pedal Binding

Check pedal shaft and bushings.

LUBRICATE pedal shaft and bushings in pedal support with Motorcraft 
Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M1C75-B. 

Clutch master cylinder push rod binding on passage compartment bulkhead.

INSPECT clutch master cylinder mounting surface and SERVICE as required. 

Release bearing and hub assembly binding on transmission input shaft.

LUBRICATE bearing hub with Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C 
or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B. REPLACE 
transmission input shaft if worn. 

Clutch Thud

Excessive engine crankshaft end play.

SERVICE engine per specifications. 

Clutch mounting bolts loose.

TIGHTEN clutch mounting bolts per specifications.

Clutch Vibration (Torsional), Vehicle Moving at Road Speed 49-88 km/h 
(30-55 mph)

Incorrect clutch disc installed (wrong friction lag specifications).

INSTALL specified clutch disc. 

Aftermarket (off-brand) clutch disc installed.

INSTALL specified clutch disc. 

Engine not functioning properly.

CHECK engine performance, TUNE UP engine. 

Pressure plate imbalance.

GO to Pinpoint Test E .

Incorrect installation of coupling shaft or driveshaft assembly.

INSTALL correct parts. ALIGN driveline. 

Transmission-Related Problems

Insufficient clutch reserve (excessive clutch pedal free play).

GO to Pinpoint Test F .

Gear Clash

Clutch disc warped or bent preventing full release.

REPLACE clutch disc. 

Clutch housing misalignment.

REALIGN clutch housing. 

Nicked or galled splines on clutch disc hub or transmission input 
shaft. Heavy dried grease or rust on input shaft splines.

CLEAN disc hub splines and transmission input shaft splines of grease, 
dirt or rust. REMOVE nicks or galled areas with file or emery cloth. 

Gear Jumpout

Clutch housing misalignment.

REALIGN clutch housing per this section. 

Noise, Clutch Fully Engaged

Transmission problem.

REFER to Section 07-03 for diagnosis and testing of transmission. 

Start-Up Chatter During Light Clutch Engagement in Low or Reverse

Engine roughness.

TUNE engine. SET idle speed to specifications. 

Throttle linkage improperly adjusted.

READJUST. 

Engine misaligned or not properly seated on mounts.

LOOSEN engine mount bolts, ALIGN and CENTER engine so engine mounts 
center in teardrop holes. 

Body mounts improperly tightened.

CHECK for correct front and rear body mounts, proper installation and 
bolt torque. 

Oil on clutch disc.

CORRECT leak, REPLACE disc, CLEAN pressure plate and flywheel friction 
surfaces with clean solvent (alcohol base). DEGLAZE flywheel.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Clutch Pressure Plate 

Inspect the surface of the pressure plate for burn marks, scores, 
flatness or ridges. If the pressure plate is badly heat-checked or deeply 
scored, replace the pressure plate and cover assembly.

Inspect friction surface of the pressure plate for damage or 
distortion. If friction surface is badly warped or dished in excess of 0.254 
mm (0.010 inch), replace with new pressure plate. Smooth and flat pressure 
plate surfaces must be used for satisfactory clutch life.

Clean the pressure plate and flywheel surfaces with a suitable 
commercial solvent to be sure that surfaces are free from any oil film.

 CAUTION: Do not use cleaners with a petroleum base, and do not immerse the 
pressure plate in the solvent. 

 NOTE: If a substantial difference in lever wear exists, the heavily worn 
lever is binding. Replace the pressure plate.

Using a straightedge and a feeler gauge, check the face runout of the 
pressure plate. If the runout is greater than the service limit, replace the 
clutch cover assembly. 

Service limit: 0-.508 mm (0-.02 inch) 

[FIGURE: C11476A.gif]

 NOTE: Always check the condition of the engine flywheel for cracks, heat 
checks or other damage whenever the clutch is inspected, removed or replaced.

 Clutch Wear 

[FIGURE: C8083B.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Clutch Disc/Discs

Remove the clutch from the flywheel. Refer to Section 08-01 . 

 NOTE: For dual clutch disc assemblies, the front and rear discs may have 
different thicknesses.

Check the driven disc. 

Using a vernier caliper, measure the gauge (facing) thickness in three 
or four areas around each disc. If less than the service limit, replace clutch 
disc.

356 mm (14 Inch) Stamped Angle-Spring Clutch

Standard: 11.4 mm (0.450 inch)

Service: 9.65 mm (0.380 inch)

[FIGURE: C11477A.gif]

If the thickness varies by more than .203 mm (.008 inch) on the facing 
surface, replace the disc. Measurements are taken on pad in similar location 
and distance from outer edge of clutch disc.

[FIGURE: C10322A.gif]

Check the driven disc hub spline for burrs or uneven wear. If either is 
evident, replace the clutch disc. 

Using a feeler gauge, measure the clearance between the clutch disc 
spline and the transmission input shaft spline. If the clearance is greater 
than service limit, replace the clutch disc.

Standard: 0.05-0.15 mm (0.002-0.006 inch)

Service Limit: 0.5 mm (0.02 inch)

[FIGURE: C11478A.gif]

Check the flywheel surface. Check for: 

concavity 

runout 

allowable grind for a reground flywheel 

Refer to Flywheel under Cleaning and Inspection in this section.

Check the pilot bearing. If the bearing is rough, replace it.

 NOTE: When installing a new disc, be careful not to drop it or contaminate it 
with oil or grease.

Perform the following checks.

Check the clutch disc facing for oil or grease (eliminate the source of 
any contamination).

Check the clutch disc for worn or loose facings.

Check the clutch disc for loose rivets in the hub.

Check the clutch disc for distortion.

Check for broken springs, (spring loose enough to rattle will not cause 
noise when vehicle is operating). 

Replace the clutch disc if any of these conditions are present.

[FIGURE: C10818B.gif]

 Two-Disc Clutch with Positive Separator, 356 mm (14 Inch) Applications

[FIGURE: C10323C.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Flywheel Runout Check

Secure Dial Indicator with Bracketry TOOL-4201-C or equivalent to the 
engine flywheel housing with gauge finger on the face of the flywheel near the 
outer edge. Rotate flywheel, making sure to hold it in the full forward or 
rearward position so that crankshaft end play will not be indicated as 
flywheel runout. Maximum allowable runout is 0.127 mm (0.005 inch) per inch of 
the flywheel diameter. For example, 0.178 mm (0.007 inch) runout is allowable 
for a 356 mm (14 inch) clutch.

[FIGURE: C35341A.gif]

If the clutch face runout exceeds specification, remove the flywheel 
and check for burrs between the flywheel and face of the crankshaft mounting 
flange. If no burrs exist, check the runout of the crankshaft mounting flange. 
Replace the flywheel or machine the crankshaft flywheel mounting face 
sufficiently to correct the surface if the mounting flange runout exceeds the 
specification of 0.203 mm (0.008 inch).

If the crankshaft mounting flange is not the cause of the runout, 
resurface or replace the flywheel as necessary. To resurface, refer to Section 03-00 . To remove or replace the flywheel, refer to Section 03A-01 or Section 03B-01 .

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Clutch Release Bearing

Wipe all oil and dirt off the release bearing. The bearing is 
prelubricated and should not be cleaned with solvent.

Inspect the release bearing as follows:

Hold the bearings, hub and back plate and rotate the outer race while 
applying pressure. If the bearing rotation is rough, replace the bearing. If 
bearing is good, remember to refill grease in inside diameter pocket.

Inspect/remove any surface scoring or burrs that may affect the sliding 
motion of the release bearing on the transmission input shaft retainer. Any 
scoring or burrs should be polished off with a fine grade emery paper.

Inspect release bearing hub groove for freedom from nicks and burrs or 
lever wear. Replace the bearing only if there is excessive wear on lever 
groove or yoke contact surface.

Prior to reinstallation, lubricate for release bearing operation with 
lithium-base grease Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B at the following points:

annular groove (grease pocket) of release bearing inside diameter

thin coat on inside diameter of release bearing

release bearing retention clips and fingers of clutch release lever

fulcrum point of clutch release lever

Failure situations for release bearing operation:

Too little clutch pedal free play may allow contact of clutch fingers 
on bearing, thus resulting in a continuous running bearing.

Riding the clutch pedal has the same effect as above.

Misalignment of clutch release lever.

Misalignment between engine and the transmission will exhibit symptoms 
such as transmission jumping out of gear, driveshaft vibration, excessive spin 
time resulting in gear clash, and clutch chatter on start-up.

ADJUSTMENTS

Flywheel Housing Alignment 

Inspection or alignment of the flywheel housing is indicated when 
symptoms exist of excessive transmission gear wear, transmission jumping out 
of gear, driveline vibration, clutch pedal vibration or scrubby feel, pilot 
bearing noise, release bearing noise, or excessive clutch spin time. Common 
complaint areas or obvious misadjustment should always be checked and 
corrected prior to checking alignment to be sure the basic system is in 
working order. 

Remove the transmission and flywheel housing from the vehicle as 
outlined in the appropriate transmission section in Group 07. 

Examine the slave cylinder push rod clevis pin for excessive wear. 
Replace clevis pin as required. 

Examine release lever hole or fork end holes for excessive elongation 
and replace as required. 

Make sure that the cross-shaft and fork assembly rotates freely and has 
no play in the clutch housing bushings. If play exists, replace bushings and 
shaft as required. 

Check that the release lever tips are not excessively worn and that the 
curved portion of the lever is curved with no flat spots. Also, check that the 
locating flats do not show signs of excessive wear or grooving. Replace if 
excessive wear is noted. 

Make sure that the flywheel input shaft pilot bearing turns smoothly 
and freely and that the grease shield is functioning properly. 

Inspect the flywheel. Inspect the flywheel surface for excessive wear 
or scoring. If it is heat checked or warped, resurface or replace the 
flywheel. To resurface the flywheel, refer to Section 03-00 . To remove or 
replace the flywheel, refer to Section 03A-01 or Section 03B-01 . 

Inspect the mating faces of the transmission clutch housing and the 
engine flywheel housing. Any appreciable wear on either housing will cause 
misalignment. Most wear is found on the lower half of the facings between the 
3 and 8 o'clock positions. Replace housing if worn. 

[FIGURE: C35301A.gif]

Secure the dial indicator to engine flywheel or crankshaft, and place 
the gauge finger against the flywheel housing bore. Rotate the flywheel by 
hand, marking the high and low points with chalk or soapstone. Total indicated 
difference between high and low points must not exceed 0.203 mm (0.008 inch).

[FIGURE: C35331A.gif]

Now move the gauge finger to contact the face of the engine flywheel 
housing. Rotate the flywheel and mark high and low points. Total runout should 
not exceed 0.203 mm (0.008 inch). If the flywheel housing bore or face runout 
is not within specification, refer to Alignment Correction .

[FIGURE: C35311B.gif]

The total runout will be the difference between the highest plus and 
minus readings. Maximum total runout of the flywheel housing pilot is 0.203 mm 
(0.008 inch) with No. 2 SAE housings.

[FIGURE: C35321A.gif]

Next, secure the dial indicator to the engine flywheel housing with 
gauge finger on the face of the flywheel near the outer edge. Rotate flywheel. 
Maximum allowable runout is 0.127 mm (0.005 inch) per inch of flywheel 
diameter. For example, 0.178 mm (0.007 inch) runout is allowable for a 356 mm 
(14 inch) clutch. 

[FIGURE: C35341A.gif]

Now move the gauge finger to contact the pilot bearing bore surface. 
Rotate flywheel. Maximum allowable runout is 0.127 mm (0.005 inch). 

Exceeding these limits causes misalignment. If not corrected, 
misalignment causes premature wear of drivetrain components. 

[FIGURE: C35351A.gif]

 NOTE: Exceeding these limits causes misalignment. If not corrected, 
misalignment causes premature wear of drivetrain components.

Use dial indicator to measure the flywheel crankshaft face. Secure the 
dial indicator to the engine flywheel housing with the gauge finger against 
the crankshaft face, near the outer edge. Turn the crankshaft to obtain 
readings. A runout of 0.0381 mm (0.0015 inch) on the face is allowed.

[FIGURE: C35361A.gif]

================================================================================
PAGE 3497
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 08-00: Clutch System, Service

1997 CF8000 and CFT8000 Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Alignment Correction 

Since any change in face alignment will change bore alignment, it may 
be possible to correct bore alignment by changing the face alignment. Face 
alignment can be changed by shimming between the flywheel housing and engine. 
The following illustration shows the type of shim which can be fabricated.

[FIGURE: DC0017A.gif]

The shim required is one half the maximum (minus) indicator reading, 
and should be located at the point of maximum (minus) indicator reading. 

If both the bore and face alignment are out of limits, shim between the 
flywheel housing and engine to bring the face alignment within limits. Check 
the bore alignment. 

If the bore alignment is out of limits and face alignment is within 
limits, shim the flywheel housing to the limit of face misalignment and check 
the bore alignment. If it is not within limits, replace the housing.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Clutch System

The purpose of the clutch is to transfer power from the engine to the 
drivetrain. It connects and disconnects a manually-operated transmission and 
the remainder of the drivetrain from the engine. This permits starting and 
stopping the vehicle, shifting and changing speeds that correspond to the 
engine speed through gear reductions for both forward and reverse directions.

The clutch consists of a splined driven plate (clutch disc) that is 
held in position by the transmission input shaft and a clutch cover (pressure 
plate) that is bolted to the flywheel. The driven plate is a metal disc, faced 
on both sides with ceramic or organic friction material. The pressure plate is 
a metal member that houses and engages the driven plate. This solid member 
(clutch assembly), when engaged, forms a continuous system through which power 
from the engine is transferred to the transmission and then to the rear wheels 
for forward or reverse rotation. Another internal part is the pilot bearing, 
mounted either in the flywheel or crankshaft. The bearing supports the end of 
the input shaft. It is designed for long life and requires no periodic 
maintenance.

When the clutch is engaged, the pressure springs load the pressure 
plate holding the clutch disc(s) firmly between the flywheel and the pressure 
plate. As the clutch pedal is actuated, movement is transferred through the 
mechanical linkage to the release shaft and clutch release lever. On a 
pull-type design clutch, as the release shaft turns, the release lever pulls 
back on the release bearing, unloading the levers and pressure springs, which 
permits the pressure plate to move away from the clutch disc. The clutch disc 
is disengaged from the engine flywheel and the transmission can be shifted to 
another gear.

The pull-type design clutch features an adjustable pressure plate that 
has centrally located angle pressure springs isolated from the heat of the 
pressure plate. The pressure plate also carries return springs to obtain 
positive pressure plate return at the clutch release. The clutch release 
bearing rotates continuously and only carries a thrust load when the clutch is 
released. The release bearing can be lubricated through the transmission lower 
inspection opening in the clutch housing.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Clutch Brake 

The purpose of the clutch brake is to slow down or stop the 
transmission input shaft from rotating on non-synchronized transmissions. This 
permits a clean engagement of either first or reverse gears when starting the 
vehicle from a standstill.

Non-synchronized transmissions use a torque limiting clutch brake. The 
brake is a steel hub with two tangs, encased in a cover that has a facing 
material bonded to both sides. The torque limiting feature is provided by an 
internal slip washer, loaded by a wave spring washer, that is then driven by 
the hub. The spring washer reacts against the clutch brake cover on the one 
side and the internal slip washer on the other, providing a clamping force and 
creating a breakaway torque within the brake. This feature is called torque 
limiting. The hub and spring washer combination slips with respect to the 
covers after approximately 24 Nm (18 lb-ft) load has been 
exceeded. This protects the outer facings.

When the operator depresses the clutch pedal beyond the normal clutch 
disengage position, the clutch release bearing comes in contact with the 
clutch brake and the transmission input shaft bearing cover. Because the tangs 
on the brake hub are engaged in the transmission input shaft splines, the 
transmission is slowed down or stopped. The driver can then shift from first 
to reverse or from reverse to first without clashing or putting undue strain 
on the gears.
