DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Hoses, Pressure and Return

The power steering hoses use O-ring seals at the quick connect 
fittings. There are two possible leak points at the steering gear fittings.

A leak might occur between the power steering hose (pressure or return 
hose) and the hose nut, or between the hose nut and the steering gear housing 
or pump outlet fitting.

================================================================================
PAGE 3595
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 11-02A: Steering Gear, Power, Ross TAS65

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Mechanical Operation

Power is transmitted to the steering gear output shaft (sector shaft) 
by gear teeth in the rack piston. The gear teeth in the rack piston mate with 
the teeth on the sector shaft. Fluid from the engine-driven pump is directed 
to the power cylinder via the control valve, which is concentric to the input 
shaft. 

When force is exerted on the steering wheel to start a steering 
maneuver, the force is transmitted to the input shaft of the steering gear. 
The input shaft is connected to the worm by a torsion bar centering device and 
applies a rotational force to the worm through this connection. In response to 
this rotational force, the worm, acting through the recirculating ball 
mechanism, tries to move the rack piston axially. The rack piston axial 
movement is resisted by its engagement to the sector shaft. Because of this 
resistance, the torsion bar is twisted by the input shaft. 

The steering gear input shaft is also the inner member (spool) of the 
rotary control valve. The outer valve member is integral with the worm and 
rotates as a unit. As the torsion bar transmits rotational force from the 
input shaft to the worm, it acts as a spring, deflecting and allowing the 
input shaft to rotate relative to the worm and valve unit. This relative 
rotation between the input shaft and the worm actuates the control valve.

================================================================================
PAGE 3596
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 11-02A: Steering Gear, Power, Ross TAS65

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Hydraulic Operation

The control valve is an open-center type and when it is in the neutral 
position, the inlet and outlet ports and both cylinder cavities are 
interconnected and there is no flow going to either cylinder cavity. However, 
fluid is circulated from the pump through the control valve and back to the 
reservoir. The pressure in both cylinder cavities is equal and low, sufficient 
only to overcome friction in the lines and the fittings from the outlet port 
to the reservoir. 

As the valve is actuated, the valving edges begin to close, restricting 
flow through the control valve. This restriction directs a portion of the 
fluid flow from the pump to one or the other cylinder cavities. That portion 
of the flow that is not required for the steering maneuver passes through the 
control valve and back to the reservoir. At the same time, the other cylinder 
cavity is opened to the return port and expels fluid back to the reservoir. 

The amount of flow which is directed to the cylinder cavity is 
proportional to the speed at which the steering wheel is being turned. 
Pressure required to complete a steering maneuver is dependent on the amount 
of resistance presented by the steered wheels. The control valve senses these 
requirements and supplies fluid to the cylinder at the proper flow rate and 
pressure. 

As fluid is supplied to the cylinder, the rack piston moves axially, 
rotating the sector shaft and steering the vehicle. The worm is now able to 
rotate in response to the force being applied by the rack piston through the 
recirculating ball and helical screw. Steering action will continue in this 
manner as long as the driver continues to turn the steering wheel. When the 
steering maneuver is completed and effort on the steering wheel is relaxed, 
the torsion bar brings the control valve back to its neutral position. 

If the steered wheels are subjected to shock loads, forces are 
transmitted through the sector shaft to the rack piston and on to the worm. 
This actuates the control valve which directs high pressure fluid to the 
proper cylinder to resist the shock load. By absorbing the shock loads 
hydraulically, objectionable kickback at the steering wheel is prevented. 

The gear is equipped with a pressure relief valve, which limits maximum 
supply pressure to protect the pump, but does not reduce the pressure as the 
steered wheels approach the axle stops. 

Tripping the relief valve maintains a constant pressure in the power 
cylinder by allowing a portion of the flow from the pump to circulate through 
the gear and back to the reservoir. Since fluid is allowed to circulate 
through the gear, the pressure relief valve is not required to activate when 
the wheels reach full turn and the amount of heat generated by the pump is 
reduced greatly. 

The TAS65 gear is equipped with two hydraulic relief poppet valves that 
were automatically set to trip and relieve pressure just before reaching the 
axle stops. This was achieved after initial installation in the vehicle at the 
first right and left turn. The pressure relief poppet valves will 
automatically reset themselves within the poppet adjustment limits if the axle 
stops are reset for increased steering gear travel. These limits are based on 
acceptable equipment revisions from original factory installations. 

If the axle stops are set for decreased steering gear travel, the 
steering gear must be removed from the vehicle and disassembled. The poppet 
adjustment seat and the sleeve assemblies must be reset for automatic 
adjustment after installation. 

Some TAS gears which are mounted with the output shaft above the rack 
piston bore are equipped with either an automatic bleed system or a manual 
bleed screw. 

The procedure for servicing or using the manual bleed screw is 
described under Input Shaft Seal in 
the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

If the unit has an automatic bleed system, no servicing is required.

PAGE 3597

Section 11-02A: Steering Gear, Power, Ross TAS65

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Rotary Valve 

The rotary valve combines simplicity of construction with desirable 
performance characteristics. The speed at which the driver can turn the 
steering wheel with power assist is dependent upon the pump flow (measured in 
gallons per minute, gpm, or liters per minute, lpm) directed to a cylinder 
cavity. The control valve controls the flow. 

The pressure (measured in pounds per square inch or bar) required for 
the gear to steer the vehicle is created by the power steering pump. The 
control valve senses these requirements and directs fluid to the appropriate 
cylinder cavity in the steering gear (and in the auxiliary cylinder if it is a 
dual steering system) at the proper flow rate and pressure. 

The higher pressure a steering gear can withstand, the more work it can 
perform. The maximum operating pressure for all TAS gears is 14996 kPa (2175 
psi). Maximum flow rate for TAS65 is 26.5 lpm (7 gpm). 

The TAS series gears can steer a vehicle within its front end weight 
rating through a turn at low speed and engine idle. As the driver turns the 
steering wheel faster or slower, more or less fluid will be required by the 
gear.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Input Shaft Seal 

 NOTE: This procedure uses the vehicle's power steering pump to force out the 
input shaft seal; the input shaft seal is forced out by pressure. To use this 
procedure, the power steering pump should have a minimum of 10,342 kPa (1500 
psi) available.

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Pitman Arm Puller

T64P-3590-F

 Removal 

Disconnect return line from the steering gear and plug the line. Also 
cap the return port of the gear with a high-pressure fitting.

[FIGURE: G7885A.gif]

Remove the steering column from the gear input shaft.

[FIGURE: G7886A.gif]

Remove the dirt and water seal from the steering gear.

[FIGURE: G7887A.gif]

 NOTE: Be careful not to scratch the bore with the screwdriver. 

Wipe out the grease and then remove the spiral retaining ring. Use a 
screwdriver inserted into the notch formed in the end of the ring. 

[FIGURE: G7888A.gif]

Slip the steering column back onto the input shaft with the pinch bolt 
installed, but not tightened.

[FIGURE: G7889A.gif]

Tie or wrap a shop towel around the input shaft area and place a drip 
pan under the vehicle to catch the oil.

[FIGURE: G7890A.gif]

 WARNING: DO NOT MIX OIL TYPES. ANY MIXTURE OR ANY UNAPPROVED OIL COULD LEAD TO 
SEAL DETERIORATION AND LEAKS. A LEAK COULD ULTIMATELY CAUSE LOSS OF FLUID, 
WHICH COULD RESULT IN A LOSS OF POWER STEERING ASSIST. 

Add fluid as necessary to the full line on the dipstick.

With the vehicle in neutral, momentarily turn the starter (quickly turn 
off the engine if it starts). 

Remove the shop towel. Disconnect the steering column, and remove the 
input shaft seal.

[FIGURE: G7891A.gif]

Check the seal area of the valve housing for any seal fragments. Remove 
any that are found.

[FIGURE: G7892A.gif]

Check the seal for heat damage. If the seal is stiff and brittle, and 
not pliable like the new seal, it is probably heat-damaged. Determine and fix 
the cause of excessive heat in the power steering system.

[FIGURE: G7893A.gif]

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Do not use a socket to install the input shaft seal. You will not be 
able to control seal installation depth, possibly causing a leak. 

Put clean High-Temperature 4x4 Front Axle and Wheel Bearing Grease 
E8TZ-19590-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C198-A between the 
seal lips on the inside diameter of the new input shaft seal and place it over 
the input shaft, garter spring side first. Place Input Seal Installer J37073 
or equivalent over the input shaft and against the seal, small diameter end 
first. Tap the seal installer tool until the tool shoulder is square against 
the valve housing. Remove any seal material that may have sheared off in the 
seal bore or retaining ring groove.

[FIGURE: G7894A.gif]

Insert new retaining ring into the groove.

[FIGURE: G7895A.gif]

Pack the end of the valve housing bore around the input shaft with 
High-Temperature 4x4 Front Axle and Wheel Bearing Grease E8TZ-19590-A or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C198-A. Apply more of the grease 
to a new dirt and water seal and install it over the input shaft. Seat it in 
the groove behind the serrations and against the valve housing.

[FIGURE: G7896A.gif]

Reconnect the steering column to the input shaft and tighten the pinch 
bolt to torque level specified.

[FIGURE: G7897A.gif]

 CAUTION: Make sure poppets are set correctly before beginning this procedure. 

Reconnect the return line to the steering gear return port.

[FIGURE: G7898A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not allow the fluid level to drop significantly or run out of the 
reservoir. This can induce air into the system. 

Fill the reservoir nearly full. Do not steer. Start and run the engine 
for 10 seconds, then shut it off. Check and refill the reservoir. Repeat at 
least three times, checking the reservoir each time.

Start the engine and let it idle for two minutes. Do not steer. Shut 
off the engine and check the fluid level in the reservoir. Refill as required. 

Start the engine again. Steer the vehicle from full left to full right 
several times. Shut off engine and check the fluid level in reservoir. Add 
fluid as necessary, to the full line on the dipstick. 

Automatic bleed systems should now be free of trapped air. For manual 
bleed systems, continue with Step 10. 

 CAUTION: Do not turn steering wheel with bleed screw loosened. 

Start engine and let it idle. Steer from full left to full right 
several times. Stop steering and loosen the manual bleed screw about one turn. 
Allow air and aerated fluid to bleed out until you see only clear fluid. Close 
the bleed screw. Shut off engine and check and refill the reservoir as 
required. 

Repeat Step 10 three or four times until all the air is discharged. 
Tighten the manual bleed screw to 3.4 Nm (30 lb-in).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Steering Gear 

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Pitman Arm Puller

T64P-3590-F

During the steering gear removal, observe the following precautions: 

 CAUTION: Never steam clean or high-pressure wash the hydraulic steering 
components or unit. Do not force or abuse the closely fitted parts or damage 
will result. 

 CAUTION: Never use a hammer to forcefully loosen, remove or install the U-joint 
from the steering gear input shaft. Severe damage to the steering gear can 
result. 

 CAUTION: The input shaft and valve worm assembly must not be rotated more than 
one and one-half revolutions while the drag link is disconnected from the gear 
assembly. This will prevent possible misadjustments of the automatic poppet 
system. 

Drain the steering assembly. 

Thoroughly clean off all outside dirt, especially around the fittings. 

Plug all port holes immediately after removing the hoses and before 
removing the gear from the vehicle. 

Finish cleaning and dry the gear before placing the gear on a workbench.

 Removal 

Disconnect the power steering pressure line at the gear. 

Disconnect the power steering return line at the gear.

 CAUTION: Do not use a hammer on the pitman arm to remove it from sector shaft as 
internal damage to steering gear can result. Always use Pitman Arm Puller 
T64P-3590-F to remove the pitman arm from the sector shaft. 

Remove the cotter pin, the bolt and the nut that fasten the pitman arm 
to the sector shaft. Remove the pitman arm from the sector shaft using Pitman 
Arm Puller T64P-3590-F.

 CAUTION: Do not pound the intermediate shaft U-joint or input shaft coupling off 
the input shaft as internal damage to the steering gear can result. 

Remove the bolt and the nut holding the U-joint to the steering gear 
input shaft.

Remove the bolts and the nuts holding the steering gear to the frame 
side rail. Remove the steering gear.

 Installation 

Place the steering gear on the side rail. Install the bolts, the nuts 
and the washers and tighten to 338-407 Nm (250-300 lb-ft).

 CAUTION: Do not pound the intermediate shaft U-joint or input shaft coupling on 
the input shaft as internal damage to the steering gear can result. 

Place the intermediate shaft U-joint on the steering gear input shaft. 
Tighten nut to 42-56 Nm (31-41 lb-ft).

 WARNING: WHEN USING A CHISEL TO SPREAD A PINCH BOLT-TYPE PITMAN ARM BOSS FOR 
ASSEMBLY TO THE SHAFT, MAINTAIN A FIRM GRIP ON THE CHISEL AT ALL TIMES. 
FAILURE TO DO THIS CAN RESULT IN THE CHISEL FLYING LOOSE, WHICH COULD CAUSE AN 
INJURY. NEVER LEAVE THE CHISEL WEDGED IN THE PITMAN ARM BOSS. DO NOT USE A 
HAMMER ON THE PITMAN ARM TO INSTALL THE PITMAN ARM ON THE SECTOR SHAFT AS 
INTERNAL DAMAGE TO STEERING GEAR CAN RESULT. 

Place the pitman arm on the steering gear sector shaft, making sure the 
timing mark on the pitman arm aligns with the timing mark on the sector shaft. 
Use a chisel to help spread the pitman arm to slide on the shaft.

Install the bolt and nut. Tighten the nut to 299-406 Nm
 (220-300 lb-ft). 

Connect the power steering pressure and return lines to the gear. 

Fill the reservoir with Motorcraft MERCON® ATF 
XT-2-QDX or MERCON® equivalent. 

Start the engine, turn the steering wheel from left to right and check 
for fluid leaks.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Steering Gear 

 Disassembly 

 CAUTION: Do not clamp against the body of the housing as this can damage the 
housing and cause difficulties during the disassembly and assembly procedures. 
If mounting boss or flange is not accessible, fabricate and attach a mounting 
plate to the housing mounting bosses. 

Put the steering gear in a vise so that the input shaft is in a 
horizontal direction. Tighten the jaws of the vise on the mounting flange or 
the boss of the housing.

Put a pan under the steering gear. Unplug the hydraulic ports on the 
gear. Drain the fluid from the gear. 

Use a 3/4-inch or 11/16-inch twelve point socket to rotate the input 
shaft and valve worm assembly until the timing mark on the end of the sector 
shaft is aligned with the timing mark on the end of the housing trunnion.

[FIGURE: G68061A.gif]

Use a small screwdriver to remove the dirt and water seal from the 
housing trunnion. Remove any paint or corrosion from the exposed area of the 
sector shaft with a fine grade of emery cloth.

[FIGURE: G6807B.gif]

Tape the serrations and the bolt groove of the sector shaft with one 
layer of masking tape. The tape should not extend onto the diameter of the 
sector shaft bearing.

[FIGURE: G8405A.gif]

Remove the jam nut from the sector shaft adjusting screw.

[FIGURE: G8406A.gif]

 NOTE: The bolts that fasten the side cover to the housing are equipped with a 
ring or a washer under the head of the bolt. If you replace one or more bolts, 
you must replace them with bolts of the same design and length as the bolt 
being removed. Do not use a substitute. 

Be prepared for more fluid drainage and remove the six bolts that 
fasten the side cover to the housing.

[FIGURE: G6808B.gif]

Remove the side cover and sector shaft assembly as a unit from the 
gear. If necessary, lightly tap on the end of the shaft with a soft mallet. 
Remove and discard side cover gasket.

[FIGURE: G8407A.gif]

Remove and discard vent plug. Remove reverse threaded sector shaft 
adjusting screw by turning the screw clockwise through the side cover. Pull 
the sector shaft out of the side cover.

[FIGURE: G6809B.gif]

 CAUTION: Don't damage the bore or DU bushing when removing the seal. 

Clamp the side cover in a vise. Place a standard 5/8-inch or 11/16-inch 
3/8 drive socket in the center of the side cover. Pry seal out with a roll 
head pry bar, using the socket for support. Discard seal and remove the socket.

Inspect the sector shaft assembly for damaged adjusting screw threads. 
The staked retainer must be locked in place and have no cracks. The adjusting 
screw must rotate by hand with no perceptible end play (lash). 

If replacement is required, refer to Adjusting Screw and Retainer in 
the Disassembly and Assembly portion of this section. If no damage was noted, 
proceed to Step 13.

[FIGURE: G8408A.gif]

If equipped, remove relief valve cap, O-ring and two-piece relief valve 
from valve housing. Discard O-ring. Note the position of spring to relief valve.

[FIGURE: G8409A.gif]

Remove and discard dirt and water seal from input shaft.

[FIGURE: G8410A.gif]

Clean any paint or corrosion from exposed area of input shaft.

[FIGURE: G8411A.gif]

Remove the four Torx® head valve housing bolts.

[FIGURE: G8412A.gif]

 CAUTION: The set position of poppet seat and sleeve assemblies must not be 
disturbed if the poppets are not going to be replaced or pushed in during 
assembly. 

Be prepared for more fluid drainage and remove the rack piston 
subassembly. Place the assembly on a clean cloth.

[FIGURE: G8413A.gif]

 CAUTION: If the automatically set poppets are not to be removed for replacement 
or to be reset for automatic repositioning after the next installation, make 
sure the set position of the poppet adjuster seat and sleeve assembly is not 
disturbed. The steering gear should be identified to the vehicle it is removed 
from and noted that the poppet adjuster seat and sleeve assemblies are set for 
that particular vehicle only. 

 NOTE: If the Teflon® rack piston seal is on the end of the 
rack piston away from the rack piston bore opening, cut the seal. Remove the 
seal ring from the rack piston when it is exposed in the sector shaft cavity 
of the housing during the removal of the rack piston assembly, the input shaft 
valve, worm assembly and the valve piston. This prevents the seal from 
"hanging up" as it exits the housing sector shaft cavity. 

Remove and discard the seal rings from the valve housing.

[FIGURE: G68121A.gif]

If the clip-type ball return guide is used, bend down the tabs against 
the hex-head bolts. Remove the bolts and the clip. Discard the clip.

[FIGURE: G68131A.gif]

If a cap-type return guide is used, remove and discard the two special 
sealing screws that fasten the cap to the piston. Remove the cap and cap seal. 
Discard the seal.

[FIGURE: G68141A.gif]

 NOTE: Left ball return guide halves are copper-plated for identification and 
right guides are not plated. 

Make sure the rack piston is on a cloth so the steel balls that fall 
out won't roll very far. Remove ball return guide halves by carefully 
inserting a screwdriver between the rack piston and guides.

 CAUTION: The steel balls are a matched set. If any are lost, the complete set 
must be replaced by service balls. There are 32 factory balls installed in 
TAS65. 

Remove the steel balls from the rack piston by rotating the input 
shaft, valve, worm assembly until the balls fall out. Place the balls and 
return guides in a cup or other container and make sure all the balls have 
been removed.

[FIGURE: G8414A.gif]

Remove the input shaft, valve worm and valve housing subassembly from 
the rack piston.

[FIGURE: G6815B.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

3K748

Rack Piston

2

3B541

O-Ring

3

3B541

Teflon® Seal Ring

4

3647

Service Balls

5

3523

Ball Return Guide Halves

Cut and remove the Teflon® seal ring and the O-ring 
from the rack piston if not removed during Step 17.

[FIGURE: G8415A.gif]

 NOTE: TRW recommends the poppet adjuster seat and sleeve assemblies not be 
removed unless replacement of poppet components is required. 

Inspect poppet stems and seat and sleeve assemblies for damage. Push 
poppet stems; they should spring back. Push poppet seat; it should not move by 
hand. If components are bent or broken, or if poppet stems don't spring back 
or poppet seat moves by hand, go to Poppet Component Replacement in the 
Disassembly and Assembly portion of this section. Otherwise, proceed to Step 26.

Inspect valve housing/worm screw subassembly for heat damage or bearing 
roughness. If these conditions are present, or if there is excessive internal 
leakage, or if preload adjustment is required, refer to Worm and Valve Sleeve 
in the Disassembly and Assembly portion of this section. If not, proceed to 
Step 27.

[FIGURE: G8416A.gif]

Remove the retaining ring that is closest to the output end of the 
housing trunnion.

[FIGURE: G68231A.gif]

Remove and discard the dirt seal from the housing trunnion.

[FIGURE: G68241A.gif]

Insert a screwdriver from the trunnion end of the housing and carefully 
push the seal and the spacer washer out of the other end of the housing 
without damaging the sealing area or the spacer washer. Discard the seal.

[FIGURE: G68251A.gif]

Inspect roller bearing in the housing for brinelling or spalling. 
Inspect retaining ring for damage. If replacement of either part is required, 
refer to Housing Roller Bearing or Retaining Ring Replacement in the 
Disassembly and Assembly portion of this section. If not, proceed to Step 31. 

Inspect the following for damage: 

poppet fixed stop screw and washer 

poppet adjusting screw and sealing nut 

pressed-in grease fitting 

auto-bleed plug 

manual bleed screw 

auxiliary port plugs and O-rings 

If any are damaged, refer to Housing Ports, Plugs, Screws and Fittings 
in the Disassembly and Assembly portion of this section. If not, proceed to 
Cleaning and Inspection in this section. 

 Assembly 

 NOTE: Bolt torques are given for both dry threads and lubricated threads. TRW 
recommends lubricating threads with oil and using the lubricated torque 
specifications.

 NOTE: Replace all of the seals, the seal rings and the gaskets every time the 
gear is disassembled. 

Install a new dirt seal into the trunnion end of the sector shaft bore 
of the housing. Make sure the seal is installed against the bearing and the 
lip of the seal faces outward.

[FIGURE: G68321A.gif]

Install the second retaining ring. Make sure the ring is firmly seated 
in the groove in the housing.

[FIGURE: G68331A.gif]

 NOTE: A dab of grease applied to the small diameter of the washer will hold 
it in place during installation of the seal. 

Install washer into the side cover side of housing seal bore with small 
diameter piloted into retaining ring. 

[FIGURE: G8418A.gif]

Assemble new seal onto Bearing and Seal Tool J37071 or equivalent so 
the lip with the garter spring is toward the shoulder of the tool. 

Working from the side cover side of the housing, pilot the seal tool 
into the washer and bearing and press with a force of 445-3,560 N (100-800 
lbf) until the seal is seated against washer.

[FIGURE: G8419A.gif]

Liberally pack the area between dirt seal and pressure seal including 
roller bearing with High-Temperature 4x4 Front Axle and Wheel Bearing Grease 
E8TZ-19590-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C198-A.

[FIGURE: G8420A.gif]

Lightly oil new seal ring and assemble in valve housing mounting face 
groove. Oil new seal ring and assemble in valve housing mounting face groove.

[FIGURE: G8421A.gif]

Install a new backup O-ring and then a new Teflon® 
seal ring on rack piston. Do not over-stretch these rings as you install them. 
Do not allow the Teflon® seal ring to be twisted.

[FIGURE: G8422A.gif]

Apply clean oil to housing cylinder bore. Place the rack piston in the 
housing piston bore with ball return guide holes up.

[FIGURE: G8423A.gif]

Insert the worm screw into the rack piston close to maximum depth, 
without the valve housing making contact with the poppet stem. Insert two 
7/16-14 Ready Bolts through valve housing bolt holes and tighten into housing 
to support the worm screw. Line up rack piston ball guide holes with the worm 
ball track grooves by rotating the input shaft.

[FIGURE: G8424B.gif]

 WARNING: DO NOT SEAT GUIDES WITH A HAMMER. DAMAGE TO GUIDES CAN RESULT IN 
SUBSEQUENT LOCKUP OR LOSS OF STEERING. 

 CAUT

================================================================================

1997 Cargo

Section 11-02A: Steering Gear, Power, Ross TAS65

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Adjusting Screw and Retainer 

 Disassembly 

 NOTE: A service sector shaft will come assembled with the adjusting screw and 
retainer. 

Inspect the sector shaft bearing and sealing areas and sector teeth 
contact surfaces for brinelling, spalling or cracks. Run your fingernail edge 
across these areas to detect steps. Remove masking tape from the shaft and 
inspect for twisted or otherwise damaged serrations. If any of these 
conditions exist, replace the sector shaft.

[FIGURE: G68291A.gif]

If damage was not found in Step 1, place the sector shaft firmly in a 
soft-jawed vise and unstake the retainer. Turn the retainer out of the sector 
shaft pocket. 

If necessary, remove the adjusting screw. If adjusting screw is 
replaced, retainer must also be replaced.

[FIGURE: G8440A.gif]

 Assembly 

If the adjusting screw has been removed, coat the expanded end of the 
new adjusting screw with a suitable grade of wheel bearing grease and insert 
into recess in end of sector shaft.

[FIGURE: G8441A.gif]

 WARNING: STAKE THE RETAINER SECURELY INTO THE SECTOR SHAFT SLOTS. IF THE 
RETAINER IS BROKEN OR CRACKED DURING THE STAKING, REPLACE IT. FAILURE TO DO SO 
COULD RESULT IN THE LOSS OF MANUAL AND POWER STEERING CONTROL. 

Thread a new sector shaft screw retainer into the sector shaft. Tighten 
and then stake the retainer in the two slots provided. The adjusting screw 
should rotate freely by hand, with very little end play, 0-0.05 mm 
(0.000-0.002 inch).

[FIGURE: G8442A.gif]

1997 Cargo

Section 11-02A: Steering Gear, Power, Ross TAS65

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Worm and Valve Sleeve

 Disassembly 

With worm vertical, place the valve housing, input shaft, valve, worm 
assembly in a vise.

[FIGURE: G8450A.gif]

Unstake the valve housing where it was upset into the adjuster lock nut 
slot. Also unstake adjuster nut from adjuster.

[FIGURE: G8451A.gif]

Using Adjuster Lock Nut Tool J37464, turn bearing adjuster lock nut out 
of the valve housing.

[FIGURE: G8452A.gif]

Using Adjuster Tool J37070 or equivalent turn bearing adjuster out of 
the valve housing.

[FIGURE: G8453A.gif]

Remove and discard seal ring and O-ring from bearing adjuster.

[FIGURE: G8454A.gif]

Remove the input shaft, valve, worm assembly from the valve housing.

[FIGURE: G8455A.gif]

Remove thin thrust washer and thrust bearing from input shaft.

[FIGURE: G8456A.gif]

Remove thick thrust washer and thrust bearing from valve housing. For 
alternate construction TAS65 gears, remove spacer sleeve, thin washer, thrust 
bearing and thick washer.

[FIGURE: G8457A.gif]

 CAUTION: Exercise special care when removing seal to prevent damaging the valve 
housing seal bore. 

Remove and discard seal rings and O-rings from valve housing.

[FIGURE: G8459A.gif]

Turn over valve housing and remove retaining ring.

[FIGURE: G8460A.gif]

 NOTE: The valve housing also utilizes a ball plug for manufacturing purposes 
that must not be removed. 

Tap input shaft seal out of valve housing. Discard seal.

[FIGURE: G8461A.gif]

 Assembly 

 CAUTION: Input shaft, valve, worm assembly must not be disassembled further. The 
components are a select fit at assembly and are available only as part of this 
subassembly. If disassembled further, the subassembly must be replaced. 

Inspect the sealing areas of input shaft and valve for nicks and run 
your fingernail edge across the sealing surfaces to detect steps. Inspect for 
discoloration from excess heat. Inspect input shaft ball track grooves for 
brinelling or spalling. If any of these conditions exist, you must replace the 
input shaft, valve, worm assembly, valve housing and balls. Also replace rack 
piston if brinelling or spalling is found.

[FIGURE: G68281A.gif]

Inspect the thrust bearing rollers for any deterioration. Inspect 
thrust washers for brinelling, spalling, or cracks. Replace any part with 
these conditions. 

Alternate construction: if spacer sleeve is damaged, replace the input 
shaft, valve, worm subassembly and use thick washer and roller bearing only 
during reassembly.

[FIGURE: G8462A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not clamp against threaded port hole or relief valve hole sealing 
faces when placing valve housing in vise. 

Place valve housing firmly in a vise so the input shaft, valve, worm 
assembly can be assembled vertically with worm end up.

[FIGURE: G8463A.gif]

Oil and assemble a new O-ring into its counterbore in valve housing.

[FIGURE: G8464A.gif]

Lightly oil and assemble new O-ring and new seal ring into the large 
diameter seal ring groove in valve housing, bending and working them in and 
smoothing them out as necessary.

[FIGURE: G8465A.gif]

 CAUTION: If you are replacing the input shaft, valve, worm assembly, discard 
spacer sleeve and thin washer. 

Install roller thrust bearing and then the thick washer onto input 
shaft end of input shaft, valve, worm subassembly, seating them against the 
input shaft thrust face.

[FIGURE: G8466A.gif]

Alternate construction: assemble spacer sleeve onto input shaft with 
radiused side toward valve. Make sure sleeve is square. Assemble thin washer, 
thrust bearing and thick washer onto input shaft behind spacer sleeve.

[FIGURE: G8467A.gif]

Lightly oil and assemble new seal ring onto input shaft and against the 
thick thrust washer to hold the bearing components in place.

[FIGURE: G8468A.gif]

Dip the input end of the input shaft, valve, worm assembly into oil up 
to the worm lead. Assemble the input shaft end of the assembly into the valve 
housing until it is firmly seated.

[FIGURE: G8469A.gif]

Apply oil and assemble the other thrust bearing and then the thin 
thrust washer over the ball groove end of worm, and seat them against the 
shoulder of input shaft, valve, worm assembly.

[FIGURE: G8470A.gif]

 NOTE: Make sure the valve housing, adjuster lock nut and bearing adjuster 
threads are clean and free of any staking burrs that would impede the lock nut 
from turning freely on adjuster or the adjuster turning freely in valve 
housing. 

Lightly oil a new O-ring and assemble into the seal groove in bearing 
adjuster. Oil and work a new seal ring into the same groove and smooth it out.

[FIGURE: G8471A.gif]

Lightly oil and assemble bearing adjuster over worm and into valve 
housing. Tighten adjuster to 18 Nm (13 lb-ft) indicated 
torque using a torque wrench inserted in Adjuster Tool J37070. This will seat 
the components. Back off adjuster 1/4 to 1/2 turn.

[FIGURE: G8472A.gif]

Reverse assembly in vise so the worm end is down. With an inch-pound 
torque wrench on the input shaft, note torque required to rotate input shaft 
360 degrees in each direction. Tighten the bearing adjuster to increase the 
maximum torque at the input shaft 0.5-1.0 Nm (5-9 lb-in) over 
that which was previously noted.

[FIGURE: G8473A.gif]

 NOTE: The bearing adjuster, lock nut and valve housing flange should be 
flush. If not, the seal ring or O-ring may be out of position, which will 
result in axial lash.

Again reverse assembly in vise. Lightly oil and assemble new lock nut 
onto bearing adjuster with radius (slightly rounded) side down. Tighten lock 
nut while holding bearing adjuster in position established in Step 13 with 
Adjuster Tool J37070 or equivalent. When using a torque wrench in Adjuster 
Lock Nut Tool J37464 or equivalent, the torque wrench reading should be 152 Nm
 (112 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: G8474A.gif]

Recheck input shaft torque. It should match torque measured in Step 13. 
Repeat Steps 13 and 14 if necessary.

[FIGURE: G8475A.gif]

Stake valve housing into the clockwise-most corner of two opposing 
slots in lock nut. Stake the lock nut into the adjuster in two places (180 
degrees apart) at threaded area. Choose areas that have not been previously 
staked. 

After staking, torque required to rotate input shaft must be 0.5-1.0 Nm
 (5-9 lb-in) greater than the torque noted in Step 13. 
Torque value must not exceed 2.5 Nm (22 lb-in). Unstake and 
readjust if necessary.

[FIGURE: G8476A.gif]

Reposition worm screw/valve housing subassembly in soft-jawed vise, 
clamping tightly against valve housing, so that the worm screw is pointing 
sideways.

Apply clean grease to the outside and inside diameters (fill cavity 
between the lips) of the new input shaft seal and assemble it, garter spring 
side first over the input shaft. Align seal in the valve housing seal bore. 

 CAUTION: The input shaft seal must be square in the seal bore and installed to 
the correct depth. 

Assemble Input Seal Installer Tool J37073 or equivalent, small diameter 
end first, over the input shaft and against the seal. Tap the seal installer 
tool until the tool shoulder is squarely against the valve housing. This will 
correctly position the seal in the housing bore just beyond the retaining ring 
groove.

[FIGURE: G8477A.gif]

Remove any seal material that may have sheared off and is in seal bore 
and retaining ring groove.

Insert new retaining ring into its groove in valve housing.

[FIGURE: G8478A.gif]

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Housing Roller Bearing or Retaining Ring Replacement 

 Disassembly 

 CAUTION: The bearing must be pressed out from the side cover side to protect 
seal counterbore. Be sure to use a bearing removal tool that will clear the 
retaining ring. 

If roller bearing in housing needs to be replaced, place the bearing 
removal end of the Bearing and Seal Tool J37071 or equivalent against the side 
cover end of the bearing and press it out of trunnion end of the bearing bore. 
Discard bearing.

[FIGURE: G8479A.gif]

If the retaining ring that is still in the housing bearing bore needs 
to be replaced, remove it through the trunnion end of the bearing bore to 
protect the pressure seal bore area from being damaged.

[FIGURE: G8480A.gif]

 Assembly 

Insert retaining ring, if it was removed, into the housing bore from 
the trunnion end (to protect sealing area). Make sure it is seated in the 
retaining ring groove closest to side cover end of the bearing bore. Lubricate 
the bearing bore.

[FIGURE: G8481A.gif]

 CAUTION: Use the bearing installation end of the tool. If the bearing removal 
end of the bearing and seal tool is used to press in bearing, the cage on the 
new bearing may be damaged. 

Using Bearing and Seal Tool J37071 or equivalent press the roller 
bearing into the housing from the trunnion end of bearing bore until it is 
seated against the retaining ring. Be sure the housing is square with the 
press base and the bearing is not cocked.

[FIGURE: G8482A.gif]

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Housing Ports, Plugs, Screws and Fittings 

 Disassembly and Assembly 

If damaged, remove and replace the poppet fixed stop screw and washer. 
Tighten to 54 Nm (40 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: G8483A.gif]

If damaged, remove poppet adjusting screw and sealing nut without 
allowing the nut to change its position on the screw. 

Assemble the new nut onto the new adjusting screw, matching its 
position to the nut and screw removed. Tighten sealing nut to 47 Nm
 (35 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: G8484A.gif]

If damaged, remove and replace automatic bleed screw. Tighten to 54 Nm
 (40 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: G8485A.gif]

If damaged, remove and replace manual bleed screw. Tighten to 3.4 Nm
 (30 lb-in). 

If damaged, remove and replace permanent auxiliary port plugs and 
O-rings. Assemble new O-rings on port plugs and tighten to their respective 
ports in the housing or valve housing to 41 Nm (30 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: G8486A.gif]

If damaged, remove grease fitting from housing. If the fitting is 
broken off, use suitable extractor to remove. 

To replace, hold a piece of tubing that will clear the head of fitting 
over a new fitting and tap fitting into the housing.

[FIGURE: G8487A.gif]

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Final Adjustment 

 NOTE: The worm preload adjustment was done when the input shaft, valve, worm 
assembly was installed into the valve housing. 

 CAUTION: Do not rotate the input shaft more than one and one-half revolutions 
from the center position until the steering gear is installed, during the 
poppet setting procedure. Doing so could make the automatic poppets 
inoperative, which would require disassembly of the steering gear to 
reposition poppet seat and sleeve assemblies. 

 NOTE: Initial poppet contact will occur at less than one input shaft rotation 
in one direction from the steering gear center position if new or reset poppet 
adjuster seat and sleeve assemblies are installed in the unit. 

Use a 3/4-inch or 11/16-inch twelve point socket to rotate the input 
shaft, valve, worm assembly until the timing mark on the end of the sector 
shaft is aligned with the timing mark on the end of the housing trunnion.

[FIGURE: G68061A.gif]

 NOTE: This procedure will properly mesh and seat the rack piston and the 
sector shaft teeth for final adjustments. 

Turn the sector shaft adjusting screw clockwise to provide 5.0-5.5 Nm
 (45-50 lb-in) of torque required to rotate the input shaft 
and valve worm assembly through 180 degrees each side of center.

[FIGURE: G8437A.gif]

Turn the sector shaft adjusting screw counterclockwise one-half turn 
and note the maximum torque required to rotate the input shaft, valve, worm 
assembly through 180 degrees each side of center.

[FIGURE: G8438A.gif]

Adjust the sector shaft adjusting screw clockwise to increase the 
maximum torque noted in Step 3 by 0.8 Nm (7 lb-in). Tighten 
jam nut firmly against side cover while holding the adjusting screw in place. 

Tighten the jam nut to 58 Nm (43 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: G8439A.gif]

Check the rotating torque of the input shaft, valve, worm assembly 
again. Readjust if the torque exceeds 4.5 Nm (40 lb-in). 

Plug all ports until the gear is installed in the vehicle.

[FIGURE: G68631A.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Steering Gear

 WARNING: SINCE SOLVENTS ARE FLAMMABLE, BE EXTREMELY CAREFUL WHEN USING ANY 
SOLVENT. EVEN A SMALL EXPLOSION OR FIRE COULD CAUSE INJURY OR DEATH. 

 WARNING: WEAR SAFE EYE PROTECTION AND BE SURE TO COMPLY WITH OSHA OR OTHER 
MAXIMUM AIR PRESSURE REQUIREMENTS. 

Make sure that all seal surfaces and seal cavities are free from nicks 
and corrosion. If any part is nicked or corroded where sealing occurs, replace 
the parts to make sure they seal properly. 

Wash all parts in a clean petroleum-base solvent. Air blow the parts 
until dry.

Inspect the teeth of the rack piston for cracks and wear. If a step is 
detected by running a fingernail horizontally across the tooth surface, the 
rack piston, the sector shaft and the set of 32 service balls must be replaced.

[FIGURE: G68261A.gif]

Inspect the internal ball track grooves of the rack piston for 
brinelling (dents) or spalling (flaking). If either condition exists, replace 
the rack piston, input shaft, worm valve assembly and the set of balls as an 
assembly.

[FIGURE: G68271A.gif]

Inspect the input shaft, worm valve assembly, ball track grooves, 
thrust bearing, and the ball bearing areas for brinelling (dents) or spalling 
(flaking). Inspect the sealing areas of the input shaft and valve for nicks. 
Run a fingernail edge across the sealing surfaces to detect steps. Inspect for 
discoloration from excess heat. If any of these conditions exist, replace the 
input shaft, valve housing, valve worm assembly and the set of balls as an 
assembly. Also replace rack piston if brinelling or spalling is found.

[FIGURE: G68281A.gif]

 NOTE: In performing the internal leakage test after assembling the gear, make 
sure internal leakage over 3.8 lpm (1.0 gpm) is not caused by the improper 
installation of seals on the wormshaft, rack piston and valve assembly. 

Replace the housing only if internal leakage is greater than 3.8 lpm 
(1.0 gpm). Make sure a seal is not causing the leak. The bore of the housing 
may show signs of scoring but these signs may indicate normal wear.

Inspect the face of the housing for nicks that would prevent proper 
sealing. Replace the housing if the nicks cannot be easily removed with a 
fine-tooth flat file without damage to the housing. 

Inspect side cover DU bushing for damage. Also check side cover bushing 
to sector shaft clearance. If damage exists, or if clearance exceeds 0.20 mm 
(0.008 inch), replace side cover/bushing assembly. 

[FIGURE: G8417A.gif]

 NOTE: A service sector shaft assembly will have the adjusting screw and the 
retainer installed. The screw and the retainer can be serviced separately. 

Remove all masking tape from the sector shaft. Inspect the bearing, 
sealing and tooth contact surfaces on the sector shaft for brinelling, 
spalling or cracks. Run the edge of a fingernail across these areas to detect 
steps. Inspect for cracks. Look for twisted or damaged serrations. Replace the 
sector shaft if any of these conditions exist.

[FIGURE: G68291A.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Steering Gear Housing

Inspect the steering gear housing for cracks and stripped threads and 
the mating surfaces for burrs. Inspect the piston bore for scoring or wear. If 
necessary, replace the steering gear housing. Surface burnishing is acceptable 
if no significant step can be felt.

ADJUSTMENTS

Sector Shaft Adjustment 

Refer to the Power Steering Gear illustration in the Removal and 
Installation portion of this section. 

 CAUTION: This adjustment must be performed with the sector shaft on its center 
of travel. 

 CAUTION: The input shaft must not be rotated more than one and one-half 
revolutions when the drag link is disconnected from the steering gear to avoid 
possible misadjustment of the automatic poppet system. 

 NOTE: If the adjusting screw jam nut screw is accessible, this adjustment can 
be completed on the vehicle. Otherwise, the steering gear must be removed from 
the vehicle. 

 NOTE: If this adjustment is being performed with the steering gear on the 
vehicle, remove the drag link from the pitman arm. 

Put the sector shaft in the center of travel. Rotate the input shaft 
until the timing marks across the end of the sector shaft are perpendicular to 
the input shaft and the valve worm is in line with the timing mark on the end 
of the housing trunnion.

[FIGURE: G67711A.gif]

With the steering gear in the center position, grasp the pitman arm and 
gently try to move the arm back and forth in the direction of travel. 
Fingertip force is adequate to detect the lash of a loose sector shaft. There 
must be no movement of the input shaft or the sector shaft.

[FIGURE: G6772B.gif]

Loosen the jam nut on the sector shaft adjusting screw. If no lash is 
detected, turn the adjusting screw counterclockwise until lash is detected at 
the output shaft.

 CAUTION: Overadjustment of the shaft adjusting screw in the clockwise direction 
could result in a no-recovery, oversteering or darting condition of the 
vehicle. 

To adjust, slowly turn the adjusting screw clockwise until no lash is 
felt at the pitman arm. Use no more than 14 Nm (10 lb-ft) of 
torque. From the no-lash position, turn the screw clockwise an additional 
1/8-3/16 turn. Hold the adjusting screw in place and tighten the jam nut to 58 Nm
 (43 lb-ft).

Turn the input shaft one-quarter turn each side of center and recheck 
the pitman arm for lash. No lash should be felt. If lash exists, repeat Steps 
1-4. 

 CAUTION: Maintain grease in the sector shaft bearing through the grease fitting 
in the housing using only a hand-operated grease gun. Add grease until it 
begins to extrude past the dirt and water seal. Do not use a power grease gun 
because it will supply grease too fast. This could adversely affect the 
high-pressure seal and contaminate the hydraulic fluid. 

If the adjustment was done with the steering gear on the vehicle, 
install the drag link to the pitman arm. If the steering gear was removed from 
the vehicle, install the gear in the vehicle.

[FIGURE: G67731A.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Steering Pump

The ZF power steering pump has been specially designed to supply 
pressurized oil to power steering units. 

The ZF power steering pump is directly driven by the engine. As the 
driven shaft rotates the rotor, the slipper vanes inside on the pump also 
move. The centrifugal force and pressurized oil forces the slipper vanes 
against the track of the cam ring. The oil passes from the two pressure 
chambers to the area between the rear cover and faceplate, pressing this plate 
against the cam ring at operating pressure. The oil then passes through a 
flow-limiting valve to the pressure line.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Steering Pump, Power, Direct Drive

 Removal 

Tilt open cab and latch. 

Drain cooling system. 

Remove turbocharger air inlet and outlet pipes. 

Position drain pan under power steering pump. 

Loosen clamp and disconnect supply hose from power steering pump. 

Disconnect pressure hose from power steering pump. 

Disconnect water pump-to-air compressor water hose and pull out of the 
way. 

Remove two bolts and power steering pump. 

Remove gasket and clean gasket surfaces. 

 Installation 

Position new gasket on power steering pump. Use a small amount of 
grease to hold in place. 

Position power steering pump and start two bolts. 

Tighten two pump retaining bolts and nuts to 30-40 Nm 
(22-30 lb-ft). 

Connect water pump-to-air compressor water hose. 

Connect pressure hose to power steering pump. 

Connect supply hose to power steering pump and tighten clamp. 

Install turbocharger air inlet and outlet pipes. 

Fill cooling system. 

Fill power steering reservoir to proper level with Motorcraft MERCON®
 ATF XT-2-QDX or MERCON® equivalent. 
Refer to Section 11-00 .

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Steering Linkage

The steering linkage on Cargo consists of right- and left-hand spindle 
assemblies attached to an I-beam front axle. Separate steering and spindle 
arms attach to the spindles. A tie rod, adjustable for toe-in, is connected 
between the left- and right-hand spindle arms. The drag link is connected 
between the steering arm and the pitman arm on the steering gear.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Drag Link 

 Removal 

Replace the drag link if the ball stud at the pitman arm or the 
steering arm is excessively loose or if the drag link is damaged.

Remove cotter pins and nuts from ball studs. 

Remove ball studs from arms. 

 Installation 

 NOTE: One end of drag link is identified as AXLE and is installed in axle 
steering arm.

Position drag link ball studs in arms and install nuts.

Tighten at both ends to 149-203 Nm (110-150 lb-ft). If 
required, advance the nut to the next castellation to install new cotter pin.

================================================================================

Section 11-03: Steering Linkage

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Grease Seals

 Removal 

Remove sliding seal from socket.

 NOTE: Do not use liquid solvents of any type to clean these parts. 

Thoroughly wipe away all grease and foreign material from around ball 
stud and throat of socket.

 Installation 

Install a new sliding seal over ball stud.

Assemble ball stud into steering arm or pitman arm and tighten nut. 

Grease ball joint with Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B until excess grease is 
pushed out from under the seal.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Tie Rod Ends

 Removal 

If the tie rod end ball stud is excessively loose, replace the tie rod 
end as follows. 

Remove cotter pin and nut from tie rod end ball stud. 

Remove ball stud from spindle arm. 

Loosen clamp bolt and turn tie rod end out of rod. Count number of 
turns needed to remove tie rod end. 

[FIGURE: G9004A.gif]

 Installation 

Lubricate threads of a new tie rod end, and turn it into rod to about 
same distance old rod end was installed. This will provide an approximate 
toe-in setting. 

Install ball stud in spindle arm. Tighten nut to 102-142 Nm
 (75-105 lb-ft) on 9K axle or to 149-203 Nm
 (110-150 lb-ft) on 12K-13K axles.

If necessary, advance nut to the next castellation to install a new 
cotter pin. Install new cotter pin.

Check toe-in and adjust, if necessary. Refer to Section 04-00 . Tighten 
rod end clamps to 68-95 Nm (50-70 lb-ft) after adjusting 
toe-in.

Tie rod clamps should be positioned as shown in the above illustration.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Tie Rod, Front Wheel Spindle

 Removal 

Replace the wheel spindle tie rod if the end threads are stripped or if 
the rod is bent. Do not attempt to straighten a bent rod. 

Loosen both wheel spindle tie rod end clamps. 

Unthread wheel spindle tie rod until rod drops off both ends. Count 
number of turns needed to remove rod ends. The right rod end has a right-hand 
thread; the left-hand rod end has a left-hand thread. 

 Installation 

Lubricate threads on wheel spindle tie rod and turn a tie rod end into 
tube about one thread. 

Start other end and continue to turn rod until rod ends have entered 
rod to about same distance old rod was installed. This will provide an 
approximate toe-in setting. 

The tie rod ends should be parallel with each other and in the same 
plane within five degrees. 

Check toe-in and adjust, if necessary. Be sure to tighten connecting 
rod end clamps after adjusting toe-in. Refer to Section 04-00 .

 NOTE: Replace the pitman arm if it is bent, if the ball stud hole is

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Spindle/Steering Arm 

 Removal 

Replace the spindle or steering arm if it is bent or damaged. Do not 
attempt to straighten a bent spindle or steering arm. 

Remove spindle tie rod end ball stud or drag link ball stud from 
spindle or steering arm. 

Remove cotter pin and attaching nut from arm. Remove arm from spindle. 
Drive arm out of spindle, if necessary. 

 Installation 

 NOTE: Unique arms are used for different front axles and wheelbases. Refer to 
the Master Parts Catalog for part number information.

Install a new spindle/steering arm in spindle.

 NOTE: The spindle hole is slotted to align arm with a key.

Insert key in slot from nut side of spindle. Be sure key is flush with 
slot face of spindle. 

Install spindle/steering arm attaching nut. On 9K axle, tighten spindle 
arm attaching nut to 299-406 Nm (220-300 lb-ft) and tighten 
steering arm attaching nut to 489-650 Nm (360-480 lb-ft). On 
12K-13K axles, tighten spindle arm attaching nut to 489-650 Nm
 (360-480 lb-ft) and tighten steering arm attaching nut to 733-989 Nm
 (540-730 lb-ft).

If necessary, advance nut to next castellation to install new cotter 
pin. Install new cotter pin.

Install tie rod end ball stud or drag link ball stud in arm. Install 
ball stud nut. Tighten tie rod attaching nut to 102-142 Nm 
(75-105 lb-ft) on 9K axle or to 149-203 Nm (110-150 lb-ft) on 
12K-13K axles. Tighten drag link attaching nut to 149-203 Nm 
(110-150 lb-ft).

If necessary, advance nut to next castellation to install new cotter 
pin. Install new cotter pin.

Check toe-in and adjust, if necessary. Refer to Section 04-00 .

Section 11-04: Steering Column

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Steering Column

The steering wheel is splined to the steering shaft and retained by a 
self-locking nut. The steering shaft passes through the steering column tube 
(secured to the dash panel) and is supported in the tube by two ball bearings. 
The lower end of the shaft passes through a shroud which is riveted to the cab 
floor. A plastic dust seal is sandwiched between the shroud and the cab floor. 

The male splined steering shaft is allowed to slide into a female 
splined universal slip-yoke attached to the steering gear input shaft. The 
shaft is allowed to slide to compensate for cab articulation and tilting of 
vehicle cab.

 Slip Yoke and Steering Shaft 

[FIGURE: G9403A.gif]

Steering Column 

 Removal 

Make sure front wheels are in straight-ahead position. Remove battery 
cover and disconnect battery negative cable. 

Tilt vehicle cab. Remove pinch bolt and nut securing steering shaft 
universal joint to steering gear input shaft and disconnect joint. Lower 
vehicle cab. 

Remove steering wheel. 

Remove screws securing two-piece steering column shroud. Remove shroud.

[FIGURE: G50061B.gif]

Make sure steering column lock is in unlocked position. 

Disconnect direction indicator, windshield wiper, and ignition switch 
multi-plugs.

Screw and Washer

Drill two shear-head bolts from switch assemblies and separate 
assemblies from steering column tube. 

Remove bolts and washers securing steering column bracket to pedal box. 
Carefully lift steering shaft assembly until universal joint is clear of lower 
shroud. Remove assembly from vehicle.

[FIGURE: G5008C.gif]

 Installation 

 NOTE: Vehicles fitted with shear bolts must have shear bolts fitted in lower 
two positions. 

Position steering shaft assembly in vehicle and carefully guide 
universal joint assembly through lower shroud. Position steering column 
bracket against pedal box. Secure with bolts and washers. Tighten securely.

Fit two halves of switch casting to steering column tube, and install 
two new shear-head bolts. Tighten bolts until heads shear. Reconnect direction

input shaft. Care should be taken to make sure that bolt aligns with whistle 
notch in gear input shaft. Install bolt nut and flatwashers. Tighten to 42-57 Nm
 (31-42 lb-ft).

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Steering Column

 Disassembly 

Remove tube-to-steering column support bracket nut and bolt. Separate 
the assembly. 

Remove circlip from upper end of sliding universal joint assembly. 
Remove universal joint assembly from steering shaft. Separate the two halves 
of the bushing and remove O-ring and rubber boot. 

 CAUTION: The spring loading on the assembly is between 983-1370 N (221-308 lbf). 

Place the support shaft and column tube assembly in a vise with pads on 
vise jaws to prevent damage. Push column tube toward the lower end of shaft to 
release load on the upper circlip. Remove circlip without releasing the 
tolerance ring from upper bearing.

Remove steering shaft from lower end of column tube. The lock ring will 
help to remove the lower bearing assembly. 

Remove upper bearing assembly using a long, soft drift to push the 
bearing from the column tube. Take care not to damage the bearing seals. 

Remove the lower circlip washer, spring, tolerance ring, and bearing 
assembly, if they are still on the shaft. 

Inspect shaft splines for damage or wear, replace if necessary. 
Separate bearing assemblies. Do not intermix parts. Inspect bearings for wear. 
Replace as necessary if pitting or galling is present. Check spring for wear 
or damage.

 Assembly 

Clean bearing assemblies in approved solvent, taking care not to 
intermix bearing components. Lubricate bearings with Motorcraft Premium 
Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESA-M1C75-B.

Install lower bearing assembly tolerance ring, spring, and washer. 
Install lower circlip in groove on shaft. 

Slide the column tube over the top of the shaft until lower bearing is 
seated in belled end of the column tube. 

Place shaft in vise and install upper bearing, tolerance ring, washer 
and circlip over the upper end of the shaft. 

Push column tube downward to allow installation of upper bearing, 
tolerance ring, washer and circlip. 

Install rubber boot. 

Lubricate shaft splines with Motorcraft Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C 
or -K or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B. Install O-ring and 
lower circlip. 

Install shaft into universal joint making sure the arrows on shaft and 
joint are in alignment. 

Lubricate O-ring and shaft with grease. Install the two halves of split 
bushing around O-ring and slide the bushing into the end of the sliding joint. 

 NOTE: Take care not to over lubricate or a hydraulic lock could develop, 
preventing the sliding joint from working properly. 

Reinstall grease fitting if removed. Compress the sliding joint by hand 
and apply two or three strokes of grease.

 NOTE: Before tightening to specified torque, check that the mounting bracket 
pivots on column tube bracket.

Install steering column support bracket over the steering column tube 
bracket. Install dished washers to each shouldered bolt. Slide the bolts 
through the column tube bracket into the support bracket. Install nuts (or 
special shear nuts) for vehicles with steering column lock. Tighten to 21-32 Nm
 (15-24 lb-ft). Make sure bolts locate correctly in column 
tube bracket.

Section 11-05: Steering Column Switches

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Turn Signal Switch

The turn signal switch is mounted on a plate attached to the steering 
column main housing. The mounting plate and switch are concealed under the 
steering wheel and behind the steering column shroud. The switch is operated 
by a lever that extends through a protective boot on the left side of the 
steering column.

The switch is normally in a centered or OFF position. Moving the lever 
upward closes the switch contacts that complete the circuit to the right turn 
signal lamps. Downward movement of the switch completes the left turn signal 
lamp circuit. When the switch lever is moved upward or downward through the 
spring-loaded detent, it remains in this position until it is moved back to 
the center position by hand, or automatically by the switch-cancelling cam.

The switch-cancelling cam is mounted on the steering wheel shaft and 
will rotate with the shaft whenever the steering wheel is turned. When the 
steering wheel is returned from a left- or right-hand turn, the cam eccentric 
pushes the spring-loaded detent over center and returns the switch to the OFF 
position.

 Steering Column Switches 

[FIGURE: K9068D.gif]

The electrical contact connected to the lever receives battery feed 
through a single wire from the turn signal flasher. When the lever is moved up 
or down, the feed contact completes the circuit to the left- or right-hand 
turn signal lamps.

================================================================================
PAGE 3638
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 11-05: Steering Column Switches

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Ignition Switch

The ignition lock cylinder and switch are a single component. When the 
lock cylinder ignition key is turned to different positions, it is aligning 
electrical contacts in the ignition switch. Electrical contacts are made in 
the ACC (accessory), RUN and START positions. In the OFF position, the switch 
is open and the key can be removed.

The ignition switch and lock cylinder assembly is mounted below and 
behind the steering column switch mounting plate where it is concealed by the 
steering column shroud. An opening in the right side of the shroud provides 
key access to the lock cylinder.

For security purposes, the ignition lock cylinder is attached to the 
switch plates with shear bolts. During vehicle assembly these bolts are 
installed to a specific torque where the bolt heads break off. The bolt shank 
must be drilled out in order to remove the ignition lock cylinder and switch.

================================================================================
PAGE 3639
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 11-05: Steering Column Switches

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Wiper Control Switch

The windshield wiper switch is mounted on a plate attached to the 
steering column main housing. The mounting plate and switch are concealed 
under the steering wheel and behind the steering column shroud. The switch is 
operated by a lever that extends through a protective boot on the right side 
of the steering column. The switch provides four positions — 
OFF, LOW, HIGH and INTERVAL. The windshield wipers operate at low speed when 
the lever is moved upward from the OFF position one detent. Moving the lever 
upward to the second detent is the high speed position. If the vehicle is 
equipped with interval wipers, moving the lever downward from the OFF position 
provides this function.

[FIGURE: K9221C.gif]

Battery feed to the wiper switch is provided by a single wire from the 
fuse panel. When the lever is moved to the LOW or HIGH position, electrical 
contacts within the switch align directly and complete the feed circuit 
directly to the wiper motor. In the interval wipe position, the battery feed 
circuit is completed to the wiper timer relay, which completes the motor 
circuit at 5-second intervals.

================================================================================
PAGE 3640
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 11-05: Steering Column Switches

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Windshield Washer Switch

The windshield washer switch is located on the end of the wiper switch 
lever. When the button is pressed, a set of electrical contacts is closed and 
completes the battery feed circuit to the washer pump motor. When it is 
released, spring pressure returns the washer button to the OFF position and 
opens the electrical contacts.

[FIGURE: K22924A.gif]

================================================================================
PAGE 3641
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 11-05: Steering Column Switches

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

High Beam/Flash-to-Pass Switch

The high beam headlamp switch is contained in the turn signal switch 
and is operated by the turn signal switch lever. If the headlamps are on and 
the lever is pulled toward the steering wheel through the switch detent, the 
high beam headlamps come on and remain on. The high beams are turned off by 
pulling the lever toward the steering column. If the headlamps are on or off, 
it is possible to use the flash-to-pass function in the switch. Pulling the 
turn signal lever toward the steering wheel to the switch detent, but not 
through it, will turn on the high beam headlamps. When the lever is released, 
the switch will return to the OFF position.

[FIGURE: K22925A.gif]

The switch receives battery feed from two sources. One is a constant 
feed and supplies the flash-to-pass contacts. The other feed is supplied from 
the headlamp switch. In the headlamp position, the battery feed circuit to the 
high beam switch is completed to either the high or low beams. Moving the turn 
signal switch handle switches the battery feed contacts between the high and 
low beam circuits.

================================================================================
PAGE 3642
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 11-05: Steering Column Switches

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Horn Switch

The horn switch is located on the end of the turn signal lever. When 
the button is pressed, a set of electrical contacts is closed and the battery 
feed circuit to the horn is completed. When released, spring pressure returns 
the horn button to the OFF position and opens the electrical contacts.

[FIGURE: K22927A.gif]

ADJUSTMENTS

High Beam/Flash-to-Pass Switch

The headlamp high beam switch, mounted on the steering column, can 
cause an erratic or continual ON condition for the headlamps. 

The following procedure is used to adjust the high beam 
switch/flash-to-pass in order to prevent an occasional short circuit condition 
between the contact points.

Disconnect battery negative cables. 

Push back rubber boot on turn signal lever. 

Locate high beam switch contact points on the lower forward section. 

 CAUTION: Do not overbend or the flash-to-pass will become inoperative. 

Insert a screwdriver between the contact points and pry the front point 
slightly outward and away from the other. 

[FIGURE: K10146C.gif]

Push rubber boot on turn signal lever back to steering column. 

Connect battery negative cables and check high beam 
switch/flash-to-pass function.

BASIC PRINCIPLES

Heat Transfer

If two substances of different temperature are placed near each other, 
the heat in the warmer substance will always travel to the colder substance 
until both are of equal temperature. For example, a piece of ice in an ice box 
does not communicate its coldness to the bottle of milk standing nearby. 
Rather, the heat in the warm milk automatically flows into the ice.

To determine the amount of heat that transfers from one substance to 
another, science uses the British Thermal Unit or BTU. One BTU is the amount 
of heat required to raise the temperature of 0.45 kg (1 lb) of water 0.556°
C (1°F). For example, to raise the 
temperature of 0.45 kg (1 lb) of water from 0 to 100°C (32 to 
212°F), one BTU of heat must be added for each degree rise in 
temperature or a total of 180 BTU's of heat.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Safety Precautions

 WARNING: CARBON MONOXIDE IS COLORLESS, ODORLESS AND DANGEROUS. IF IT IS 
NECESSARY TO OPERATE THE ENGINE WITH THE VEHICLE IN A CLOSED AREA SUCH AS A 
GARAGE, ALWAYS USE AN EXHAUST COLLECTOR TO VENT THE EXHAUST GAS OUTSIDE THE 
CLOSED AREA. 

Whenever components in the engine compartment or instrument panel areas 
are being serviced, the battery ground cable must be disconnected to eliminate 
the possibility of electrical shorts. Extreme care must be exercised when 
performing electrical tests where the battery must be connected to operate the 
system.

================================================================================
PAGE 3651
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 12-00: Climate Control System, Service

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Service Precautions

 WARNING: NEVER REMOVE THE RADIATOR CAP UNDER ANY CIRCUMSTANCES WHILE THE ENGINE 
IS OPERATING. SWITCH OFF THE ENGINE AND WAIT UNTIL IT HAS COOLED. EVEN THEN, 
USE EXTREME CARE WHEN REMOVING THE CAP FROM THE RADIATOR SUPPLY TANK. WRAP A 
THICK CLOTH AROUND THE CAP AND TURN IT SLOWLY TO THE FIRST STOP. STEP BACK 
WHILE THE PRESSURE IS RELEASED FROM THE COOLING SYSTEM. WHEN YOU ARE SURE ALL 
THE PRESSURE HAS BEEN RELEASED, PRESS DOWN ON THE CAP — STILL 
WITH A CLOTH — TURN AND REMOVE IT. STAND CLEAR OF THE RADIATOR 
SUPPLY TANK OPENING. HOT COOLANT CAN SPLASH OUT. FAILURE TO FOLLOW THESE 
INSTRUCTIONS CAN RESULT IN SERIOUS PERSONAL INJURY FROM HOT COOLANT OR STEAM 
BLOWOUT AND/OR DAMAGE TO THE COOLING SYSTEM OR ENGINE.

Section 12-02: Heating and Defrosting

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Climate Control Assembly

The ventilation and heating system control is located on the lower 
central part of the instrument panel, just below the radio.

The system is controlled by two levers that adjust the temperature and 
airflow direction.

 Airflow Control 

All heater assemblies contain a heater core and a blower. The air 
(forced by blower or ram effect) passes through the heater core and discharges 
through various outlets.

 Temperature Control 

Air is heated as it passes through the heater core (connected to the 
engine cooling system). Water circulation is controlled by a valve actuated by 
the temperature lever on the control panel. In this way, the water flow 
control valve permits the tuning of the heater core temperature and, 
consequently, of the air passing through the heater core.

When the airflow or the heater system is turned on, the air circulation 
to the cab interior is obtained by means of airflow direction grilles.

 Blower Motor Control 

The airflow system uses a two-speed motor connected to dual fans. A 
switch located just below the control panel controls blower motor speed.

================================================================================
PAGE 3660
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 12-02: Heating and Defrosting

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Blower Motor

The airflow system uses a two-speed blower motor connected to dual fans 
to control the volume of air moving through the heating and defrosting system. 
This blower motor is controlled by a blower motor switch located just below 
the control panel on the center area of the instrument panel. The blower motor 
switch has three positions, OFF, LOW and HIGH.

================================================================================
PAGE 3661
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 12-02: Heating and Defrosting

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Blower Motor Resistor

The amount of electrical current allowed to reach the blower motor 
determines blower motor speed. This electrical current is governed by the 
blower motor resistor located on the blower motor. Current is directed through 
the blower motor resistor by the position of the blower motor switch. When the 
blower motor switch is in the LOW position, current is directed through the 
resistor to restrict the amount of current reaching the blower motor, 
resulting in a low blower motor speed. When the blower motor switch is set at 
the HIGH position, current is allowed to bypass the resistor and feed directly 
to the blower motor resulting in a high blower motor speed. If the blower 
motor resistor is found to be defective, it cannot be serviced internally and 
must be replaced.

================================================================================
PAGE 3662
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 12-02: Heating and Defrosting

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Instrument Panel Registers

There are four air outlet registers found on the instrument panel. 
These are located as follows: one on the extreme left of the instrument panel, 
one on the extreme right of the instrument panel and two located in the 
central portion of the instrument panel. These registers can be independently 
adjusted to direct airflow left, right, up and down. These four instrument 
panel registers are in addition to the two floor registers and four outlet 
registers located along the top of the instrument panel used to direct heated 
air upward for windshield defrosting.

================================================================================
PAGE 3663

1997 Cargo

Section 12-02: Heating and Defrosting

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Heater Core

The heater core consists of a number of fins and tubes positioned to 
extract available heat from the engine coolant and transfer that heat to the 
air that passes through the core. This heated air is directed to the passenger 
compartment through the heater assembly, which contains the heater core and 
blower motor.

================================================================================
PAGE 3664
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 12-02: Heating and Defrosting

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

System Airflow

The following illustration shows vehicle system airflow.

[FIGURE: K91751A.gif]

 FLOOR/PANEL 

This position of the function control lever directs air through the 
system windshield, floor, side panel and center panel (unheated) vents.

 DEFROST 

This position of the function control lever directs air through the 
windshield and side panel vents. The center panel vents, if left open, will 
provide unheated air. Airflow from the side panel vents, when directed toward 
the door windows, will help avoid side glass fogging.

 PANEL 

This position of the function control lever directs unheated air 
through the center panel vents only.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Safety Precautions

 WARNING: CARBON MONOXIDE IS COLORLESS, ODORLESS AND DANGEROUS. IF IT IS 
NECESSARY TO OPERATE THE ENGINE WITH THE VEHICLE IN A CLOSED AREA SUCH AS A 
GARAGE, ALWAYS USE AN EXHAUST COLLECTOR TO VENT THE EXHAUST GAS OUTSIDE THE 
CLOSED AREA. 

Whenever components in the engine compartment or instrument panel areas 
are being serviced, the battery ground cable must be disconnected to eliminate 
the possibility of electrical shorts. Extreme care must be exercised when 
performing electrical tests where the battery must be connected to operate the 
system.
