REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Climate Control Assembly

 Removal 

Disconnect battery ground cable.

Remove ash receptacle.

Remove six screws retaining the center finish trim panel to the 
instrument panel.

Carefully pull center finish trim panel down and away from the 
instrument panel far enough to clear the climate control assembly. Be careful 
not to dislodge any electrical connectors from the center finish trim panel.

Reinstall the two upper screws that retain the radio support bracket to 
ensure the radio remains in place during climate control assembly removal.

Remove the four screws that retain the climate control assembly to the 
instrument panel.

Carefully pull the climate control assembly away from the instrument 
panel far enough to gain access to the rear of the assembly.

Disconnect the illumination socket from the climate control assembly.

Remove the function control lever cable retaining clip from the back of 
the assembly.

Carefully remove the function control cable from the assembly. Some 
articulation may be required to disconnect the cable Z-bend from the assembly. 
Pay particular attention to the cable mounting adjustment hole. Install the 
new cable in the same position.

Repeat Steps 8 and 9 for the temperature control cable.

Remove the climate control assembly.

 Installation 

Insert temperature control cable Z-bend into the same adjustment hole 
on the climate control assembly as was described in removal procedures.

Install the temperature control cable retainer clip to the climate 
control assembly while holding the temperature control cable in position.

Repeat Steps 1 and 2 for the function control cable.

Install illumination socket in climate control assembly.

Position the climate control assembly in instrument panel and install 
the four screws that retain the assembly.

Remove the two screws previously installed to support the radio.

Install the center finish trim panel. Make sure to align the locating 
tabs found at the top of the trim panel with the locating notches in the 
instrument panel. Make sure all electrical connectors are properly installed.

Install six screws that retain the center finish trim panel to the 
instrument panel.

Test the system for proper operation.

Install ash receptacle.

Reconnect battery ground cable.

================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 12-02: Heating and Defrosting

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Climate Control Assembly Illumination Bulbs

 Removal 

Remove ash receptacle.

Remove six screws retaining the center finish trim panel to the 
instrument panel.

Carefully pull center finish trim panel down and away from the 
instrument panel far enough to clear the climate control assembly. Be careful 
not to dislodge any electrical connectors from the center finish trim panel.

Reinstall the two upper screws from the center finish trim panel to 
secure the radio in place during climate control assembly removal.

Remove the four screws that retain the climate control assembly in the 
instrument panel.

Carefully pull the climate control assembly from the instrument panel 
far enough to gain access to the illumination bulb socket located on the left 
side of the climate control assembly.

Remove the illumination bulb socket from the climate control assembly 
by pulling straight away from the assembly. A slight side-to-side rocking 
motion may be necessary to assist in socket removal.

Remove miniature bulb from the illumination socket by pulling straight 
away from the socket.

 Installation 

Obtain a replacement miniature bulb. Refer to the Master Parts Catalog 
for correct miniature bulb application.

Install miniature bulb in illumination bulb socket.

Install illumination bulb socket in climate control assembly.

Install four screws that retain climate control assembly to instrument 
panel.

Remove two upper screws retaining the radio and install the center 
finish trim panel in the instrument panel. Make sure to align the locating 
tabs on the center finish trim panel with the locating notches on the 
instrument panel.

Install six screws retaining the center finish trim panel to the 
instrument panel.

Install the ash receptacle.

Check system for proper operation.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Blower Motor Switch

 Removal 

Disconnect battery ground cable.

Remove ash receptacle.

Remove six screws retaining the center finish trim panel to the 
instrument panel.

Carefully pull the center finish trim panel down and away from the 
instrument panel far enough to clear the climate control assembly. Be careful 
not to dislodge any electrical connectors attached to the center finish trim 
panel.

Disconnect the hardshell electrical connector from the backside of the 
blower motor switch.

Depress the two retaining tabs (one on each side) of the blower motor 
switch and remove the switch by pulling it through the front of the center 
finish trim panel.

 Installation 

Working from the front of the center finish trim panel, install the 
blower motor switch by aligning the blower motor switch locating tabs with the 
locating notches on the center finish trim panel and push the switch into 
place until the retaining tabs snap into place on the back of the trim panel.

Connect the hardshell electrical connector to the blower motor switch.

Install the center finish trim panel. Make sure to align the center 
finish trim panel locating tabs found at the top of the trim panel with the 
locating notches in the instrument panel. Make sure all electrical connectors 
are properly installed.

Install six screws that retain the center finish trim panel to the 
instrument panel.

Test system for proper operation.

Install the ash receptacle.

Reconnect battery ground cable.

Heater Case 

 Removal 

Apply parking brake and disconnect battery ground cable. 

Remove switch panel retaining screws. Pull panel down to clear 
retaining lugs, then pull away from console.

[FIGURE: L53541A.gif]

Disconnect vent tubes to face level vents. Disconnect harness 
connectors and release panel. 

Remove windshield demister vent tubes and vent tube retaining clips 
from heater body.

[FIGURE: K19550B.gif]

Glove Compartment

Remove heater control illumination bulb holder and heater control 
panel. Then disconnect heater connectors. 

Remove the fuse module cover to access the passenger-side foot level 
vent and the heater assembly retainer bolt. Remove the foot level vent and the 
heater assembly retainer bolt.

[FIGURE: K16753B.gif]

Remove the right-hand instrument panel to access the brake control 
valve panel-to-console retaining nuts. 

Remove the four retaining nuts and position the brake control valve 
panel out of the way to access the driver-side foot level vent and the heater 
assembly retainer bolt.

[FIGURE: K16755C.gif]

Remove the foot level vent and the heater assembly retainer bolt. 

Lift front access panel and remove grille. 

 NOTE: Note which hose is connected to the inlet and outlet tubes.

Disconnect heater hoses, taking adequate precautions to collect 
coolant. Carefully secure heater hoses in an upright position to a suitable 
point on cab. 

 NOTE: If necessary, loosen two center grille mounting brackets to allow 
removal. 

Remove air pipe support bracket and heater retaining bolts. Make sure 
there is sufficient slack in air pipes for heater removal by cutting away 
securing straps as necessary, carefully noting their position. Remove heater 
from vehicle.

 Installation 

Fit heater in cab opening. Tighten retaining bolts, making sure the 
hood strap and air pipe support brackets are connected. Reconnect wiper 
linkage if previously disconnected. 

 NOTE: Make sure the heater hoses are connected to the proper inlet or outlet 
position.

Position heater hoses, then connect heater inlet hose and retaining clip.

[FIGURE: L5356C.gif]

Inside cab, install heater retaining bolts to mounting brackets. Refit 
fuse module cover (where fitted) and foot level vents. 

Install the brake control valve panel and four retaining nuts to 
console. Install the right-hand instrument panel. 

Connect heater electrical connects, then install heater control panel 
and illumination bulb holder. 

Install vent tube clips and windshield demister tube to heater body and 
connect vent tubes. It may be necessary to remove the small section of the 
glove compartment to install the passenger-side windshield demister tube.

[FIGURE: K16757B.gif]

Position switch panel, then connect face level vents and harness 
connectors. 

Locate switch panel retaining lugs. Install and tighten securing screws. 

Water blending heater only: Set heater temperature control to maximum 
heat position. 

Reconnect battery ground cable. 

Take adequate precautions to collect any spilled coolant, then start 
and run engine until all air in heater radiator has been expelled. Connect 
heater outlet hose and install retaining clip. Add coolant to the specified 
level. Check operation of blower motor. 

Fit new securing straps to air pipes, as necessary.

 NOTE: If the grille brackets were removed during removal of the heater, make 
sure they are correctly aligned and the retaining bolts are securely 
tightened. 

Refit grille, and lower front access panel.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Blower Motor Resistor 

 Removal 

Disconnect battery ground cable. 

Lift front access panel and remove grille. 

Remove fan covers and remove motor cover retaining screw.

[FIGURE: L77771A.gif]

Note their positions and disconnect the lead wires from the heater 
blower motor resistor assembly. 

Remove retaining strap screw and remove resistor assembly.

[FIGURE: L77781A.gif]

 Installation 

Position resistor and strap assembly and install retaining screw. 

Connect wire leads to resistor assembly. 

Position motor cover and install retaining screw. Install fan covers. 

Install grille and lower the access panel. 

Connect battery ground cable and check operation of blower motor.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Heater Water Hoses 

 Removal 

 NOTE: Note heater hose routing prior to removal.

Tilt cab and disconnect battery ground cable. Drain cooling system, as 
necessary. 

Note positions of any straps fitted to damaged hose, then cut away 
straps. 

Disconnect damaged hose from engine union. Then remove hose from hose 
retaining bracket, if so equipped. 

Lower cab, raise front access panel, and remove grille. 

Disconnect hose from heater, then remove it from hose retaining bracket 
and from vehicle. 

 Installation 

 NOTE: Route the heater hoses to the previously noted positions to ensure 
proper heater operation.

To install inlet hose, position new hose and route it through hose 
retaining bracket. Connect hose to heater, making sure the heater hose clamp 
is tightened to specification. Refer to Specifications in this section.

To install outlet hose, position new hose and route it through hose 
retaining bracket. 

Close front access panel and tilt cab. 

Route hose through hose retaining bracket. Connect hose to engine 
union. Make sure heater hose clamp is tightened to specification. Refer to Specifications 
 in this section.

Fit new straps to noted positions and lower cab. 

Fill cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 . 

Reconnect battery ground cable.

Section 13-00: Instrument Cluster and Panel Lighting

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Instrument Cluster and Panel Lighting

The instrument cluster and panel lighting is controlled by the main 
light switch. When the switch is in the HEAD or PARK position, battery voltage 
is supplied to the illumination lights. The lights can be dimmed manually with 
the instrument panel rheostat.

Section 13-01: Instrument Cluster, Conventional

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Instrument Cluster (IC)

The instrument panel consists of three modules containing a group of 
instruments. The right and left modules are attached at the top by means of 
quick-release fasteners. At the bottom, they are retained with tabs so that 
the panel can be tilted forward to allow access behind panel. 

[FIGURE: K24291A.gif]

The center module includes a speedometer and an odometer. The left unit 
contains a tachometer, an engine coolant temperature gauge, an oil pressure 
gauge, a set of warning lamps and a rotating switch knob for the front lamps, 
tail lamps and headlamps. A fuel level gauge, an air pressure gauge, a 
voltmeter, and other warning lamps are installed on the right module.

High Beam Indicator (Part of 10B987)

 WARNING: DO NOT DRIVE THE VEHICLE WHEN THE LOW AIR PRESSURE BUZZER IS SOUNDING 
OR THE LOW AIR PRESSURE WARNING LIGHT IS LIT. THESE WARNINGS INDICATE THERE IS 
NOT ENOUGH AIR PRESSURE FOR THE BRAKE SYSTEM TO OPERATE PROPERLY. 

The conditions monitored are low engine oil pressure, high engine 
coolant temperature, low coolant level, exhaust brake activation, air 
conditioning compressor temperature, high automatic transmission temperature 
(or DO NOT shift), anti-lock brake operation, low air pressure, parking brake, 
differential lockout activation, daytime running lamps and cab lock. These 
lamps will turn on and remain on if any of these conditions exist, until the 
condition is corrected or the key is turned to the OFF position. 

The low engine oil pressure, high engine coolant temperature, and low 
coolant level warning lamps are accompanied by a warning chime and, in 
vehicles equipped with the engine shutdown system option, automatic engine 
shutdown.

PAGE 3683
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 13-01: Instrument Cluster, Conventional

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Fuel Level Indication System

The fuel level indication system is an electromagnetic system and 
consists of a fuel indicator gauge mounted in the instrument cluster and a 
fuel level sensor located in the fuel tank. The system operates directly from 
battery voltage and indicates fuel level condition based on the variable 
resistance of the fuel level sensor.

 Fuel Gauge 

The magnetic gauge movement consists of three primary coils, one of 
which is wound at a 90-degree angle to the other two. The coils form a 
magnetic field which varies in direction according to the variable resistance 
of the sending unit which is connected between two of them. A primary magnet, 
to which a shaft and pointer are attached, rotates to align to this primary 
field, resulting in pointer position.

 NOTE: There is no adjustment, calibration or maintenance required for these 
gauges.

 Fuel Level Sensor 

The fuel level sensor consists of a variable screened resistor made up 
of a ceramic substrate. It is controlled by the action of an attached float in 
the fuel tank. When the fuel level is low, resistance in the fuel level sensor 
is high. When the fuel level is high, the resistance in the fuel level sensor 
is low. As the float moves from empty to full, the resistance will gradually 
and continuously decrease.

================================================================================
PAGE 3684
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 13-01: Instrument Cluster, Conventional

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Coolant Temperature Indication System

The engine coolant temperature indication system is a magnetic gauge 
system. It consists of a magnetic engine coolant temperature gauge mounted in 
the instrument cluster and an engine coolant temperature sender unit.

 Instrument Cluster Temperature Gauge 

The magnetic gauge movement consists of two primary coils, one of which 
is wound at a 90-degree angle to the other. The coils form a magnetic field 
which varies in direction according to the variable resistance of the sender 
unit which is connected between them. A primary magnet, to which a shaft and 
pointer are attached, rotates to align to this primary field, resulting in 
pointer position. 

 NOTE: There is no adjustment, calibration or maintenance required for the 
gauge. 

 High Coolant Temperature Warning 

This red light will come on to indicate a high engine temperature. If 
the light comes on, operate the engine at a low rpm (approximately 1000 rpm) 
for five minutes, then low idle for 30-60 seconds. Stop the engine and let it 
cool. This procedure allows a hot engine to cool gradually. Check the coolant 
level, following the instructions about care in removing the filler cap. If 
the engine coolant is low, add coolant gradually, with the engine running.

PAGE 3685
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 13-01: Instrument Cluster, Conventional

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Oil Pressure Indication System

A red indicator lamp glows and a buzzer sounds when the oil pressure is 
below a specified value. The lamp should come on when the key is first turned 
to the RUN position. The indicator lamp should go out after the engine is 
started, indicating that the oil pressure has reached a normal operating 
value. 

The lamp is connected between the oil pressure switch unit (mounted on 
the engine) and the coil terminal of the ignition switch. 

 Oil Pressure Gauge 

The direct reading engine oil pressure indicating system consists of an 
oil pressure gauge mounted in the instrument cluster and a pressure tube 
connected to the engine. As the engine oil pressure increases, a Bourdon tube 
in the gauge deflects, causing the pointer to move.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Charge Indication System

The voltmeter is a gauge which measures the voltage potential at the 
battery to indicate the battery state of charge. The voltmeter is not 
adjustable and must be replaced if inoperative. 

 Battery Voltage Gauge 

Voltage applied across the terminals of the battery voltage gauge 
causes a gauge movement response proportional to the input. This positions the 
gauge pointer to indicate the appropriate voltage.

 NOTE: There is no adjustment calibration or maintenance required for this 
gauge.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Air Pressure Gauge

This gauge shows the amount of air pressure in the brake system 
(green/primary and red/secondary) in pounds per square inch. When the pressure 
is too low for normal brake operation (less than 414 kPa [
60 psi]), and when the key is turned to the RUN position a warning buzzer 
sounds and the warning light comes on. All vehicles have a dual-pointer air 
pressure gauge to indicate the pressure in each of the two brake circuits.

 Odometer Replacement

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Programmable Speedometer/Odometer Module

The programmable electric speedometer/odometer is standard on all Cargo 
vehicles. The instrument features an analog air-core meter movement for speed 
indication and a digital stepper motor to drive the odometer. Both mechanisms 
are inherently rugged with improved accuracy because of the digital technology 
and relatively few moving mechanical parts.

The instrument panel receives electrical pulses from a vehicle speed 
sensor (VSS). The sensor detects the teeth of a 16-tooth interrupter mounted 
in most transmissions or signal generator mounted in the rear on some 
automatic transmissions. These electrical pulses are converted to an analog 
speedometer/odometer display. The speedometer is designed so that the pointer 
will not return to zero with the key off. This should never be interpreted as 
a damaged unit.

Only a single external adjustment is necessary to calibrate both the 
speedometer and odometer. There is a 10-position DIP rocker switch for this 
calibration.

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Trip Odometer

The trip odometer registers distance driven and can be reset to zero by 
depressing the button.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Tachometer

The electric tachometer is standard on CF-Series vehicles. The 
instrument features an analog air core meter movement indicating engine speed 
in revolutions per minute (rpm). The tachometer has few moving mechanical parts.

The tachometer receives electrical pulses from a vehicle speed sensor 
(VSS). The VSS is mounted in the flywheel housing. It reads engine rpm. The 
electrical pulses are converted to an analog tachometer display.

 NOTE: The tachometer pointer will not return to zero with the key off. This 
should never be interpreted as an inoperative condition.

There is only one electrical adjustment. An eight-position DIP switch 
is necessary for engine calibration.

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Warning Indicators

 Anti-Lock Brakes 

The anti-lock brake system uses one amber ABS warning light to alert 
the driver of malfunctions in the system.

The amber ABS warning light will come on for numerous reasons. It warns 
the driver that the ABS has been disabled. Normal power-assisted braking 
remains but the wheels can lock during a panic stop while the indicator is on. 
Certain procedures must be followed to find the concern in this situation. 
Refer to Section 06-09 for diagnosis and testing of the system.

 Low Oil Pressure 

This red light will come on to indicate low engine oil pressure. If the 
light comes on while the engine is running, there is a loss of pressure. If 
this occurs, stop your vehicle as soon as possible, turn off the engine and 
check the oil level. Add oil if necessary.

 Low Coolant 

All vehicles equipped with diesel engines have a low coolant warning 
system with a red indicator light. If this light comes on, correct the low 
coolant condition immediately, following the instructions about care in 
removing the filler cap.

 High Beam 

This blue indicator light will glow when the headlamps are operating on 
high beam. To change your headlamps from low to high beam or high to low beam 
pull the turn signal lever away from the instrument panel.

 LH/RH Turn 

This green indicator will flash when the turn signal lever is pushed up 
for a right turn and down for a left turn.

 Coolant Temperature 

This red light will come on to indicate a high engine coolant 
temperature. If the light comes on, operate the engine at a low rpm 
(approximately 1000 rpm) for five minutes, then low idle for 30-60 seconds. 
Stop the engine and let it cool. This procedure allows a hot engine to cool 
gradually. 

 WARNING: NEVER REMOVE THE RADIATOR CAP UNDER ANY CONDITIONS WHILE THE ENGINE IS 
OPERATING. FAILURE TO FOLLOW THESE INSTRUCTIONS CAN RESULT IN DAMAGE TO THE 
COOLING SYSTEM OR ENGINE AND/OR PERSONAL INJURY.

TO AVOID HAVING SCALDING HOT COOLANT OR STEAM BLOW OUT OF THE RADIATOR, 
USE EXTREME CARE WHEN REMOVING THE CAP FROM A HOT RADIATOR. IF POSSIBLE, WAIT 
UNTIL THE ENGINE HAS COOLED, THEN WRAP A THICK CLOTH AROUND THE RADIATOR CAP 
AND TURN IT SLOWLY TO THE FIRST STOP. STEP BACK WHILE THE PRESSURE IS RELEASED 
FROM THE COOLING SYSTEM. WHEN YOU ARE SURE ALL THE PRESSURE HAS BEEN RELEASED, 
PRESS DOWN ON THE CAP (STILL WITH A CLOTH), TURN AND REMOVE IT. 

Check the coolant level, following the instructions about care in 
removing the filler cap. Refer to Section 03-03 for cooling system service. If 
the engine coolant is low, add coolant gradually, with the engine running.

 Transmission Temperature, Allison MT Automatic Transmission Only 

This light comes on to indicate maximum transmission-to-cooler oil 
temperature of 149°C (300°F). Should the 
light come on, stop the vehicle and shift the transmission to neutral. 
Accelerate the engine to 1200-1500 rpm to allow the transmission to return to 
normal, 71-104°C (160-220°F), before 
resuming operation. Check transmission oil level.

 Do Not Shift, Allison MD Transmissions Only 

If this light illuminates (accompanied by eight seconds of short beeps 
from the shift selector) while the vehicle is in operation, it indicates that 
the electronic control unit (ECU) has detected that the transmission operating 
parameters have been exceeded and that the shifts are being restricted (i.e., 
upshifts and downshifts may be restricted). Also, the SELECT digit on the 
shifter display will be blank. A diagnostic code will be recorded in the ECU 
if this should happen. The transmission will continue to operate in order for 
the owner to seek service assistance. If the vehicle is equipped with a shift 
lever and the lever is moved, a continuous alarm will be sounded until the 
original shift lever position has been restored. If equipped with a 
push-button shifter, it will not accept new commands.

 Wait To Start 

When this indicator is illuminated, it indicates that the air intake 
(inlet manifold) heater is in operation.

 Exhaust Brake 

This light will illuminate when the engine exhaust brake is in the ON 
position.

 Low Air 

All vehicles are equipped with a low air pressure warning light. The 
air brake systems are split or dual systems. If there is a loss of air 
pressure to either system, to a level below 414 kPa (60 psi), the red warning 
light will illuminate and the buzzer will sound. The remaining brake system is 
capable of stopping the vehicle. However, the stopping distance will be greater.

 Differential Lock 

This red indicator light will come on when the differential lockout 
control and/or wheel to wheel lock is in the LOCK position to indicate that 
the lockout mechanism in the tandem rear axle is engaged to provide extra 
traction, or if the single axle wheel lock is engaged.

 Cab Lock 

This indicator will illuminate to warn you that the cab is not locked 
securely.

 Parking Brake 

Whenever the parking brake is applied with the key in the RUN position 
a red warning light will illuminate to warn you to release the parking brake 
before driving the vehicle.

 Daytime Running Lamps 

If this amber warning lamp is on it indicates that the headlamps are 
illuminated at reduced intensity for daytime driving. For more information 
refer to Section 17-04 .

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Instrument Cluster

 Inspection and Verification 

Visually inspect the components. Check for damaged components, blown 
fuses, loose or corroded connections. Check the wiring harness for obvious 
signs of shorts, opens, bad connections or damage.

Verify circuit operation. Verify speedometer and odometer operation by 
road testing the vehicle.

Refer to the Electrical and Vacuum Troubleshooting Manual for the 
connector numbers in the pinpoint tests.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Instrument Cluster Lenses

 CAUTION: The use of vinyl cleaners and similar other cleaning agents to clean 
the vehicle interior and/or indicator lamp lens has resulted in damage to the 
indicator lamp lens. The chemical content of these cleaning agents 
(O-dichlorobenzene, ethyl alcohol and/or Cellosolve), has produced fogging, 
spotting, stain, or splotches of the lenses, either through overspray or 
direct use on the lenses. Therefore, extreme caution should be taken during 
interior cleanup to prevent overspray of cleaning agents which contain the 
chemical contents mentioned from contacting the indicator lamp lens. 

The indicator lamp lens should be cleaned with Ultra-Clear Spray Glass 
Cleaner E4AZ-19C507-AA or equivalent commercial cleaning product, meeting Ford 
specification ESR-M14P5-A, using a clean, soft, lint-free cloth. The Ford 
Glass Cleaner has been specially formulated for cleaning windows in automotive 
vehicles and is approved for use in cleaning the plastic indicator lamp lens. 
Read and carefully follow the directions on the container for best results.

ADJUSTMENTS

Tachometer Calibration 

The tachometer is calibrated according to engine type, specifically, 
the number of flywheel teeth. The tachometer can be calibrated by setting 
eight dip switches on back of the tachometer. The switches have the numbers 1 
through 8 embossed on the switch. To calibrate the tachometer, the switches 
are set so each switch is either in the ON or OFF position, depending on the 
engine type. A switch is set to the ON position when the switch is depressed 
towards the number on top of the switch. A switch is set to the OFF position 
when the switch is depressed at the bottom of the switch, away from the switch 
number.

 NOTE: Settings are shown on the tachometer case label.

[FIGURE: K19634A.gif]

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

ADJUSTMENTS

Speedometer Calibration

To ensure that the electronic speedometer system operates accurately, 
inspect the vehicle speed sensor (VSS) periodically. Check the VSS for metal 
filings accumulating on the sensor pole face at the following kilometer 
(mileage) intervals: 800 (500), 20,000 (12,500), 40,000 (25,000), 60,000 
(37,500), 80,000 (50,000). Scheduled maintenance beyond 80,000 kilometers 
(50,000 miles) should occur at subsequent 80,000 kilometer (50,000 mile) 
intervals. Metal filings that have developed on the sensor pole face must be 
removed to maintain system integrity. The programmable electronic speedometer 
instrument requires no maintenance.

The bank of switches that are located at the rear of the electronic 
speedometers require setting for proper operation of the speedometer and 
odometer unit. The transmission-mounted speed sensor transmits a signal to the 
speedometer/odometer that is dependent on:

rear axle ratio.

tire revolutions per mile (rpm), which is based on tire height.

 Rear Axle Ratio Determination 

The axle ratio can be determined by referring to the information 
delivered with the vehicle or finding the metal tag attached to the 
differential. If the vehicle has a two-speed differential (e.g., 4.15/5.72:1), 
use the smaller number (4.15 in this case) in all calculations.

 Tire Revolutions Per Mile Determination 

The revs per mile can be calculated as follows:

Measure the tire height (ground to top of tire) in inches with the 
vehicle on level ground, loaded, with the tires "cold" and inflated to the 
recommended pressure. Measure to the nearest 1/8 inch. Use the following table 
to convert fractions to decimals. (If calculation is done in centimeters, 
divide tire height by 2.54 to convert to inches.)

1/8 — .125

1/4 — .25

3/8 — .375

1/2 — .5

5/8 — .625

3/4 — .75

7/8 — .875

(Example: If tire height is 36-1/8 inch, use 36.125 in your revs per 
mile calculation)

Divide 20,168 (constant) by the tire height to get the revs per mile.

(Example: 20,168/36.125 = 558.28)

 Calibration Frequency Determination 

Multiply the axle ratio times the revs per mile times 0.267 (constant)

(Example: 558.28 x 4.10 x 0.267 = 611.49)

Round the 611.49 to the closest whole number, which is 611.

 Determine Speedometer/Odometer Switch Setting 

Determine which type speedometer/odometer you are installing. The 
following procedure applies for both "stand-alone" and gauge "cluster" type 
speedometer/odometer units. (Replacement units are either the 12-switch Beede 
or 10-switch Ametek type. The 10-switch Beede has been discontinued for 
service.)

If the unit you are calibrating is a 10-switch type, determine if it is 
an Ametek or Beede by looking at the type of electrical connection on the 
back. The Beede has four "studs," while the Ametek has a single plug-in type 
connector. If your 10-switch Beede is replaced with a 10-switch Ametek, a 
simple electrical jumper wire will be included with the new speedometer.

There are three speedometer setting charts (Ametek 10-position, Beede 
10-position and Beede 12-position). Using the correct speedometer setting 
chart on the following pages, find the Test Freq in the left-hand column and 
read the switch settings in the next column. A number means that switch is to 
be placed in the ON or closed position and a period "." means that switch is 
to be placed in the OFF or open position (e.g., using the Beede 12-Position 
chart and the 611 test frequency calculated in the example, the chart gives 
the switch settings as: (1.3456.8.0.B). This means that switches 1, 3, 4, 5, 
6, 8, 10, 12 are ON and switches 2, 7, 9, 11 are OFF. The letters A and B are 
used to represent switches 11 and 12. There are at least three different 
styles of switches with unique switch position labeling. Ignore the switch 
position labeling. Pushing the top of the switch IN turns the switch ON. 
Pushing the bottom of the switch IN turns the switch OFF.

Section 13-09: Engine Protection System

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Engine Protection System Components

The engine protection system is designed to prevent engine damage 
resulting from operation of the engine during prolonged periods of low oil 
pressure, high coolant temperature or low coolant level. 

Switches or sensors provide information to the system's electronic 
module. When one of the monitored engine systems is not functioning properly, 
a warning lamp in the instrument panel will illuminate. Warning lamps are 
provided for the following: 

low oil pressure 

high coolant temperature 

low coolant level 

The low oil pressure, high coolant temperature and low coolant level 
warning lamps are accompanied by an audible warning. In vehicles equipped with 
the engine shutdown option, the audible warning will be heard with the warning 
lamp illumination and after 30-40 seconds, the engine will stop running. The 
30-40 second delay is provided to allow removal of the vehicle from the road. 
After the engine stops running, it can be restarted and operated for 
approximately an additional 30-40 seconds. There is no limit to how many times 
the shutdown system will allow the engine to be restarted. This feature is 
only provided to allow the vehicle to be driven off the road. Any attempt to 
use this feature to drive the vehicle very far will result in serious engine 
damage. 

The engine protection system shares the following components with the 
engine shutdown system:

fuel shutoff solenoid

fuel shutoff relay

 Fuel Control 

The fuel shutoff solenoid is used to allow or cut off fuel supply to 
the engine. This solenoid moves the fuel rack into the fuel ON and OFF 
positions. Power for the solenoid is controlled by the ignition switch and 
relays in the system.

The fuel shutoff solenoid has two coils within one housing. A powerful 
pull-in coil pulls the fuel shutoff lever to the OPEN position. The pull-coil 
is fed from the switched side of the starter motor relay and energized 
whenever the ignition switch is in the START position. At the same time, a 
much less powerful hold coil is fed from a start/run circuit. When the 
ignition switch is released to the RUN position, the pull-coil drops out and 
the hold coil is left to keep the fuel shutoff lever in the OPEN position.

 CAUTION: The pull-coil draws a considerable amount of current while it is 
energized. Do not allow it to remain energized for longer than 30 seconds, or 
damage to the coil can result. 

The fuel shutoff electrical system consists primarily of the following 
components:

Fuel shutoff solenoid, located next to the fuel injection pump.

[FIGURE: K19637A.gif]

Fuel shutoff relay, located in the fuse panel position A.

[FIGURE: K16850B.gif]

 Fuel Shutoff Relay 

[FIGURE: K24290A.gif]

Pin Number

Circuit Function

86

Malfunction Signal from Low Coolant Level, Brake Low Air Pressure Buzzer,
and Fuel Valve Warning Switch

 Start 

When the ignition switch is placed in the START position, the starter 
motor relay is energized, the starter is actuated and current is applied to 
the fuel shutoff solenoid pull coil through Circuit 669 (R/BL). The fuel 
shutoff solenoid pulls the shutoff lever to the OPEN position to allow fuel to 
flow while the engine cranks and starts. Also, Circuits 974 (O) and 69 (R/GN) 
are on in both START and RUN positions.

 Run 

After starting, the ignition switch is placed in the RUN position and 
power is interrupted to Circuit 32 (R/BL).

The starter motor relay is de-energized and current is no longer 
supplied to the fuel shutoff solenoid pull coil. In the RUN position, Circuit 
974 (O) continues to energize the fuel shutoff relay (Relay A). Current from 
Circuit 69 (R/GN) is supplied to the fuel shutoff solenoid hold coil through 
fuel shutoff relay. The hold coil allows the fuel shutoff solenoid to hold the 
shutoff lever in the OPEN position with less current draw.

 NOTE: Circuits 974 (O) and 69 (R/GN) have power in both START and RUN 
positions.

 Shutoff 

Turning the ignition switch to the OFF position will interrupt the 
current to the fuel shutoff relay Circuits 974 (O) and 69 (R/GN) and the fuel 
shutoff solenoid hold coil. The fuel shutoff solenoid will then allow the 
shutoff lever to return to the OFF position and the engine will shut down.

Indicator lamps in the instrument panel for low oil pressure, high 
coolant temperature and low coolant level.

Section 13-09: Engine Protection System

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Engine Audible Warning and Shutdown Activation 

When the engine alarm/shutdown module is grounded at one or more of its 
three inputs, it immediately sounds the audible warning. After approximately 
30-40 seconds, if equipped for engine shutdown, it opens the battery circuit 
for the fuel shutoff relay and the engine is shut off.

================================================================================
PAGE 3722
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 13-09: Engine Protection System

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Prove-Out Mode 

During engine crank (key in START position), a proveout relay closes, 
grounding the low coolant level and high coolant temperature warning indicator 
lamp circuit, the engine shutdown/audible warning circuit, and the proveout 
circuit of the engine alarm/shutdown module. Thus, the audible warning is 
activated and the following warning indicator lamps are illuminated during 
engine crank: 

coolant temperature 

coolant level 

The oil pressure warning indicator lamp proves out through its own 
switch. Since oil pressure is already low during engine crank, it is grounded 
with key on-engine off.

 NOTE: Other warning indicator lamps are proved out through another prove-out 
relay.

================================================================================
PAGE 3723
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 13-09: Engine Protection System

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Low Oil Pressure Detection 

The oil pressure switch is normally closed. The presence of adequate 
oil pressure (55-83 kPa [8-12 psi] or higher) opens the oil 
pressure switch, turning off the oil pressure warning indicator lamp and the 
audible warning. When oil pressure is insufficient, the oil pressure switch 
closes, grounding the oil pressure warning indicator lamp circuit and the 
engine alarm/shutdown module circuit. The indicator lamp illuminates and the 
engine alarm/shutdown module sounds a warning signal. If the circuit is 
activated (grounded) for 30-40 seconds or longer, and if equipped with engine 
shutdown, the engine alarm/shutdown module opens the battery circuit for the 
fuel shutoff relay and causes engine shutdown.

 NOTE: At extremely cold temperatures, with high viscosity oil, the engine 
shutdown system may shut the engine down before the oil pressure has had time 
to build up.

================================================================================
PAGE 3724
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 13-09: Engine Protection System

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

High Coolant Temperature Detection 

The coolant temperature switch is normally open. When the coolant 
temperature is excessive (103°C (218°F) or 
higher), the switch closes, grounding the coolant temperature warning 
indicator lamp circuit and the engine alarm/shutdown module circuit. The 
indicator lamp illuminates and the engine alarm/shutdown module sounds a 
warning signal. If the circuit is activated (grounded) for 30-40 seconds, and 
if equipped with engine shutdown, the engine alarm/shutdown module opens the 
battery circuit for the fuel shutoff relay that opens the battery circuit for 
the fuel shutoff solenoid hold-in coil that causes engine shutdown.

================================================================================
PAGE 3725
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 13-09: Engine Protection System

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Low Coolant Level Detection 

The engine alarm/shutdown module monitors the resistance between the 
tip and the threaded base of the low coolant level sensor. When the coolant 
level drops far enough that the low coolant level sensor is no longer 
submerged, the engine alarm/shutdown module senses the increase in resistance 
(air has a much higher resistance than coolant). After a short delay (1-3 
seconds), the engine alarm/shutdown module grounds the low coolant level 
warning indicator lamp circuit. The coolant level warning indicator lamp is 
illuminated, and the engine alarm/shutdown module sounds a warning signal. If 
the circuit to the engine alarm/shutdown module is open for 30-40 seconds, and 
if equipped with engine shutdown, the engine alarm/shutdown module opens the 
battery circuit for the fuel shutoff relay that opens the battery circuit for 
the fuel shutoff solenoid hold-in coil that causes engine shutdown.

 NOTE: The resistance value of pure antifreeze (without water mix) is high and 
the low coolant level sensor may indicate a low level reading if it is 
submerged in pure antifreeze. During a system refill, if the coolant supply 
tank is filled with pure antifreeze, the low coolant level sensor may have to 
be jumpered to allow the engine to run long enough to mix the antifreeze with 
the existing coolant (water/antifreeze) in the system.

Section 13-10: Gauge, Warning Indicator, Brake Operation

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Warning Indicators, Dual Brake

The direct air pressure indication system consists of a dual air 
pressure gauge with dual pointers mounted in the instrument cluster, a two-way 
check valve and air tubes connected at the pressure pickup point on the 
vehicle. As the system's air pressure increases, the Bourdon tubes in the dual 
air pressure gauge deflect, causing the pointers to move. The two air pressure 
indicating systems measure the air reservoir's pressure.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Air Pressure Gauge 

 Removal 

Set parking brake and disconnect battery ground cable(s). 

Pull lanyards on the primary and secondary air tank drain valves until 
the pressure is exhausted. Air tanks are located inside the right and left 
side rails behind the air supply tank. 

 CAUTION: The cluster panel assembly is retained by a wire assembly. Handle with 
care to avoid damage to the wires. 

Turn two quick-release quarter-turn fasteners counterclockwise on right 
cluster panel. Pull top of the cluster panel outward to get sufficient access 
to inside cluster. 

[FIGURE: K16790A.gif]

Disconnect illumination bulb socket wiring connector from the dual air 
pressure gauge. 

Disconnect two air lines from the dual air pressure gauge. 

[FIGURE: K16791A.gif]

Remove air line adapters. 

[FIGURE: K16794A.gif]

Remove two nuts and bracket securing the dual air pressure gauge to 
cluster panel. Remove dual air pressure gauge from the cluster panel. 

[FIGURE: K16795A.gif]

 Installation 

Position certified dual air pressure gauge into the cluster panel. 

Install bracket, two nuts, and secure. 

[FIGURE: K16796A.gif]

Install the air line adapters.

Connect two air lines and check for leaks. 

Connect illumination bulb wiring connector to the dual air pressure 
gauge. 

Position the cluster panel in instrument panel. Make sure that locating 
tabs at bottom of panel are engaged with instrument panel. Engage 
quick-release 1/4-turn fasteners. 

Connect battery ground cable(s), charge primary and secondary air 
systems and check operation of the dual air pressure gauge.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Low Pressure Indicator Switch 

Two low air pressure switches are mounted to the foot brake valve. One 
switch monitors the primary supply and the other monitors the secondary 
supply. The switches close to operate a brake low air pressure buzzer and 
light when low air pressure is detected.

 Removal 

Turn ignition switch to OFF position and exhaust air from brake system. 

Disconnect wire at low air pressure switch. 

Unscrew low air pressure switch and remove it. 

 Installation 

Using Ford Pipe Sealant with Teflon® D8AZ-19554-A or 
equivalent meeting Ford specifications WSK-M2G350-AZ and ESR-M18P7-A, install 
low air pressure switch. 

Connect air lines as required. 

Connect low air pressure switch electrical connector. 

[FIGURE: H8177A.gif]

Turn ignition switch to RUN to verify that brake low air pressure 
buzzer and brake low air pressure warning indicator lamp are actuated before 
charging system.

Section 14-00: Battery and Charging System, Service

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Battery and Charging System

 Inspection and Verification 

 WARNING: KEEP BATTERIES OUT OF REACH OF CHILDREN. BATTERIES CONTAIN SULFURIC 
ACID. AVOID CONTACT WITH SKIN, EYES, AND CLOTHING. SHIELD YOUR EYES WHEN 
WORKING NEAR THE BATTERY TO PROTECT AGAINST POSSIBLE SPLASHING OF THE ACID 
SOLUTION. IN CASE OF ACID CONTACT WITH SKIN OR EYES, FLUSH IMMEDIATELY WITH 
WATER FOR A MINIMUM OF 15 MINUTES AND GET PROMPT MEDICAL ATTENTION. IF ACID IS 
SWALLOWED, CALL A PHYSICIAN IMMEDIATELY. 

 WARNING: BATTERIES NORMALLY PRODUCE EXPLOSIVE GASES THAT CAN CAUSE PERSONAL 
INJURY. DO NOT ALLOW FLAMES, SPARKS OR LIGHTED SUBSTANCES TO COME NEAR THE 
BATTERY. WHEN CHARGING OR WORKING NEAR A BATTERY, ALWAYS SHIELD YOUR FACE AND 
PROTECT YOUR EYES. ALWAYS PROVIDE VENTILATION. 

Verify the vehicle owner's original concern by operating the engine to 
duplicate the concern.

Inspect to determine if one of the following mechanical or electrical 
concerns apply.

 VISUAL INSPECTION CHART

Mechanical

Electrical

Before attempting to test a battery. Give it a thorough examination to
determine if it has been damaged.

Batteries are tested to determine the state of charge and ability to
crank an engine. The result of these tests is to show that the battery is
either good, needs recharging, or must be replaced.

Preliminary checks to the charging system should be made regardless of
the fault condition. These checks include:

Check the fuses/fuse links to the generator to make sure that they are
not burned or damaged. This condition, resulting in an open circuit or high
resistance, can cause erratic or intermittent charging system concerns.

Check battery posts and cable terminals for clean and tight
connections. Clean the posts and the cables to ensure good electrical contact.

Check for secure connections at the generator output, generator
regulator and engine ground. Also check the connection at the load
distribution point.

Check the generator drive belt to ensure proper tension and no slip
between the generator pulley and the drive belt. Refer to Section 03A-05 or
 Section 03B-05 .

Check battery for full charge as outlined.

Before performing charging system tests on the vehicle, note conditions
such as: slow cranking, discharged battery, charge indicator lamp stays ON
with engine running, charge indicator lamp does not illuminate with ignition
switch in RUN and engine not running, etc. This information will aid in
isolating the part of the system causing the symptom.

When a relatively new battery is discharged, test for current drain.
The following are some of the most common current drain concerns:

Glove compartment lamp stays on with the door closed.

Engine compartment lamp stays on constantly.

License plate lamp or interior lamp stays on constantly.

Other electronic component damage.

Battery, starting system, and lighting system concerns can be caused by 
poor charging system performance. The charging system can also cause an 
overload in other areas of the electrical system. 

To correctly identify the area where the difficulty lies, isolate the 
battery, the charging system, and the electrical circuits. Check the battery 
before any electrical system diagnosis, to see if it has the ability to accept 
and hold a charge. Refer to Section 14-01 . If the battery is good, check the 
charging system to see if it can keep the battery charged. 

If the battery cannot meet specifications, it must be replaced. 

If the battery meets the required specifications, it must be fully 
charged before proceeding with the diagnosis of other electrical system 
components. 

Before testing any of the individual charging system components, 
perform general component tests in this section. The component tests will 
determine which components require servicing.

Perform Pinpoint Test A using Rotunda Inductive Dwell-Tach-Volts Ohms 
Tester 164-R0254 or equivalent. Be careful when using the ohmmeter near hot 
circuits. The component to be checked should be disconnected from the circuit 
or the battery terminals should be disconnected. Use Rotunda Charging/Starting 
Analyzer 164-R0251 or equivalent for testing the charging system. Test 
instructions are provided with the analyzer. 

 CAUTION: Damage to the component being checked can occur during testing if it is 
not disconnected from the circuit, or if the battery terminals are not 
disconnected. 

Continue through the Diagnosis and Testing until service has been 
completed. Test the system again to see if the service has corrected the 
system. 

 Symptom Chart — Battery And Charging System

Troubleshooting or diagnosis is required before performing electrical 
system service. Even where an obvious fault makes the replacement of a unit 
necessary, find out why the unit failed. If a problem is diagnosed correctly, 
unnecessary service is prevented, the time the vehicle is out of operation 
will be decreased and the service performed will be permanent. 

When performing charging system tests with a voltmeter, turn off all

ADJUSTMENTS

Regulator Output, Delco Generator

Remove the access pipe plug from the integral charging system. 

Turn the adjusting screw one or two notches clockwise to raise the 
voltage setting and one or two notches counterclockwise to lower the voltage 
setting. 

Replace the access pipe plug. 

After adjusting the setting, check for an improved battery condition 
over a service period of reasonable length. If adjusting the setting does not 
correct the battery condition, remove the generator for service. 

Remember that if the battery state of charge is low, the regulator may 
not be limiting the voltage, and turning the adjusting screw will show no 
change on the voltmeter. However, turning the adjusting screw will change the 
voltage setting to a new value, which will be indicated by the voltmeter when 
the battery state of charge increases.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Battery

 Removal 

Remove hex nuts and battery cables from battery terminals (negative 
first). 

Clean cable terminals with an acid neutralizing solution and terminal 
cleaning brush. 

Remove hold-down clamps. 

Test battery and determine if it should be: 

placed back in service

recharged before being placed back in service

replaced with a Motorcraft or equivalent battery

 WARNING: WHEN LIFTING A PLASTIC-CASED BATTERY, AVOID PUTTING EXCESSIVE PRESSURE 
ON THE END WALLS, WHICH CAN CAUSE ACID TO SPEW THROUGH THE VENT CAPS, CAUSING 
PERSONAL INJURY OR DAMAGE TO THE VEHICLE OR BATTERY. LIFT WITH A BATTERY 
CARRIER OR WITH YOUR HANDS ON OPPOSITE CORNERS. 

Remove battery using a suitable battery carrier.

 Installation 

Clean cable terminals and hold-down clamps with a wire brush. Replace 
all cables or parts that are worn or frayed. 

[FIGURE: J3887A.gif]

Clean battery tray with a wire brush and scraper. 

Place battery in tray with positive and negative terminals in the 
original positions. 

Install battery cable hex nuts and bolts. 

Assemble and tighten hold-down clamps so battery is secure. Do not 
overtighten.

Secure cables (positive first) to proper terminals. Do not overtighten. 
Apply a small quantity of Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent 
grease meeting Ford specification ESA-M1C75-B to terminals.

SERVICE PROCEDURES

Battery Charging

 WARNING: WEAR SAFETY GLASSES. BATTERY CHARGING CAN BE DANGEROUS. WHILE BEING 
CHARGED, THE BATTERY PRODUCES A POTENTIALLY EXPLOSIVE MIXTURE OF HYDROGEN AND 
OXYGEN GASSES. KEEP SPARKS, FLAMES AND LIGHTED CIGARETTES AWAY FROM BATTERIES. 
REMEMBER, IN CASE OF ACID CONTACT WITH SKIN, EYES OR CLOTHING, FLUSH 
IMMEDIATELY WITH LARGE AMOUNTS OF WATER. GET MEDICAL ATTENTION. 

 WARNING: BATTERIES NORMALLY PRODUCE EXPLOSIVE GASES THAT CAN CAUSE PERSONAL 
INJURY. DO NOT ALLOW FLAMES, SPARKS OR LIGHTED TOBACCO TO COME NEAR THE 
BATTERY. WHEN CHARGING OR WORKING NEAR A BATTERY, ALWAYS SHIELD YOUR FACE AND 
PROTECT YOUR EYES. ALWAYS PROVIDE VENTILATION. 

 WARNING: WHEN LIFTING A PLASTIC-CASED BATTERY, AVOID PUTTING EXCESSIVE PRESSURE 
ON THE END WALLS, WHICH CAN CAUSE ACID TO SPEW THROUGH THE VENT CAPS, CAUSING 
PERSONAL INJURY OR DAMAGE TO THE VEHICLE OR BATTERY. LIFT WITH A BATTERY 
CARRIER OR WITH YOUR HANDS ON OPPOSITE CORNERS. 

 WARNING: KEEP BATTERIES OUT OF REACH OF CHILDREN. BATTERIES CONTAIN SULFURIC 
ACID. AVOID CONTACT WITH SKIN, EYES, OR CLOTHING. SHIELD YOUR EYES WHEN 
WORKING NEAR THE BATTERY TO PROTECT AGAINST POSSIBLE SPLASHING OF THE ACID 
SOLUTION. IF ACID CONTACTS SKIN OR EYES, FLUSH IMMEDIATELY WITH WATER FOR A 
MINIMUM OF FIFTEEN MINUTES AND GET PROMPT MEDICAL ATTENTION. CALL A PHYSICIAN 
IMMEDIATELY. 

 NOTE: Perform battery tests to determine battery state of charge and capacity 
or ability to crank an engine. The ultimate result of these tests is to 
determine if the battery is good, needs recharging or must be replaced. 

Before attempting to test a battery, it is important to give the 
battery a thorough examination to determine if it has been damaged. 

Remove negative battery cable, then positive cable.

Check for dirty or corroded connections.

Clean terminals and clamps, if necessary.

Check for loose battery posts. If posts are loose, replace the battery.

Check battery cover by first removing hold-downs and shields.

Check for broken or cracked case or cover. Replace battery if case or 
cover is damaged.

Perform battery capacity test if current battery appears to be in good 
shape. Use a high rate discharge tester with a variable rate control or a 
fused rate tester with meter compensation for different electrical sizes. 
(Follow instructions supplied with tester.)

 NOTE: Recommended discharge rate at 27°C (81°
F): one-half the cold cranking amperage.

Voltage readings at 15 seconds for a good battery are shown on the 
following chart.

Approximate Battery Temperature

Minimum Load Voltage

9.6

21°C (70°F)

9.6

16°C (61°F)

9.5

-1°C (30°F)

9.1

-7°C (20°F)

8.9

-12°C (10°F)

8.7

-18°C (0°F)

8.5

Wait two minutes and check the open circuit voltage (OCV). Measure OCV 
with a digital voltmeter capable of reading 1/100 volt.

Battery is OK if minimum load voltage and OCV measure above 12.40. If 
battery measures below 12.40, charge for 20 minutes @ 35 amp. Repeat battery 
capacity test. If battery OCV measures above 12.40, but failed minimum load 
voltage, replace worn battery.

Before recharging a discharged battery, inspect and service the 
following conditions if they exist:

loose generator belt 

pinched or grounded generator or voltage regulator wiring harness 

loose harness connections at the generator or voltage regulator 

loose or corroded connections at battery, starter relay or engine ground 

excessive battery drain due to hood, glove compartment and courtesy 
lamps remaining on (damaged or misadjusted switch, glove compartment left 
open, etc.)

The state of charge for Motorcraft Heavy-Duty batteries is determined 
by comparing the measured battery terminal voltage with the Voltage/State of 
Charge table. 

 VOLTAGE/STATE OF CHARGE

Measured Voltage

State of Charge

Specific Gravity

12.30

25%

1.170

Cold batteries will not readily accept a charge. Therefore, batteries 
should be allowed to warm up to approximately 5°C (41°
F) before charging. This may require four to eight hours at 
room temperature depending on the initial temperature and battery size. 

A battery that has been completely discharged may be slow to accept a 
charge at the normal charger setting. When batteries are in this condition, 
charging can be started by using the dead battery switch on chargers so 
equipped. 

To determine whether a battery is accepting a charge, follow charger 
manufacturer's instructions for use of dead battery switch. If switch is the 
spring-loaded type, it should be held in the ON position for up to 3 minutes.

After releasing switch, and with charger still on, measure battery 
voltage. If it shows 12 volts or higher, the battery is accepting a charge and 
is capable of being recharged. However, it may require up to two hours of 
charging with batteries colder than 5°C (41°
F) before the charge rate is high enough to show on the charger ammeter. It 
has been found that all non-damaged batteries can be charged by this 
procedure. If a battery cannot be charged by this procedure, it must be 
replaced.

 Procedure to Charge a Known Good Battery 

 WARNING: WEAR SAFETY GLASSES. BATTERY CHARGING CAN BE DANGEROUS. WHILE BEING 
CHARGED, THE BATTERY PRODUCES A POTENTIALLY EXPLOSIVE MIXTURE OF HYDROGEN AND 
OXYGEN GASSES. KEEP SPARKS, FLAMES AND LIGHTED CIGARETTES AWAY FROM BATTERIES. 
REMEMBER, IN CASE OF ACID CONTACT WITH SKIN, EYES OR CLOTHING, FLUSH 
IMMEDIATELY WITH LARGE AMOUNTS OF WATER. GET MEDICAL ATTENTION. 

 NOTE: If excessive gassing or electrolyte spewing occurs during the charge, 
discontinue charging. The battery has reached serviceable charge. If the 
battery will not accept at least 5A after 20 minutes of charging, replace the 
battery. 

A rapid recharge procedure has been developed for recharging batteries 
that have passed the Battery Capacity Test and only need a recharge.

The battery can be rapidly recharged by using either of the following 
methods: 

Perform a two-hour charge using 20A constant current (manual setting on 
charger). 

Perform a two-hour charge using a constant potential (automatic setting 
on charger).

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Battery Cleaning 

Keeping the battery top clean and dry reduces the need for service and 
extends battery life. Make certain the cable clamps are tightly fastened to 
the battery posts. If corrosion is found, disconnect the cables and clean 
clamps and posts with a wire brush. Neutralize the corrosion with a solution 
of baking soda and water. After installing cables, apply a small quantity of 
Premium Long-Life Grease XG-1-C or -K or equivalent grease meeting Ford 
specification ESA-M1C75-B to each battery post to help prevent corrosion.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Tools 

Using properly designed tools can prevent damage to the battery, 
battery cables and hold-down bracketry. They can also reduce potential hazards 
to both technician and vehicle being serviced. 

Tools and equipment manufactured for servicing batteries have parts 
insulated to help prevent arcing. This feature can reduce potential component 
damage and fire hazards if a tool is dropped and shorts the battery terminals. 

 Pliers 

Battery pliers have jaws specifically designed to grip cable clamp 
bolts securely. Exercise care when removing or replacing the cable clamp bolts 
to make sure the battery terminal is not subjected to any excessive lateral or 
twisting forces. Such forces could cause major damage to the internal 
components of the battery and result in leakage at the terminals. 

 Clamp Puller 

Use a clamp puller to remove a cable clamp from the battery terminal. 
The jaws exert a force on the top of the battery post to remove the clamp. 
Proper use of this tool prevents the damaging lateral or twisting forces that 
result when using a pry bar or plier. 

[FIGURE: J3889A.gif]

 Clamp Spreader 

The spreader is used to expand the cable clamp after it has been 
removed from the terminal. The cable clamp can then be easily placed in its 
correct position on the terminal. 

[FIGURE: J3890A.gif]

 Terminal Cleaning Brush 

The terminal cleaning brush is designed to clean both the threaded 
battery terminal and the mating surface of the cable connector. 

[FIGURE: J3887A.gif]

 Carrier 

 WARNING: WHEN LIFTING A PLASTIC-CASED BATTERY, AVOID PUTTING EXCESSIVE PRESSURE 
ON THE END WALLS, WHICH CAN CAUSE ACID TO SPEW THROUGH THE VENT CAPS, CAUSING 
PERSONAL INJURY OR DAMAGE TO THE VEHICLE OR BATTERY. LIFT WITH A BATTERY 
CARRIER OR WITH YOUR HANDS ON OPPOSITE CORNERS. 

Use a suitable battery carrier for lifting and transporting the 
battery. The illustration shows a clamp-type carrier used to grip the 
sidewalls of the container just below the lip of the cover. The carrier is 
used on the sidewalls, rather than the end walls, since the sidewalls have 
additional strength from the inner cell partitions. This is particularly 
important with polypropylene-cased batteries that have flexible end walls.

Section 14-02A: Generator, Integral Regulator, 95 Ampere

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Charging System

The Motorcraft 95-ampere generator is belt-driven from the engine. 
Field current is supplied from the voltage regulator, mounted on the rear of 
the generator, to the rotating field of the generator through two brushes and 
two slip rings.

[FIGURE: J5683B.gif]

================================================================================
PAGE 3755
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 14-02A: Generator, Integral Regulator, 95 Ampere

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Generator

The generator produces power in the form of alternating current. The 
alternating current is rectified to direct current by six diodes. The voltage 
regulator automatically adjusts the generator field current to maintain the 
generator output voltage within prescribed limits to correctly charge the 
battery. The generator is self-current limiting. 

If equipped with a warning lamp, the regulator voltage control circuit 
is turned on when the ignition key is in RUN and voltage is applied to the 
voltage regulator I terminal through a resistor in the I circuit. When the 
ignition is off, the control circuit is turned off and no field current flows 
to the generator. 

On warning lamp-equipped vehicles, the warning lamp is connected across 
the terminals of a 420-ohm resistor at the instrument cluster. Current passes 
through the warning lamp when the key is in RUN and there is no voltage at 
terminal S. When voltage at S rises to a preset value, the voltage regulator 
switching circuits stop the flow of current into terminal I and the lamp turns 
off. 

System voltage is sensed and generator field current is drawn through 
terminal A. The voltage regulator switching circuits will turn the warning 
lamp on, indicating a system fault if terminal A voltage is excessively high 
or if the terminal S voltage signal is abnormal. 

A fuse link is included in the charging system wiring harness on all 
models to prevent damage to the wiring harness and generator if the wiring 
harness should become grounded, or if a booster battery is connected to the 
charging system with the wrong polarity. Refer to Electrical and Vacuum 
Troubleshooting Manual for fuse link description.

================================================================================
PAGE 3756
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 14-02A: Generator, Integral Regulator, 95 Ampere

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Voltage Regulator

When the engine is started, the following conditions exist:

Generator begins to generate alternating current (AC).

The alternating current (AC) is converted to direct current (DC) by the 
rectifier.

Current is supplied through the vehicle's system through the output 
stud located on the rear of the generator.

Generator output current is determined by the voltage at the A circuit 
(battery sense voltage).

A circuit voltage is compared to a set voltage internal to the voltage 
regulator.

Voltage regulator controls the generator field current to maintain 
proper generator output.

Set voltage will vary with temperature.

Set voltage is typically higher in the winter.

Set voltage is typically lower in the summer.

Varying set voltage allows for better recharge in the winter. 

Varying set voltage reduces the chance of overcharging the battery in 
summer.

================================================================================
PAGE 3757
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 14-02A: Generator, Integral Regulator, 95 Ampere

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Generator Circuit

 Circuit Description 

 Battery Positive Voltage (B+) Output 

The generator output is supplied through the battery positive voltage (B+
) output connection to the battery and electrical system.

 I Circuit 

The I circuit, or ignition circuit, is used to turn on the voltage 
regulator. This circuit is powered up with the ignition switch in the RUN 
position. This circuit is also used to turn on the charge indicator lamp if 
there is a fault in the charging system operation or associated wiring circuits.

 A Circuit 

The A circuit, or battery sense circuit, is used to sense battery 
voltage. This voltage is used by the voltage regulator to determine the 
generator output. This circuit also is used to supply power to the generator 
field coil. This circuit is hot at all times. The circuit is also connected to 
the load distribution point and is a protected circuit.

 S Circuit 

The S circuit, or stator circuit, is used to feed back a voltage signal 
from the generator to the voltage regulator. This voltage, typically half 
battery voltage, is used by the voltage regulator to turn off the charge 
indicator lamp.

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Belt Tension Gauge

T63L-8620-A

Disconnect battery ground cable. 

Disconnect the wire harness attachments to the generator assembly. Pull 
the two connectors straight out. 

Loosen the generator pivot bolt. Remove the adjustment arm bolt from 
the generator. 

Disengage the generator drive belt from the generator pulley. 

Remove the generator pivot bolt and generator assembly. 

 Installation 

Position the generator assembly on the engine. 

Install the generator pivot and adjuster arm bolts, but do not tighten 
the bolts until the belt is tensioned. 

Connect the wiring harness to the generator assembly. Push the two 
connectors straight in. 

Install the drive belt over the generator pulley. 

Adjust the belt tension and tighten the adjuster and pivot bolts to 
specification. Check belt tension using Belt Tension Gauge T63L-8620-A or 
Rotunda Belt Tension Gauge 014-R1056 or equivalent. Apply pressure to

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Generator

Rotate the front bearing on the drive end of the rotor shaft. Check for 
any scraping noise, looseness or roughness. Look for excessive lubricant 
leakage. If any of these conditions exist and wiping down with clean cloth or 
blowing off with compressed air does not correct the condition, replace the 
generator. 

Check the pulley and fan for excessive looseness on the rotor shaft and 
for cracks or other damage. Replace any pulley or fan that is loose, cracked 
or bent. 

Check both the front and rear housings for cracks, particularly in the 
webbed areas at the mounting ear. Replace generator if housing is damaged or 
cracked. 

 Generator Brushes 

Replace the brushes if they are worn shorter than 6.35 mm (1/4 inch) 
from the shunt.

Section 14-02B: Generator, 100 and 115 Ampere Delco

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Charging System

The electrical charging system is a negative ground system consisting 
of a generator, voltage regulator, charge indicator lamp (optional), storage 
battery, wiring and cables. Refer to the Electrical 
and Vacuum Troubleshooting Manual for schematics and locations of components and wiring.

[FIGURE: J6211B.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

10334

Slip Ring End (SRE) Housing

2

10336

Stator

3

10333

Drive End (DE) Housing

4

—

Adjustment Lug (Part of 10346)

5

10A310

Fan

6

10344

Pulley

7

—

Mounting Lugs (Part of 10346)

The only difference between the 100 and 115 ampere generators is the 
drive pulleys installed on each. The 100 and 115 ampere generators are 
one-wire systems (the minimum number of lead wire connections necessary at the 
generator for proper operation). With a one-wire system, there is residual 
magnetism in the rotor at start-up. As the generator rotor begins turning, the 
residual fields around the rotor induce voltages in the stator windings. The 
faster the rotor turns, the higher the voltage induced in the stator windings 

Once the speed and output are up to specification, the voltage 
available at the diode trio becomes sufficient to supply field current for 
normal operations. If an indicator light is connected in series with the I 
terminal, the light will be on while the generator comes up to speed. The 
indicator lamp will light due to a voltage imbalance between the battery 
voltage on one side of the light and system voltage coming from the diode trio 
on the other side of the light. Once the generator output voltage equals the 
battery voltage, the voltages are balanced on both sides of the indicator 
light. With no difference in potential, the light turns off.

Once the system voltage exceeds 14 volts, the voltage regulator will 
turn off the field current to prevent the voltage from rising any higher. This 
causes the magnetic field around the rotor to collapse, which reduces the 
generator output voltage. As the voltage falls below the battery voltage, the 
voltage regulator turns the field current back on, which allows the magnetic 
field to build up again. This cycle is repeated many times a second, so 
quickly that the output voltage is steady for all practical purposes and the 
indicator light cannot turn on and off fast enough to keep pace and so stays 
off unless a prolonged voltage imbalance should occur. The system voltage is 
used to control the output, which eliminates the need for extra sense wiring.

[FIGURE: J6212A.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Generator

The 21-SI series Delcotron® generator is a 
high-output integral charging system with built-in rectifier and voltage 
regulator that produces DC current. The 21-SI generator can be operated in 
either a clockwise or counterclockwise direction at continuous speeds of up to 
10,000 rpm (intermittent speeds of up to 12,000 rpm are also acceptable). The 
ambient temperature range for proper operation is -34°C to +
93°C (-30°F to +
200°F).

The B+ terminal has 1/4-inch threads, as does the ground 
terminal hole.

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Voltage Regulator

The voltage regulator is a solid-state integrated circuit-type with a 
nominal regulated voltage setting of 14.0 volts. In addition, the voltage 
regulator features flat temperature compensation, low parasitic draw and low 
turn-on speed with improved radio frequency interference (RFI) suppression 
capability and load dump protection from voltage spikes. The voltage regulator 
limits system voltage by switching the ground circuit for the rotor field on 
and off.

PAGE 3771
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 14-02B: Generator, 100 and 115 Ampere Delco

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Generator Circuit

 Circuit Description 

The generator output or B+ terminal is connected to the 
battery positive terminal. The ground path is through the generator housing 
and mounting back to the battery negative terminal. When the voltage regulator 
switches the ground circuit on, the battery voltage passes through the 
rectifier bridge and into a diode trio, which passes the voltage to the rotor 
through a brush and slip ring assembly located on the rotor shaft. This will 
cause a magnetic field to build up around the rotor windings. The voltage 
regulator also receives battery voltage that it uses to compare with the 
voltage produced by the generator. When the generator voltage exceeds 14 
volts, the voltage regulator switches off the ground circuit going to the 
rotor, which collapses its field and reduces the output momentarily.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Charging System

The electrical charging system is a negative ground system consisting 
of a generator, voltage regulator, storage battery, wiring and cables. Refer 
to the Electrical and Vacuum Troubleshooting 
Manual for schematics and locations of components and wiring.

The 130-ampere generator is a one-wire system (the minimum number of 
lead wire connections necessary at the generator for proper operation). With a 
one-wire system, there is residual magnetism in the rotor at start-up. As the 
generator rotor begins turning, the residual fields around the rotor induce 
voltages in the stator windings. The faster the rotor turns, the higher the 
voltage induced in the stator windings.

Once the system voltage exceeds 13.5-13.7 volts, the voltage regulator 
will turn off the field current to prevent the voltage from rising any higher. 
This causes the magnetic field around the rotor to collapse, which reduces the 
generator output voltage. As the voltage falls below the voltage regulator 
setting, the voltage regulator turns the field current back on, which allows 
the magnetic field to build up again. This cycle is repeated many times a 
second, so quickly that the output voltage is steady for all practical 
purposes. The system voltage is used to control the output, which eliminates 
the need for extra sense wiring.

================================================================================
PAGE 3779
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 14-02C: Generator, 130 Ampere Prestolite

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Generator

The Prestolite 130-ampere generator is a self-current limiting unit 
with a fully adjustable voltage regulator. 

The generator features sealed ball bearings with rotor slip rings and 
generator brush and terminal holders that are in a sealed housing mounted on 
the slip ring end housing. Six generator diodes mounted in heat sinks convert 
alternating current from the delta wound stator into direct current. A radio 
voltage regulator capacitor connected between the heat sinks assists in 
suppressing transient voltage spikes that could possibly damage the generator 
diodes.

[FIGURE: J5694A.gif]

The generator brush and terminal holders and voltage regulator are 
located in a waterproof housing that can be removed for replacement or 
inspection without disassembling the generator.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Generator

 WARNING: HYDROGEN AND OXYGEN GASES ARE PRODUCED DURING NORMAL BATTERY OPERATION. 
THIS GAS MIXTURE CAN EXPLODE IF FLAMES, SPARKS OR LIGHTED SUBSTANCES ARE 
BROUGHT NEAR THE BATTERY. WHEN CHARGING OR USING A BATTERY IN AN ENCLOSED 
SPACE, ALWAYS PROVIDE VENTILATION AND SHIELD YOUR EYES. 

 WARNING: KEEP BATTERIES OUT OF REACH OF CHILDREN. BATTERIES CONTAIN SULFURIC 
ACID. AVOID CONTACT WITH SKIN, EYES OR CLOTHING. ALSO, SHIELD YOUR EYES WHEN 
WORKING NEAR THE BATTERY TO PROTECT AGAINST POSSIBLE SPLASHING OF THE ACID 
SOLUTION. IN CASE OF ACID CONTACT WITH SKIN, EYES OR CLOTHING, FLUSH 
IMMEDIATELY WITH WATER FOR A MINIMUM OF FIFTEEN MINUTES. IF ACID IS SWALLOWED, 
DRINK LARGE QUANTITIES OF MILK OR WATER, FOLLOWED BY MILK OF MAGNESIA, A 
BEATEN EGG, OR VEGETABLE OIL. CALL A PHYSICIAN IMMEDIATELY.

 Removal

Remove the lead from the voltage regulator terminal. 

Remove the three screws retaining the voltage regulator to the generator.
