Replace generator brush and terminal holders less than 4.76 mm (0.188 
inch) in length.

[FIGURE: J43461A.gif]

 Installation 

Before installing the voltage regulator, insert the outer generator 
brush and terminal holder into the housing and compress the generator brush 
spring using a small screwdriver or similar tool. 

 NOTE: A suitable pin can be made using drill rod or a 1/32-inch diameter 
drill. 

While holding the generator brush spring compressed, insert a pin 
through the top hole in the rear of the housing so the generator brush spring 
is held in a compressed position. 

Install and compress remaining generator brush and terminal holder in a 
similar manner. 

Hold the generator brush springs in a compressed position by pushing 
the pin farther into the brush housing.

[FIGURE: J43471A.gif]

Slowly push the voltage regulator into the brush housing making sure 
the respective screws go through the positive and negative jumpers. 

Install the voltage regulator mounting screws and hand-tighten. 

 CAUTION: Do not tighten nuts with brush pin in place; damage to the voltage 
regulator will result.

(10-12 lb-in).

Install the lead to the voltage regulator terminal.

Connect the battery ground cable.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Generator 

 Disassembly 

Hold generator pulley with a strap wrench and remove shaft nut with an 
impact gun. Remove generator pulley, generator fan, Woodruff key, and 
generator fan/pulley spacer.

Remove the 5/16-18 and 1/4-20 nuts from the positive and negative 
generator output terminals. 

 NOTE: Due to the application of Loctite® to the four brush 
housing screws, heat might need to be applied to assist in removing the 
screws. Use a large soldering iron or gun (300 to 500 watts). Hold the iron on 
each screw head for 40-50 seconds (a drop of solder on the iron's tip will 
help heat transfer). After applying heat to the screw head, remove immediately 
with a screwdriver. 

Remove the four 8-32 screws holding the generator brush holder in 
place. Remove assembly. 

Remove three self-locking nuts and through-bolts. 

 NOTE: If drive end housing binds on stator and coil, loosen by tapping gently 
on mounting ear with fiber hammer. Make sure drive end housing separates from 
stator and coil, and that stator and coil remains attached to slip ring end 
housing to avoid damage to stator leads. 

Remove generator rotor and drive end housing from stator and coil and 
slip ring end housing. 

Remove three nuts securing stator leads to terminals and remove stator 
and coil.

Remove nuts from positive and negative output terminal bolts. Remove 
bolts.

Remove hex screws. 

Remove radio voltage regulator capacitor connected between the heat 
sinks. 

Remove two screws, lockwashers, guard washers and insulating washers 
retaining lower end of heat sinks. 

Noting location of insulating washers and bushings, remove heat sinks. 

 NOTE: There are two bushings in each terminal hole. 

Remove terminal stud insulating washers from housing.

Using a puller or arbor press, remove the rear bearing from the

Remove four screws and bearing retainer. Press bearing out of drive end

 Slip Ring Bearing Replacement 

With a soldering iron, remove the wire connecting the generator rotor 
to the outside rotor slip ring.

Bend unsoldered wire so it is parallel to the shaft. 

Unsolder the wire from the inside rotor slip ring.

With a gear puller or an arbor press, pull off the rotor slip ring and 
the insulation washer. 

 NOTE: While replacing the bearing keep the new rotor slip ring in a warm 
place so it will press on easily without cracking. 

Remove the bearing using a gear puller; an arbor press can also be used 
with fixture plates behind the bearing. 

Install the new bearing using a pipe or tube to press on the inner race 
of bearing. 

After the new bearing has been pressed on the rotor shaft, press on the 
new rotor slip rings, making sure the slot lines up with the slot in the 
shaft. 

Press new rotor slip rings on the shaft. Apply enough pressure to 
prevent the insulation washer from turning all the way to the shoulder. 

Solder the leads of the generator rotor to new rotor slip rings.

 NOTE: Concentricity of the rotor slip ring with the bearing surfaces of the 
shaft should be held to within 0.05 mm (0.002 inch) total indicator reading. 

Put the generator rotor in a lathe. Take a light cut from the 
circumference of rotor slip rings so they are concentric with the shaft. 

 Assembly 

Place slip ring end of rotor shaft in an arbor press, making sure rotor 
slip rings are not damaged. 

Press the rear housing on rotor shaft. Use a sleeve or pipe so pressure 
is applied on rear bearing inner race only. 

Place positive and negative rectifiers in the slip ring end housing and 
install the lower mounting screws. Do not tighten screws at this time.

Install positive and negative output terminals as shown.

Tighten two screws on bottom of the two rectifier assemblies to

Install radio voltage regulator capacitor and capacitor terminals to 
bottom of rectifiers with self-tapping screws. Clean paint from around holes 
before installing leads. 

Place a positive rectifier terminal and a negative rectifier terminal 
on each of the three terminal screws on the terminal board. Route the leads as 
shown.

[FIGURE: J47271A.gif]

Inspect O-ring in slip ring end housing bearing bore and replace if 
necessary. 

Place the stator and coil on the slip ring end housing. Place the 
stator leads on the three terminal board screws. 

Make sure assembly screw holes in the stator and coil and slip ring end 
housing are aligned. 

Install rectifier leads and stator leads with self-locking nuts. 

Support the slip ring end housing on flat plates in an arbor press. 

Press the slip ring end bearing into slip ring end housing by pressing 
on the rotor shaft. 

Align assembly screw holes in the slip ring end housing, stator and 
coil and the drive end housing. 

Install three assembly screws and fasten generator together with 
plastic stop nuts tightened to 5-6 Nm (45-50 lb-in). 

Install generator brush holder with four No. 8 round head screws. Apply 
Threadlock® and Sealer EOAZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification WSK-M2G315-A5 (Type II). Make sure sealing ring is properly 
installed between the generator brush holder and the slip ring end housing. 

Press generator brush and terminal holders in brush openings and 
temporarily pin into place with a 1/32-inch diameter drill or a piece of stiff 
wire. 

Install voltage regulator, Belleville washers and jumpers.

Remove pin to release generator brush spring.

Tighten screws to secure the voltage regulator to generator brush holder.

Install jumpers to negative and positive output terminals and to 
voltage regulator terminals with nuts and lockwashers.

[FIGURE: J4348B.gif]

Install lead to voltage regulator terminal with No. 10 nut and 
lockwasher. 

Slide generator fan/pulley spacer on shaft and install woodruff key, 
generator fan, generator pulley, and generator pulley nut. Hold the generator 
pulley with a strap wrench and tighten nut to 26-30 Nm (19-22 
lb-ft). 

Install the generator on the vehicle.

After the battery has been connected, momentarily flash the field by 
connecting a jumper between the charge indicator light terminal and the 
generator positive output terminal. This will restore residual magnetism that 
may have been weakened by handling or service procedures.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Generator

Clean the generator housing with particular care around the vents. Use 
care not to push dirt or debris into the generator through the air vents. Do 
not use solvents unless the generator is disassembled. Solvent runoff may 
carry dirt into the generator.

Inspect the generator for broken or cracked mounting lugs. Inspect for 
loose mounting bolts, loose wires and cracked or burned insulation. Service or 
replace as necessary.

 Generator Components 

The internal parts of the generator may be cleaned with a mild solvent 
and wiped with a soft cloth. Inspect for broken or cracked parts, cracked, 
broken or missing insulation. Service or replace as necessary.

Do not submerge the generator bearings in solvent. The solvent may 
dissolve the lubricant and cause damage if the bearings are installed.

Voltage Regulator

the generator, the voltage regulator may be cleaned with a mild solvent and 
dried completely. Inspect for broken or cracked parts or broken, cracked or 
missing insulation. Service or replace as necessary.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Radio Reception

 Antenna Position 

The AM and FM stereo antenna has a range of about 32 km (20 miles) 
before interference noises are heard. This means that in concern areas with 
tall buildings or hills, select the strongest possible station. The electronic 
radio automatically tunes to the center of any given station, eliminating the 
need for manual fine tuning.

 Antennas and Mobility 

Although an automotive radio antenna will give outstanding mobile 
reception, it cannot provide the continuous reception of home audio 
components. The home receiver is not limited by the vehicle operating 
characteristics and certain geographical effects as is the mobile unit. For 
example, for the best FM reception, the automotive antenna should be designed 
like a TV antenna and pointed in the direction of the station. The best AM 
antenna is a long piece of wire; the higher the wire, the better the 
reception. However, because of design necessity, the automotive antenna is 
restricted in size, height and direction and must receive both AM and FM 
stations. This means that a limited amount of the station's signal reaches the 
vehicle radio.

 Tuning 

Fine tuning is not required for the radio chassis. The electronic radio 
chassis automatically tunes the radio chassis to the center of the station 
where it will obtain minimum noise and best possible reception.

 Tone Control 

Favoring the rear radio speakers in noisy areas will help to reduce 
noise.

 FM Flutter 

Flutter can best be described as repeated pops and hissing bursts heard 
in the radio speaker, during an otherwise good broadcast. Usually this 
condition exists while traveling in the fringe area of the station. Flutter 
will become more severe beyond approximately 40 km (25 miles) of the station. 
The signal loss becomes greater away from the station, until finally noise 
takes over and reception becomes impossible. Flutter can also be noticed near 
the station because of the line-of-sight characteristics of FM radio waves. 
This condition can occur when a building or large structure is between the 
radio receiver and the station being received. Some of the FM signal bends 
around the building, but certain spots have almost no signal. Some of these 
signal losses are only a few inches wide and if the vehicle is parked in one 
of these dead spots, you will only hear noise from the radio speaker. After 
moving out of the shadow of the structure, the station will return to normal. 
Flutter will not occur on AM because the AM radio waves are much longer than 
FM waves.

 FM Multi-Path Cancellation 

Another effect caused by the line-of-sight characteristics is called 
cancellation. This condition exists when the radio waves are reflected from 
objects or structures. The noise produced by cancellation is similar to 
flutter, with the addition of distortion in the program. A more familiar 
description of cancellation is its similarity to the multiple ghosts and 
picture jumping that occurs on television when a low flying plane passes. The 
same condition exists in the vehicle, except that the vehicle is moving and 
the reflecting structure is stationary. The reflected signal cancels the 
normal signal, causing the antenna to pick up noise and distortion. 
Cancellation effects are most prominent in metropolitan areas, but can also 
become quite severe in hilly terrain and low-lying roadways.

 FM Strong Signal Capture and AM Overloading 

FM capture is an unusual condition that occurs when traveling in the 
vicinity of a broadcast tower. If listening to a weak FM station when passing 
the broadcast tower, a stronger station can interfere without changing the 
tuning control. When passing the tower, the station may switch back and forth 
a few times before returning to the station originally tuned. When several 
broadcast towers are present (common in metropolitan areas) several stations 
can overload the receiver resulting in considerable station changing, mixing 
and distortion. Fortunately, this condition is localized and it will not harm 
the receiver. Some overloading can also be noticed on AM, but usually to a 
lesser degree.

 Receiving FM Stereo 

Because more data is carried in the FM stereo waves than in the 
monaural FM broadcasts, flutter, cancellation and capture are even more 
noticeable. The FM stereo noise-free broadcast range is approximately 8 km (5 
miles) less than that received with the monaural FM radio. The AM/FM stereo 
radio might never encounter any of these troublesome conditions as they are 
more prominent in metropolitan areas, hilly terrain and low-lying roadways. 
However, when diagnosing FM stereo concerns, it is recommended to tune to the 
strongest FM stereo station.

 Stereo Indicator Inoperative or Flickering (AM and FM Reception Are OK) 

A weak or distant signal can cause the stereo indicator to flicker. 
Tune radio to a nearby FM stereo station. If reception is good, but stereo 
indicator is still intermittent, remove radio chassis for service.

 Radio Tests 

Internal diagnostic examination of the radio chassis should be left to 
the authorized radio service center. However, the automotive technician should 
be able to analyze and isolate radio chassis reception conditions to the 
proper area or component causing the condition. All radio chassis conditions 
can be isolated to one of five general areas:

antenna system

radio chassis

speaker system

radio noise suppression equipment

radio amplifier

 Interfering Noises 

The vehicle ignition system is a possible source of radio interference. 
This high-voltage switching system produces a radio frequency electromagnetic 
field that radiates at AM, FM and CB frequencies. Although components have 
been designed into the vehicle to minimize this concern, the noise is more 
noticeable if the radio is tuned slightly off-channel when listening to FM 
programs. Vehicle electrical accessories and owner add-on accessories can also 
contribute to radio interference. Furthermore, there are many noise sources 
which are external to the vehicle. These include power lines, communication 
systems, ignition systems of other vehicles, neon signs, etc.

Noise or static can result from many causes. Three of the most common 
sources of radio noise are ignition noise, missing or poor grounds and missing 
or damaged noise suppression components.

 Missing or Poor Grounds 

Check bond strap grounding effectiveness by wedging a large file 
between metal parts, such as between the tail pipe and body, or between the 
fender and frame, to ensure proper ground while the radio chassis is playing 
and the engine is running. Listen for a decrease in the objectionable radio 
noise. If a reduction in radio noise is noted, first try tightening body and 
exhaust system clamps and brackets. Then, if necessary, install a new bond 
strap between the two metal parts to ensure proper ground.

 Missing or Damaged Noise Suppression Components 

Refer to the description for Missing or Poor Grounds.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Audio Systems

 Inspection and Verification 

 NOTE: Many customers do not understand the limitations of FM reception. Refer 
the customer to the owner guide for information about the limitations of FM 
radio performance.

If AM reception is extremely poor and FM reception drifts or appears to 
have trouble holding stations, make sure the antenna and antenna connectors 
are properly mated. If the antenna connectors are properly mated but the 
reception is still poor, refer to the symptom chart in this section.

If only FM reception is poor, it is unlikely that the antenna is at 
fault. Remove the radio chassis for service.

If the tape player will not accept cartridge, eats tape, plays too fast 
or too slow, etc., and AM and FM are operating properly, check operation of 
the tape player by using a known good cassette/cartridge. 

If the condition is not corrected by the substitution of a known good 
cassette/cartridge, the radio chassis must be removed and sent to an 
authorized service facility for service.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Cassette Tape Player Head

 CAUTION: Excess alcohol on the swab may run down the capstan and damage the 
bearings. Do not use carbon tetrachloride. 

The playback head and capstan in the tape player can accumulate tape 
coating residue (oxide) as the tape passes over the head. This accumulation 
needs to be periodically removed, as part of normal maintenance, if it causes 
weak or wavering sound. It is recommended, for best performance, that the 
player be cleaned every 10 to 12 hours of playing time using a Ford cassette 
player cleaning cartridge or equivalent. An alternate method of cleaning can 
be done by holding the player door open and cleaning the playback head with a 
cotton swab slightly moistened with alcohol. To clean the capstan, trip the 
on-off switch at the slot with eraser end of a pencil and hold the 
alcohol-moistened swab against the rotating capstan.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Antenna

The FM stereo antenna has a range of about 32 km (20 miles) before 
interference noises are heard. This means that in areas with tall buildings or 
hills, it is necessary to select the strongest possible station.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Antenna 

 Removal 

Remove antenna lead-in cable from back of radio. Remove cable from 
retaining clips that route cable to roof-mounted antenna mast assembly. 

Remove mounting cover. 

Have an assistant hold antenna cable so that cable stud does not rotate 
when nut is removed. Remove nut, lockwasher, and antenna mast assembly. 
Inspect for corrosion. Clean connections, if necessary. 

Remove antenna base and antenna gasket from top surface of cab exterior. 

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Tighten nut securing antenna mast to 5-6 Nm (44-55 
lb-in).

[FIGURE: K14185B.gif]

Section 17-01: Lighting, Exterior

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Headlamps 

Two rectangular halogen headlamps are used. Each of these sealed beams 
has two filaments, one for high beam and one for low beam. Headlamps are 
controlled by the headlamp switch on the instrument panel. High beam/low beam 
selection is located on the turn signal stalk on the steering column. 

 Daytime Running Lamps 

Refer to Section 17-04 .

================================================================================
PAGE 3815
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 17-01: Lighting, Exterior

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Headlamp Switch 

The headlamp switch is a combination, three-position switch that 
controls the circuits to the headlamps and exterior lamps (except stoplamps 
and turn signal/hazard warning lamps and backup lamps). Circuits are connected 
to the switch by a molded connector. 

The headlamp switch is powered through a fuse link at the fuse box. The 
fuse link is powered directly with battery voltage. Headlamp circuits on the 
output side of the headlamp switch feed the headlamp dimmer switch, which 
feeds the headlamps, and the exterior lighting relay, which feeds the fuse 
panel that distributes power to the exterior lamps. 

 Panel Dim Switch 

The instrument cluster illumination can be dimmed using the panel dim 
switch.

[FIGURE: K24538A.gif]

================================================================================
PAGE 3816
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 17-01: Lighting, Exterior

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Stoplight Switch 

The stoplight switch is located at the left, lower rear of the cab on 
vehicles equipped with the tractor package, and at the left, lower front of 
the cab on trucks. The switch is threaded into a pressure port of the air 
pressure manifold. 

[FIGURE: K16609A.gif]

================================================================================
PAGE 3817
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 17-01: Lighting, Exterior

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Lamps — Parking, Tail/Marker

 Parking 

The parking lamp system includes all external lamps except the 
stoplamps, turn signal lamps, backup lamps and headlamps. The parking lamps 
are actuated when the headlamp switch is in the second or third position. 

[FIGURE: K91061C.gif]

 Tail 

The rear stoplamps are operated by two air pressure switches fitted on 
the output side of the control valve. When the foot brake is applied, the 
control valve is actuated and air pressure in each of the dual lines activates 
the air pressure switches. The air pressure switches are wired in parallel 
circuit. 

[FIGURE: K9102D.gif]

 Marker 

The marker lamps are operated by placing the three-position headlamp 
switch in either the second or third (headlamps ON) position. The marker lamps 
can be turned off momentarily (blinked) by pressing the marker lamp blink 
switch. 

[FIGURE: K91071A.gif]

[FIGURE: K9104B.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Lamps, License

The stop/tail/backup lamp is illuminated when the headlamp switch is in 
the PARK or HEAD position. A clear shield at the bottom of the left lamp 
allows illumination of the license plate.

================================================================================
PAGE 3819
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 17-01: Lighting, Exterior

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Lamps, Backup 

The backup lamps are actuated by a lock cylinder on the transmission. 
When the ignition switch lock cylinder is in the RUN or START position and the 
transmission is placed in REVERSE, a switch on the transmission is actuated 
and illuminates the backup lamps. The backup lamp is contained in the center 
of the rear lamp assembly.

================================================================================
PAGE 3820
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 17-01: Lighting, Exterior

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Turn Signals 

The left switch on the steering column controls the high-low beam 
selection of the headlamps (pull switch arm toward driver and release). This 
switch also controls the horn (push end of knob toward steering column) and 
turn signal (lift upward or press downward for direction). An instrument panel 
lamp indicates high-beam operation when lamps are on, and corresponding signal 
lamps of the panel flash to signal a turn. 

[FIGURE: K91131B.gif]

Section 17-01: Lighting, Exterior

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Lamps, Roof Marker

The five lamps mounted on the roof of the vehicle are on whenever the 
headlamp switch is in the PARK or HEADLAMP position.

The circuit includes a blink switch. The rocker-type switch is located 
in the left switch bank. When the switch is pressed the roof marker lamps are 
turned off. When released, the switch returns to the ON position.

[FIGURE: K22966A.gif]

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Hazard Warning Flasher Switch 

The hazard warning flasher switch is located in the center portion of 
the instrument panel, on the right side of the steering column. The front and 
rear turn signal lamps flash intermittently when the hazard warning flasher 
switch is actuated. 

[FIGURE: K9114D.gif]

Indicator Flasher

located in the upper left of the fuse panel.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Lighting, Exterior

 Inspection and Verification, General 

Common point diagnosis should be used to isolate a problem in a 
multi-load circuit (a circuit with more than one operating component) without 
making any tests. If one system functions properly but another does not, the 
problem is in the part of the circuit unique to the inoperative system. 

If more than one circuit does not operate, check for blown fuses. 

Before performing any lighting system tests, make sure the battery is 
in a fully charged condition and all battery cable connections are clean and 
tight. 

A visual inspection is an important part of the lighting system test. 
Check for wires with frayed or damaged insulation, loose connections and 
improper wiring harness routing.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Headlamps

 Inspection and Verification 

Visually inspect the components of the headlamp system.

Shake the wiring harness. Look for obvious signs of shorts, opens or 
damage.

If the fault is not visually evident, verify condition and refer to the 
following symptom chart.

Correct any problems found by the visual inspection before performing 
further tests of the lighting system. For example, a loose ground strap 
between the engine and body dash panel can cause an intermittent operation of 
the lamps and gauges. Inspect and tighten (if necessary) the ground strap 
retaining screws at the back of the engine and the body dash panel.

Refer to the Electrical and Vacuum Troubleshooting Manual for the

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Headlamp Switch 

 Removal 

Disconnect battery ground cable. 

Turn lock screws and open left instrument cluster. 

Disconnect plug on back of light switch. 

Squeeze tabs on light switch and pull switch out front of instrument 
cluster panel. 

 Installation 

Push light switch into instrument cluster panel. 

Plug in connector to light switch. 

Close instrument cluster panel and latch lock screws. 

Connect battery ground cable and check headlamp switch operation.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Turn Signal/High Beam Switch

 Removal 

Position vehicle so that wheels are in a straight-ahead position. 

Make sure dimmer switch is in low beam position and turn signal 
position is neutral. Do not change these switch positions during switch removal.

Apply parking brake and disconnect battery ground cable. 

 NOTE: Scribe an arrow on the steering shaft, and a small mark on the steering 
wheel that coincides with the first mark. This is done to ensure correct 
positioning of the steering wheel when installing. 

Remove steering wheel center cap. 

Remove steering wheel retaining nut and remove steering wheel. 

 NOTE: One screw must be removed from the underside of the mounting. 

Remove steering column securing screws. Separate shrouds, and remove. 

Remove multi-plug connector and securing screws. 

Remove self-cancelling collar and switch as a single unit by carefully 
lifting them both from steering shaft. 

 Dimmer Switch 

[FIGURE: K9068D.gif]

 Installation 

Install self-cancelling collar/switch as a single unit. Make sure 
self-cancelling collar is aligned properly with steering shaft recess. 

[FIGURE: K90691A.gif]

Align switch and install securing screws. 

Connect multi-plug connector. Make sure that the wiring is not twisted 
and does not restrict switch operation. 

Hold each steering column shroud in place and install securing screws. 

Align mark on steering wheel with mark on the steering shaft and 
position wheel onto shaft. 

Install steering wheel retaining nut and install steering wheel center 
cap.

Connect battery ground cable and release the parking brake. Check 
dimmer switch operation.

ADJUSTMENTS

Headlamp 

 Setup Requirements 

Before making any headlamp adjustments, perform the following 
preparatory steps: 

Remove ice or mud from underhood assembly fender area (or wheel 
housing). 

Make sure all tires are inflated to recommended pressures. 

Check springs for sag or broken leaves. 

Take into consideration incorrect wheel alignment or improper tracking 
of the rear axle. 

Make sure there is no load in vehicle other than fuel tank one-half 
full. 

Clean lenses and aiming pads. 

Check for bulb burn-out and proper beam switching. 

Make sure light output is well toward normal new lamp value. 

Park vehicle on a level floor, perpendicular to aiming surface, at a 
distance of 7.62 m (25.0 ft) from the flat white aiming screen. 

 NOTE: The aiming screen must be perpendicular to floor within ±
 5 degrees.

Make headlamp aim adjustment with Rotunda Headlamp Aiming Kit 196-00001 
or equivalent. Use the most recent instructions. 

The kit equipment can be calibrated to accommodate a slight slope in 
floor. 

 Headlamp Aim Adjustments, Setup Requirements

 Procedure for Adjustment 

The high beam is automatically adjusted when the low beam is adjusted. 

Always bring each beam into final position by turning adjusting screws 
clockwise so that headlamp will be held against the tension springs when the 
operation is completed. 

When setup requirements are satisfied, perform the following steps for 
headlamp adjustment. 

Right headlamp: Cover left headlamp and turn headlamps on, in low beam 
position. 

Horizontal adjustment: Turn adjustment screw (B) at left of sealed beam 
retainer ring: 

CLOCKWISE moves the beam to the right. 

COUNTERCLOCKWISE moves the beam to the left. 

[FIGURE: K90631A.gif]

Vertical adjustment: Turn adjustment screw (A) at top of sealed beam 
retainer ring: 

CLOCKWISE moves the beam upward. 

COUNTERCLOCKWISE moves the beam downward. 

Turn off headlamps, allow lamps to cool, and remove left headlamp cover. 

Left headlamps: Cover the right headlamp and turn headlamps on, in low 
beam position. 

Horizontal adjustment: Turn adjustment screw (C) at right of sealed 
beam retainer ring: 

CLOCKWISE moves the beam to the left. 

COUNTERCLOCKWISE moves the beam to the right. 

[FIGURE: K90641A.gif]

Vertical adjustment: Turn adjustment screw (A) at top of the sealed 
beam retainer ring: 

CLOCKWISE moves the beam upward. 

COUNTERCLOCKWISE moves the beam downward. 

Turn off headlamps, allow lamps to cool, and remove right headlamp 
cover.

ADJUSTMENTS

Headlamp Dimmer Switch, Procedure for Adjustment 

 CAUTION: Do not overbend or the flash-to-pass will become inoperative. 

The headlamp dimmer switch, mounted to the steering column, may cause 
an erratic or continual ON condition for the headlamps. 

The following procedure is used to adjust the dimmer 
switch/flash-to-pass, in order to prevent an occasional short circuit 
condition between the contact points. 

Disconnect battery ground cables. 

Push back rubber boot on turn signal lever. 

Locate dimmer switch contact points on the lower forward section. 

Insert a screwdriver between the contact points and pry the front tab 
slightly outward and away from the other. 

Push rubber boot on turn signal lever back to steering column. 

Connect ground cables to batteries and check dimmer switch operation. 

 Headlamp Dimmer Switch Adjustment 

[FIGURE: K10146C.gif]

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Courtesy Lamps

 Inspection and Verification

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Lamps, Dome 

 Removal 

To replace the bulbs, carefully remove the dome lamp assembly from the 
headliner of the cab by pressing the driver side end of the assembly while 
pulling down on lamp housing. Bulbs are exposed at the side of the assembly 
and are easily removed when cool.

To replace dome lamp housing, remove two leads, one from the end and 
one from the top of the housing, and replace unit.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Section 17-04: Lamps, Daytime Running

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Canadian Daytime Running Lamp (DRL) System 

The Canadian daytime running lamp (DRL) system is designed to turn the 
high beam headlamps on, with a reduced light output, and without illuminating 
the high beam indicator lamp in the instrument panel when the following 
conditions are met: 

The ignition switch lock cylinder is in the RUN position.

The parking brake is fully released.

The headlamp switch is in the OFF or PARK position.

The daytime running lamps (DRL) control module is grounded through the 
low beam input when the DRL system is active.

 NOTE: When the DRL system is active, the pulsed voltage on the high beam 
circuit cannot be measured accurately. If the low beam headlamps or the high 
beam headlamps are inoperative, refer to Section 17-01 .

 U.S. Daytime Running Lamp System 

The U.S. daytime running lamp (DRL) system is designed to turn the low 
beam headlamps on, at a reduced light intensity, when the following conditions 
are met:

The ignition switch lock cylinder is in the RUN position.

The parking brake is fully released.

The headlamp switch is in the OFF or PARK position.

The daytime running lamps (DRL) control module is grounded through the 
high beam input when the DRL system is active.

 NOTE: When the DRL system is active, the pulsed voltage on the low beam 
circuit cannot be measured accurately. If the low beam headlamps or the high 
beam headlamps are inoperative, refer to Section 17-01 .

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Daytime Running Lamp (DRL) System

 Inspection and Verification 

Before performing any lighting systems tests, check that the battery is 
fully charged, battery connections are clean and tight, and burned out fuses 
and bulbs have been replaced. The DRL system also requires the parking brake 
switch light to function correctly.

running lamps to duplicate the concern.

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Engine Identification

For engine identification and adjustment information, a label, or 
dataplate, is attached to the side of the front gear housing in front of the 
fuel pump. Always refer to the label when replacement parts are required or 
when checking engine calibrations. Some engine parts may vary with engine 
application and vehicle type. The identification codes will ensure that the 
proper parts are obtained. The codes contain all pertinent information 
relating to dates, optional equipment and revisions. The Ford Master Parts 
Catalog contains a complete listing of the codes and their application. In 
addition, there is an engine serial number located on a pad at the lower right 
side of the block.

[FIGURE: A17169A.gif]

================================================================================
PAGE 4082
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 03A-01: Engine, FD-1060 Diesel

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Cylinder Head

The cylinder head is a one-piece, crossflow design with two valves per 
cylinder. The head has integrally cast valve guides and hardened valve seat 
surfaces which can be repaired using the appropriate service parts. 

The cylinder head has a cast intake manifold, fuel filter head, 
thermostat housing and an internal water bypass. The injectors are mounted in 
the head for direct injection into the cylinders. Separate pedestals for each 
cylinder are used to support and route oil to the rocker levers. 

The cylinder head gasket is a laminated design with print-o-seal on 
both sides around the water holes. A fire ring in the gasket seals the 
cylinder bores. The gasket also provides orifices to control coolant 
circulation past and around the cylinder bores.

================================================================================
PAGE 4083
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 03A-01: Engine, FD-1060 Diesel

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Manifolds

The intake manifold is integral with the cylinder head. The exhaust 
manifold mounts to the right side of the cylinder head and is designed to 
maintain exhaust velocity to provide maximum input to the turbocharger. 
Exhaust exits via the exhaust pipe, through the muffler and tail pipe.

================================================================================
PAGE 4084
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 03A-01: Engine, FD-1060 Diesel

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Exhaust Brake 

 CAUTION: Exceeding maximum exhaust pressure will result in engine damage. 

The following guidelines must be followed when installing an exhaust 
brake on Ford FD-1060 diesel engines or the warranty may be voided.

Exhaust brake assembly must be mounted a minimum of 1.7 meters (5.5 
feet) downstream from the turbocharger. 

Maximum allowable exhaust back pressure is 231 kPa (35 psi) for blue 
striped standard exhaust valve springs (248 kPa [36 psi] 
for white standard exhaust valve springs), and 414 kPa (60 psi) for white 
striped heavy-duty exhaust valve springs, all at 2750 rpm.

================================================================================
PAGE 4085
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 03A-01: Engine, FD-1060 Diesel

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Cylinder Block

The cylinder block has provisions for the oil cooler housing, 
thermostat seats, coolant bypass line, water pump volute, oil pump housing, 
water pump inlet and bored piston cylinders with spacing between cylinders to 
provide room for dry liners, if needed for service. 

The six-cylinder crankshaft is a balanced, forged steel, full fillet 
hardened unit with seven main bearing journals. The lower crankshaft main 
bearing halves are all the same. All of the upper crankshaft main bearing 
halves are the same except for the No. 6 journal which uses a flanged upper 
bearing shell. The flanges on the bearing shell control the end thrust of the 
crankshaft. Oversize main bearings and thrust bearings are available for 
service. 

All crankshaft seals are the Teflon® lay-down lip 
(scroll) type. The Teflon® lay-down lip type seal does not 
contain a spring on the back of the sealing lip. The sealing lip is a thin, 
stiff piece of Teflon®. 

Teflon® seals must be dry before installation. Do not 
lubricate the seal lip or the shaft. After the first few turns of the shaft, a 
thin film of Teflon® is transferred from the seal lip to the 
shaft. If the shaft is not clean and dry, this transfer will not occur and the 
seal will leak. 

The pistons have a cast aluminum body, high swirl combustion bowl and 
three ring grooves. The top ring groove has a ni-resist insert with a Keystone 
profile. The piston pin end of the connecting rod is angle cut to provide 
additional bearing surface. The rod end is fitted with a bronze bushing. Steel 
backed tri-metal bearings are used in production for the additional loading 
resulting from turbocharging and aftercooling. 

Oversize service rod bearings are available for use with reground 
crankshafts. 

A free-floating, hollow piston pin is used to attach the piston to the 
connecting rod. Lubrication of the pin and journal is accomplished by residual 
spray from piston cooling. 

The camshaft is gear driven from the crankshaft. A replaceable bushing 
is used for the front journal to carry the side loading from the accessory 
drive. The remainder of the journals operate in cast iron bores in the 
cylinder block. The camshaft has lobes to operate the intake and exhaust 
valves and a special lobe to drive the lift pump. The camshaft lobes contact 
mushroom-shaped valve tappets which operate the push rods. The operating arm 
of the lift pump rides directly on the special lobe on the camshaft.

================================================================================
PAGE 4086
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 03A-01: Engine, FD-1060 Diesel

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Lubrication System 

 Lubricating System Flow 

[FIGURE: A17164A.gif]

 Lubricating Oil Pump 

FD-1060 engines use a gerotor-type lubricating oil pump (1) located in 
the lower right area of the front face of the block.

 Pressure Regulating Valve 

The pressure regulating valve (2) is designed to keep the oil pressure 
from exceeding 483 kPa (70 psi). When the oil pressure from the pump is 
greater than 483 kPa (70 psi), the pressure regulating valve opens uncovering 
the dump port so part of the oil is routed to the oil pan. Because of 
manufacturing tolerances of the components and the oil passages, the oil 
pressure can differ between engines. 

 Oil Cooler 

The engine uses full flow, plate-type lubricating oil coolers (3). The 
oil flows through a cast passage in the cooler cover and through the element 
where it is cooled by engine coolant flowing past the plates of the element. 
The six-cylinder engine uses an element with seven plates. 

 Oil Filters 

After the oil is cooled, it flows through the full flow filter (4). 

 Oil Filter Bypass Valve 

The oil cooler cover contains an oil filter bypass valve (5) that will 
let the oil flow bypass a plugged filter. The oil filter bypass valve is 
designed to open when the pressure drop across the filter is more than 172 kPa 
(25 psi), as with a plugged filter, and lets the oil continue on through the 
engine. When a filter becomes plugged, an oil pressure decrease of 60 kPa (10 
psi) or less from the normal operating pressure can be observed on the vehicle 
oil pressure gauge. 

 Lubrication for the Turbocharger 

The turbocharger receives filtered, cooled and pressurized lubricating 
oil through a supply line from the oil filter head. A drain line connected to 
the bottom of the turbocharger housing returns the oil to the oil pan through 
a fitting in the cylinder block. 

 Turbocharger Lubrication 

[FIGURE: A17165A.gif]

 Lubrication for the Power Components 

The main bearings and the valve train are lubricated by pressurized oil 
directly from the main oil rifle. The other power components, connecting rods, 
pistons, and camshaft receive pressurized oil indirectly from the main oil 
rifle. 

The drillings in the crankshaft supply oil to the connecting rod 
bearings. The oil is supplied to the camshaft journals through drillings in 
the crankshaft main bearing saddle. Smaller drillings in the crankshaft main 
bearing saddle supply oil to the piston cooling nozzles. The spray from the 
nozzles provides cooling for the pistons and also provides lubrication for the 
piston pins. 

The number one crankshaft main bearing saddle does not contain a piston 
cooling nozzle. Cylinder No. 1 receives the lubricating and cooling spray from 
the nozzle located in the No. 2 crankshaft main bearing saddle. Cylinder No. 2 
receives the spray from the No. 3 crankshaft main bearing saddle, etc. 

 Power Component Lubrication

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Lubrication for the Overhead

Lubrication for the valve train is supplied through separate drillings 
in the cylinder block. The oil flows through the drillings and across the oil 
transfer slot in the cylinder head gasket. From the transfer slot, the oil 
flows around the outside diameter at the cylinder head capscrew, across a slot 
in the bottom of the rocker lever support, and up a vertical drilling in the 
support. From these drillings, oil flows through drillings in the rocker lever 
shaft to lubricate the rocker levers. Oil flows through a drilling in the 
rocker levers to fill a channel cast into the top of the levers. The oil from 
the channel lubricates the intake and exhaust valve stems, push rods and 
tappets.

================================================================================
PAGE 4088
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 03A-01: Engine, FD-1060 Diesel

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Cooling System 

Coolant is drawn from the radiator by the integrally mounted water 
pump. The output from the water pump empties into the oil cooler cavity of the 
cylinder block.

[FIGURE: A21465A.gif]

The coolant then circulates around each cylinder and crosses the block 
to the fuel pump side of the engine.

[FIGURE: A21466A.gif]

Coolant then flows up into the cylinder head, crosses over the valve 
bridges and down the exhaust manifold side of the engine to the integral 
thermostat housing.

[FIGURE: A21467A.gif]

As the coolant flows across the head toward the thermostat housing, it 
provides cooling for the injector nozzle. When the engine is below operating 
temperature, the thermostat is closed, and the coolant flow bypasses the 
radiator and goes to the water pump inlet via internal drillings in the block 
and cylinder head.

[FIGURE: A21468A.gif]

Item

Part Number

—

Bypass Closed

6

—

Coolant Flow Back to Radiator

 CAUTION: Never operate the engine without a thermostat. Without a thermostat, 
the coolant will not flow to the radiator and the engine will overheat. 

When operating temperature is reached, the thermostat opens, blocking 
the bypass passage to the water pump and opening the outlet to the radiator.

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Air System 

Air is pulled into the engine from an air filter. Clean air is very 
important to the life of the engine. Ingested dust and dirt can damage the 
cylinders very quickly. 

On turbocharged engines, the intake air flow is from the air cleaner to 
the turbocharger and then routed to the charge air cooler located in front of 
the radiator. Air leaves the charge air cooler and is routed to the intake 
manifold where it is forced into the cylinders and used for combustion. The 
cooler reduces the temperature of the air, which lowers combustion chamber 
temperatures, and in turn reduces NOx emissions. Also, cooling the air makes 
it more dense allowing more fuel to be injected into the engine to increase 
the power-to-weight ratio.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Engine 

 Removal 

Remove hood and front bumper, and disconnect battery ground cable. 

Drain engine oil and coolant. 

Release air system pressure (if so equipped). 

Remove air cleaner assembly, turbocharger air supply tube and 
turbo-to-charge air cooler tube. 

Position drain pan and disconnect power steering pump supply hose at 
pump. 

Disconnect power steering pump pressure hose at pump. 

Disconnect brake air compressor air supply hose at compressor (if so 
equipped). 

Remove fan shroud retaining bolts and hang shroud over fan. 

Disconnect the radiator upper and lower hoses. 

Disconnect coolant purge and supply hoses at coolant reservoir. 

Disconnect low coolant sensor at reservoir. 

Remove the two radiator coolant recovery reservoir-to-mounting bracket 
retaining bolts and remove reservoir. 

Disconnect the overflow hose at the radiator. 

Remove the radiator retaining bolts and remove the radiator and charge 
air cooler as an assembly. 

Remove shroud and remove fan blade-to-hub retaining bolts. Remove fan. 

Disconnect brake compressor pressure hose or hydraulic brake lines (if 
so equipped). 

Mark brake compressor governor hoses (if so equipped) prior to 
removing. Disconnect hoses. 

Remove hose retainers at engine block. 

Position hoses away from engine. 

Disconnect oil cooler line at cooler and position out of way. 

Disconnect exhaust pipe at turbocharger. 

Remove air hose from air charge cooler to intake manifold. 

Disconnect heater hoses from tubes at top of thermostat housing. 

Disconnect throttle cable, hand throttle cable and transmission 
kickdown cable (automatic transmission only) and position aside. 

Cut tie wraps and disconnect generator electrical harness. 

Disconnect wiring to coolant temperature senders on thermostat housing. 

Disconnect wiring from starter motor. 

Disconnect speed sensor at flywheel housing. 

Remove cable clamp retaining nut at flywheel housing. 

Remove fuel lines-to-flywheel housing retaining bolts. 

Disconnect two fuel lines at rear of fuel block and cap all openings. 

Remove ground wire retaining bolt at flywheel housing. 

Disconnect electrical connector at fuel shutoff solenoid. 

Loosen clamps and remove oil fill hose. 

Disconnect lower radiator hose at engine. 

Remove lower radiator hose strap retaining bolt and remove hose. 

Remove exhaust pipe clamp retaining nut. Remove exhaust pipe. 

Remove transmission. Refer to the appropriate section in Group 07 for 
procedure. 

 NOTE: Lift engine only by front and rear lifting eyes attached to cylinder 
head. 

Install engine lifting equipment on engine.

Remove the rear engine mount retaining bolts. 

Remove the front mount-to-crossmember retaining bolts. 

Position lifting equipment and remove engine assembly from the vehicle. 

Mount engine on a suitable engine stand and move to work area.

 NOTE: For fastener torque values, refer to Torque Specifications at the end 
of this manual.

Attach front mount-to-crossmember retaining bolts.

Attach ground wire retaining bolt to flywheel housing.

Remove protective caps from two fuel lines and attach to rear of fuel 
block.

Attach fuel lines-to-flywheel housing retaining bolts.

Attach cable clamp retaining nut at flywheel housing.

Connect speed sensor at flywheel housing.

Connect wiring for starter motor.

Connect wiring to coolant temperature senders on thermostat housing.

Connect generator electrical harness.

Connect throttle cable, hand throttle cable and transmission kickdown 
cable.

Connect heater hoses at top of thermostat housing.

Connect exhaust pipe at turbocharger.

Connect oil cooler line to oil cooler.

Connect brake compressor governor hoses (if so equipped) and attach 
hose retainers to engine block.

Connect brake compressor hose or hydraulic brake lines (if so equipped).

Attach fan to hub and install shroud.

Install radiator and charge air cooler.

Attach overflow hose to radiator.

Assemble coolant reservoir.

Connect low coolant sensor at coolant reservoir.

Connect radiator upper and lower hoses.

Connect the brake air compressor air supply hose to compressor (if so 
equipped).

Connect the power steering pump pressure hose to the pump.

Connect the turbocharger-to-charge air cooler, turbocharger air supply 
tube, and air cleaner assembly.

Add engine oil and coolant.

Install hood and front bumper.

Connect battery ground cable.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Valve Cover, Rocker Arms and Push Rods 

 Removal 

Remove the retaining bolts and valve covers.

[FIGURE: A17276A.gif]

Loosen the rocker arm adjusting screw lock nuts. Loosen the adjusting 
screws until they stop.

[FIGURE: A17277A.gif]

 NOTE: If the rocker arms and push rods are to be disassembled and inspected 
for reuse, refer to Rocker Arms and Shaft in the Disassembly and Assembly 
portion of this section. 

Remove the rocker arm shaft support bolts from the rocker lever 
pedestals. Remove the pedestals, rocker arms, and the push rods. 

[FIGURE: A17278A.gif]

 Installation 

Install the push rods into the sockets of the valve tappets. Lubricate 
the push rod sockets with clean engine oil.

[FIGURE: A17279A.gif]

Make sure the rocker lever adjusting screws are completely backed out.

[FIGURE: A17280A.gif]

Make sure the dowel rings in the pedestals are installed into the dowel 
bores.

[FIGURE: A17281A.gif]

Use clean engine oil to lubricate the threads and under the heads of 
the rocker arm shaft support bolts. Install the rocker arm shaft support bolts 
into the pedestals.

[FIGURE: A17295A.gif]

Tighten in the following sequenced steps: 

Step 1 (long rocker arm shaft support bolts only): tighten the rocker 
arm shaft support bolts to 90 Nm (66 lb-ft). Recheck bolts 
for 90 Nm (66 lb-ft). 

Step 2 (long rocker arm shaft support bolts only): tighten the rocker 
arm shaft support bolts to 120 Nm (90 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A17296A.gif]

Step 3: After the long rocker arm shaft support bolts have been 
tightened to 120 Nm (90 lb-ft), rotate an additional 90 
degrees.

[FIGURE: A17297A.gif]

Tighten the 8 mm rocker arm shaft support bolts to 21-27 Nm
 (16-19 lb-ft). 

Adjust the valves. Refer to Valve Adjustment, Cold in the Adjustments 
portion of this section. 

Install valve covers and tighten bolts to 21-27 Nm 
(16-19 lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Valve Spring, Valve Spring Retainer and Valve Stem Seal

Broken valve springs or damaged valve stem seals and retainers can be 
replaced without removing the cylinder head, provided damage to the valve or 
valve seal has not occurred.

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Valve Spring Compressor

T83T-6513-A

 Removal 

Remove the valve cover and rocker arm assembly.

Remove the fuel injectors.

Install an air line using the Compression Test Adapter D92T-6600-A or 
equivalent in the injector nozzle hole and turn on the air supply.

 CAUTION: Take care not to drive the valve into the piston. Doing so could damage 
the valve and/or piston. Make sure the piston is not at TDC when loosening the 
retainers from the locks. 

 NOTE: It may be necessary to break the retainer loose from the valve locks. 
This can be done by tapping the edge of the retainer with a plastic hammer or 
by placing a socket (of approximately the same outside diameter) on the 
retainer and tapping the socket with a plastic hammer. Do not strike the tip 
of the valve stem.

Use Valve Spring Compressor T83T-6513-A to compress the valve spring.

[FIGURE: A21985A.gif]

Use a pencil magnet to remove the valve collets. Discard the valve 
collets.

Slowly release the pressure on the valve spring.

Remove the valve spring retainer and the valve spring.

Remove the valve spring seat/valve seal assembly.

 NOTE: If air pressure has forced the piston to the bottom of the cylinder, 
any removal of air pressure will allow the valve(s) to fall into the cylinder. 
A rubber band, tape or string wrapped around the end of the valve stem will 
prevent this condition and will still allow enough travel to check the valve 
for binding.

Remove the valve stem seal.

[FIGURE: A90331A.gif]

[FIGURE: A23419A.gif]

 Installation 

Inspect the cylinder head and valve assembly as described in this 
section. Inspect the valve stem for damage. Rotate the valve and check valve 
stem tip for eccentric (out-of-round) movement. Check for binding by moving 
the valve up and down through its normal travel in the valve guide checking 
for binds. If valve has been damaged, it will be necessary to remove cylinder 
head for repairs. Inspect the retainer locks for excessive wear, and replace 
in pairs, as necessary. 

If the valve is OK, hold it in the closed position and apply air 
pressure within the cylinder. This will hold the valve in the closed position.

Lubricate the valve stem with recommended quality engine oil.

Install the valve spring seat/valve seal assembly over the valve stem. 
To prevent oil carry-over, the seals are color coded and must be installed as 
follows:

Exhaust valve: orange (with 64 grooves per inch)

Intake valve: black (with 40 grooves per inch)

[FIGURE: A18316A.gif]

Install the valve springs.

Install the valve spring retainers.

[FIGURE: A18317A.gif]

Use Valve Spring Compressor T83T-6513-A to compress the valve springs.

[FIGURE: A21985A.gif]

 NOTE: Use new valve spring retainer collets when rebuilding the cylinder head.

Install the new valve spring retainer collets.

 WARNING: WEAR EYE PROTECTION. IF THE COLLETS ARE NOT CORRECTLY INSTALLED, THEY 
CAN FLY OUT WHEN THE STEMS ARE HIT WITH A HAMMER. 

Use a plastic hammer to gently hit the top of the valve stems to make 
sure the valve collets are correctly seated in the spring retainer.

[FIGURE: A18319A.gif]

Remove the compressor tool. Turn off the air and remove the air line 
adapter.

Install the rocker arm assembly, push rods and valve cover.

Water Pump

 Removal

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Oil Seal, Crankshaft, Front 

 Removal 

 NOTE: Removal is easier if the crankshaft pulley is loosened before removing 
the belt. 

Remove the drive belt.

[FIGURE: A17366A.gif]

Remove the crankshaft pulley.

[FIGURE: A17373A.gif]

Remove the front cover.

[FIGURE: A17374A.gif]

Remove the oil seal from the front cover. Drive the oil seal from the 
back side of the cover toward the front side of the cover, while supporting 
the front cover.

[FIGURE: A17375A.gif]

Clean the crankshaft front seal bore in the front cover and the 
crankshaft surface free of all oil and crankshaft front seal residue.

[FIGURE: A17376A.gif]

 NOTE: If the crankshaft has excessive wear, a service wear sleeve is 
available. 

Inspect the crankshaft for excessive wear.

[FIGURE: A17377A.gif]

Clean the gasket sealing surfaces of the block and front cover of all 
gasket material.

 Installation 

Apply a bead of Loctite® 227 or equivalent to the 
outside diameter of the seal.

 CAUTION: To prevent damage to the crankshaft front seal carrier, hit the 
installation tool alternately at the 12, 3, 6 and 9 o'clock positions. 

Use the installation tool and a hammer to install the seal to the 
correct depth while supporting the back side of the cover.

[FIGURE: A17379A.gif]

 CAUTION: Always use a seal pilot when installing a seal. 

Install the pilot from the seal kit onto the crankshaft.

[FIGURE: A17380A.gif]

Install the front cover and gasket, making sure the seal slides over 
the pilot. Remove the pilot.

[FIGURE: A17381A.gif]

Install the front cover mounting capscrews and tighten to 21-27 Nm
 (16-19 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A17382A.gif]

Install the crankshaft pulley. Do not tighten the capscrews to the 
correct torque value at this time.

[FIGURE: A17367A.gif]

Install the drive belt. Check torque of belt tensioner mounting bolts. 
Correct torque value is 43 Nm (32 lb-ft).

Tighten the crankshaft vibration damper capscrews to 119-131 Nm
 (89-96 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A17383A.gif]

 Wear Sleeve, Front Crankshaft Replacement 

 Removal 

Remove the fan drive belt, vibration damper, gear cover and seal. Refer 
to Oil Seal, Crankshaft, Front in the Removal and Installation portion of this 
section.

 CAUTION: Do not nick or gouge the crankshaft with the chisel. If the crankshaft 
is damaged, it must be replaced. 

Use a hammer and dull chisel only as wide as the wear sleeve. Make one 
or two soft blows across the wear sleeve. This will expand the wear sleeve 
allowing the sleeve to be removed.

[FIGURE: A23643A.gif]

Clean and inspect the crankshaft at the oil seal area for dirt, nicks, 
chisel marks, scratches, rust or corrosion, or other damage that would prevent 
a proper wear sleeve installation.

 Installation 

Use Cummins Engine Company Part No. 3823908, Crankshaft Front Wear 
Sleeve Installation Tool, to install the wear sleeve to the correct position 
on the crankshaft.

 Crankshaft Front Wear Sleeve Installation Tool 

[FIGURE: A23644A.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

1

—

Spacer (Part of 3823908)

2

—

Hairpin, Cotter (Part of 3823908)

3

—

Driver (Part of 3823908)

4

—

Capscrew, M14 x 1.5 x 60 mm (Part of 3823908)

Apply a thin coat of engine oil 15W-40 to the driver inside diameter 
and capscrew threads.

[FIGURE: A23645A.gif]

Position the chamfered end of the wear sleeve onto the end of the 
crankshaft.

[FIGURE: A23646A.gif]

Position the counterbore end of the driver onto the wear sleeve.

[FIGURE: A23647A.gif]

Install two capscrews (without spacers or hairpin cotters) through the 
driver and onto the crankshaft capscrew holes. Align the wear sleeve and 
driver perpendicular with the crankshaft. Tighten the capscrews finger-tight.

[FIGURE: A23648A.gif]

 NOTE: To prevent damage to the wear sleeve, do not exceed one-half revolution 
of each capscrew. Alternately tighten the capscrews until the sleeve is 
installed to a depth of approximately 16 mm (0.625 inch). Approximate torque 
value 20 Nm (15 lb-ft).

Remove the capscrews and install a spacer on each capscrew. Install the 
two capscrews again.

[FIGURE: A23649A.gif]

Continue to alternately tighten the capscrews until the bottom of the 
driver contacts the end of the crankshaft.

[FIGURE: A23650A.gif]

Remove the driver. Use the hairpin cotters to secure the capscrews and 
spacers to the tool during storage.

[FIGURE: A23651A.gif]

 NOTE: The wear sleeve and oil seal mating surface must be clean and dry to be 
sure of proper oil sealing.

Clean the wear sleeve and crankshaft of any lubricant.

Install the oil seal, crankshaft front cover, vibration damper and fan 
drive belt. Refer to Oil Seal, Crankshaft Front in the Removal and 
Installation portion of this section.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Camshaft Drive Gear and Thrust Plate, In-Vehicle

 Removal 

Remove the following components as described in this section:

Valve cover

Rocker arm assemblies

Push rods

Crankshaft vibration damper

Front cover

Fuel lift pump (refer to Section 03A-04A )

 NOTE: It is necessary to partially remove the camshaft to replace the 
camshaft gear; therefore, the tappets must be raised and secured with the 
dowel rods.

Insert Lifter Holders, part of Lifter Holder Set D94T-6500-A or 
equivalent, such as wooden dowels, securely into each tappet. Use a soft-face 
hammer if necessary.

[FIGURE: A17395A.gif]

Pull each valve tappet up until it makes contact with the cylinder 
block. Put a rubber band around two dowels to hold the tappets off the 
camshaft. 

[FIGURE: A18268A.gif]

Rotate the crankshaft to align the timing marks before trying to remove 
the camshaft.

[FIGURE: A17397B.gif]

Remove the capscrews from the thrust plate.

 NOTE: Rotate the camshaft as it is being removed. Use extreme care to be sure 
the camshaft bushings are not damaged during the camshaft removal process.

Remove the camshaft from the cylinder block just enough to expose the 
first two camshaft lobes.

[FIGURE: A23421A.gif]

Install retainer to secure the camshaft in position. Secure the 
retainer between the second camshaft lobe and the second camshaft journal 
using an 8 mm x 1.25 capscrew in one of the holes used to secure the camshaft 
thrust plate.

[FIGURE: A23422A.gif]

Position the gear remover yoke over the first camshaft journal and 
assemble the rods through the access holes in the camshaft gear web. Assemble 
the remainder of the tool as shown. Gear installer yoke is not used for 
camshaft gear removal. Tighten the nuts and rods finger-tight.

[FIGURE: A23423A.gif]

Tighten the pressing screw by hand while positioning the gear remover 
mandrel between the screw press and the end of the camshaft.

[FIGURE: A23424A.gif]

 CAUTION: Hold the tool securely while tightening the pressing screw to prevent 
the tool and camshaft gear from falling during removal. 

Tighten the pressing screw in a clockwise direction while keeping the 
tool from rotating using the torque arm as shown.

[FIGURE: A23425A.gif]

Remove the tool and camshaft gear assembly from the vehicle. 
Disassemble the tool.

 Installation 

Assemble the Cam Gear Installer to the camshaft gear. Place the rods 
through the holes in the camshaft gear and screw the rods into the gear 
installer yoke. Secure the screw press to the rods with the nuts. The nuts and 
rods need only to be finger-tight. Turn the forcing screw counterclockwise as 
far as it will go.

Make sure the chamfer in the camshaft gear will be positioned towards 
the cylinder block during camshaft gear installation.

[FIGURE: A23426A.gif]

Lubricate the inside diameter of the camshaft gear and the end of the 
camshaft. Position the tool and camshaft gear assembly over the camshaft and 
slide the gear installer yoke over the front camshaft journal.

[FIGURE: A23427A.gif]

Engage the camshaft gear keyway with the camshaft locating pin and, by 
hand, turn the forcing screw clockwise until the camshaft gear, camshaft, and 
tool are all held firmly together and properly aligned with each other.

[FIGURE: A23428A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not use an impact wrench with this tool, otherwise damage can result 
to the camshaft gear, camshaft or the tool. 

Tighten the forcing screw in the clockwise direction while keeping the 
tool from rotating using the torque arm inserted in the screw press.

[FIGURE: A23425A.gif]

While turning the forcing screw, the effort required should increase 
steadily until the camshaft gear is against the camshaft shoulder.

When the camshaft gear is pressed firmly against the camshaft shoulder, 
the camshaft gear installation is complete.

[FIGURE: A23429A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not try to force the camshaft into the camshaft bore as damage to 
the camshaft bushing can result. 

Install the camshaft. While pushing in slightly, rotate the camshaft 
and carefully work the camshaft through the camshaft bushings. As each 
camshaft journal passes through a bushing, the camshaft will drop slightly and 
the camshaft lobes will catch on the bushings. Rotating the camshaft will free 
the lobe from the bushing and allow the camshaft to be installed.

[FIGURE: A17418A.gif]

Before the camshaft gear engages the crankshaft gear, check the 
camshaft for ease of rotation. When installed properly, the camshaft should 
rotate freely.

Align the timing marks on the camshaft with the timing mark on the 
crankshaft.

[FIGURE: A18275A.gif]

 CAUTION: Make sure the camshaft assembly does not drop on your fingers when 
installing the thrust plate. 

Install the camshaft thrust plate.

[FIGURE: A18276A.gif]

Install the camshaft thrust plate capscrews and tighten to 21-27 Nm
 (16-19 lb-ft).

 NOTE: If the camshaft end clearance is greater than the stated limit, the 
thrust plate must be replaced.

Measure camshaft end clearance with a dial indicator. End clearance is 
controlled by the thickness of the thrust plate and the groove in the 
camshaft. Camshaft end clearance limits are 0.12-0.34 mm (0.005-0.013 inch).

 NOTE: The gears must be replaced if the backlash is greater than the above 
limit.

 NOTE: Excessive gear backlash can be caused by worn camshaft bushings.

Put a dial indicator on the camshaft gear and check the gear backlash 
between the camshaft gear and the crankshaft gear. Camshaft gear backlash 
limits are 0.076-0.330 mm (0.003-0.013 inch).

Remove the wooden dowel rods from the valve tappets.

Install all parts that were removed:

Fuel lift pump

Front cover

Crankshaft vibration damper

Push rods

Rocker arm assemblies

Valve cover

 Removal

Fan blade pulley

Camshaft

[FIGURE: A17422A.gif]

Set the camshaft, camshaft gear side up, in press and press off the

[FIGURE: A17424A.gif]

Remove the camshaft key.

[FIGURE: A17425A.gif]

 NOTE: If the fretting, burrs or raised material cannot be removed with 
Scotch-Brite® 7448 or equivalent, replace the gear. 

Visually inspect the camshaft gear for cracks, chipped or broken teeth. 
Inspect the bore of the gear for fretting or burrs.

[FIGURE: A17426A.gif]

 NOTE: If the keyway is damaged or the burrs cannot be removed, the gear must 
be replaced. 

Inspect the camshaft sprocket keyway for burrs. Remove burrs with 
Scotch-Brite® 7448 or equivalent.

[FIGURE: A17427A.gif]

 NOTE: If fretting or burrs cannot be removed with Scotch-Brite®
 7448 or equivalent, replace the camshaft. 

Visually inspect the camshaft nose for fretting or burrs.

[FIGURE: A17428A.gif]

 Installation 

Install the key.

[FIGURE: A17429A.gif]

Lubricate the camshaft surface with Engine Assembly Lubricant 
D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A.

[FIGURE: A17430A.gif]

 WARNING: WEAR PROTECTIVE GLOVES TO HANDLE THE HOT GEAR. 

 CAUTION: The gear will be permanently distorted if overheated. The oven 
temperature must never exceed 177°C (350°F). 

Heat the camshaft gear in Rotunda Gear/Bearing Heater 164-R3900 or 
equivalent at 149°C (300°F) for 45 minutes. 

 NOTE: Make sure the gear is seated against camshaft shoulder. 

 NOTE: Do not stop once you have begun to install the gear onto the camshaft. 
Do not turn the gear while you are installing it. The gear will get stuck on 
the camshaft once you stop or if you turn the gear while installing it. If 
this occurs, remove the gear and start again. 

Install the gear with the timing marks away from the camshaft.

[FIGURE: A17432A.gif]

Using a .001-inch feeler gauge, check to see if the feeler gauge can be 
inserted between the gear and the shoulder on the camshaft. If the feeler 
gauge can be inserted, the gear is not properly seated.

[FIGURE: A17433A.gif]

Install the following as outlined in this section: 

Camshaft

Front cover

Crank pulley

Fan blade pulley

[FIGURE: A17422A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Crankshaft Gear

 Removal 

Remove crankshaft from engine. 

Using Bearing Pulling Attachment D84L-1123-A, Push-Puller Set 
D80L-927-A and Shaft Protector D80L-625-5 or equivalents, remove gear from 
crankshaft. 

[FIGURE: A17880C.gif]

Remove all burrs and make sure the crankshaft sprocket surface on the 
end of the crankshaft is smooth. 

 Installation 

If previously removed, install the alignment pin until it bottoms in 
the bore. 

 CAUTION: The gear will be permanently distorted if overheated. The oven 
temperature must never exceed 177°C (350°F). 

Heat the crankshaft gear in Rotunda Gear/Bearing Heater 164-R3900 or 
equivalent for 45 minutes as 149°C (300°F). 

Apply a thin coat of lubricant on the nose of the crankshaft. 

 WARNING: WEAR PROTECTIVE GLOVES TO PREVENT PERSONAL INJURY. 

 NOTE: Do not stop once you have begun to install the gear onto the 
crankshaft. Do not turn the gear while you are installing it. The gear will 
get stuck on the crankshaft once you stop or if you turn the gear while 
installing it. If this occurs, remove the gear and start again. 

Install the hot gear up to the crankshaft shoulder with the timing mark 
facing out. 

Install the crankshaft.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Geartrain Timing, Initial

 Removal 

The timing pin assembly is precisely located on the gear housing to 
correspond to Top Dead Center (TDC) for cylinder No. 1. Failure to locate the 
timing pin assembly to TDC for cylinder No. 1 prior to removal will result in 
incorrect fuel injection timing.

 NOTE: If the timing pin has been damaged and cannot be used to locate TDC, 
refer to Relocating the Timing Pin Assembly, Cylinder Head Installed in the 
Removal and Installation portion of this section for procedure. If the 
cylinder head is removed, refer to Relocating Timing Pin Assembly, Cylinder 
Head Removed in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

Locate top dead center (TDC) for cylinder No. 1 by barring engine 
slowly while pressing on the engine timing pin.

[FIGURE: A17171A.gif]

Remove the timing pin assembly and seal.

[FIGURE: A17435A.gif]

 Installation 

Install a new O-ring into the groove of the timing pin assembly. 
Lubricate the O-ring with 15W-40 engine oil.

With a coat of Threadlock® 262 E2FZ-19554-B or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G351-A6 to the threads of the Torx®
 screws and install the timing pin assembly.

Push the pin into the hole in the cam gear to align the housing.

 CAUTION: To prevent damage to the pin and gear, make sure the timing pin is 
disengaged before rotating the crankshaft. 

Hold the pin in while tightening the Torx® screws to 5 Nm
 (5 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A17436B.gif]
