REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Camshaft and Valve Tappets

 NOTE: If camshaft gear is to be replaced, refer to Camshaft Drive Gear and 
Thrust Plate in the Removal and Installation portion of this section. 

A replacement camshaft does not come with a new camshaft gear. If the 
camshaft is to be replaced and the original gear is in good condition, the 
gear must be pressed off and installed on the replacement camshaft. 

 Removal 

 Preparatory Steps: 

Remove the following:

Valve covers 

Push rods 

Drive belt 

Crankshaft pulley 

Front cover

Fuel transfer pump

Using an appropriate dial indicator, measure camshaft sprocket 
backlash. If backlash is out of specifications, gear must be replaced. Refer 
to Removal and Installation, Camshaft Drive Gear and Thrust Plate in this 
section. 

[FIGURE: A17879A.gif]

Insert Lifter Holder Set D94T-6500-A or equivalent through the push rod 
holes and into the top of each tappet securely. When properly installed, the 
holders can be used to pull the tappets up and should not be able to be pulled 
out without considerable effort.

[FIGURE: A17395A.gif]

Pull the tappets up and wrap a rubber band around the top of the lifter 
holders. This will prevent the tappets from dropping down.

[FIGURE: A17396A.gif]

Rotate the crankshaft engine to align the crankshaft to camshaft timing 
marks.

[FIGURE: A17397B.gif]

Remove the capscrews from the thrust plate.

[FIGURE: A17398A.gif]

 CAUTION: Use care when removing camshaft so as not to nick camshaft journals, 
lobes or bores. 

Remove the camshaft and thrust plate. 

[FIGURE: A17399A.gif]

To aid in tappet removal and to prevent tappets dropping down into oil 
pan, fabricate a trough and insert the trough to the full length of the 
camshaft bore.

[FIGURE: A17400A.gif]

Make sure the trough is positioned so it will catch the tappet when the 
holder is removed.

[FIGURE: A17401A.gif]

Remove only one tappet at a time. Remove the rubber band from the two 
companion tappets, securing the tappet not to be removed with the rubber band.

[FIGURE: A17402A.gif]

Pull the lifter holder from the valve tappet bore allowing the tappet 
to fall into the trough.

[FIGURE: A17401A.gif]

When the tappet is dropped into the trough, most of the time it will 
fall over. However, if it doesn't, gently shake the trough just enough to 
allow the tappet to fall over before removing.

[FIGURE: A17404A.gif]

[FIGURE: A17405A.gif]

 NOTE: Special care must be taken when removing the No. 6 cylinder tappets, 
not to knock or shake the tappet over the end of the trough. 

Carefully pull the trough and tappet from the camshaft bore and remove 
the tappet. Repeat the process until all tappets are removed.

[FIGURE: A17406A.gif]

Inspect the tappets and camshaft. Refer to Camshaft 
and to Valve Tappets in the Cleaning and Inspection portion of this section. 

 Installation 

Insert the fabricated trough the full length of the camshaft bore.

[FIGURE: A17400A.gif]

Lower the valve tappet installation tool down the push rod hole, 
through the valve tappet bore, and into the trough.

[FIGURE: A17407A.gif]

Feed the installation tool through the camshaft bores by carefully 
pulling the trough/installation tool out the front. The barrier at the rear of 
the trough will pull the tool out most of the time.

[FIGURE: A17408A.gif]

Lubricate the tappets with Engine Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A.

[FIGURE: A17409B.gif]

Insert the installation tool into the tappet.

[FIGURE: A17410A.gif]

Slide the trough into the camshaft bore.

[FIGURE: A17400A.gif]

Pull the tool/tappet through the camshaft bore and up into the valve 
tappet bore.

[FIGURE: A17411A.gif]

If difficulty is experienced in getting the tappet to make the bend 
from the trough up to the valve tappet bore, pull the trough out enough to 
allow the tappet to drop down and align itself, then pull the tappet up into 
the bore.

[FIGURE: A17412A.gif]

After the tappet has been pulled up into position, slide the trough 
back into the camshaft bore and rotate it one-half turn. This will position 
the round side of the trough up, which will hold the tappet in place.

[FIGURE: A17413A.gif]

 NOTE: To aid in removing the installation tool after the tappet is installed, 
work the tool in and out of the tappet several times before installing the 
tappets. 

Remove the installation tool from the tappet.

[FIGURE: A21470A.gif]

Install Lifter Holder Set D94T-6500-A or equivalent into the top of the 
tappet. Wrap rubber bands around the lifter holders to secure the tappets. 

Repeat this process until all tappets have been installed. 

[FIGURE: A17415A.gif]

Before installing the camshaft, apply a coat of Engine Assembly 
Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A 
to the front camshaft bore.

[FIGURE: A17416A.gif]

Lubricate the camshaft lobes, journals and thrust washer with Engine 
Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESR-M99C80-A.

[FIGURE: A17417A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not try to force the camshaft into the camshaft bore as damage to 
the camshaft bushing can result. 

Install the camshaft. While pushing in slightly, rotate the camshaft 
and carefully work the camshaft through the camshaft bushings. As each 
camshaft journal passes through a bushing, the camshaft will drop slightly and 
the camshaft lobes will catch on the bushings. Rotating the camshaft will free 
the camshaft lobe from the bushing and allow the camshaft to be installed.

[FIGURE: A17418A.gif]

Before the camshaft gear engages the crankshaft gear, check the 
camshaft for ease of rotation. When installed properly, the camshaft should 
rotate freely.

[FIGURE: A17419A.gif]

Install the thrust washer. Align the timing marks as illustrated and 
finish installing the camshaft.

[FIGURE: A17397B.gif]

Install the thrust plate capscrews and tighten to 21-27 Nm
 (16-19 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A17420A.gif]

Measure to verify the camshaft has proper backlash and end play: 

A = 0.12 to 0.34 mm (0.005 to 0.013 inch) 

B = 0.076 to 0.330 mm (0.003 to 0.013 inch)

[FIGURE: A17421A.gif]

Complete the installation of the removed parts as outlined in this 
section: 

Front cover 

Vibration damper 

Push rods

Rocker levers and valve cover 

Fuel transfer pump 

Drive belt

Operate the engine at idle for 5 to 10 minutes and check for leaks and 
proper operation.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Camshaft Rear Cover

 Removal 

 NOTE: It is necessary to remove the rear camshaft cover when the camshaft 
bearings are being removed and replaced.

If the camshaft has not been removed from the block, pry the cover from 
the rear countershaft bore with a wide-lipped screwdriver.

[FIGURE: A108141A.gif]

If camshaft removal is necessary or if the camshaft has been removed, 
insert a long rod through the camshaft bore and knock the cover out. Be 
careful not to damage the cam bearing surfaces.

 Installation 

Clean all of the old sealer from the cover. If the sealing edge is 
nicked or damaged, replace the cover.

Liberally coat the sealing edge of the rear cam cover with Perfect Seal 
Sealing Compound F2AZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specifications 
ESR-M18P2-A and ESE-M4G115-A.

Tap the rear cam cover into place with a soft mallet until it is fully 
seated.

[FIGURE: A107771A.gif]

 Removal

Remove the camshaft gear and camshaft thrust plate.

outlined in this section.

Remove the tappets. Be sure to keep tappets in order so they may be 
reinstalled in the original order.

Inspect the camshaft bushing for pitting or scoring.

 NOTE: If the bores without a bushing are worn beyond the limit, the engine 
must be removed for machining and installation of service bushings.

Measure the camshaft bore.

[FIGURE: A23670A.gif]

Mark the camshaft bushing and cylinder block to align the oil hole in 
the cylinder block with the oil hole in the bushing.

[FIGURE: A23671A.gif]

Check the oil hole alignment between the bush and cylinder block. A 3.2 
mm (0.128 inch) Allen wrench must be able to pass through the hole.

[FIGURE: A23672A.gif]

[FIGURE: A23673A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Piston and Piston Rings

 Removal 

Drain the engine coolant. 

Remove the cylinder head as outlined. 

Drain the lubricating oil. After oil is drained, reinstall drain plug 
and a new sealing washer. Tighten to 77-83 Nm (57-61 lb-ft). 

Remove the dipstick bayonet. 

Remove the oil pan and gasket. 

 NOTE: Each connecting rod cap and connecting rod should be marked from the 
factory with a four-digit number for identification. Each connecting rod 
cap/connecting rod identification number is different. This is done because 
each connecting rod cap/connecting rod is align bored. 

Mark each connecting rod cap according to cylinder.

[FIGURE: A17310A.gif]

Rotate the engine until the pistons are below the carbon deposits which 
are found above the piston ring travel area. 

Use a scraper or a blunt-edged instrument to loosen the carbon 
deposits. Do not damage the cylinder with the scraper.

[FIGURE: A17311A.gif]

Remove the remaining carbon with a Scotch-Brite® 
cleaning pad or equivalent.

 WARNING: TO PREVENT SERIOUS EYE DAMAGE WEAR EYE PROTECTION DURING THIS OPERATION. 

 CAUTION: Do not use the steel wire wheel in the piston travel area. operate the 
wheel in a circular motion to remove the deposits. 

 NOTE: An inferior quality wire wheel will lose steel bristles during 
operation, thus causing additional contamination. 

An alternative method to remove the carbon ridge is to use a high 
quality steel wire wheel installed in a drill or die grinder.

[FIGURE: A17312A.gif]

 NOTE: On pistons with anodized coatings, do not stamp on the anodized coating 
or on the outer rim. 

Mark each piston according to the cylinder.

[FIGURE: A17313A.gif]

Remove the capscrews, connecting rod cap and rod bearings.

[FIGURE: A17314A.gif]

Push the connecting rod and piston assembly out of cylinder bore. Care 
must be taken not to damage the connecting rod or bearing during their removal.

[FIGURE: A17315A.gif]

Disassemble the piston and connecting rod. Refer to Piston and 
Connecting Rod in the Disassembly and Assembly portion of this section. 

 Installation 

Install the bearing halves into both the rod and the connecting rod 
cap. Make sure the tang on the bearing halves is in the slot of the connecting 
rod cap and rod.

[FIGURE: A17316A.gif]

Lubricate the rod bearings with a light film of Engine Assembly 
Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A. 

Lubricate the piston rings and piston skirts with clean engine oil. 

 CAUTION: If using a strap-type ring compressor, make sure the inside end of the 
strap does not hook on a ring gap and break the piston ring. 

Position the piston rings.

[FIGURE: A17317A.gif]

Compress the piston rings.

[FIGURE: A17318A.gif]

Lubricate the cylinder bore with clean engine oil. 

Position the crankshaft rod journal for the piston to be installed to 
bottom dead center (BDC). 

[FIGURE: A17319A.gif]

 NOTE: Take care not to damage the cylinder wall when inserting the connecting 
rod. 

Position the piston and connecting rod assembly into cylinder bore with 
the word "front" on piston toward the front of the cylinder block.

[FIGURE: A17320A.gif]

Carefully push the piston into the bore while guiding the connecting 
rod to the crankshaft journal.

[FIGURE: A17321A.gif]

Lubricate the threads and underside of the connecting rod capscrew 
heads with engine oil.

 CAUTION: The four-digit number stamped on the rod and connecting rod cap at the 
parting line must match and be installed on the oil cooler side of the engine. 

Install the connecting rod cap and capscrews to the connecting rod.

[FIGURE: A17322A.gif]

Alternately, tighten the two capscrews in the following three steps: 

Step 1. 35 Nm (26 lb-ft)

Step 2. 70 Nm (51 lb-ft)

Step 3. 100 Nm (73 lb-ft)

[FIGURE: A17323A.gif]

Measure the side clearance between the connecting rod and crankshaft. 
Side clearance limits are 0.10 to 0.33 mm (0.004 to 0.013 inch). Do not 
measure the clearance between the connecting rod cap and crankshaft.

[FIGURE: A17324A.gif]

 CAUTION: The crankshaft must rotate freely. 

 CAUTION: If the connecting rod is not properly oriented (tang opposite the 
camshaft), it will contact the camshaft and prevent the crankshaft from 
rotating. 

Check for freedom of rotation as the connecting rod caps are installed. 
If the crankshaft does not rotate freely, check the installation of the rod 
bearings and the connecting rod bearing size.

[FIGURE: A17325A.gif]

Use Silicone Gasket and Sealant F6AZ-19562-AA or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification WSE-M4G323-A6 to fill the joints between the pan rail, gear 
housing and rear cover.

[FIGURE: A17326A.gif]

Coat both sides of the oil pan gasket with Perfect Seal Sealing 
Compound F2AZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specifications ESR-M18P2-A 
and ESE-M4G115-A.

[FIGURE: A17327A.gif]

Assemble the oil pan, gasket and capscrews as illustrated and install. 
Tighten capscrews to 21-27 Nm (16-19 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A17328A.gif]

Install the oil level indicator.

Install the cylinder head. Refer to Cylinder Head in the Removal and 
Installation portion of this section. Fill the cooling system and fill the 
engine with oil.

[FIGURE: A17329A.gif]

Prelube (prime) the engine prior to start-up by disconnecting the fuel 
shutoff solenoid and cranking the engine until the oil pressure gauge reads 
pressure, or no more than 30 seconds. Allow the starter to cool for two 
minutes between crank times.

Operate the engine to normal operating temperature and check for leaks.

[FIGURE: A17330A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Connecting Rod Bearings 

 Removal 

Drain the engine oil. 

Remove the oil pan and gasket. 

Rotate the crankshaft to position two of the connecting rods at bottom 
dead center (BDC).

[FIGURE: A17336A.gif]

Remove the connecting rod capscrews and connecting rod caps.

[FIGURE: A17314A.gif]

Remove the lower bearing shell from the connecting rod cap and mark it 
with the letter L (lower) and the cylinder number it was removed from.

[FIGURE: A17337A.gif]

Push the rod away from the crankshaft to allow the upper bearing shell 
to be removed.

[FIGURE: A17338A.gif]

Remove the upper bearing shell and mark it with the letter U (upper) 
and the cylinder number it was removed from.

[FIGURE: A17339A.gif]

Clean and inspect the Bearings and Connecting Rod Caps . Refer to the 
Cleaning and Inspection portion of this section. 

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Used bearings must be installed in the same location from which they 
were removed. 

Use Engine Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESR-M99C80-A to coat the inside diameter of the bearing shell 
halves.

[FIGURE: A17340A.gif]

Install the upper bearing shell in the connecting rod with the tang of 
the bearing in the slot of the rod.

[FIGURE: A21469A.gif]

Install the lower bearing shell in the connecting rod cap with the tang 
of the bearing in the slot of the connecting rod cap. Use Engine Assembly 
Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A 
to coat the inside diameter of the bearing shell.

[FIGURE: A17342A.gif]

Use clean engine oil to lubricate the threads and underside of the 
connecting rod capscrew head.

[FIGURE: A17343A.gif]

 NOTE: The four-digit number stamped on the rod and connecting rod cap at the 
parting line must match and be installed on the oil cooler side of the engine. 

Install the connecting rod cap and capscrews to the connecting rod.

[FIGURE: A17344A.gif]

Alternately tighten the two capscrews in the following three-step 
sequence: 

Step 1. 35 Nm (26 lb-ft) 

Step 2. 70 Nm (51 lb-ft) 

Step 3. 100 Nm (73 lb-ft)

[FIGURE: A17323A.gif]

Measure the side clearance between the connecting rod and crankshaft. 
Do not measure the clearance between the connecting rod cap and crankshaft. 
Side clearance limits are 0.10 to 0.33 mm (0.004 to 0.013 inch).

[FIGURE: A17345A.gif]

 CAUTION: The crankshaft must rotate freely. 

Check for freedom of rotation as the connecting rod caps are installed. 
If the crankshaft does not rotate freely, check the installation of the rod 
bearings and connecting rod bearing size. 

[FIGURE: A17325A.gif]

Install the engine lubricating oil pan and gasket. 

Fill the engine with oil.

[FIGURE: A17346A.gif]

Operate the engine to normal operating temperature and check for leaks.

[FIGURE: A17330A.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Main and Thrust Bearings, Engine in Vehicle

 Removal 

Drain the oil and remove the oil pan.

[FIGURE: A17347A.gif]

 NOTE: Before removing the crankshaft main bearing caps, make certain that the 
crankshaft main bearing caps are clearly marked for their location on the oil 
cooler side of the crankshaft main bearing cap. 

Perform a visual inspection of the main bearings and crankshaft main 
bearing journals. Remove the No. 2 and 3 crankshaft main bearing caps and 
check the crankshaft journals for signs of overheat, deep scratches or other 
damage. If there is no damage, there is no need to pull the other crankshaft 
main bearing caps at this time.

[FIGURE: A17348A.gif]

Inspect the crankshaft main bearing caps for dents, cracks, or other 
damage.

[FIGURE: A17349A.gif]

 NOTE: If the crankshaft main bearing journals or crankshaft main bearing caps 
are damaged, the engine will need to be removed to complete the overhaul. 

Inspect the crankshaft main bearing journals for deep scratches, 
indications of overheating and other damage.

[FIGURE: A17350A.gif]

Remove all crankshaft main bearing caps except the No. 1 and 7 
crankshaft main bearing cap for six-cylinder engine. 

Use a pin to roll out the upper bearings from between the crankshaft 
and cylinder block. 

To make a pin, grind a 6 mm capscrew to the dimensions shown.

[FIGURE: A17352A.gif]

Install the pin into the oil hole in the crankshaft. Rotate the 
crankshaft so the pin pushes against the end of the bearing opposite the tang. 
Remove the bearing. 

Follow this procedure to remove the other bearings.

[FIGURE: A17353A.gif]

Inspect all crankshaft main bearing caps and crankshaft main bearing 
journals.

[FIGURE: A17350A.gif]

Determine the size of the bearing removed and obtain the same size for 
installation. 

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Do not lubricate the side of the bearing that is against the cylinder 
block. 

Apply a coat of Engine Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A to the new upper bearings.

[FIGURE: A17355A.gif]

Position the new bearing on the crankshaft and install as far as 
possible by hand.

[FIGURE: A17356A.gif]

 CAUTION: Make sure the pin does not slide under the bearing. 

Using the pin, finish pushing the bearing in slowly, being sure it is 
aligned with the block. Make sure the tang on the bearing sets into the notch.

[FIGURE: A17357A.gif]

[FIGURE: A17358A.gif]

Install the lower bearings into the crankshaft main bearing caps. Apply 
a coat of Engine Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESR-M99C80-A to the bearings.

[FIGURE: A17359A.gif]

 CAUTION: Make sure the crankshaft main bearing caps are correctly installed with 
the number toward the oil cooler side of the engine. 

Install a crankshaft main bearing cap after each upper bearing is 
installed to keep the bearing in place while the other uppers are installed. 
Tighten the capscrews to 50 Nm (37 lb-ft). Do not tighten to 
the final torque value at this time.

Use the same procedure to remove and install rear crankshaft main 
bearing cap, No. 5 or No. 7.

[FIGURE: A17361A.gif]

 CAUTION: Use care so the screwdriver does not damage the crankshaft or cylinder 
block. 

Use a flat-blade screwdriver. Gently bump the end of the bearing to 
loosen it from the block. Then, use finger pressure against the upper shell 
and rotate the crankshaft to roll the bearing out.

[FIGURE: A17362A.gif]

 NOTE: The front crankshaft main bearing journal, No. 1, does not contain a 
drilled oil passage. The pin cannot be used to replace the bearing. 

Lubricate and install the bearing. Use the screwdriver to push the 
bearing into position as you rotate the crankshaft.

[FIGURE: A17363A.gif]

 CAUTION: The crankshaft must rotate freely after each crankshaft main bearing 
cap is tightened. 

Tighten the main bearing capscrews evenly in the following three-step 
sequence: 

Step 1. 60 Nm (44 lb-ft) 

Step 2. 119 Nm (87 lb-ft) 

Step 3. 176 Nm (129 lb-ft) 

Check the bearing installation and the size of the bearings if the 
crankshaft does not rotate freely.

 NOTE: The dimensions of the thrust bearing and crankshaft main bearing 
journal determine end play. 

Measure the crankshaft end play. Following are dimension A end play 
limits: 

minimum 0.127 mm (0.005 inch) maximum 0.355 mm (0.014 inch)

[FIGURE: A17365A.gif]

Install the oil pan and gasket. 

Fill the system with engine oil. Operate the engine at idle for 5 to 10 
minutes. Check for loose parts and leaks.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Crankshaft Rear Oil Seal

 Removal 

Remove the transmission. Refer to the appropriate section in Group 07. 

Remove the flywheel.

[FIGURE: A17384A.gif]

Drill two holes 180 degrees apart into the crankshaft rear oil seal 
carrier.

[FIGURE: A17385A.gif]

Using a No. 10 sheet metal screw and a slide hammer dent puller, remove 
the rear seal.

[FIGURE: A17386A.gif]

 Installation 

 CAUTION: The crankshaft rear oil seal lip and the sealing surface on the 
crankshaft must be free from all oil residue to prevent oil leaks. 

Clean and dry the crankshaft sealing surface.

[FIGURE: A17387A.gif]

Install the seal pilot, provided in the replacement kit, onto the 
crankshaft. Push the seal onto the pilot and crankshaft. Remove the seal pilot.

[FIGURE: A17388A.gif]

Use the alignment tool to install the seal to the correct depth in the 
housing. Use a hammer to drive the seal into the housing until the alignment 
tool tops against the housing. Hit the tool at 12, 3, 6 and 9 o'clock 
positions to drive the seal evenly and to prevent bending the crankshaft rear 
oil seal carrier.

[FIGURE: A17389A.gif]

Install the flywheel. Tighten the capscrews in sequence as shown in the 
illustration, to 130-144 Nm (97-106 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A17390A.gif]

Install the clutch, transmission and starter. Operate the engine and 
check for leaks. 

 Wear Sleeve, Rear Crankshaft Seal 

 Removal 

Remove the transmission. Refer to the appropriate section in Group 07.

Remove the clutch and flywheel, if so equipped. Refer to Section 08-01 .

Remove the flywheel housing. Refer to Flywheel Housing in the Removal 
and Installation portion of this section.

Remove the four lubricating oil pan mounting capscrews that secure the 
oil pan to the rear cover.

 CAUTION: Use extreme care when releasing the oil pan gasket from the rear cover 
to prevent damage to the gasket. If the gasket is damaged, the oil pan must be 
removed and the gasket replaced. 

Insert a feeler gauge or shim stock between the rear cover and the oil 
pan gasket. Move the feeler gauge or shim stock back and forth to release the 
gasket from the rear cover.

[FIGURE: A23652A.gif]

Remove the capscrews from the rear cover and remove the cover from the 
crankshaft flange. Remove the seal from the rear cover.

[FIGURE: A23653A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not nick or gouge the crankshaft with the chisel. If the crankshaft 
is damaged, it must be replaced. 

Use a dull chisel that is only as wide as the wear sleeve. Make one or 
two soft blows with a hammer across the wear sleeve. This will expand the wear 
sleeve allowing the sleeve to be removed.

[FIGURE: A23654A.gif]

Clean the gasket surface of the rear cover, crankshaft flange, and 
cylinder block.

[FIGURE: A23655A.gif]

Inspect the crankshaft flange and rear cover for dirt, nicks or other 
damage.

[FIGURE: A23656A.gif]

 Installation 

 CAUTION: The seal installation is used to properly align the rear cover. Do not 
push the cover in any direction to prevent irregular lip position after seal 
installation. 

 NOTE: Install the rear cover capscrews. Do not tighten. If the oil pan is 
installed, loosen the oil pan capscrews to allow clearance for rear cover and 
gasket clearance.

Install rear cover and gasket.

[FIGURE: A23657A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not use any kind of lubricant to install the oil seal. The oil seal 
must be installed with the lip of the oil seal and crankshaft clean and dry to 
ensure proper oil sealing. 

 NOTE: The combination crankshaft oil seal and wear sleeve is installed on the 
crankshaft as an assembly.

 NOTE: The oil seal for a wet flywheel housing requires soap on the outside 
diameter of the seal case. Nothing is required on the outside diameter of the 
seal case for dry housings.

Use Cummins Engine Company Service Tool Part No. 3824078 to install the 
oil seal and wear sleeve assembly.

 Crankshaft Wear Sleeve Installation Tool 

[FIGURE: A23658A.gif]

Apply a small amount of clean engine oil to the crankshaft threaded 
studs and the inside diameter of the crankshaft rear seal and wear sleeve 
installation tool. Install two threaded studs into the crankshaft.

Position the chamfered end of the wear sleeve onto end of the 
crankshaft. Position the counterbore end of the installation tool over the 
threaded studs and align with wear sleeve, perpendicular to end of crankshaft.

 NOTE: Do not exceed one-half revolution of each nut to prevent wear sleeve 
binding and irregular stretch.

Install washers and nuts onto the threaded studs. Alternately tighten 
the nuts until the installation tool contacts the end of the crankshaft. 
Tighten to 20 Nm (15 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A23659A.gif]

Remove the installation tool and the threaded studs.

Align the rear cover even with both sides of the oil pan rail on the 
cylinder block. Tighten the rear cover capscrews to 8-10 Nm 
(6-7 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A23660A.gif]

 NOTE: Make sure to fill the joint between the lubricating oil pan rail and 
rear cover with Silicone Gasket and Sealant F6AZ-19562-AA or equivalent 
meeting Ford specification WSE-M4G323-A6.

Trim the gaskets even with the oil pan mounting surface.

[FIGURE: A23661A.gif]

 NOTE: The oil pan capscrews should be torqued within 15 minutes after 
applying sealant.

Install four capscrews that hold the oil pan to the rear cover. Tighten 
to 21-27 Nm (16-19 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A23662A.gif]

Install the flywheel housing as described in this section.

Install the clutch and flywheel, if so equipped. Refer to Section 08-01 .

Install the transmission. Refer to the appropriate section in Group 07.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Gear Cover

 Removal 

 NOTE: If a new gear cover is to be installed, remove engine dataplate and 
attach to new gear cover.

Remove the following as described in this section: 

Valve covers, rocker levers and push rods 

Vibration damper 

Camshaft

Front cover

Remove the fuel injection pump. Refer to Section 03A-04A .

Remove the six front oil pan capscrews.

[FIGURE: A17438A.gif]

Remove the gear cover capscrews.

[FIGURE: A17439A.gif]

Using a feeler gauge, attempt to separate the oil pan gasket from the 
gear cover.

[FIGURE: A17440A.gif]

Remove the gear cover.

[FIGURE: A17441A.gif]

Clean the gasket material from the cylinder block.

[FIGURE: A17442A.gif]

Inspect the oil pan gasket. If it is not torn, coat with Perfect Seal 
Sealing Compound F2AZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specifications 
ESR-M18P2-A and ESE-M4G115-A.

[FIGURE: A17443A.gif]

If the gasket is torn, it may be repaired. Cut the torn gasket off, 
even with the front of the engine block.

[FIGURE: A17444A.gif]

Using the old gasket as a pattern, cut the front section of a new 
gasket to the same size.

[FIGURE: A17445A.gif]

Clean the sealing surfaces and coat the new gasket on both sides with 
Perfect Seal Sealing Compound F2AZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specifications ESR-M18P2-A and ESE-M4G115-A.

[FIGURE: A17446A.gif]

Use common thread or a very fine wire to hold the new oil pan gasket 
splice in position as illustrated for the repair.

[FIGURE: A17447A.gif]

 Installation 

 NOTE: When properly trimmed, the gear cover gasket should be even with the 
oil pan gasket when installed. 

Mark and trim 1.59 mm (0.078 inch) off the new gear housing gasket.

[FIGURE: A17448A.gif]

Coat both sides of the gear cover gasket with Perfect Seal Sealing 
Compound F2AZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specifications ESR-M18P2-A 
and ESE-M4G115-A.

[FIGURE: A17449A.gif]

Position the gear cover gasket on the alignment dowels.

[FIGURE: A17450A.gif]

 CAUTION: If a new gear cover or other than the original gear housing is 
installed, the timing pin assembly must be accurately located. Refer to 
Removal and Installation, Relocating Timing Pin Assembly procedure in this 
section. 

Carefully install the gear cover, making sure both gaskets are in 
place. Tighten screws to 21-27 Nm (16-19 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A17451A.gif]

Start the oil pan capscrews in the holes not being used to tie the 
gasket in place.

[FIGURE: A17452A.gif]

Remove the thread or wire holding the gasket in place.

[FIGURE: A17453A.gif]

Install the remaining two capscrews and tighten the capscrews to 21-27 Nm
 (16-19 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A17454A.gif]

Lubricate the camshaft and thrust plate with Engine Assembly Lubricant 
D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A.

[FIGURE: A17455B.gif]

 NOTE: Make sure the alignment marks on the camshaft and camshaft gears are 
aligned. 

Install the camshaft thrust plate. 

[FIGURE: A17456B.gif]

Install the camshaft thrust plate capscrews. Tighten to 21-27 Nm
 (16-19 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A17457A.gif]

Measure to verify the camshaft has proper backlash and end play: 

A = 0.12 to 0.34 mm (0.005 to 0.013 in.) 

B = 0.076 to 0.330 mm (0.003 to 0.013 in.)

[FIGURE: A17458A.gif]

Remove the lifter holders from the tappets.

[FIGURE: A17459A.gif]

Install and lubricate the push rods and complete the installation of 
the rocker levers as described in Removal and Installation, Valve Cover, 
Rocker Arms and Push Rods .

[FIGURE: A21471A.gif]

Complete the installation of the removed components as described in 
this section: 

Adjust the valves 

Install front cover 

Install vibration damper 

Install fuel injection pump (refer to Section 03A-04A )

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Relocating Timing Pin Assembly, Cylinder Head Removed 

 CAUTION: The timing pin assembly is precisely located on the gear housing to 
correspond to TDC for cylinder No. 1. The timing pin assembly must be 
relocated if the gear housing is replaced. 

Remove the front cover.

Temporarily install the crankshaft damper and a pointer fabricated from 
No. 16 gauge wire. Put a flatwasher between the pointer and gear housing to 
prevent damage to gear housing.

[FIGURE: A18283A.gif]

Fabricate a steel plate to the dimensions shown in the following 
illustration. 

Using two flywheel housing bolts, clamp the fabricated plate across 
number one cylinder. 

Rotate the crankshaft until number one piston touches the plate, then 
mark the damper. 

Rotate the crankshaft in the opposite direction until the piston 
touches the plate, and mark the damper again. 

Mark the damper exactly half way between the two marks. This is top 
dead center. 

Remove the plate and rotate the crankshaft until the wire pointer 
aligns with the new TDC mark. 

Look for the timing pin hole in the back of the camshaft gear. If the 
hole is not visible, rotate the crankshaft 360 degrees. 

Install a new O-ring into the groove of the timing pin assembly. 
Lubricate the O-ring with 15W-40 engine oil.

Apply a coat of Threadlock® 262 E2FZ-19554-B or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G351-A6 to the threads of the Torx®
 screws and install the timing pin assembly.

Push the pin into the hole in the cam gear to align the housing.

 CAUTION: To prevent damage to the pin and gear, be sure the timing pin is 
disengaged before rotating the crankshaft. 

Hold the pin in while tightening the Torx® screws to 5 Nm
 (44 lb-in). Check the pin to be sure it did not slip out 
of the camshaft gear hole when the screws were tightened.

[FIGURE: A18289A.gif]

Remove the vibration damper and wire pointer.

[FIGURE: A18290A.gif]

Install the gear cover. Refer to Cover, Front in the Removal and 
Installation portion of this section.

Install the vibration damper. Refer to Crankshaft Pulley and/or 
Damper in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

PAGE 4118
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 03A-01: Engine, FD-1060 Diesel

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Relocating Timing Pin Assembly, Cylinder Head Installed 

 CAUTION: The timing pin assembly is precisely located on the gear housing to 
correspond to top dead center (TDC) for cylinder No. 1. The timing pin 
assembly must be relocated if the gear housing is replaced. 

Remove the front cover. Refer to Removal and Installation, Cover, Front .

Locate top dead center (TDC) for cylinder No. 1 by barring engine 
slowly while pressing on the engine timing pin.

[FIGURE: A17171A.gif]

[FIGURE: A18281A.gif]

 CAUTION: If a gear housing other than the original housing is installed, the 
timing pin assembly must be accurately aligned to correspond to TDC for 
cylinder No. 1. 

Remove the timing pin assembly and seal.

Verify the timing marks on the crankshaft and camshaft are aligned or 
the hole in the back of the camshaft gear is visible through the gear housing.

[FIGURE: A18282A.gif]

To align the assembly, temporarily install the vibration damper and a 
pointer fabricated from No. 16 gauge wire. Put a flatwasher between the 
pointer and gear housing to prevent damage to the gear housing.

[FIGURE: A18283A.gif]

Remove high pressure fuel lines.

 NOTE: This step is important to release cylinder pressure so the crankshaft 
can be rotated smoothly to locate TDC for cylinder No. 1.

Remove all injector nozzles.

Remove the valve cover.

Adjust the intake valve rocker lever on No. 1 cylinder to have zero 
valve clearance.

[FIGURE: A18284A.gif]

Rotate the crankshaft 90 degrees in the direction of normal engine 
rotation.

[FIGURE: A18285B.gif]

 NOTE: Leave the adjusting screw in this position until TDC is established.

Tighten the adjusting screw for the No. 1 intake valve five complete 
turns of the screw.

 CAUTION: Use extreme care that the piston does not push against the exhaust 
valve with so much force that it bends the push rod, valve stem, or damages 
the valve head or piston. 

Rotate the crankshaft slowly in the direction opposite engine rotation 
until the piston just touches the intake valve.

Mark the vibration damper.

[FIGURE: A18286B.gif]

 CAUTION: Make sure the piston touches the valve with approximately the same 
amount of force as in the previous step. 

Rotate the crankshaft in the direction of engine rotation until the 
piston just touches the intake valve.

Mark the vibration damper.

Measure the distance and mark the damper at one-half the distance 
between the two marks. This mark is the TDC mark.

[FIGURE: A18287B.gif]

 CAUTION: Failure to loosen the No. 1 intake valve adjusting screw will result in 
bending the push rod, valve stem or damage to valve face or piston when the 
crankshaft is rotated. 

Completely loosen the No. 1 intake valve adjusting screw.

Rotate the crankshaft in the direction of engine rotation until the 
pointer is aligned with the TDC mark then an additional one full revolution 
(360 degrees).

[FIGURE: A18288A.gif]

Look through the back side of the gear housing for the timing pin hole 
in the camshaft gear. If the hole is not visible, the crankshaft must be 
rotated one revolution.

Install a new O-ring into the groove of the timing pin assembly. 
Lubricate the O-ring with 15W-40 engine oil.

Apply a coat of Threadlock® 262 E2FZ-19554-B or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G351-A6 to the threads of the Torx®
 screws and install the timing pin assembly.

Push the pin into the hole in the camshaft gear to align the housing.

 CAUTION: To prevent damage to the pin and gear, make sure the timing pin is 
disengaged before rotating the crankshaft. 

Hold the pin in while tightening the Torx® screws to 5 Nm
 (44 lb-in). Check the pin to be sure it did not slip out 
of the camshaft gear hole when the screws were tightened.

[FIGURE: A18289A.gif]

Remove the vibration damper and wire pointer.

[FIGURE: A18290A.gif]

Install the front cover. Refer to Cover, Front in the Removal and 
Installation portion of this section.

Install the vibration damper. Refer to Crankshaft Pulley and/or 
Damper in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

Adjust the No. 1 intake valve clearance to 0.25 mm (0.010 inch). Refer 
to Valve Adjustment, Cold, in the Adjustments portion of this section.

Install the valve cover with a new seal.

Install the injector nozzles and high pressure fuel lines, then bleed 
fuel system. Refer to Section 03A-04A .

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Flywheel Housing 

 Removal 

Remove the transmission, clutch and all related components (if so 
equipped). Refer to the appropriate section in Group 07 and to Section 08-01 .

[FIGURE: A17466A.gif]

Remove the flywheel.

[FIGURE: A17384A.gif]

Adequately support the engine to prevent damage. Disconnect the battery 
cables and remove the starter motor.

[FIGURE: J5186B.gif]

Disconnect both rear engine supports.

Remove the flywheel housing capscrews.

[FIGURE: A17469A.gif]

 CAUTION: The component weighs 23 kg (50 lb) or more. To avoid personal injury, 
use a hoist or get assistance to lift the component. 

Use a rubber hammer to loosen the flywheel housing. Remove the flywheel 
housing and flywheel housing seal.

[FIGURE: A17470A.gif]

 WARNING: WHEN USING A STEAM CLEANER, WEAR PROTECTIVE CLOTHING AND SAFETY GLASSES 
OR A FACE SHIELD. HOT STEAM CAN CAUSE SERIOUS PERSONAL INJURY. 

Use steam or solvent to clean the flywheel housing. Dry with compressed 
air.

[FIGURE: A17471A.gif]

Inspect the flywheel housing for cracks, especially in the bolt pattern 
area. Visually inspect all surfaces for nicks, burrs, or cracks. Use fine 
crocus cloth to remove small nicks and burrs.

[FIGURE: A17472A.gif]

Inspect for damaged threads commonly caused by cross-threaded capscrews 
or installing an incorrect capscrew. Heli-coils are available to repair 
damaged threads.

[FIGURE: A17473A.gif]

 Installation 

Install flywheel housing seal and lubricate with Multi-Purpose Grease 
DOAZ-19584-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specifications ESR-M1C159-A and 
ESB-M1C93-B.

[FIGURE: A17474B.gif]

 NOTE: Be sure the flywheel housing seal is not damaged during installation. 

Visually inspect the rear face of the cylinder block and flywheel 
housing mounting surface for cleanliness and raised nicks or burrs. Install 
the flywheel housing over the two ring dowels.

[FIGURE: A17475A.gif]

Tighten the flywheel housing capscrews in sequence shown to 75-81 Nm
 (56-59 lb-ft) for a cast iron housing, or 54-61 Nm
 (40-45 lb-ft) for an aluminum housing.

[FIGURE: A17476A.gif]

Check the flywheel housing bore and flywheel housing face alignments. 
Refer to Section 03-00 . 

Install the transmission, clutch and related components.

Sending Unit

 Removal

Unscrew the unit from its mounting.

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Be sure to use Pipe Sealant with Teflon® D8AZ-19554-A

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Cylinder Head

 Removal 

 NOTE: It is easier and faster to remove the cylinder head as an assembly, and 
then remove additional components on the bench after the cylinder head is out 
of the vehicle. 

Disconnect the battery ground cables and drain the engine coolant.

Working from the right side of the engine compartment, remove the air 
cleaner assembly, air cleaner support and the turbocharger air inlet adapter. 
Cap the turbocharger air inlet. 

Disconnect the air-to-air tube from the charge air cooler and the 
turbocharger. Remove the air-to-air tube. Cap the charge air cooler inlet and 
turbocharger outlet. 

Disconnect the ether cold start line from the intake manifold (if so 
equipped). 

Remove the turbocharger oil supply and return lines. 

Disconnect the temperature sender wire on the thermostat housing. 

Remove the engine oil filter. 

Remove the exhaust pipe band clamp on the turbocharger exhaust outlet. 

Disconnect the upper radiator hose, the heater hoses to the thermostat 
housing and the heater hose from the heater hose tube assembly. 

Remove the generator drive belt, the upper generator bracket, and the 
bolt securing the generator lower support to the thermostat housing. 

Remove the bolt securing the heater hose tube to the cylinder head, 
loosen the flange nut and remove the heater hose tube. 

Working from the left side of the engine compartment, disconnect the 
air-to-air tube from the charge air cooler and the intake manifold. Remove the 
air-to-air tube. Cap the charge air cooler outlet. 

On vehicles equipped with hydraulic brakes, remove the brake hydraulic 
pump belt, and remove the brake pump from the mounting bracket. Position the 
pump out of the way. 

On air brake-equipped vehicles, remove the air compressor air inlet 
hose. 

Remove the bolts securing the engine cooling fan hub to the engine, and 
remove the fan and hub as an assembly.

[FIGURE: A17302A.gif]

Remove the wiring brackets from the rocker arm cover. 

Disconnect the injector high pressure lines from the injectors and the 
injection pump. Cap all lines to prevent contamination.

[FIGURE: A17303A.gif]

Disconnect the fuel supply hose at the fuel sediment bowl and the 
supply hose for the lift pump. Remove the fuel line from the lift pump to the 
fuel filter assembly. Cap all lines to prevent contamination. 

Remove the fuel filter. 

Disconnect the air inlet temperature sensor, remove the electrical 
bracket from the cylinder head and position the wiring harness out of the way. 

Remove the rocker arm covers and loosen all of the rocker arm adjusting 
nuts and screws. 

Mark the rocker arm pedestals for installation in the same locations. 
Remove the rocker arm shaft support bolts and remove the rocker arm and 
pedestal assemblies. Remove the push rods, noting their locations.

[FIGURE: A17304A.gif]

Remove the cylinder head bolts in the sequence shown.

[FIGURE: A17305A.gif]

Using a suitable lifting device, remove the cylinder head from the 
vehicle.

[FIGURE: A17306A.gif]

Remove additional components from the cylinder head as required for 
service. 

Inspect the cylinder head and block. Refer to Section 03-00 . 

 Installation 

 NOTE: Oversize service head gaskets are used when the cylinder head surface 
on the block or the cylinder head has been machined. Oversize service gaskets 
are available in either 0.25 mm (0.010 inch) oversize or 0.50 mm (0.020 inch) 
oversize. 

Install any components removed from the cylinder head after removal 
from the vehicle. 

Position a new cylinder head gasket on the engine block observing 
correct alignment with the holes in the engine block. Using a suitable lifting 
device, position the cylinder head on the engine and seat it onto the 
alignment dowels.

[FIGURE: A17307A.gif]

Position the push rods in their correct positions into the valve 
tappets. Lubricate the push rod sockets and the valve stem ends with fresh 
engine oil.

[FIGURE: A17308A.gif]

 CAUTION: Refer to the Cleaning and Inspection portion of this section for 
guidelines on cylinder head bolt reuse. If they are too long, they will not 
properly clamp down the cylinder head. 

With the rocker arm adjusting screws completely loosened, position the 
rocker arm pedestals. Apply a light coating of fresh engine oil to the rocker 
arm shaft support bolt threads (long bolts), and under the bolt head, and 
install the retaining bolts (long bolts) hand-tight. 

Lightly lubricate the remaining cylinder head bolt threads and under 
the bolt heads, and install them hand-tight.

[FIGURE: A17309A.gif]

 CAUTION: The following procedure must be used for cylinder head bolt 
installation. 

Tighten the cylinder head bolts in the sequence shown using the Torque 
Plus Angle as follows: 

Tighten all cylinder head bolts in sequence to 90 Nm 
(66 lb-ft). 

Recheck all cylinder head bolt torques in sequence to 90 Nm
 (66 lb-ft). 

Tighten only the six long cylinder head bolts (4, 5, 12, 13, 20 and 21) 
in sequence to 120 Nm (90 lb-ft). 

Recheck the six long cylinder head bolts in sequence to 120 Nm
 (90 lb-ft). 

Following the sequence shown, turn all cylinder head bolts an 
additional 90 degrees. 

Recheck all cylinder head bolt torques by turning to 136 Nm
 (102 lb-ft). If any cylinder head bolts turn, loosen that 
cylinder head bolt and retighten it per Steps a through f above.

[FIGURE: A17305A.gif]

Install the remaining (short) rocker arm shaft support bolts and 
tighten to 21-27 Nm (16-19 lb-ft). 

Adjust the valve clearances. Refer to Valve Adjustment, Cold in the 
Adjustments portion of this section. 

Install the rocker arm covers. 

Connect the air inlet temperature sensor, and install the electrical 
bracket to the cylinder head. 

Install a new fuel filter. 

Connect the fuel supply hose to the fuel sediment bowl and the supply 
hose for the lift pump. Install the fuel line to the lift pump and the fuel 
filter assembly. 

Connect the injector high pressure lines to the injectors and the 
injection pump. 

Install the wiring brackets to the rocker arm covers. 

Position the engine cooling fan and hub to the engine and tighten the 
bolts to 24 Nm (18 lb-ft). 

On air brake-equipped vehicles, install the air compressor air inlet 
hose. 

On vehicles equipped with hydraulic brakes, install the brake hydraulic 
pump assembly and adjust the belt to specifications. 

Working from the left side of the engine compartment, connect the 
air-to-air tube to the charge air cooler and the intake manifold. 

Install heater hose tube to cylinder head.

Install bolt securing generator lower support to thermostat housing. 
Install upper generator bracket and drive belt. Check torque of belt tensioner 
mounting bolts. Correct torque value is 43 Nm (32 lb-ft).

Connect upper radiator hose, the heater hoses to the thermostat housing 
and the heater hose to the heater hose tube assembly.

Install the exhaust pipe band clamp on the turbocharger exhaust outlet.

Install new oil filter.

Connect the temperature sender wire on the thermostat housing.

Install the turbocharger oil supply and return lines.

If so equipped, connect the ether cold start line to the intake manifold.

Connect the air-to-air tube to the charge air cooler and the 
turbocharger.

Install the turbocharger air inlet adapter, air cleaner support and the 
air cleaner assembly.

 CAUTION: New turbochargers must be pre-lubricated with 50-60 cc (2 to 3 ounces) 
of clean engine oil. After pouring oil into the turbocharger, rotate the 
turbine wheel to allow oil to enter the bearing housing. 

Fill the engine crankcase with engine oil. Add engine coolant.

Connect battery ground cable.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Flywheel

 Removal 

Remove the vehicle driveline and transmission. Refer to the appropriate 
section in Group 07.

Remove the clutch discs and the pressure plate, if so equipped. Refer 
to Section 08-01 .

 NOTE: Use Engine Barring Tool D92T-6000-C or equivalent to hold the flywheel 
to prevent rotation.

Remove two capscrews 180 degrees apart. Install two M12 x 1.25 x 90 mm 
guide pins.

[FIGURE: A17462A.gif]

 NOTE: If a clutch is used in the equipment, the threads in the clutch 
pressure plate mounting capscrew holes can be metric or standard. Be sure to 
use the correct capscrews.

Determine the capscrew thread design and size and install two T-handles 
in the flywheel at points A and B.

Remove the remaining six flywheel mounting capscrews.

[FIGURE: A18294A.gif]

 CAUTION: The component weighs 23 kg (50 lb) or more. To avoid personal injury, 
use a hoist or get assistance to lift the component. 

Remove the flywheel from the guide pins.

[FIGURE: DA0180A.gif]

If ring gear requires replacement, refer to Flywheel 
Ring Gear in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

 Installation 

 NOTE: Use a new pilot bearing when installing a new or rebuilt clutch.

Use a mandrel and a hammer to remove the pilot bearing.

Use a Scotch-Brite® 7448 or equivalent to clean the 
pilot bore.

 NOTE: The pilot bearing must be installed even with the pilot bore surface.

Use a mandrel and hammer to install the pilot bearing.

[FIGURE: A18296A.gif]

Install two M12 x 1.25 x 90 mm guide pins into the crankshaft flange 
180 degrees apart.

 NOTE: If a clutch is used in the equipment, the threads in the clutch 
pressure plate mounting capscrew holes can be metric or standard. Make sure to 
use the correct capscrews.

Determine the capscrew thread design and size and install two T-handles 
into the flywheel at points A and B.

[FIGURE: A18297A.gif]

Visually inspect rear face of crankshaft and flywheel mounting flange 
for cleanliness and raised nicks or burrs.

 CAUTION: The component weighs 23 kg (50 lb) or more. To avoid personal injury, 
use a hoist or get assistance to lift the component. 

Install the flywheel on the guide pins.

Lubricate the threads of the capscrews and the surface of the washers 
with 15W-40 engine oil.

Install the six capscrews.

Remove the T-handles and guide pins.

Install the remaining capscrews into the holes from which the guide 
pins were removed.

Hold the crankshaft when tightening the flywheel capscrews.

Tighten the capscrews in the sequence shown (a star pattern) to 130-144 Nm
 (97-106 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A17390A.gif]

Install the clutch discs and pressure plate. Refer to Section 08-01 . 

Install the vehicle transmission and driveline. Refer to the 
appropriate section in Group 07.

 Removal

 Installation

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Piston Grading

 CAUTION: If a new cylinder block or crankshaft is used, a piston grading 
procedure must be used. 

Install the connecting rod and piston assembly into the No. 1 cylinder 
without the rings installed.

[FIGURE: A23634A.gif]

 CAUTION: The connecting rod bearing shells must be installed in the original 
connecting rod and cap. 

Install the upper bearing shell in the connecting rod with the tang of 
the bearing in the slot of the connecting rod. Use clean engine oil to coat 
the inside diameter of the connecting rod shell.

[FIGURE: A23635A.gif]

Install the bearing shell in the connecting rod cap with the tang of 
the bearing in the slot of the cap. Use clean engine oil to coat the inside 
diameter of the bearing shell.

[FIGURE: A23636A.gif]

The four-digit number stamped on the connecting rod and cap at the 
parting line must match and be installed on the oil cooler side of the engine. 
Install the connecting rod cap and capscrews to the connecting rod. Tighten 
capscrews to 35 Nm (26 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A23637A.gif]

Clean and remove all burrs from the cylinder block head deck. Zero Dial 
Indicator/Magnetic Base D78P-4201-B or equivalent.

[FIGURE: A23638A.gif]

 NOTE: Do not place the indicator tip on the anodized area.

Move the dial indicator over the piston, directly over the piston pin, 
to eliminate any side to side movement.

[FIGURE: A23665A.gif]

Rotate the crankshaft to top dead center (TDC). Rotate the crankshaft 
clockwise and counterclockwise to find the highest dial indicator reading. 
Record the reading.

[FIGURE: A23666A.gif]

Remove the piston and connecting rod assembly from the No. 1 cylinder 
and install the assembly into the No. 2 cylinder. Repeat the procedure for 
every cylinder using the same piston and connecting rod.

[FIGURE: A23667A.gif]

Determine the grade of the piston being used for grading by referring 
to the chart. The four digits on top of the piston are the last four digits of 
the part number.

[FIGURE: A23668A.gif]

[FIGURE: A17486A.gif]

[FIGURE: A17487A.gif]

[FIGURE: A17403A.gif]

 CAUTION: Keep the valves in a labeled rack for a correct match with companion

[FIGURE: A17489A.gif]

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Piston and Connecting Rod 

 Disassembly 

Remove the retaining rings.

[FIGURE: A17494A.gif]

 NOTE: Heating the piston is not required.

Remove the piston pin. 

[FIGURE: A17495A.gif]

Using a piston ring expander, remove the piston rings.

[FIGURE: A17496A.gif]

Clean and inspect the piston, pin and connecting rod as outlined under Cleaning and Inspection 
. 

 Piston-to-Cylinder Bore Fit 

Cylinder bore measurements are made from 25.4 mm (1.0 inch) below the 
cylinder to 144.3 mm (4.5 inch) below the cylinder. Orientation is parallel to 
the crankshaft. Record the measurements at these two places.

[FIGURE: A24931A.gif]

Measure piston diameter at right angles to the pin bore and 12 mm (0.47 
inch) from the bottom of the skirt.

[FIGURE: A24932A.gif]

Subtract the piston bore diameter from the cylinder bore diameter. 
Acceptable clearance is 0.113-0.293 mm (0.005-0.0115 inch).

 Assembly 

 CAUTION: If a piston ring expander tool is being used, be careful not to 
overexpand the piston ring. 

Be sure FRONT marking on piston and the numbers on the rod and 
connecting rod cap are oriented as illustrated.

[FIGURE: A17497A.gif]

Install the retaining ring in the piston pin retainer groove on the 
front side of the piston.

[FIGURE: A17498A.gif]

 NOTE: Pistons do not require heating to install the pin, however, the pistons 
do need to be at room temperature or above.

Lubricate the pin and piston pin bores with engine oil and install the 
pin. 

Install the second retaining ring.

[FIGURE: A17499A.gif]

Check the piston ring gap.

[FIGURE: A23677A.gif]

Position each piston ring in the cylinder and use a piston to square it 
with the bore. A = 89 mm (3.5 inch).

[FIGURE: A17501A.gif]

Use a feeler gauge to measure the piston ring gap.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Core Plugs

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Impact Slide Hammer

T50T-100-A

Impact Slide Hammer

T59L-100-B

 Removal 

To remove a large core plug, drill a 12.70-mm (0.5-inch) hole in the 
center of the plug and remove with Impact Slide Hammer T59L-100-B or 
T50T-100-A or pry it out with a large drift punch. On a small core plug, drill 
a 6.35-mm (0.25-inch) hole in the center of the plug and pry it out with a 
small pin punch. 

Clean and inspect the plug bore. 

 Installation 

Inspect the plug bore for any damage that would interfere with the 
proper sealing of the plug. 

Coat the plug and bore lightly with an oil-resistant (oil galley) or 
Perfect Seal Sealing Compound F2AZ-19554 or equivalent meeting Ford 
specifications ESR-M18P2-A and ESE-M4G115-A. 

Install the plug bore following the procedure for cup-type or 
expansion-type below. 

 Cup-Type 

Cup-type core plugs are installed with the flanged edge outward. The 
maximum diameter of this plug is located at the outer edge of the flange. The 
flange on cup-type plugs flares outward with the largest diameter of the outer 
(sealing) edge.

 CAUTION: It is imperative to pull the plug into the machined bore by using a 
properly designed tool. Under no circumstances is the plug to be driven into 
the bore using a tool that contacts the flange. This method will damage the 
sealing edge and will result in leakage or plug blowout. 

[FIGURE: A3217E.gif]

Item

Part Number

Description

—

Sealing Edge 

 CAUTION: If the core plug replacing tool has a depth seating surface, do not 
seat the tool against a non-machined (casting) surface. 

The flanged (trailing) edge must be below the chamfered edge of the 
bore to effectively seal the plugged bore. 

 Expansion-Type 

Expansion-type core plugs are installed with the flange edge inward. 
The maximum diameter of this plug is located at the base of the flange with 
the flange flaring inward.

 CAUTION: It is imperative to push or drive the plug into the machined bore using 
a properly designed tool. Under no circumstances is the plug to be driven 
using a tool that contacts the crowned portion of the plug. This method will 
expand the plug prior to installation and may damage the plug and/or plug 
bore. 

 CAUTION: If the core plug replacing tool has a depth seating surface, do not 
seat the tool against a non-machined (casting) surface. 

When installed, the trailing (maximum) diameter must be below the 
chamfered edge of the bore to effectively seal the plugged bore. 

 Cylinder Block, Side 

 Removal 

Clean the area near the expansion plug of all debris.

[FIGURE: A24933A.gif]

Remove the large expansion plugs from the cylinder block.

[FIGURE: A24934A.gif]

Thoroughly clean the expansion plug hole.

[FIGURE: A24935A.gif]

Visually inspect the core plug bore for damage.

[FIGURE: A24936A.gif]

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Excessive sealant can run back into the engine and cause damage to 
other components. Allow the sealant to dry for a minimum of 2 hours before 
operating the engine. 

Apply a 2 mm (0.078 inch) bead of expansion plug lock 'N seal, Cummins 
part number 3375068 or equivalent to the outside diameter of the expansion 
plug and the inside diameter of the expansion plug bore.

[FIGURE: A24937A.gif]

 NOTE: The expansion plug must be installed with the edge of the expansion 
plug 0.5-1.0 mm (0.020-0.040 inch) deeper than the entrance chamfer of the bore.

Install the expansion plug.

[FIGURE: A24938A.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Valve Tappets 

 CAUTION: Any time a new camshaft is installed, new tappets must also be installed. 

Clean the valve tappets with solvent and dry with compressed air.

Inspect the socket, stem and face for excessive wear, cracks and other 
damage. Visual limits: (A) normal contact (exaggerated); (B) and (C) irregular 
contact; do not reuse. 

[FIGURE: A17570C.gif]

Pit marks on the valve tappet face are acceptable. 

The following criteria define the size of the pits allowed. 

A single pit cannot be greater than 2 mm (0.078 inch). 

Interconnection of pits is not allowed. 

Total pits when added together should not exceed 6 mm (0.236 inch) 
diameter or a total of four percent of the valve tappet face. 

No pitting is allowable on the edges of the wear face of the valve 
tappet. 

[FIGURE: A17571A.gif]

Measure the valve tappet stem diameter for: minimum 15.936 mm (0.627 
inch) and maximum 15.977 mm (0.629 inch).

[FIGURE: A17572A.gif]

[FIGURE: A17573A.gif]

[FIGURE: A17575A.gif]

Inspect the cam lobes for pitting. A single pit must not be greater

[FIGURE: A17577A.gif]

[FIGURE: A17578A.gif]

[FIGURE: A17579A.gif]

area of a 2 mm (0.078 inch) circle within ±20 degrees of

[FIGURE: A17580A.gif]

Inspect the camshaft bore for obvious damage and excessive wear.

[FIGURE: A17587A.gif]

 NOTE: If the camshaft bores without a bushing are worn beyond the limit, the

replacement of the cylinder block. 

Measure the camshaft bore inside diameter. Maximum ID for No. 1 bushing

mm (2.1324 inch).

[FIGURE: A17588A.gif]

[FIGURE: A17589A.gif]

Mark the camshaft bushing and cylinder block to align the oil hole in

[FIGURE: A17590A.gif]

Install the bushing so that it is even with the front face of the

[FIGURE: A17591A.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Camshaft Bearing

 Inspection 

Inspect the camshaft bearing for pitting or scoring. Measure the 
clearance between the internal diameter of the bearing and the outside 
diameter of the respective camshaft journal. If the clearance exceeds 0.184 mm 
(0.007 inch) remove and install a new bearing.

PAGE 4140
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 03A-01: Engine, FD-1060 Diesel

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Camshaft Drive Gear and Thrust Plate

 Inspection 

Clean the gear, thrust plate and spacer in solvent. 

Check the gear and thrust plate for scores or nicks. Also, check the 
gear for the condition of the teeth wear pattern. Discard parts that show 
signs of excessive wear. 

Measure the thickness of the thrust plate. If the thrust plate is less 
than 9.340 mm (0.368 inch), discard the thrust plate and install a new one.

Check the keyway and key on the end of the camshaft. If the key is 
damaged, install a new key before installing the gear. Use a carborundum stone 
to remove minor gear teeth imperfections. If tooth wear or damage is severe, 
install a new gear.

Section 03A-01: Engine, FD-1060 Diesel

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Piston and Pin

 Cleaning 

 CAUTION: Be sure the cleaning solvent is approved for aluminum. Damage to the 
pistons can result. 

Allow the pistons to soak for a minimum of 30 minutes in a tank 
containing an approved cleaning solvent for aluminum.

 CAUTION: Do not clean the pistons and rods in an acid tank. 

 CAUTION: Do not use a metal brush. A metal brush will damage the piston ring 
grooves. Do not use glass beads to clean the grooves. Walnut shell or plastic 
bead blasting may be used on grooves with a ni-resist insert and on the dome 
or crown of the piston. Use the minimum effective pressure and do not 
concentrate the spray in one area for an extended period of time. The 
recommended blast pressure for plastic bead blasting is: 276 kPa (40 psi). Do 
not use glass beads or walnut shell blasting on the aluminum grooves or piston 
pin bores. This can cause the piston pin bore to crack or the piston rings to 
not seat. 

Wash the pistons and rods in a strong solution of laundry detergent in 
hot water. Use a non-metallic brush to remove carbon deposits.

 CAUTION: Do not use a piston ring groove cleaner. Make sure not to scratch the 
piston ring sealing surface in the piston ring groove. 

Clean the remaining deposits from the piston ring grooves with the 
square end of a broken piston ring. 

Wash the pistons again in a detergent solution or solvent. After 
rinsing, use compressed air to dry. 

 Inspection 

Inspect the piston for damage and excessive wear. Check the top, ring 
grooves, skirt and piston pin bore.

[FIGURE: A17533A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not use pistons with cracks. 

Inspect the piston bowl, pin bore and skirt for cracks or other damage.

Measure the piston skirt diameter as illustrated: minimum 101.823 mm 
(4.0088 inch) and maximum 101.887 mm (4.0107 inch).

[FIGURE: A17534B.gif]

Use a new piston ring and feeler gauge to measure the clearance in the 
piston ring groove.

[FIGURE: A17535A.gif]

Measure the piston pin bore diameter: minimum 40.028 mm (1.5759 inch)

 WARNING: WHEN USING A STEAM CLEANER, WEAR PROTECTIVE CLOTHING AND SAFETY GLASSES

[FIGURE: A17539A.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Crankshaft

 Cleaning and Inspection 

 CAUTION: A limited number of crankshaft main bearing or rod bearing journals 
will be ground 0.25 mm (0.010 inch) or 0.05 mm (0.002 inch) undersize in 
production. Engines equipped with undersize crankshafts will be identified 
with one of the following codes on the right front of the block near the 
engine code. 

 NOTE: If a new crankshaft is used, a piston grading procedure must be used. 
Refer to Piston Grading in the Removal and Installation portion of this section.

 Code 

 (M) — Undersize main bearing journals

 (P) — Undersize rod bearing journals

 (MP) — Undersize main and rod bearing 
journals.

 CAUTION: Handle the crankshaft with care to avoid possible damage to the 
finished surfaces. 

If the crankshaft gear teeth are excessively worn or chipped, install a 
new crankshaft gear which must be fully located on the shoulder of the 
crankshaft. Refer to Crankshaft Gear in the Removal and Installation portion 
of this section.

Clean the crankshaft with solvent, then blow out all oil passages with 
compressed air.

Measure the diameter of each journal in at least four places to 
determine an out-of-round, taper or undersize condition.

[FIGURE: A100941A.gif]

On an engine used with a manual transmission, check the fit of the 
clutch pilot bearing in the bore of the crankshaft. A needle roller bearing 
and adapter assembly is used as a clutch pilot bearing. It is press-fit 
directly into the engine crankshaft and should not be loose. Inspect the inner 
surface of the bearing for wear or a bell-mouth condition. Check the inside 
diameter of the bearing to see if it is worn or damaged. The bearing and 
adapter assembly cannot be serviced separately. The needle bearing clutch 
pilot can only be installed with the seal end of the bearing facing the 
transmission. The bearing and seal are pregreased and do not require 
additional lubrication. A new bearing must be installed whenever a bearing is 
removed.

Inspect the pilot bearing, when used, for roughness, evidence of 
overheating or loss of lubricant. Replace if any of these conditions are found.

Examine the rear oil seal journal for score marks, remove minor 
imperfections with fine emery cloth (600 grade). Clean journal around its 
circumference, not lengthwise. Clean the rear oil seal journal thoroughly with 
solvent after using emery cloth.

 Journals, Refinishing 

Dress minor imperfections such as scores, nicks or burrs with an oil 
stone. If the journals are severely marred or exceed the service limit, they 
must be refinished to size for the next undersize bearing. 

If required, machine the journals to give the proper clearance with the 
next undersize bearing. If the journals will not clean up to maximum undersize 
bearing available, replace the crankshaft. 

Always reproduce the same journal shoulder radius that existed 
originally. Too small a radius will result in fatigue failure of the 
crankshaft. Too large a radius will result in bearing failure due to radius 
ride of the bearing. 

After refinishing the journals, chamfer the oil holes. Polish the 
journal with a No. 320 grit polishing cloth and engine oil (crocus cloth can 
also be used as a polishing agent) to obtain a smooth finish.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Crankshaft Main Bearings 

 Cleaning 

 CAUTION: Do not scrape gum or varnish deposits from the bearing shells. 

Bearings that are to be reused should be identified so they can be 
installed in their original locations. 

Clean the bearing inserts and caps thoroughly in solvent, and dry them 
with compressed air. 

 Inspection 

Inspect each bearing carefully. Bearings that have a scored, chipped or 
worn surface should be replaced. Typical examples of unsatisfactory bearings 
and their causes are shown in the illustration. The copper lead bearing base 
may be visible through the bearing overlay. If the base showing is less than 
20 percent of the total area, the bearing is not excessively worn. It is not 
necessary to replace the bearing if the bearing clearance is within 
recommended limits. Check the clearance of bearings that appear to be 
satisfactory with Plastigage® as outlined below.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Cylinder Head Bolts 

 NOTE: It is possible to reuse cylinder head bolts up to ten times before it 
exceeds the specified length. 

 NOTE: Immediately after cleaning and inspecting, apply a light coat of engine 
oil to the cylinder head bolts that are to be reused. 

Cylinder head bolts must be checked for length before they can be 
reused. If they are too long, they will not properly clamp down the cylinder 
head. 

Also, any cylinder head bolt that shows signs of cracking, pitting or 
rusting must be replaced. 

Measure the cylinder head bolt from under the shoulder to the end of

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Cylinder Head 

 Cleaning 

Clean the carbon from the fuel injector nozzle seat using a suitable 
fuel injector bore brush.

[FIGURE: A17512A.gif]

Remove all gasket material from all gasket surfaces. Use a Scotch-Brite®
 pad or equivalent. Do not use anything that would scratch 
mating surface.

Clean the buildup of deposits from the coolant passages. Excessive 
deposits can be cleaned in an acid tank but the cup plugs must first be removed.

[FIGURE: A17514A.gif]

Clean the combustion deck with a Scotch-Brite® pad or 
an equivalent cleaning pad and diesel fuel or solvent.

[FIGURE: A17515A.gif]

 WARNING: WEAR PROTECTIVE EYE COVERING. 

 NOTE: An inferior quality wire wheel will lose steel bristles during 
operation, thus causing additional contamination. 

Clean carbon deposits from the valve pockets with a high quality steel 
wire wheel installed in a drill or a die grinder.

[FIGURE: A17516A.gif]

Wash the cylinder head in hot 88°C (190°
F) soapy water solution for 30 minutes. After rinsing, use 
compressed air to dry the cylinder head.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Flywheel 

 Automatic Transmission 

Inspect the flywheel for cracks or other damage that would make it 
unfit for further service. Inspect the flywheel ring gear for worn, chipped or 
cracked teeth. If the teeth are damaged, replace the ring gear and flywheel 
assembly. 

With the flywheel installed on the crankshaft, check the gear face 
runout. 

 Manual Transmission 

Inspect the flywheel for cracks, heat check, or other damage that would 
make it unfit for further service. Machine the friction surface of the 
flywheel if it is scored or worn. If it is necessary to remove more than 1.0 
mm (0.040 inch) of stock from the original thickness, replace the flywheel. 

Inspect the ring gear for worn, chipped or cracked teeth. If the teeth 
are damaged, replace the ring gear. 

With the flywheel installed on the crankshaft, check the flywheel face 
runout. Refer to Section 03-00 .

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Oil Pan

 Cleaning 

Scrape any dirt or metal particles from the inside of the pan. Scrape 
all old gasket material from the gasket surface. Wash the pan in a solvent and 
dry it thoroughly. Make sure all foreign particles are removed.

 Inspection 

Check the pan for cracks, holes or damaged drain plug threads. Check 
the gasket surface for damage caused by overtightened bolts. Replace with a 
new oil pan if repairs cannot be made.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Oil Pump 

 Cleaning 

Wash all parts in a solvent and dry them thoroughly with compressed 
air. Use a brush to clean the inside of the pump housing and the pressure 
relief valve chamber. Make sure all dirt and metal particles are removed. 

 Inspection 

 NOTE: Internal components are not serviced. If any component is out of 
specification, the pump assembly must be replaced. 

Check the inside of the pump housing and the inner and outer gears for 
damage or excessive wear. 

Check the mating surface of the pump cover for wear. Minor scuff marks 
are normal, but if the cover, gears or housing surfaces are excessively worn, 
scored or grooved, replace the pump. Inspect the rotor for nicks, burrs or 
score marks. Remove minor imperfections with an oil stone. 

Measure the inner to outer rotor tip clearance with feeler gauge 
inserted 13 mm (0.5 inch) minimum. Inner and outer rotor tip clearance must 
not exceed 0.1778 mm (0.007 inch).

[FIGURE: A23430A.gif]

With the rotor assembly installed in the housing, place Straightedge 
D83L-4201-A or equivalent over the rotor assembly and the housing. 

Measure the vertical clearance (rotor end play) between the 
straightedge and both the inner rotor and the outer race. Maximum clearance 
must not exceed 0.127 mm (0.005 inch).

[FIGURE: A23431A.gif]

Measure clearance between outer rotor and housing in several areas 
around the circumference of the outer rotor. Clearance must not exceed 0.381 
mm (0.015 inch).

[FIGURE: A23432A.gif]

Measure backlash between oil pump drive gears. Backlash must not exceed 
0.33 mm (0.013 inch).

[FIGURE: A23433A.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Cylinder Head Deck 

 Cleaning 

 NOTE: Excessive deposits may be cleaned in an acid tank, but the camshaft 
bushings must first be removed to prevent damage.

Place clean lint-free rags over the pistons to prevent dirt from 
falling into the engine.

Plug or cover the coolant and oil passages in the cylinder block deck.

Use a gasket scraper to clean the cylinder block deck surface.

Use Scotch-Brite® 7448 or equivalent and solvent to 
remove any residual gasket material from the cylinder block deck surface.

 WARNING: WHEN USING COMPRESSED AIR TO CLEAN CAPSCREW HOLES, ALWAYS WEAR SAFETY 
GLASSES OR A FACE SHIELD TO PROTECT THE EYES. PERSONAL INJURY CAN RESULT. 

 NOTE: Make sure the cylinder head capscrew holes are clean.

Use compressed air to clean debris from the capscrew holes.

Inspect the coolant passages. Build-up of deposits in the coolant 
passages can cause engine overheating. A large buildup of rust and lime will 
require removal of the cylinder block for cleaning in a hot tank.

Be sure the coolant passages are clean.

[FIGURE: A18331A.gif]

 Inspection 

 CAUTION: Do not proceed with the repair if the cylinder block head deck is 
damaged or not flat. The engine will have to be removed for resurfacing the 
block. 

 NOTE: The cylinder block head deck can be resurfaced in a machine shop and a 
thicker surface head gasket installed to keep the piston-to-head clearance the 
same.

Use a straightedge and feeler gauge to measure the overall flatness of 
the cylinder head deck. The overall flatness, side-to-side, must not exceed 
0.075 mm (0.003 inch). The overall flatness, end-to-end, must not exceed 0.305 
mm (0.012 inch) with no more than 0.010 mm (0.0004 inch) variation within a 
50-mm (2-inch) diameter area. 

Visually inspect for any localized dips or imperfections. If present, 
the cylinder head deck must be reground.

[FIGURE: A17624A.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Water Thermostat

 NOTE: If the problem being investigated is insufficient heat, the thermostat 
should be checked for leakage. This can be done by holding the thermostat up 
to a lighted background. Light leakage around the thermostat valve (thermostat 
at room temperature) is unacceptable and the thermostat must be replaced. On 
some thermostats, a slight leakage of light at one or two locations on the 
perimeter of the valve may be detected. This should be considered normal.

Remove the thermostat and immerse it in boiling water. Replace the 
thermostat if it does not open more than 6.35 mm (0.25 inch) after one minute 
in water.
