REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Camshaft and Valve Tappets

 Removal with Oil Pan Installed 

 NOTE: On tilt hood vehicles, it is necessary to remove the radiator, charge 
air cooler and air conditioning condenser to facilitate camshaft removal. 
Also, once these items are removed, it is necessary to remove the front engine 
support-to-frame bolts and lift the front of the engine about six inches so 
the camshaft will clear the lower radiator support.

Remove the following components:

valve cover

rocker arm assemblies

push rods

crankshaft vibration damper

front cover

fuel lift pump. Refer to Section 03A-04A .

The valve tappets can be removed with the oil pan installed by using a 
tappet removal tool kit consisting of:

valve tappet tray (1)

dowel rods (12)

rubber bands (12)

nylon string (1)

[FIGURE: A18267A.gif]

Lift the tappets so the camshaft can be removed using the kit shown.

 NOTE: It is necessary to remove the camshaft to replace the valve tappets; 
therefore, the tappets will be raised and secured with the dowel rods.

 NOTE: Number each tappet with the cylinder number position as it is removed. 
The tappets must be installed in the same positions as removed.

Insert Lifter Holders, part of Lifter Holder Set D94T-6500-A, or 
equivalent, such as wooden dowels, securely into each tappet. Use a soft-face 
hammer if necessary.

[FIGURE: A17395A.gif]

Pull each valve tappet up until it makes contact with the cylinder 
block. Put a rubber band around two dowels to hold the tappets off the 
camshaft. 

[FIGURE: A18268A.gif]

Remove the nut and washer from the fuel injection pump drive gear.

[FIGURE: A18269A.gif]

Install the puller on the drive gear. Tighten the capscrews until the 
gear is loose on the fuel injection pump driveshaft.

Remove the fuel injection pump drive gear.

 NOTE: If the camshaft or gear is being replaced due to geartrain noise, check 
the gear backlash.

 NOTE: Excessive gear backlash can be caused by worn camshaft bushings.

Position an indicator on a tooth of the camshaft gear.

[FIGURE: A18270A.gif]

Note the camshaft gear backlash and end clearance. Mark the camshaft 
gear and crankshaft gear for further analysis if backlash or end clearance 
exceeds limits. Camshaft end clearance (A) limits are 0.12-0.46 mm 
(0.0047-0.0181 inch). Camshaft gear backlash (B) limits are 0.152-0.38 mm 
(0.006-0.015 inch).

[FIGURE: A18271A.gif]

Rotate the crankshaft to align the timing marks before trying to remove 
the camshaft.

[FIGURE: A17397B.gif]

Remove the capscrews from the thrust plate.

 NOTE: Rotate the camshaft as it is being removed. Use extreme care to make 
sure the camshaft bushings are not damaged during the camshaft removal process.

Remove the camshaft thrust plate and camshaft from the cylinder block.

To aid in tappet removal and to prevent tappets from dropping down into 
oil pan, fabricate a trough and insert the trough to the full length of the 
camshaft bore.

[FIGURE: A17400A.gif]

Make sure the trough is positioned so it will catch the tappet when the 
holder is removed.

Only remove one tappet at a time. Remove the rubber band from the two 
companion tappets, securing the tappet not to be removed with the rubber band.

[FIGURE: A17402A.gif]

Remove the rubber bands from the wooden dowels that are used to hold 
the tappets up during camshaft removal/installation.

Remove the tappets from the wooden dowels.

Pull the wooden dowel from the tappet bore allowing the tappet to fall 
into the trough.

[FIGURE: A17401A.gif]

When the tappet is dropped into the trough, most of the time it will 
fall over. However, if it doesn't, gently shake the trough just enough to 
allow the tappet to fall over before removing.

Carefully pull the tray and tappet from the camshaft bore and remove 
the tappet. Repeat the process until all tappets are removed.

 NOTE: Special care must be taken not to knock or shake the tappet over the 
end of the trough when removing the No. 6 cylinder tappets.

Carefully pull the trough and tappet from the camshaft bore and remove 
the tappet. Repeat the process until all tappets are removed.

Inspect the tappets and camshaft. Refer to Camshaft and refer to Valve 
Tappets in the Cleaning and Inspection portion of this section.

 Removal with Oil Pan Removed 

 NOTE: Only four tappets are accessible at one time. The crankshaft must be 
rotated three times to access all of the tappets.

Rotate the crankshaft to access the tappets.

[FIGURE: A18272A.gif]

Only remove the rubber bands from the wooden dowels holding the 
accessible tappets.

Remove the accessible tappets/dowels.

 Installation with Oil Pan Installed 

Insert the plastic tray or trough the full length of the camshaft bore.

[FIGURE: A17400A.gif]

Insert the installation tool through the tappet bore and into the 
trough. Feed the installation tool through the camshaft bore by carefully 
pulling the trough out the front. The barrier at the rear of the trough will 
pull the tool out most of the time.

[FIGURE: A17410A.gif]

Lubricate the tappets with Engine Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A.

 NOTE: To aid in removing the installation tool after the tappet is installed, 
move the tool in and out of the tappet bore several times before installing 
the tappets.

Insert the installation tool into the tappet.

Slide the trough into the camshaft bore.

Pull the installation tool and tappet through the camshaft bore and up 
into the tappet bore.

[FIGURE: A17411A.gif]

If difficulty is experienced in getting the tappet to make the bend 
from the trough up to the tappet bore, pull the trough out enough to allow the 
tappet to drop down and align itself, then pull the tappet up into the bore.

After the tappet has been pulled up into position, slide the trough 
back into the camshaft bore and rotate it one half turn. This will position 
the round side of the trough up, which will hold the tappet in place.

[FIGURE: A17413A.gif]

Remove the installation tool from the tappet.

Insert a lifter holder or wooden dowel rod into the top of the tappet. 
Wrap rubber bands around the wooden dowels to secure the tappets. Repeat this 
process until all tappets have been installed.

Remove the trough from the camshaft bore.

[FIGURE: A17414B.gif]

 Installation with Oil Pan Removed 

Lubricate the tappets with Engine Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A.

 NOTE: Only four tappets are accessible at a time which will require rotation 
of the engine to install the remaining tappets.

Insert the wooden dowel rods used for holding the tappets up during 
camshaft removal into the tappets.

Insert the dowel rods with the tappets attached through the tappet bores.

[FIGURE: A18273A.gif]

Wrap rubber bands around the wooden dowels to secure the tappets. 
Repeat this process until all tappets have been installed.

[FIGURE: A18274A.gif]

Install the oil pan.

 NOTE: The crankshaft should be positioned so the No. 1 cylinder is at 
approximately TDC, so the camshaft does not hit the crankshaft counterweight 
during installation.

Before installing the camshaft, apply a coat of Engine Assembly 
Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A 
to the front camshaft bore.

[FIGURE: A17416A.gif]

Lubricate the camshaft journals and lobes, and the thrust plate with 
Engine Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESR-M99C80-A.

[FIGURE: A17417A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not try to force the camshaft into the camshaft bore as damage to 
the camshaft bushing can result. 

Install the camshaft. While pushing in slightly, rotate the camshaft 
and carefully work the camshaft through the camshaft bushings. As each 
camshaft journal passes through a bushing, the camshaft will drop slightly and 
the camshaft lobes will catch on the bushings. Rotating the camshaft will free 
the lobe from the bushing and allow the camshaft to be installed.

[FIGURE: A17418A.gif]

Before the camshaft gear engages the crankshaft gear, check the 
camshaft for ease of rotation. When installed properly, the camshaft should 
rotate freely.

Align the timing marks on the camshaft with the timing mark on the 
crankshaft.

[FIGURE: A18275A.gif]

 CAUTION: Make sure the camshaft assembly does not drop on your fingers when 
installing the thrust plate. 

Install the camshaft thrust plate.

[FIGURE: A18276A.gif]

Install the camshaft thrust plate capscrews and tighten to 24 Nm
 (18 lb-ft).

 NOTE: If the camshaft end clearance is greater than the stated limit, the 
thrust plate must be replaced.

Measure camshaft end clearance with a dial indicator.

End clearance is controlled by the thickness of the thrust plate and 
the groove in the camshaft. Camshaft end clearance limits are 0.12-0.46 mm 
(0.0047-0.0181 inch).

 NOTE: The gears must be replaced if the backlash is greater than the above 
limit.

 NOTE: Excessive gear backlash can be caused by worn camshaft bushings.

Put a dial indicator on the camshaft gear and check the gear backlash 
between the camshaft gear and the crankshaft gear. Camshaft gear backlash 
limits are 0.152-0.38 mm (0.006-0.015 inch).

Remove the wooden dowel rods from the valve tappets.

Install all parts that were removed:

fuel lift pump

fuel injection pump drive gear

front cover

vibration damper

push rods

rocker assemblies

valve cover

Fill the engine with oil.

Fill and bleed the engine cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 .

Operate the engine at idle until the coolant temperature reaches 82°
C (180°F) and check for leaks and proper 
operation.

Camshaft Rear Cover

 Removal 

 NOTE: It is necessary to remove the rear camshaft cover when the camshaft

If the camshaft has not been removed from the block, pry the cover from 
the rear countershaft bore with a wide-lipped screwdriver.

[FIGURE: A108141A.gif]

ESR-M18P2-A and ESE-M4G115-A.

Tap the rear cam cover into place with a soft mallet until it is fully 
seated.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Piston and Piston Rings

 Removal 

Remove engine from vehicle and place on engine stand.

Remove the cylinder head.

Remove the oil pan and suction tube.

Roll the engine to a vertical position. Rotate the engine enough so the 
pistons are below the carbon deposits which are found above the ring travel 
area.

 CAUTION: Use care not to damage the liner when removing carbon. 

Use a scraper or blunt edged instrument to loosen the carbon deposits. 

[FIGURE: A24605A.gif]

Remove any remaining carbon with a cleaning ad.

 WARNING: TO PREVENT SERIOUS EYE DAMAGE, WEAR EYE PROTECTION DURING THIS OPERATION. 

 CAUTION: Do not use the steel wire wheel in the piston travel area. Operate the 
wheel in a circular motion to remove the deposits. 

An alternative method to remove the carbon ridge is to use a 
high-quality steel wire wheel installed in a drill or die grinder.

[FIGURE: A24606A.gif]

Mark each rod cap according to cylinder.

Mark each piston according to the cylinder.

Remove the nuts from the connecting rod capscrews. Tap on the rod bolts 
to loosen and remove the rod cap.

Push the connecting rod and piston assembly out of the bore.

Remove piston rings from piston.

 Installation 

Position the oil ring expander in the oil control ring groove.

[FIGURE: A17504A.gif]

Install the oil control ring with the end gap opposite the ends on the 
expander.

 NOTE: The top surface of the upper two rings is identified with the word TOP 
or the supplier mark. 

Install the intermediate and top ring with the word TOP or supplier 
mark up.

[FIGURE: A24607A.gif]

Install bearing shells into both the connecting rod and the cap. 
Lubricate the connecting rod and cap bearings with clean engine oil.

Lubricate the rings and piston skirts with clean engine oil.

Position the rings.

[FIGURE: A17317A.gif]

Turn the crankshaft until connecting rod journal for the piston to be 
installed is at bottom dead center. 

Using clean engine oil, lubricate the cylinder walls and crankshaft 
journal with clean engine oil.

Compress the rings using a strap-type ring compressor.

Position the piston and rod assembly into the cylinder bore with the 
word FRONT on the piston toward the front of the engine. Push the piston into 
the bore until the top of the piston is approximately 50 mm (2 inches) below 
the top of the bore.

Pull the connecting rod onto the crankshaft journal.

[FIGURE: A18245A.gif]

Lubricate the connecting rod bolts with clean engine oil.

 CAUTION: The number stamped on the rod and cap at the parting line must match 
and be installed on the camshaft side of the engine. 

Install the connecting rod cap and start the connecting rod nuts. 

Lubricate under the connecting rod nuts with clean engine oil.

[FIGURE: A24608A.gif]

Tighten the connecting rod cap to the connecting rod evenly. Tighten 
the connecting rod nuts in three steps to the following torques.

Step 1 — 40 Nm (30 lb-ft)

Step 2 — 80 Nm (59 lb-ft)

Step 3 — 120 Nm (88 lb-ft)

Move the connecting rod side to side to verify side clearance.

[FIGURE: A24609A.gif]

Measure the side clearance between the connecting rod and the 
crankshaft. Clearance should be 0.1-0.3 mm (0.004-0.012 inch).

[FIGURE: A24610A.gif]

Install suction tube and oil pan.

Install the cylinder head.

Install engine in vehicle.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Cylinder Liner

 Removal 

Drain the cooling system.

Remove the cylinder head.

Drain the engine oil. After the oil is drained, reinstall the drain 
plug and a new gasket. Tighten to 80 Nm (59 lb-ft).

Remove the oil pan and oil suction tube.

[FIGURE: A23471A.gif]

Remove the pistons and the connecting rods.

[FIGURE: A18219A.gif]

 NOTE: Before removing the cylinder liners, visually inspect the condition to 
determine reuse.

Visually inspect the inside diameters of the liner for cracks, scuffing 
or scoring.

 NOTE: If a fingernail catches in the scratch, the liner must be replaced.

Inspect the inside diameters for vertical scratches deep enough to be 
felt with a fingernail.

Visually inspect the inside diameter for liner bore polishing. A 
moderate polish produces a bright mirror finish in the worn area with traces 
of the original hone marks or an indication of an etch pattern. A heavy polish 
produces a bright mirror finish in the worn area with no traces of hone marks 
or an etch pattern.

Do not reuse liners exhibiting heavy polish or any indications of 
particle embedment from a failure. Severely worn liners will have a ridge near 
the top of the liner bore.

[FIGURE: A18232A.gif]

If the wear pattern indicates the liner bore is not straight or not 
round, use a dial bore gauge to measure the liner inside diameter in four 
places 90 degrees apart at the top and bottom of the piston travel area.

Cylinder Liner Dimensions

mm

Inch

Maximum Out of Round

0.04

0.0016

Maximum Taper

0.04

0.0016

Maximum Inside Diameter

114.117

4.4928

 NOTE: If a liner bore is not acceptable for reuse, it must be replaced. 
Damaged liners cannot be honed or deglazed. This would destroy the cross-hatch 
pattern needed for oil control.

 NOTE: Do not remove or disturb the liner seals for liners which pass the 
inspection criteria.

Liner protrusion is the distance the liner protrudes above the block 
face. Before removing the liners, check the protrusion in the unclamped state. 
Cylinder liner protrusion limits are 0.025-0.122 mm (0.001-0.0048 inch).

[FIGURE: A18233A.gif]

If the liner was installed correctly and the liner protrusion is out of 
limits, it will be necessary to machine the counterbore and add shims to 
restore to the original specifications.

Use clean shop rags to cover the crankshaft to prevent debris from 
falling into the main journal area or into the connecting rod journal oil 
drilling.

 CAUTION: The liner puller must be installed and used as described to avoid 
damage to the cylinder block. The puller must not contact the block casting at 
points A, B, C and D. 

 NOTE: The liner puller must be centered on the top of the cylinder block.

Insert the liner puller into the top of the cylinder block.

[FIGURE: A18234A.gif]

Turn the puller jackscrew clockwise to loosen the liner from the 
cylinder block. Use both hands to remove the liner.

[FIGURE: A18235A.gif]

 CAUTION: The liner puller must be installed and used as described to avoid 
damage to the cylinder block. The puller plate must be parallel to the main 
bearing saddles and must not overlap the liner outside diameter. 

 NOTE: The liner puller must be centered on the top of the cylinder block.

Insert the liner puller into the top of the cylinder block.

[FIGURE: A18236A.gif]

Turn the puller jackscrew clockwise to loosen the liner from the 
cylinder block. Use both hands to remove the liner.

Use Dykem® or equivalent to mark the cylinder number 
on each liner.

 Installation 

 CAUTION: Clean all deposits and debris from sealing surfaces A, B and C. Use 
Scotch-Brite® 7448 or equivalent and cleaning solvent to 
polish the surfaces. Due to the critical machined tolerances, care should be 
taken not to remove any additional material. 

 NOTE: If surface C has cracks or signs of extreme wear, the counterbore will 
require machining and the installation of shims for the correct liner 
protrusion.

Cylinder liner shims are available as follows:

 CYLINDER LINER SHIM THICKNESS

Part No.

mm

Inch

3924445

[FIGURE: A18237A.gif]

Lubricate surfaces A and B with clean 15W40 engine oil.

 NOTE: Part No. 3823567, cutter plate, and Part No. 3823570, cutter bit, must 
be used with the counterbore machining tool.

Machine the counterbore to the proper depth.

[FIGURE: A18238A.gif]

Clean the combustion deck with a gasket scraper or Scotch-Brite®
 7448 cleaning pad or equivalent and diesel fuel or solvent.

Thoroughly flush the block with mineral spirits or cleaning solvent.

Remove the shop rags and clean the crankshaft with a cleaning solvent.

Blow dry the cylinder bores and crankshaft and wipe them clean with a 
lint-free cloth.

 NOTE: The cylinder liner must be installed within 15 minutes after applying 
oil to the cylinder liner O-ring seal.

Use clean 15W40 engine oil to coat the cylinder liner O-ring seals.

Install new O-ring seals on the cylinder liners.

Make sure the cylinder liner O-ring is not twisted or damaged during 
installation.

[FIGURE: A18239A.gif]

 NOTE: When reusing liners, install them in the same cylinder from which they 
were removed and rotate them 45 degrees (1/8 turn) from their original 
position. When correctly installed, any cylinder liner pitting will be 
positioned so the pitted surface is rotated away from the original location 
where pitting occurred.

Install the cylinder liner into the cylinder block bore.

 NOTE: If the cylinder liner does not rest on the cylinder block counterbore 
seat, remove the cylinder liner. Inspect the counterbore seat and cylinder 
liner for nicks, burrs or dirt. Install the cylinder liner again.

Use a cylinder liner driver and a leather mallet to drive the cylinder 
liner into the bore.

[FIGURE: A18240A.gif]

Use two cylinder head capscrews and position the two cylinder liner 
clamps as illustrated.

Tighten the capscrews to 68 Nm (50 lb-ft).

Remove the clamps and repeat this procedure until all cylinder liners 
have been clamped and released.

[FIGURE: A18241A.gif]

Cylinder liner protrusion is the distance the cylinder liner protrudes 
above the block face. Measure the cylinder liner protrusion at four points, 90 
degrees apart. Cylinder liner protrusion limits are 0.025-0.122 mm 
(0.001-0.0048 inch).

[FIGURE: A18242A.gif]

If the cylinder liner protrusion varies more than 0.025 mm (0.001 inch) 
for 180 degrees, install and tighten the cylinder liner clamps again. Inspect 
the cylinder liner protrusion again.

[FIGURE: A17874A.gif]

 NOTE: If the out-of-limit condition is minimal, tolerance stack-up may allow 
the cylinder liner protrusion limits to be obtained by installing other new 
cylinder liners in the out-of-limit bore.

If the cylinder liner protrusion still varies more than 0.025 mm (0.001 
inch), perform the following:

Remove the cylinder liner.

[FIGURE: A18244A.gif]

Inspect the cylinder liner sealing edge for burrs, dirt or damage.

Replace the cylinder liner if it is damaged.

Install the cylinder liner again.

Inspect the cylinder liner protrusion.

If the cylinder liner protrusion still does not meet the 
specifications, machine the cylinder block liner counterbore and add 
counterbore shims to adjust the cylinder liner protrusion to the proper 
specifications.

[FIGURE: A18238A.gif]

Use a feeler gauge to inspect the cylinder liner-to-block clearance at 
the four block casting points. Cylinder liner-to-block clearance limit is 
0.229 mm (0.009 inch).

[FIGURE: A18231A.gif]

If the cylinder liner-to-block clearance is less than 0.229 mm (0.009 
inch), perform the following:

Remove the cylinder liner.

Inspect the cylinder liner and cylinder block for dirt or damage.

Replace the cylinder liner if it is damaged.

Install the cylinder liner again.

Measure the cylinder liner bore for out-of-roundness at points C, D, E, 
F and G. Measure each point in the direction AA and BB. The cylinder liner 
bore must not be more than 0.04 mm (0.0016 inch) out of round.

If the cylinder liner bore is more than 0.04 mm (0.0016 inch) out of 
round, remove the cylinder liner so the cylinder block liner bore can be 
measured.

[FIGURE: A18229A.gif]

Install the pistons and connecting rods.

[FIGURE: A18245A.gif]

Install the oil pan and suction tube.

Install the cylinder head.

Fill the engine cooling system.

Fill the engine with oil.

Prelube (prime) the engine prior to start-up by disconnecting the fuel 
shutoff solenoid and cranking the engine until the oil pressure gauge reads 
pressure, or no more than 30 seconds. Allow the starter to cool for two 
minutes between crank times.

Bleed the engine cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 .

Bleed the fuel supply lines and injector high pressure fuel lines. 
Refer to Section 03A-04A .

Operate the engine to normal operating temperature and check for leaks.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Connecting Rod Bearings

 Removal 

Drain the engine oil. After the oil is drained, reinstall the drain 
plug with a new gasket. Tighten to 80 Nm (59 lb-ft).

Remove the oil pan and oil suction tube.

[FIGURE: A23471A.gif]

Rotate the crankshaft to position two of the connecting rods at bottom 
dead center (BDC).

[FIGURE: A17336A.gif]

Loosen, but do not remove, the connecting rod capscrew nuts.

Hit the connecting rod capscrew nuts with a plastic hammer to loosen 
the rod caps.

Remove the capscrew nuts and rod cap.

Remove the lower bearing shell from the rod cap and mark it with the 
letter L (lower) and the cylinder number from which it was removed.

[FIGURE: A17337A.gif]

Push the rod away from the crankshaft to allow the upper bearing shell 
to be removed.

Remove the upper bearing shell and mark it with the letter U (upper) 
and the cylinder number from which it was removed.

[FIGURE: A17339A.gif]

Clean and inspect the bearings and caps. Refer to Cleaning and 
Inspection in this section.

 Installation 

 CAUTION: The connecting rod and bearing shell mating surfaces must be clean and 
dry when the bearing shells are installed. Used bearings must be installed in 
their original locations. 

Use Engine Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESR-M99C80-A to lubricate the inside diameter of the upper 
bearing shell.

Install the upper bearing shell in the connecting rod with the tang of 
the bearing in the slot of the rod.

[FIGURE: A21469A.gif]

Install the bearing shell in the connecting rod cap with the tang of 
the bearing in the slot of the cap. Use Engine Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D 
or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A to coat the inside 
diameter of the bearing shell.

Use clean 15W40 oil to lubricate the threads and underside of the 
connecting rod capscrew head.

 CAUTION: The connecting rod cap number must match the number on the connecting 
rod and must be installed with the numbers aligned to prevent damage to the 
connecting rods and the crankshaft. The locking tang of the connecting rod cap 
must be toward the camshaft side of the cylinder block. 

Install the rod cap and capscrews to the connecting rod.

[FIGURE: A19035A.gif]

Alternately tighten the connecting rod capscrew nuts in a three-step 
sequence.

Step 1 — 40 Nm (30 lb-ft)

Step 2 — 80 Nm (59 lb-ft)

Step 3 — 120 Nm (88 lb-ft)

Measure the side clearance between the connecting rod and crankshaft. 
Do not measure the clearance between the rod cap and crankshaft. Side 
clearance limits are 0.10-0.33 mm (.0039-.013 inch).

 CAUTION: The crankshaft must rotate freely. 

Check for freedom of rotation as the rod caps are installed. If the 
crankshaft does not rotate freely, check the installation of the rod bearings 
and bearing size.

Install the oil suction tube and oil pan.

Fill the engine with oil.

Operate the engine until the coolant temperature reaches 82°
C (180°F) and check for leaks and proper 
operation.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Main and Thrust Bearings, Engine in Vehicle

The engine has seven main bearings. The lower bearing shells are all 
the same. All of the upper bearing shells are the same except for the No. 4 
journal. The No. 4 journal uses a flanged upper bearing shell. The flanges on 
the bearing control the end thrust of the crankshaft.

The upper bearings are grooved and have two slots in them. One slot 
aligns with the drilling from the main oil rifle and supplies oil to the 
piston cooling nozzles. The other slot supplies oil to the other piston 
cooling nozzle.

The following oversize service main and thrust bearing combinations are 
available for crankshafts that have been machined undersize, either on the 
main journal or thrust bearing face.

Main Bearing Journal Diameter

Thrust Bearing Face Thickness

Standard 0.000

O.S. 0.25 mm (0.010 Inch)

Standard 0.000

O.S. 0.50 mm (0.020 Inch)

O.S. 0.50 mm (0.020 Inch)

O.S. 0.50 mm (0.020 Inch)

 Removal 

Drain the engine oil. After the oil is drained, reinstall the drain 
plug and a new gasket. Tighten to 80 Nm (59 lb-ft).

Remove the engine oil pan and suction tube. 

 NOTE: The main caps should be numbered. If they are not, be sure to mark them 
with the correct number.

 NOTE: Do not pry on the main caps to free them from the cylinder block.

Use two of the main bearing cap bolts to wiggle the main cap loose, 
being careful not to damage the bolt threads.

[FIGURE: A18243A.gif]

Perform a visual inspection of the main bearings and crankshaft 
journals. Remove the No. 2 and 3 caps and the lower main bearing shells from 
the crankshaft journal.

Check the journals for signs of overheat, deep scratches or other 
damage. If there is no damage, there is no need to pull the other caps at this 
time.

Mark the bearing shell with the letter L (lower) and the journal number 
from which it was removed.

[FIGURE: A18257A.gif]

If the main bearings are to be removed, remove all bearing caps except 
for cylinders No. 1 and 7.

 CAUTION: Do not damage the crankshaft when removing the thrust bearing. 

 CAUTION: Do not use a capscrew or any hard metal object as this can damage the 
crankshaft and cause serious engine failure. 

Use a blunt tool to remove the No. 4 upper thrust main bearing.

To remove each remaining upper main bearing shell, install a tool 
similar to the one shown below in the oil hole of the main bearing journal. 
Several varieties of small soft metal plugs are available specifically for 
this purpose.

[FIGURE: A18258A.gif]

Rotate the crankshaft so the pin pushes against the end of the bearing 
opposite the tang. Remove the bearing.

[FIGURE: A18259A.gif]

 CAUTION: Use care so the screwdriver does not damage the crankshaft or cylinder 
block. 

 NOTE: The No. 1 main does not have a hole in the journal so the bearing 
rollout tool cannot be used to replace the bearing.

Using a flat-bladed screwdriver, gently bump the end of the No. 1 upper 
main bearing to loosen it from the block. Then, use finger pressure against 
the bearing shell and rotate the crankshaft to roll the bearing out.

 Installation 

Position the new upper bearing on the crankshaft and install as far as 
possible by hand.

 CAUTION: Make sure the pin does not slide under the bearing and damage the 
crankshaft. 

Use a main bearing rollout tool and an engine barring tool to finish 
pushing the bearing in slowly. Make sure it is aligned with the block. Make 
sure the tang on the bearing aligns with the notch.

[FIGURE: A18260A.gif]

Install the lower main bearings into the bearing caps.

Make sure the tang of the bearing shells is in the slot of the cap.

Use Engine Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESR-M99C80-A to lubricate the bearing shells.

Use clean 15W40 oil to lubricate the capscrew threads.

Drain excess oil from the capscrews before installing.

 NOTE: The main bearing caps are numbered for location. No. 1 starts with the 
front of the block, and the numbers face the camshaft side of the engine.

When correctly installed, the tangs (slots) should be on the same side.

 NOTE: Make sure the bearing does not become dislodged from the cap.

Tap the main cap gently into position.

[FIGURE: A18261A.gif]

When seated, the main bolts can be threaded in by hand.

Install a main bearing cap after each upper bearing is installed to 
keep the bearing in place while the other uppers are installed.

Tighten the capscrews to an initial torque of 50 Nm 
(37 lb-ft).

Do not tighten to the final torque value at this time.

[FIGURE: A18262A.gif]

 NOTE: The thrust journal does not have tangs or slots. Make sure the number 
stamped on the main cap is positioned to the camshaft side of the engine.

Push the crankshaft toward the center of its end thrust position to 
allow clearance for the bearing.

Since the bearing rollout tool cannot be used for the No. 1 bearing, 
use a blunt object or screwdriver to push the bearing into position as the 
crankshaft is rotated.

[FIGURE: A18263A.gif]

Tighten the capscrews in three steps following the illustrated sequence.

Step 1 — 50 Nm (37 lb-ft)

Step 2 — 119 Nm (88 lb-ft)

Step 3 — 176 Nm (129 lb-ft)

[FIGURE: A18230A.gif]

If necessary, use a magnetic base. Measure the end clearance of the 
crankshaft as follows:

Install Dial Indicator with Bracketry TOOL-4201-C or equivalent onto 
the oil pan flange.

Put the tip of the gauge against the crankshaft counterweight.

Push the crankshaft toward the rear of the cylinder block.

[FIGURE: A18246A.gif]

Set the dial indicator at zero.

Push the crankshaft toward the front of the cylinder block.

If the end clearance is less than 0.131 mm (0.005 inch), loosen the 
main bearing capscrews one turn. Push the crankshaft toward the front and then 
toward the rear of the cylinder block.

Tighten the main bearing capscrews in the sequence shown to the torque 
values listed and illustrated in Step 15.

 NOTE: Crankshafts that have been reground on the thrust bearing surfaces are 
marked for oversize thrust bearings on the No. 4 journal crankshaft 
counterweight. If the crankshaft counterweight is marked, check the thrust 
bearing part number to make sure the correct bearing size is used.

Example: 0.010 = 0.25 mm (0.010 inch)

Measure the crankshaft end clearance. The end clearance specification 
for a new or reground crankshaft with new thrust bearings is 0.131-0.332 mm 
(0.005-0.013 inch).

[FIGURE: A18247A.gif]

If the crankshaft end play is more than 0.523 mm (0.0206 inch), the 
crankshaft must be removed from the engine and repaired.

Install the oil pan and suction tube.

Fill the engine with oil.

Operate the engine until the coolant temperature reaches 82°
C (180°F), and check for oil leaks.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Crankshaft Rear Oil Seal 

 Removal 

 NOTE: It is not necessary to remove the rear cover in order to remove the 
crankshaft rear seal.

Remove the transmission. Refer to the appropriate section in Group 07.

Remove the clutch and flywheel, if so equipped. Refer to Section 08-01 .

Drill two holes, 180 degrees apart, into the outside metal part of the 
seal.

[FIGURE: A17385A.gif]

Using a No. 10 sheet metal screw and a slide hammer, remove the seal.

[FIGURE: A17386A.gif]

 Installation 

Use crocus cloth to remove any rust or other deposits from the 
crankshaft flange.

Use a clean cloth to clean the crankshaft rear flange.

 NOTE: There are two rear seal configurations used, one for dry flywheel 
housings (A) and one for wet housings (B). The seal for dry housings has an 
aluminum case with urethane coated OD. The seal for wet housings has a steel 
case with silicone coated OD. Refer the the appropriate parts catalog for the 
correct part number.

Visually inspect the seal contact area for wear. If the seal contact 
area has a groove worn deep enough to feel with a fingernail or sharp object, 
install a wear sleeve over the sealing surface.

[FIGURE: A18185A.gif]

 NOTE: Do not use any kind of lubricant to install the seal. The oil seal must 
be installed with the lip of the seal and the crankshaft clean and dry.

Install the pilot and seal from the seal replacement kit onto the 
crankshaft. For wet flywheel housings, apply a coat of mild soap to the 
outside diameter of the seal case. For dry housings, nothing is required on 
the outside diameter of the seal case.

[FIGURE: A18186A.gif]

 NOTE: Do not use any sealant on the crankshaft rear seal.

Push the seal onto the pilot and into the bore of the housing. Remove 
the pilot.

 NOTE: Make sure the seal is completely installed into the flywheel housing.

 NOTE: The oil seal for a wet flywheel housing requires soap on the outside 
diameter of the seal case. Nothing is required on the outside diameter of the 
seal case for dry housings.

 NOTE: Do not use any kind of lubricant to install the seal. The oil seal must 
be installed with the lip of the seal and the wear sleeve clean and dry.

Use the installation tool from the seal replacement kit to install the 
seal to the correct depth. To prevent damage to the seal, hit the installation 
tool alternately at the 12, 3, 6, and 9 o'clock positions.

[FIGURE: A17389A.gif]

Remove the rear crankshaft seal pilot tool.

Install the flywheel and clutch, if so equipped. Refer to Section 08-01 .

Install the transmission and driveline. Refer to the appropriate 
section in Group 07.

Operate the engine until the coolant temperature reaches 82°
C (180°F), and check for leaks and proper 
operation.

 Wear Sleeve, Rear Crankshaft Seal Replacement 

 Removal 

Remove the transmission. Refer to the appropriate section in Group 07.

Remove the clutch and flywheel, if so equipped. Refer to Section 08-01 .

Remove the flywheel housing.

Remove the four lubricating oil pan mounting capscrews that secure the 
oil pan to the rear cover.

 CAUTION: Use extreme care when releasing the oil pan gasket from the rear cover 
to prevent damage to the gasket. If the gasket is damaged, the oil pan must be 
removed and the gasket replaced. 

Insert a feeler gauge or shim stock between the rear cover and the oil 
pan gasket. Move the feeler gauge or shim stock back and forth to release the 
gasket from the rear cover.

[FIGURE: A23652A.gif]

Remove the capscrews from the rear cover, and remove the cover from the 
crankshaft flange. Remove the seal from the rear cover.

[FIGURE: A23653A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not nick or gouge the crankshaft with the chisel. If the crankshaft 
is damaged, it must be replaced. 

Use a dull chisel that is only as wide as the wear sleeve. Make one or 
two soft blows with a hammer across the wear sleeve. This will expand the wear 
sleeve allowing the sleeve to be removed.

[FIGURE: A23654A.gif]

Clean the gasket surface of the rear cover, crankshaft flange and 
cylinder block.

[FIGURE: A23655A.gif]

Inspect the crankshaft flange and rear cover for dirt, nicks or other 
damage.

[FIGURE: A23656A.gif]

 Installation 

 NOTE: Install the rear cover capscrews. Do not tighten. If the oil pan is 
installed, loosen the oil pan capscrews to allow clearance for rear cover and 
gasket clearance.

 NOTE: The seal installation is used to properly align the rear cover. Do not 
push the cover in any direction to prevent irregular lip position after seal 
installation.

Install rear cover and gasket.

[FIGURE: A23657A.gif]

 NOTE: Do not use any kind of lubricant to install the oil seal. The oil seal 
must be installed with the lip of the oil seal and crankshaft clean and dry to 
ensure proper oil sealing.

 NOTE: The combination crankshaft oil seal and wear sleeve is installed on the 
crankshaft as an assembly.

 NOTE: The oil seal for a wet flywheel housing requires soap on the outside 
diameter of the seal case. Nothing is required on the outside diameter of the 
seal case for dry housings.

Use Cummins Engine Company Crankshaft Wear Sleeve Installation Tool 
Part No. 3824078 to install the oil seal and wear sleeve assembly.

 Crankshaft Wear Sleeve Installation Tool 

[FIGURE: A23658A.gif]

Apply a small amount of clean 15W40 engine oil to the crankshaft 
threaded studs and the inside diameter of the crankshaft rear seal and wear 
sleeve installation tool. Install two threaded studs into the crankshaft.

Position the chamfered end of the wear sleeve onto end of the 
crankshaft. Position the counterbore end of the installation tool over the 
threaded studs and align with wear sleeve, perpendicular to end of crankshaft.

 NOTE: Do not exceed one-half revolution of each nut to prevent wear sleeve 
binding and irregular stretch.

Install washers and nuts onto the threaded studs. Alternately tighten 
the nuts until the installation tool contacts the end of the crankshaft. 
Tighten to 20 Nm (15 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A23659A.gif]

Remove the installation tool and the threaded studs.

Align the rear cover even with both sides of the oil pan rail on the 
cylinder block. Tighten the rear cover capscrews to 9 Nm (80 
lb-in).

[FIGURE: A23660A.gif]

 NOTE: Make sure to fill the joint between the lubricating oil pan rail and

Ford specification WSE-M4G320-A2.

Trim the gaskets even with the oil pan mounting surface.

[FIGURE: A23661A.gif]

 NOTE: The oil pan capscrews must be tightened within 15 minutes after 
applying sealant.

Install four capscrews that hold the oil pan to the rear cover. Tighten 
to 24 Nm (18 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A23662A.gif]

Install the flywheel housing.

Install the clutch and flywheel, if so equipped. Refer to Section 08-01 .

Install the transmission. Refer to the appropriate section in Group 07.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Gear Cover

The gear housing provides a support for the injection pump, timing pin 
and the accessory drive gear, if used.

The geartrain consists of the crankshaft gear, lubricating oil pump 
drive and idler gear, camshaft gear, fuel injection pump drive gear and 
accessory drive gear, if used.

Noise emitted from the gear housing can indicate worn or damaged gear 
teeth or excessive gear backlash.

Excessive gear backlash can affect engine timing and engine performance.

 Removal 

Remove the valve cover.

Remove the rocker assemblies and push rods.

Remove the drive belt, vibration damper and front cover.

Remove the fuel lift pump.

Remove the fuel injection pump. Refer to Section 03A-04A .

Remove the camshaft and tappets.

Remove the accessory drive or air compressor, if equipped. Refer to 
 Section 06-08A .

Support the front of the engine and remove the front engine mount.

[FIGURE: A18291A.gif]

Loosen all the oil pan mounting capscrews four to five turns.

Remove the four front oil pan capscrews which secure the oil pan to the 
gear housing.

 CAUTION: Use extreme caution when releasing the oil pan gasket from the gear 
housing to prevent damage to the gasket. If the gasket is damaged, it may be 
necessary to remove the oil pan and replace the gasket. Refer to procedure in 
this section. 

Insert a feeler gauge or a shim stock between the gear housing and the 
oil pan gasket. Move the feeler gauge or shim stock back and forth to release 
the gasket from the gear housing.

Remove the gear housing capscrews.

Remove the gear housing.

Clean the gasket material from the cylinder block.

 Installation 

Coat the pipe plugs with pipe sealant and install. Tighten to 7 Nm
 (62 lb-in). Do not overtighten.

If the fuel injection pump studs are damaged or being installed in a 
new housing, coat the threads with Threadlock® 262 
E2FZ-19554-B or equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G351-A6 and use 
two nuts locked together to remove and install.

If the gear housing is being replaced, remove the engine dataplate and 
install on the new housing.

[FIGURE: A18292A.gif]

If removed, install the two gear housing dowel pins.

The tapered end of the dowel fits into the cylinder block; drive the 
pin to the bottom of the hole.

[FIGURE: A18293A.gif]

Inspect the oil pan gasket. If it is not torn, apply Perfect Seal 
Sealing Compound F2AZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specifications 
ESR-M18P2-A and ESE-M4G115-A around the capscrew holes and at the joint of the 
gear housing.

If the gasket is torn, it can be repaired. Cut off the torn gasket even 
with the front of the engine block.

[FIGURE: A17444A.gif]

Using the old gasket as a pattern, cut the front section of a new 
gasket to the same size.

Clean the sealing surfaces and coat the new gasket on both sides with 
Perfect Seal Sealing Compound F2AZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specifications ESR-M18P2-A and ESE-M4G115-A.

Use common thread or a very fine wire to hold the new gasket splice in 
position.

 NOTE: When properly trimmed, the gear housing gasket will be even with the 
oil pan gasket when installed.

Mark and trim 1.59 mm (1/16 inch) off the new gear housing gasket.

[FIGURE: A17448A.gif]

Coat both sides of the gear housing gasket with Perfect Seal Sealing 
Compound F2AZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting Ford specifications ESR-M18P2-A 
and ESE-M4G115-A.

Position the gasket on the alignment dowels.

 CAUTION: If a new housing or other than the original housing is installed, the 
timing pin assembly must be accurately located. Refer to Timing Pin Assembly, 
Cylinder Head Removed or Relocating Timing Pin Assembly, Cylinder Head 
Installed in the Removal and Installation portion of this section. 

 NOTE: The location of the timing pin assembly on the gear housing is critical 
for correct engine adjustments. If the original gear housing is being 
installed, it is unnecessary to relocate the timing pin. If a new housing is 
being installed, refer to Timing Pin Assembly, Cylinder Head 
Removed or Relocating Timing Pin Assembly, Cylinder 
Head Installed in the Removal and Installation portion of this section for timing pin installation and adjustment.

Carefully install the gear housing, making sure both gaskets are in 
place. Tighten screws to 24 Nm (18 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A18192B.gif]

Start the oil pan capscrews in the holes not being used to tie the 
gasket in place.

[FIGURE: A17452A.gif]

Remove the thread or wire holding the gasket in place.

Install the remaining two capscrews and tighten to 24 Nm
 (18 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A17454A.gif]

Lubricate the camshaft and thrust plate with Engine Assembly Lubricant 
D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M99C80-A.

 NOTE: Make sure the alignment marks on the camshaft and camshaft gears are 
aligned.

Install the valve lifters, camshaft and thrust plate.

[FIGURE: A17456B.gif]

Install the thrust washer capscrews. Tighten to 24 Nm 
(18 lb-ft).

Measure to verify the camshaft has proper backlash and end play. End 
play is controlled by the thickness of the thrust plate and the groove in the 
camshaft.

Camshaft end clearance limits are 0.12-0.46 mm (0.0047-0.0181 inch). 
Camshaft gear backlash limits are 0.152-0.38 mm (0.006-0.015 inch).

Remove the lifter holders from the tappets.

Install and lubricate the push rods and complete the installation of 
the rocker levers.

[FIGURE: A17460B.gif]

Complete the installation of the removed components:

Accessory drive or air compressor. Refer to Section 06-08A .

Fuel injection pump. Refer to Section 03A-04A .

Fuel transfer pump. Refer to Section 03A-04A .

Drive belt, crankshaft vibration damper and front cover. Check torque 
of belt tensioner mounting bolts. Correct torque valve is 43 Nm
 (32 lb-ft).

Valve cover.

Operate the engine at idle for 5 to 10 minutes to check for leaks and 
proper operation.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Timing Pin Assembly, Cylinder Head Removed

 CAUTION: The timing pin assembly is precisely located on the gear housing to 
correspond to TDC for cylinder No. 1. The timing pin assembly must be 
relocated if the gear housing is replaced. 

Remove the front cover.

Temporarily install the crankshaft damper and a pointer fabricated from 
No. 16 gauge wire. Put a flatwasher between the pointer and gear housing to 
prevent damage to the gear housing .

[FIGURE: A18283A.gif]

Measure the distance between two cylinder head bolt holes. Using steel 
plate that can be fitted over a cylinder bore, drill two bolt holes to the 
measured dimensions.

Using two flywheel housing bolts, clamp the fabricated plate across No. 
1 cylinder.

Rotate the crankshaft until No. 1 piston touches the plate, then mark 
the damper.

Rotate the crankshaft in the opposite direction until the piston 
touches the plate, and mark the damper again.

Mark the damper exactly halfway between the two marks. This is top dead 
center.

Remove the plate and rotate the crankshaft until the wire pointer 
aligns with the new TDC mark.

Look for the timing pin hole in the back of the camshaft gear. If the 
hole is not visible, rotate the crankshaft 360 degrees.

Install a new O-ring into the groove of the timing pin assembly. 
Lubricate the O-ring with 15W40 engine oil.

Apply a coat of Threadlock® 262 E2FZ-19554-B or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G351-A6 to the threads of the Torx®
 screws and install the timing pin assembly.

Push the pin into the hole in the cam gear to align the housing.

 CAUTION: To prevent damage to the pin and gear, make sure the timing pin is 
disengaged before rotating the crankshaft. 

Hold the pin in while tightening the Torx® screws to 8 Nm
 (71 lb-in).

Check the pin to make sure it did not slip out of the camshaft gear 
hole when the screws were tightened.

[FIGURE: A18289A.gif]

Remove the vibration damper and wire pointer.

[FIGURE: A18290A.gif]

Install the gear cover.

Install the vibration damper.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Relocating Timing Pin Assembly, Cylinder Head Installed

 CAUTION: The timing pin assembly is precisely located on the gear housing to 
correspond to top dead center (TDC) for cylinder No. 1. The timing pin 
assembly must be relocated if the gear housing is replaced. 

Remove the front cover.

Locate top dead center (TDC) for cylinder No. 1 by barring engine 
slowly while pressing on the engine timing pin.

[FIGURE: A17171A.gif]

[FIGURE: A18281A.gif]

 CAUTION: If a gear housing other than the original housing is installed, the 
timing pin assembly must be accurately aligned to correspond to TDC for 
cylinder No. 1. 

Remove the timing pin assembly and seal.

Verify the timing marks on the crankshaft and camshaft are aligned or 
the hole in the back of the camshaft gear is visible through the gear housing.

[FIGURE: A18282A.gif]

To align the assembly, temporarily install the vibration damper and a 
pointer fabricated from No. 16 gauge wire. Put a flatwasher between the 
pointer and gear housing to prevent damage to the gear housing.

[FIGURE: A18283A.gif]

Remove high-pressure fuel lines.

 NOTE: This step is important to release cylinder pressure so the crankshaft 
can be rotated smoothly to locate TDC for cylinder No. 1.

Remove all injector nozzles.

Remove the valve cover.

Adjust the intake valve rocker lever on No. 1 cylinder to have zero 
valve clearance.

[FIGURE: A18284A.gif]

Rotate the crankshaft 90 degrees in the direction of normal engine 
rotation.

[FIGURE: A18285B.gif]

 NOTE: Leave the adjusting screw in this position until TDC is established.

Tighten the adjusting screw for the No. 1 intake valve five complete 
turns of the screw.

 CAUTION: Use extreme care that the piston does not push against the exhaust 
valve with so much force that it bends the push rod or valve stem, or damages 
the valve head or piston. 

Rotate the crankshaft slowly in the direction opposite engine rotation 
until the piston just touches the intake valve.

Mark the vibration damper.

[FIGURE: A18286B.gif]

 CAUTION: Make sure the piston touches the valve with approximately the same 
amount of force as in the previous step. 

Rotate the crankshaft in the direction of engine rotation until the 
piston just touches the intake valve.

Mark the vibration damper.

Measure the distance and mark the damper at one-half the distance 
between the two marks. This mark is the TDC mark.

[FIGURE: A18287B.gif]

 CAUTION: Failure to loosen the No. 1 intake valve adjusting screw will result in 
bending the push rod or valve stem or damage to valve face or piston when the 
crankshaft is rotated. 

Completely loosen the No. 1 intake valve adjusting screw.

Rotate the crankshaft in the direction of engine rotation until the 
pointer is aligned with the TDC mark, then an additional one full revolution 
(360 degrees).

[FIGURE: A18288A.gif]

Look through the back side of the gear housing for the timing pin hole 
in the camshaft gear. If the hole is not visible, the crankshaft must be 
rotated one revolution.

Install a new O-ring into the groove of the timing pin assembly. 
Lubricate the O-ring with 15W40 engine oil.

Apply a coat of Threadlock® 262 E2FZ-19554-B or 
equivalent meeting Ford specification WSK-M2G351-A6 to the threads of the Torx®
 screws and install the timing pin assembly.

Push the pin into the hole in the cam gear to align the housing.

 CAUTION: To prevent damage to the pin and gear, be sure the timing pin is 
disengaged before rotating the crankshaft. 

Hold the pin in while tightening the Torx® screws to 8 Nm
 (71 lb-in).

Check the pin to be sure it did not slip out of the camshaft gear hole 
when the screws were tightened.

[FIGURE: A18289A.gif]

Remove the vibration damper and wire pointer.

Install the gear cover.

Install the vibration damper.

[FIGURE: A18290A.gif]

Adjust the No. 1 intake valve clearance to 0.30 mm (0.012 inch).

Install the valve cover with a new seal.

Install the injector nozzles and high pressure fuel lines, then bleed 
fuel system. Refer to Section 03A-04A .

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Flywheel Housing

 Removal 

Remove the transmission, clutch and related components. Refer to 
 Section 08-01 and appropriate transmission section in Group 07.

Remove the flywheel.

 CAUTION: Place a wooden block the width of the oil pan between the floor jack 
and oil pan to prevent damage to the engine. 

Use a floor jack or a suitable lifting fixture to support the rear of 
the engine

Disconnect the battery cables.

Remove the starter motor. Refer to Section 03B-06 .

Remove the capscrews and both rear engine mounts.

Remove capscrews A and B, and install two M12 x 1.75 x 100 mm guide pins.

[FIGURE: A18299A.gif]

Remove the remaining capscrews.

 CAUTION: The component weighs 23 kg (50 lb) or more. To avoid personal injury, 
use a hoist or get assistance to lift the component. 

Use a rubber hammer to loosen the flywheel housing. Remove the flywheel 
housing.

Remove the sealing ring from the rear seal housing.

[FIGURE: A18300A.gif]

 WARNING: WHEN USING A STEAM CLEANER, WEAR PROTECTIVE CLOTHING AND SAFETY GLASSES 
OR A FACE SHIELD. HOT STEAM CAN CAUSE SERIOUS PERSONAL INJURY. 

Use steam or solvent to clean the flywheel housing. Dry with compressed 
air.

Inspect the flywheel housing for cracks, especially in the bolt pattern 
area. Visually inspect all surfaces for nicks, burrs, or cracks. Use fine 
crocus cloth to remove small nicks and burrs.

Inspect for damaged threads commonly caused by cross-threaded capscrews 
or by installing an incorrect capscrew. Helicoils are available to repair 
damaged threads.

 Installation 

Install two M12 x 1.75 x 100 mm guide pins into the cylinder block to 
help support and align the housing during installation.

Some dry clutch applications require a sealing ring on the seal 
housing. Install the sealing ring in the machined surface of the seal housing 
and lubricate with Multi-Purpose Grease DOAZ-19584-AA or equivalent meeting 
Ford specifications ESR-M1C159-A and ESB-M1C93-B.

[FIGURE: A18300A.gif]

Visually inspect the rear face of the cylinder block and flywheel 
housing mounting surface for cleanliness and raised nicks or burrs.

 NOTE: Be sure the sealing ring is not damaged during flywheel housing 
installation.

Install the flywheel housing making sure the housing is positioned on 
the alignment dowels and guide pins.

Remove the two M12 x 1.75 x 100 mm guide pins.

[FIGURE: A18301A.gif]

Install the mounting capscrews. Tighten in the sequence shown to 60 Nm
 (44 lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A18302A.gif]

Check the flywheel housing bore and flywheel housing face alignments. 
Refer to Section 03-00 .

Install the transmission, clutch, and all related components. Refer to 
 Section 08-01 and appropriate transmission section in Group 07.

Connect battery ground cable and starter motor.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Manifold, Exhaust

 Removal 

Remove the turbocharger. Refer to Section 03A-04B .

Remove the mounting capscrews, exhaust manifold and gaskets. When 
removing the exhaust manifold, it may be necessary to remove the coolant 
filter and thermostat housing assembly in order to remove the front upper 
exhaust manifold retaining bolt.

Clean the exhaust manifold gasket sealing surfaces.

 Installation 

"Package" the exhaust manifold capscrews and gaskets on the manifold. 
Apply anti-seize compound to the capscrews. The bead on the exhaust manifold 
gasket can be installed in either direction.

[FIGURE: A18204A.gif]

 NOTE: The tabs in the holes of the gasket are designed to hold the gasket in 
place during installation.

 NOTE: Use exhaust manifold gasket with a thickness of 0.46 mm (0.018 inch). 
Failure to use the correct thickness gasket could result in exhaust manifold 
distortion, cocking, leakage or cracking.

Install the exhaust manifold and gaskets. Tighten capscrews to 43 Nm
 (32 lb-ft). Follow the sequence shown.

[FIGURE: A18205A.gif]

After the capscrews are tightened to the correct torque value, bend 
over the lock plates to prevent the capscrews from loosening.

Install coolant filter and thermostat housing assembly, if removed.

 NOTE: It may be necessary to orient the turbocharger center bearing housing 
and/or compressor outlet.

Install the turbocharger. Refer to Section 03A-04B .

Use precoated turbocharger mounting studs or apply a thin coating of 
nickel-based, high-temperature, anti-seize compound to the coarse threads of 
the stud.

Use two nuts locked together to install the studs. Tighten to 10 Nm
 (89 lb-in).

[FIGURE: A18206A.gif]

Install the turbocharger mounting gasket with the raised bead facing 
the exhaust manifold. Install the turbocharger, tightening to 45 Nm
 (33 lb-ft).

To orient the center bearing housing, bend the lock plates, if so 
equipped, and loosen the turbine housing capscrews and position the bearing 
housing.

[FIGURE: A18207A.gif]

Section 03B-01: Engine, FD-1460 Diesel

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Cylinder Head

 Removal 

 NOTE: It is easier and faster to remove the cylinder head as an assembly, and 
then remove additional components on the bench after the cylinder head is out 
of the vehicle.

Disconnect the battery negative cable and drain the engine coolant. On 
vehicles equipped with an alligator-style hood, remove the hood.

Working from the right side of the engine compartment, remove the air 
cleaner assembly, air cleaner support and the turbocharger air inlet adapter. 
Cap the turbocharger air inlet.

Disconnect the air-to-air tube from the charge air cooler and the 
turbocharger. Remove the air-to-air tube. Cap the charge air cooler inlet and 
turbocharger outlet.

Disconnect the ether cold start line from the intake manifold (if so 
equipped).

Remove the turbocharger oil supply and return lines.

Disconnect the temperature sender wire on the thermostat housing.

Remove the engine oil filter.

Remove the exhaust pipe band clamp on the turbocharger exhaust outlet.

Disconnect the upper radiator hose, the heater hoses to the thermostat 
housing and the heater hose from the heater hose tube assembly.

Remove the generator drive belt, the generator upper bracket and the 
bolt securing the generator lower support to the thermostat housing.

Remove the bolt securing the heater hose tube to the cylinder head. 
Loosen the flange nut and remove the heater hose tube.

Working from the left side of the engine compartment, disconnect the 
air-to-air tube from the charge air cooler and the intake manifold. Remove the 
air-to-air tube. Cap the charge air cooler outlet.

On vehicles equipped with hydraulic brakes, remove the brake hydraulic 
pump belt and remove the brake pump from the mounting bracket. Position the 
pump out of the way.

On air brake-equipped vehicles, remove the air compressor air inlet hose.

Remove the bolts securing the engine cooling fan hub to the engine, and 
remove the fan and hub as an assembly.

Remove the wiring brackets from the valve cover.

Disconnect the injector high pressure lines from the injectors and the 
injection pump. Cap all lines to prevent contamination.

Disconnect the fuel supply hose at the fuel sediment bowl and the 
supply hose for the lift pump. Remove the fuel line from the lift pump to the 
fuel filter assembly. Cap all lines to prevent contamination.

Remove the fuel filter.

Disconnect the air inlet temperature sensor. Remove the electrical 
bracket from the cylinder head and position the wiring harness out of the way.

Remove the valve cover and loosen all of the rocker arm adjusting nuts 
and screws.

Mark the rocker arm shaft supports for installation in the same 
locations. Remove the rocker arm shaft support bolts and remove the rocker arm 
and rocker arm shaft support assemblies. Remove the oil transfer tubes and the 
push rods, noting their locations.

Loosen and remove the cylinder head capscrews in the sequence shown.

[FIGURE: A18208A.gif]

On vehicles equipped with a tilt hood, remove the radiator-to-cowl 
cross support rod to allow clearance for cylinder head removal.

Using a suitable lifting device, remove the cylinder head from the 
vehicle.

[FIGURE: A18209A.gif]

Remove additional components from the cylinder head as required for 
service.

Inspect the cylinder head and block. Refer to Section 03-00 .

 Installation 

 NOTE: The cylinder block and head must be clean and dry. The maximum 
allowable piston protrusion above the top of the block with a standard gasket 
is 0.4-0.7 mm (0.016-0.028 inch). If the piston protrusion is greater than 
specified, refer to Cylinder Head Deck in the Cleaning and Inspection portion 
of this section for information pertaining to thicker head gaskets.

Install any components removed from the cylinder head after removal 
from the vehicle.

Position a new cylinder head gasket on the engine block observing 
correct alignment with the holes in the engine block.

[FIGURE: A17307A.gif]

Using a suitable lifting device, position the cylinder head on the 
engine and seat it onto the alignment dowels.

Use clean 15W40 engine oil to coat the cylinder head capscrew threads 
and underneath the head flange. Do not install the capscrews with painted head 
in the center row that will be covered by the valve cover. Allow the excess 
oil to drain from the capscrew threads before installation.

 NOTE: Make sure to install the six capscrews in the holes underneath the 
injectors.

Install the capscrews into the cylinder head.

[FIGURE: A18210A.gif]

The top of the cylinder head capscrew is identified with an angle 
marking. The cylinder head capscrews must be tightened by using the three-step 
"torque plus angle" method described below.

[FIGURE: A18211A.gif]

Follow the numbered sequence and tighten all capscrews to 70 Nm
 (52 lb-ft). Follow the numbered sequence and check the 
torque on all capscrews again.

[FIGURE: A18212A.gif]

Follow the numbered sequence and tighten only the fourteen long 
capscrews to 145 Nm (105 lb-ft). Follow the numbered sequence 
and check the torque on all long capscrews again.

[FIGURE: A18213A.gif]

Follow the numbered sequence and turn all the capscrews 90 degrees as 
indicated on the capscrew head. To accurately turn the capscrew to the desired 
angle, a small dot and a window are marked on the capscrew head.

Mark the cylinder head adjacent to the dot on the capscrew head. This 
mark will serve as an indexing aid.

Rotate the capscrew until the mark that has been made on the cylinder 
head falls into the window on the capscrew head.

Use a permanent marker to mark the socket corresponding to one of the 
flats of the socket hex.

After the torque has been completed, mark the cylinder head at the 
location of the dot.

[FIGURE: A18214A.gif]

Position the socket on the capscrew so the mark on the socket is at the 
same point as the window on the capscrew.

[FIGURE: A18215A.gif]

Turn the socket until the mark of the socket aligns with the mark on 
the cylinder head.

Install the push rods, oil transfer tubes, rocker arm shaft supports 
and rocker arms in their original locations. Install rocker arm shaft support 
bolts and tighten to 55 Nm (41 lb-ft).

Install cooling fan and clutch assembly, if removed.

Raise the front of the engine to allow installation of the front engine 
mount spacer, if removed, and insulator.

Lower the engine into place and install the front engine mount main 
through-bolts and nuts.

Tighten the rear engine mount cap through-bolts.

Adjust the valves. Refer to Valve Adjustment, Cold, in the Adjustments 
portion of this section.

Install the valve cover with rubber seal and capscrews with new sealing 
O-rings. Tighten capscrews in sequence shown to 24 Nm (18 
lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A18203A.gif]

Connect the air inlet temperature sensor and install the electrical 
bracket to the cylinder head.

Install a new fuel filter.

Connect the fuel supply hose to the fuel sediment bowl and the supply 
hose to the lift pump. Install the fuel line to the lift pump and fuel filter 
assembly.

Connect the injector high pressure lines to the injectors and injection 
pump.

Install the wiring brackets to the valve cover.

Install the cooling fan and hub assembly to the engine and tighten the 
bolts to 24 Nm (18 lb-ft). Check torque of belt tensioner 
mounting bolts. Correct torque value is 43 Nm (32 lb-ft).

On air brake-equipped vehicles, install the air compressor air inlet 
hose.

On vehicles equipped with hydraulic brakes, install the brake hydraulic 
pump assembly and adjust the belt to specifications.

Working from the left side of the engine compartment, connect the 
air-to-air tube to the charge air cooler and the intake manifold.

Install the heater hose tube to the cylinder head.

Install the bolt securing the generator lower support to the thermostat 
housing. Install the generator upper bracket and generator drive belt.

Connect the upper radiator hose and heater hoses to the thermostat 
housing and the heater hose to the heater hose tube assembly.

Install the exhaust pipe band clamp on the turbocharger exhaust outlet.

Install a new engine oil filter.

Connect the temperature sender wire on the thermostat housing.

Install the turbocharger oil supply and return lines.

Connect the ether cold start line to the intake manifold (if so 
equipped).

Connect the air-to-air tube to the charge air cooler and turbocharger.

Install the air cleaner assembly, air cleaner support and the 
turbocharger air inlet adapter.

Install the hood, if previously removed.

Connect the battery negative cable(s).

Fill the engine crankcase and turbocharger with engine oil.

Fill the engine cooling system.

Prelube (prime) the engine prior to start-up by disconnecting the fuel 
shutoff solenoid and cranking the engine until the oil pressure gauge reads 
pressure, or no more than 30 seconds. Allow the starter to cool for two 
minutes between crank times.

Bleed the engine cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 .

Bleed the fuel supply lines and injector high pressure lines. Refer to 
 Section 03A-04A .

Operate the engine to normal operating temperature and check for leaks.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Flywheel

 Removal 

Remove the vehicle driveline and transmission. Refer to the appropriate 
section in Group 07.

Remove the clutch discs and the pressure plate, if so equipped. Refer 
to Section 08-01 .

 NOTE: Use Engine Barring Tool D92T-6000-A or equivalent to hold the flywheel 
to prevent rotation.

Remove two capscrews 180 degrees apart. Install two M12 x 1.25 x 90 mm 
guide pins.

[FIGURE: A17462A.gif]

 NOTE: If a clutch is used in the equipment, the threads in the clutch 
pressure plate mounting capscrew holes can be metric or standard. Be sure to 
use the correct capscrews.

Determine the capscrew thread design and size and install two T-handles 
in the flywheel at points A and B.

Remove the remaining six flywheel mounting capscrews.

[FIGURE: A18294A.gif]

 CAUTION: The component weighs 23 kg (50 lb) or more. To avoid personal injury, 
use a hoist or get assistance to lift the component. 

Remove the flywheel from the guide pins.

[FIGURE: DA0180A.gif]

If ring gear requires replacement, refer to Flywheel Ring Gear in the 
Removal and Installation portion of this section.

 Installation 

 NOTE: Use a new pilot bearing when installing a new or rebuilt clutch.

Use a mandrel and a hammer to remove the pilot bearing.

Use a Scotch-Brite® 7448 or equivalent to clean the 
pilot bore.

 NOTE: The pilot bearing must be installed even with the pilot bore surface.

Use a mandrel and hammer to install the pilot bearing.

[FIGURE: A18296A.gif]

Install two M12 x 1.25 x 90 mm guide pins into the crankshaft flange 
180 degrees apart.

 NOTE: If a clutch is used in the equipment, the threads in the clutch 
pressure plate mounting capscrew holes can be metric or standard. Be sure to 
use the correct capscrews.

Determine the capscrew thread design and size and install two T-handles 
into the flywheel at points A and B.

[FIGURE: A18297A.gif]

Visually inspect rear face of crankshaft and flywheel mounting flange 
for cleanliness and raised nicks or burrs.

 CAUTION: The component weighs 23 kg (50 lb) or more. To avoid personal injury, 
use a hoist or get assistance to lift the component. 

Install the flywheel on the guide pins.

Lubricate the threads of the capscrews and the surface of the washers 
with 15W40 lubricating oil.

Install the six capscrews.

Remove the T-handles and guide pins.

Install the remaining capscrews into the holes from which the guide 
pins were removed.

Hold the crankshaft when tightening the flywheel capscrews.

Tighten the capscrews in a star pattern to 140 Nm (101 
lb-ft).

[FIGURE: A17390A.gif]

Install the clutch discs and pressure plate. Refer to Section 08-01 . 

Install the vehicle transmission and driveline. Refer to the 
appropriate section in Group 07.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Flywheel Ring Gear

 WARNING: WEAR EYE PROTECTION WHILE DRIVING THE GEAR FROM THE FLYWHEEL. 

 Removal 

 CAUTION: Do not use a cutting torch to heat the ring gear; the flywheel can be 
damaged. 

Remove the flywheel.

Heat the outside diameter of the ring gear with a heating torch.

Use a blunt chisel or brass drift and hammer to remove the gear from 
the flywheel.

[FIGURE: A18298A.gif]

 Installation 

 NOTE: Do not attempt to install the ring gear without using heat.

 NOTE: Do not exceed the specified time or temperature. The metal hardness 
will be changed.

 NOTE: If an oven is not available, use a heating torch to heat the inside 
diameter of the new ring gear to 177°C (350°
F). Use a Tempilstik® crayon or its equivalent to check the 
gear temperature before installing it on the flywheel.

Use an oven to heat the new ring gear. Heat the ring gear for a minimum 
of 30 minutes in a preheated 177°C (350°F) 
oven. Do not heat the ring gear for more than 6 hours.

 WARNING: WEAR PROTECTIVE GLOVES TO PREVENT PERSONAL INJURY WHEN HANDLING PARTS 
THAT HAVE BEEN HEATED. 

 NOTE: The gear must be installed so the bevel on the teeth is toward the 
crankshaft side of the flywheel.

Remove the gear from the oven and install it on the flywheel before it 
cools. Allow the air to cool the gear. Do not use water or oil to reduce the 
cooling time.

Install the flywheel.

Remove front cover.

 NOTE: Prevent movement of the adjoining idler gear when checking gear

Position a dial indicator on a tooth of the oil pump gear and measure

Note the gear backlash. Mark the oil pump gear and idler gear for

 OIL PUMP GEAR BACKLASH LIMITS

Inches

0.013

Remove four oil pump retaining bolts and remove oil pump from engine.

[FIGURE: A23420A.gif]

Make sure oil pump mounting surface is clean. 

Lubricate the pump with clean engine oil and position in the front of

 NOTE: The sealing plate on the back of the pump will seat on the cylinder

Install the four mounting bolts and tighten in the sequence shown in

Step 1 — 5 Nm (44 lb-in)

Step 2 — 24 Nm (18 lb-ft)

[FIGURE: A23420A.gif]
