1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Piston and Connecting Rod

 Removal 

Drain the engine coolant.

Remove the cylinder head.

Drain the lubricating oil. After oil is drained, reinstall drain plug 
and a new sealing washer. Tighten to 80 Nm (59 lb-ft).

Remove the oil lever indicator.

Remove the oil pan, gasket and suction tube.

[FIGURE: A23471A.gif]

 NOTE: Each connecting rod cap and connecting rod should be marked from the 
factory with a four-digit number for identification. Each cap/connecting rod 
identification number is different because each cap/connecting rod is 
align-bored.

Mark each connecting rod cap according to cylinder.

Rotate the engine until the pistons are below the carbon deposits which 
are found above the piston ring travel area.

 CAUTION: Do not use emery cloth or sandpaper to remove carbon from the cylinder 
liners. Aluminum oxide or silicon particles from emery cloth or sandpaper can 
cause serious engine damage. Do not use any abrasives in the piston ring 
travel area. The cylinder liner can be damaged. 

Use a gasket scraper or a blunt-edged instrument to loosen the carbon 
deposits. Do not damage the cylinder with the scraper.

Remove the remaining carbon with a Scotch-Brite® 7448 
cleaning pad or equivalent.

 WARNING: TO PREVENT SERIOUS EYE DAMAGE, WEAR EYE PROTECTION DURING THIS OPERATION. 

 NOTE: An inferior quality wire wheel will lose steel bristles during 
operation, causing additional contamination.

An alternative method to remove the carbon ridge is to use a high 
quality steel wire wheel installed in a drill or die grinder.

Do not use the steel wire wheel in the piston travel area. Operate the 
wheel in a circular motion to remove the deposits.

 NOTE: On pistons with anodized coatings, do not stamp on the anodized coating 
or on the outer rim. Use a scribe.

Mark each piston according to the cylinder.

Rotate the crankshaft to position the connecting rod caps at bottom 
dead center (BDC) for removal.

 NOTE: Do not remove the capscrews from the connecting rods.

Loosen the connecting rod capscrew nuts.

Use a plastic hammer to hit the connecting rod capscrews to loosen the 
connecting rod caps.

[FIGURE: A18216A.gif]

Remove the nuts from the connecting rod capscrews. Tap the connecting 
rod bolts to loosen the connecting rod cap.

Remove the lower connecting rod bearing. Mark the cylinder number and 
the letter L (lower) in the flat surface of the bearing tang.

[FIGURE: A18217A.gif]

Catch the piston with one hand while using a T-handle piston pusher to 
push the connecting rod and piston assembly out of the cylinder bore, away 
from the crankshaft. Push the connecting rod until the piston rings are 
outside of the top of the cylinder liner. Take care to avoid damage to the 
crankshaft journal, connecting rod or bearing.

[FIGURE: A18218A.gif]

Use both hands to remove the piston and connecting rod assembly.

 NOTE: The piston and connecting rod assemblies must be installed in the same 
cylinder number from which they were removed to ensure proper fit of worn 
mating surfaces if parts are used again.

Use a tag to mark the cylinder number from which each piston and 
connecting rod assembly was removed.

[FIGURE: A18219A.gif]

Place the connecting rod and piston assemblies on a rack to protect 
them from damage.

[FIGURE: A18220A.gif]

Remove the upper rod bearing. Mark the cylinder number and the letter U 
(upper) in the flat surface of the bearing tang.

[FIGURE: A18221A.gif]

Disassemble the piston and connecting rod.

 Installation 

 NOTE: Connecting rod bearings are marked on the back to indicate either 
standard (STD) or oversize (OS) thickness. Refer to Specifications in this 
section.

 NOTE: If used connecting rod bearing shells are to be installed, each bearing 
shell must be installed in its original location.

Install the connecting rod bearing shells into both the connecting rod 
and connecting rod cap. Make sure the tang on the connecting rod bearing shell 
is in the slot of the connecting rod cap and connecting rod.

[FIGURE: A18222A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not lubricate the back of the connecting rod bearing shells. 

 CAUTION: Prevent dirt from mixing with the lubricant. Dirty lubricant will 
accelerate connecting rod bearing wear. 

Lubricate the connecting rod bearings with a light film of Engine 
Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESR-M99C80-A.

Lubricate the piston rings and piston skirts with clean 15W40 engine oil.

Position the ring gaps 120 degrees apart.

[FIGURE: A17317A.gif]

 CAUTION: If using a strap-type ring compressor, make sure the inside end of the 
strap does not hook on a ring gap and break the ring. 

Compress the rings using the piston ring compressor.

Use a clean lint-free cloth to clean the crankshaft bearing journals.

Use a clean lint-free cloth to wipe the cylinder bores.

Lubricate the cylinder bore with clean 15W-40 engine oil.

Rotate the crankshaft to position the journal for the connecting rod, 
which is being installed, at bottom dead center (BDC).

[FIGURE: A19057A.gif]

 CAUTION: Use care when installing the piston and connecting rod so the cylinder 
bore is not damaged. 

Position the piston and connecting rod assembly into the cylinder bore 
with the word FRONT on the piston toward the front of the cylinder block.

 NOTE: If the piston does not move freely, remove the piston and inspect for 
broken or damaged rings.

Hold the piston ring compressor against the cylinder liner. Push the 
piston through the ring compressor and into the cylinder liner.

Push the piston into the bore until the top of the piston is 
approximately 50 mm (2 inches) below the top of the bore. Then, pull the 
connecting rod onto the crankshaft journal.

[FIGURE: A17321A.gif]

Use clean 15W40 engine oil to lubricate the threads of the connecting 
rod capscrews.

Use Engine Assembly Lubricant D9AZ-19579-D or equivalent meeting Ford 
specification ESR-M99C80-A to coat the inside diameter of the connecting rod 
bearing shell.

Install the connecting rod bearing in the connecting rod cap.

 CAUTION: The four-digit number stamped on the rod and cap at the parting line 
must match and be installed on the oil cooler side of the engine. 

 NOTE: The serial numbers marked on the connecting rod and the connecting rod 
cap must be the same. The tang slot side of the connecting rod cap must be on 
the same side as the tang slot in the connecting rod when the connecting rod 
cap is installed.

Install the connecting rod cap and start the connecting rod nuts.

Use clean 15W40 engine oil to lubricate the connecting rod nuts.

Alternately tighten the connecting rod nuts in three steps to pull the 
connecting rod cap into position.

Step 1 — 40 Nm (30 lb-ft)

Step 2 — 80 Nm (59 lb-ft)

Step 3 — 120 Nm (88 lb-ft)

[FIGURE: A18223A.gif]

Shake the connecting rod after tightening to verify side clearance.

[FIGURE: A18224A.gif]

Measure the side clearance between the connecting rod and crankshaft. 
Side clearance limits are 0.10-0.33 mm (0.0039 to 0.013 inch). Do not measure 
the clearance between the rod cap and crankshaft.

 CAUTION: The crankshaft must rotate freely. 

 NOTE: If the connecting rod is not properly oriented (tang opposite the 
camshaft), it will contact the camshaft and prevent the crankshaft from 
rotating.

Check for freedom of rotation as the rod caps are installed. If the 
crankshaft does not rotate freely, check the installation of the rod bearings 
and the bearing size.

[FIGURE: A17325A.gif]

Use Silicone Rubber D6AZ-19562-AA or F4AZ-19562-B or equivalent meeting 
Ford specification WSE-M4G323-A1 to fill the joints between the pan rail, gear 
housing and rear cover.

Coat both sides of the oil pan gasket with Perfect Seal Sealing 
Compound B5A-19554-A or F2AZ-19554-AA or equivalent meeting Ford 
specifications ESR-M18P2-A and ESE-M4G115-A.

Assemble the oil pan, gasket and capscrews as illustrated and install. 
Tighten capscrews to 24 Nm (18 lb-ft).

Install the suction tube and oil pan.

[FIGURE: A23471A.gif]

Install the oil level indicator.

Install the cylinder head. Fill the cooling system and fill the engine 
with oil.

Prelube (prime) the engine prior to start-up by disconnecting the fuel 
shutoff solenoid and cranking the engine until the oil pressure gauge reads 
pressure, or no more than 30 seconds. Allow the starter to cool for two 
minutes between crank times.

Bleed the engine cooling system. Refer to Section 03-03 .

Bleed the fuel supply lines and injector high pressure lines. Refer to 
 Section 03A-04A .

Operate the engine to normal operating temperature and check for leaks.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Rocker Arms and Shaft

 Disassembly 

Remove the retaining rings, thrust washers and wavy spring washers.

[FIGURE: A18303A.gif]

Remove the rocker arms.

[FIGURE: A18304A.gif]

Remove the rocker arm shaft support assembly.

[FIGURE: A18305A.gif]

Remove the lock nut and adjusting screw. If the rocker arms and push 
rods are to be cleaned and inspected for reuse, refer to the Cleaning and 
Inspection portion of this section.

 Assembly 

Install the adjusting screw and lock nut.

Lubricate the rocker arm shaft with engine oil.

 CAUTION: Make sure to assemble the intake and exhaust rocker levers in the 
correct locations. 

Position the rocker arms on the rocker arm shaft.

[FIGURE: A18306A.gif]

Install a retaining ring, thrust washer and wavy spring washer.

[FIGURE: A18307A.gif]

Position the rocker arms on the rocker arm shaft.

Install the remaining wavy spring washer, thrust washer and retaining 
ring as shown.

 Stem to Guide Clearance

[FIGURE: A17534B.gif]

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Core Plugs

 SPECIAL SERVICE TOOL(S) REQUIRED

Description

Tool Number

Impact Slide Hammer

T50T-100-A

Impact Slide Hammer

T59L-100-B

 Removal 

To remove a large core plug, drill a 12.70-mm (0.5-inch) hole in the 
center of the plug and remove with Impact Slide Hammer T59L-100-B or 
T50T-100-A or pry it out with a large drift punch. On a small core plug, drill 
a 6.35-mm (0.25-inch) hole in the center of the plug and pry it out with a 
small pin punch.

Clean and inspect the plug bore.

 Installation 

Prior to installation, inspect the plug bore for any damage that would 
interfere with the proper sealing of the plug.

Coat the plug and/or bore lightly with an oil-resistant (oil gallery) 
or Perfect Seal Sealing Compound F2AZ-19554 or equivalent meeting Ford 
specifications ESR-M18P2-A and ESE-M4G115-A, and install it following the 
procedure for cup-type or expansion-type below.

 Cup-Type 

Cup-type core plugs are installed with the flanged edge outward. The 
maximum diameter of this plug is located at the outer edge of the flange. The 
flange on cup-type plugs flares outward with the largest diameter of the outer 
(sealing) edge.

 CAUTION: It is imperative to pull the plug into the machined bore by using a 
properly designed tool. Under no circumstances is the plug to be driven into 
the bore using a tool that contacts the flange. This method will damage the 
sealing edge and will result in leakage and/or plug blowout. 

[FIGURE: A3217E.gif]

Sealing Edge Before Installation

The flanged (trailing) edge must be below the chamfered edge of the 
bore to effectively seal the plugged bore.

If the core plug replacing tool has a depth seating surface, do not 
seat the tool against a non-machined (casting) surface.

 Expansion-Type 

 CAUTION: It is imperative to push or drive the plug into the machined bore using 
a properly designed tool. Under no circumstances is the plug to be driven 
using a tool that contacts the crowned portion of the plug. This method will 
expand the plug prior to installation and can damage the plug and/or plug bore. 

Expansion-type core plugs are installed with the flange edge inward. 
The maximum diameter of this plug is located at the base of the flange with 
the flange flaring inward.

When installed, the trailing (maximum) diameter must be below the 
chamfered edge of the bore to effectively seal the plugged bore.

If the core plug replacing tool has a depth seating surface, do not 
seat the tool against a non-machined (casting) surface.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Camshaft Drive Gear and Thrust Plate

Clean the gear, thrust plate and spacer in solvent.

Check the gear and thrust plate for scores or nicks. Also, check the 
gear or the condition of the tooth wear pattern. Discard parts that show signs 
of excessive wear.

Measure the thickness of the thrust plate. If the thrust plate is less 
than 9.340 mm (0.3677 inch), discard the thrust plate and install a new one.

Check the keyway and key on the end of the camshaft. If the key is 
damaged, install a new key before installing the gear. Use a carborundum stone 
to remove minor gear tooth imperfections. If tooth wear or damage is severe, 
install a new gear.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Piston and Pin

 Cleaning 

 CAUTION: Be sure the cleaning solvent is approved for aluminum. Damage to the 
pistons can result. 

Allow the pistons to soak for a minimum of 30 minutes in a tank 
containing an approved cleaning solvent for aluminum.

 CAUTION: Do not clean the pistons and rods in an acid tank. 

 CAUTION: Do not use a metal brush. A metal brush will damage the piston ring 
grooves. Do not use glass beads to clean the grooves. Walnut shell or plastic 
bead blasting can be used on grooves with a nickel-coated scuff-resistant 
insert and on the dome or crown of the piston. Use the minimum effective 
pressure and do not concentrate the spray in one area for an extended period 
of time. The recommended blast pressure for plastic bead blasting is 276 kPa 
(40 psi). Do not use glass beads or walnut shell blasting on the aluminum 
grooves or pin bores. This can cause the pin to crack or the rings to not seat. 

Wash the pistons and rods in a strong solution of laundry detergent in 
hot water. Use a non-metallic brush to remove carbon deposits.

[FIGURE: A23664A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not use a ring groove cleaner and make sure not to scratch the ring 
sealing surface in the piston groove. 

Clean the remaining deposits from the ring grooves with the square end 
of a broken ring.

Wash the pistons again in a detergent solution or solvent. After 
rinsing, use compressed air to dry.

 WARNING: WHEN USING A STEAM CLEANER, WEAR PROTECTIVE CLOTHING AND SAFETY GLASSES 
OR A FACE SHIELD. HOT STEAM CAN CAUSE SERIOUS PERSONAL INJURY. 

Use steam to clean the pistons.

Dry with compressed air.

 Inspection 

 NOTE: Dimensional inspection of the piston is required only when the cause of 
the lack of sealing is not apparent.

Inspect the piston for damage and excessive wear. Check the top ring 
grooves, skirt and pin bore.

[FIGURE: A17533A.gif]

 CAUTION: Do not use pistons with cracks. 

Visually inspect the piston bowl, pin bore and skirt for cracks or 
damage.

[FIGURE: A18337A.gif]

Measure the piston pin bore when the piston temperature is at 20°
C (68°F). Piston bore ID limits are 
45.006-45.025 mm (1.7719-1.7726 inch). Add 0.013 mm (0.0005 inch) to the bore 
inside diameter per 5°C (10°F) temperature 
rise up to 32°C (90°F).

Measure the piston skirt diameter as illustrated. Piston skirt OD 
limits are 113.776-113.847 mm (4.4794-4.4822 inches).

[FIGURE: A17534B.gif]

Use a micrometer and piston ring groove gauge to measure the wear of 
the top ring groove keystone angle. Use a piston ring groove gauge to measure 
the wear of the intermediate ring groove keystone angle.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Piston Rings

Clean piston rings with solvent and dry.

Abrasive wear is indicated by concentrated vertical scratches. The 
chromium plate is worn through and the face of the ring has a brighter finish 
when compared to the dull satin finish of a new ring.

[FIGURE: A24346A.gif]

Scuffing and scoring is indicated by heavy scratches, metal 
discoloration and voids (B). This damage indicates a breakdown of the oil film 
on the liner wall, causing transfer of material from the ring face of the 
liner. (A) represents new ring with ring face intact.

[FIGURE: A24347A.gif]

Oil ring plugging is indicated by deposits in the oil ring grooves (B). 
Plugging of the ring drains restricts oil drainback, which floods the ring 
belt area resulting in a loss of oil control. (A) represents oil rings with no 
deposits.

[FIGURE: A24348A.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Piston Connecting Rods

Use a nylon bristle to clean the oil drillings.

 WARNING: WHEN USING A STEAM CLEANER, WEAR PROTECTIVE CLOTHING AND SAFETY GLASSES 
OR A FACE SHIELD. HOT STEAM WILL CAUSE SERIOUS PERSONAL INJURY. 

Use steam or solvent to clean the connecting rods. Dry with compressed 
air.

Inspect the connecting rods and caps for damage.

Replace the connecting rod if the I-beam is nicked or damaged.

Visually inspect the piston pin bore for damage or misalignment of the 
oil passage and bushing.

Measure the connecting rod piston pin bushing inside diameter. 
Connecting rod pin bore specifications are 45.023-45.060 mm (1.7726-1.7740 
inch) with bushing installed.

[FIGURE: A17540A.gif]

Tap the connecting rod bolts in until the head is aligned and seated on 
the flat machined surface of the connecting rod.

 NOTE: The connecting rod cap number must match the number on the connecting 
rod and be installed with the numbers aligned.

Install the bearing shells in the connecting rod and cap. Install the 
connecting rod caps and the connecting rod nuts.

Tighten the connecting rod nuts in a three-step alternating sequence.

Step 1 — 40 Nm (30 lb-ft)

Step 2 — 80 Nm (59 lb-ft)

Step 3 — 120 Nm (88 lb-ft)

Measure the connecting rod crankshaft bore inside diameter with the 
bearing installed. Connecting rod crankshaft bore ID limits are 76.046-76.104 
mm (2.9939-2.9962 inches).

Measure and record the mean diameter of the rod journals on the 
crankshaft. Crankshaft rod journal diameter limits are 75.962-76.013 mm 
(2.9906-2.9926 inches). If crankshaft rod journals are not within the given 
specifications, the crankshaft must be removed and reground.

[FIGURE: A17543A.gif]

Out-of-roundness: 0.050 mm (0.002 inch).

Taper: 0.013 mm (0.0005 inch).

Bearing clearance: rod inside diameter minus crankshaft journal diameter.

[FIGURE: A17544B.gif]

Bearing clearance can also be determined with Plastigage®
 D81L-6002-B or equivalent during engine assembly. 
Connecting rod bearing clearance limits are 0.033-0.117 mm (0.0013-0.0046 inch).

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Connecting Rod Bearings

 WARNING: WHEN USING A STEAM CLEANER, WEAR PROTECTIVE CLOTHING AND SAFETY GLASSES 
OR A FACE SHIELD. HOT STEAM CAN CAUSE SERIOUS PERSONAL INJURY. 

Wash the bearing and rod caps. Dry with compressed air.

Visually inspect the rod caps, connecting rod bearing saddles and 
capscrews for nicks, cracks, burrs, scratches or fretting.

 NOTE: Replace any bearings with lock tang damage or scratches (deep enough to 
be felt with a fingernail). Also replace any bearings which show pitting, 
flaking, or corrosion into the lining.

 NOTE: Normal bearing wear produces a smooth finish which will wear into the 
lining. An exposed lining does not always indicate worn bearings. If large 
areas of the lining are visible in the bearings before the engine has 
accumulated 240,000 kilometers (150,000 miles) or 3,750 hours, inspect the 
engine for contamination from fine dirt particles and correct the problem.

Visually inspect the bearings for damage.

Inspect the crankshaft rod journals for deep scoring or overheating.

Use a micrometer to measure the rod journal.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Crankshaft

 NOTE: A limited number of crankshaft main bearing or rod bearing journals 
will be ground 0.25 mm (0.010 inch) or 0.05 mm (0.002 inch) undersize in 
production. Engines equipped with undersize crankshafts will be identified 
with one of the following codes on the right front of the block near the 
engine code.

(M) — Undersize main bearing journals 

(P) — Undersize rod bearing journals

(MP) — Undersize main and rod bearing journals.

 CAUTION: Handle the crankshaft with care to avoid possible damage to the 
finished surfaces. 

If the crankshaft gear teeth are excessively worn or chipped, install a 
new crankshaft gear which must be fully located on the shoulder of the 
crankshaft. Refer to Crankshaft Gear in the Removal and Installation portion 
of this section.

Clean the crankshaft with solvent, then blow out all oil passages with 
compressed air.

Measure the diameter of each journal in at least four places to 
determine an out-of-round, taper or undersize condition. For specifications, 
refer to Cylinder Block Specifications at the end of this section.

[FIGURE: A100941A.gif]

On an engine used with a manual transmission, check the fit of the 
clutch pilot bearing in the bore of the crankshaft. A needle roller bearing 
and adapter assembly is used as a clutch pilot bearing. It is press-fit 
directly into the engine crankshaft and should not be loose. Inspect the inner 
surface of the bearing for wear or a bell-mouth condition. Check the inside 
diameter of the bearing to see if it is worn or damaged. The bearing and 
adapter assembly cannot be serviced separately. The needle bearing clutch 
pilot can only be installed with the seal end of the bearing facing the 
transmission. The bearing and seal are pregreased and do not require 
additional lubrication. A new bearing must be installed whenever a bearing is 
removed.

Inspect the pilot bearing, when used, for roughness, evidence of 
overheating or loss of lubricant. Replace if any of these condition are found.

Examine the rear oil seal journal for score marks, remove minor 
imperfections with fine emery cloth (600 grade). Clean journal around its 
circumference, not lengthwise. Clean the rear oil seal journal thoroughly with 
solvent after using emery cloth.

 Journals, Refinishing 

Dress minor imperfections such as scores, nicks or burrs with an oil 
stone. If the journals are severely marred or exceed the service limit, they 
should be refinished to size for the next undersize bearing. 

If required, machine the journals to give the proper clearance with the 
next undersize bearing. If the journals will not clean up to maximum undersize 
bearing available, replace the crankshaft. 

Always reproduce the same journal shoulder radius that existed 
originally. Too small a radius will result in fatigue failure of the 
crankshaft. Too large a radius will result in bearing failure due to radius 
ride of the bearing. 

After refinishing the journals, chamfer the oil holes. Polish the 
journal with a No. 320 grit polishing cloth and engine oil (crocus cloth may 
also be used as a polishing agent) to obtain a smooth finish.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Crankshaft Main Bearings 

 Cleaning 

Bearings that are to be reused must be identified so they can be

Clean the bearing inserts and caps thoroughly in solvent, and dry them

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Cylinder Block Sleeves

 CAUTION: Do not use any abrasives in the ring travel area of the liner. The 
liner can be damaged. 

Use a soft wire brush or a fine fibrous abrasive pad such as Scotch-Brite®
 7448 or equivalent to clean the flange seating area.

 WARNING: WHEN USING A STEAM CLEANER, WEAR PROTECTIVE CLOTHING AND SAFETY GLASSES 
OR A FACE SHIELD. HOT STEAM CAN CAUSE SERIOUS PERSONAL INJURY. 

Use solvent or steam clean the liners and dry with compressed air.

 NOTE: Use lint-free paper towels to wipe the oil from the inside of the liners.

Use clean 15W40 oil to lubricate the inside diameter of the liners. 
Allow the oil to soak in the liner for 5 to 10 minutes.

Continue to lubricate the inside of the liners and wipe clean until the 
paper towel shows no gray or black residue.

Visually inspect the liners for cracks on the inside and outside 
diameters.

Inspect for cracks under the flange.

Visually inspect the outside diameter and seat area for excessive 
corrosion or pitting. Pits must not be more than 1.6 mm (0.06 inch) deep.

Replace the liner if the pits are too deep or if the corrosion cannot 
be removed with fine emery cloth.

Visually inspect the inside diameter for liner bore polishing.

A moderate polish produces a bright mirror finish in the worn area with 
traces of the original hone marks or an indication of an etch pattern.

A heavy polish produces a bright mirror finish in the worn area with no 
traces of hone marks or an etch pattern.

Replace the liner if the following condition(s) exist:

A heavy polish is present over 20 percent of the piston ring travel area.

Both moderate and heavy polish over 30 percent of the piston ring 
travel area and one half (15 percent) is heavy polish.

Measure the liner inside diameter in four places 90 degrees apart at 
the top and bottom of the piston travel area. Cylinder liner ID limits are 
114.000-114.117 mm (4.4882-4.4928 inches).

Measure the outside diameter of the liner top press fit area. Cylinder 
liner OD limits (top press fit) are 132.938-132.958 mm (5.2338-5.2346 inches).

Measure the cylinder liner bore in the block. Cylinder line bore limits 
are 132.900-132.990 mm (5.2323-5.2358 inches).

[FIGURE: A18338A.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Cylinder Head

 NOTE: Omit the first seven steps if a replacement head is to be installed.

Clean the carbon from the injector nozzle seat with an injector bore 
brush.

Scrape the gasket material from all gasket surfaces.

 CAUTION: When using a steam cleaner, wear protective clothing and safety glasses 
or a face shield. Hot steam can cause serious personal injury. 

Steam clean the cylinder head and dry with compressed air. Blow out all 
capscrew holes.

Clean the buildup of deposits from the coolant passages. Excessive 
deposits can be cleaned in an acid tank but the cup plugs must be removed first.

Use Scotch-Brite® 7448 or equivalent and solvent to 
clean the cylinder head combustion face.

Clean the exhaust manifold gasket surface.

Clean the valve cover gasket surface.

 WARNING: WEAR PROTECTIVE EYE COVERING. 

 NOTE: An inferior quality wire wheel will lose steel bristles during 
operation, causing additional contamination.

Clean carbon deposits from the valve pockets with a high quality steel 
wire wheel installed in a drill or a die grinder.

Wash the cylinder head in hot soapy water solution. After rinsing, use 
compressed air to dry the cylinder head.

Visually inspect the cylinder head and valves for obvious damage that 
would prohibit reuse. Check for cracks and damage to the deck surface that 
would result in loss of sealing.

Check for cracks on the combustion face. Cracks that extend from the 
injector bore away from the valve seats and are not over 10 mm (0.394 inch) 
long are acceptable.

[FIGURE: A18323A.gif]

Any cracks that extend from the injector bore toward the valve seats 
are unacceptable and the cylinder head must be replaced.

Cracks between the valve seats are not acceptable and the cylinder head 
must be replaced.

Use a straightedge and feeler gauge to check the cylinder head 
combustion surface for flatness.

 CYLINDER HEAD FLATNESS SPECIFICATIONS

 NOTE: A maximum of 1.00 mm (0.040 inch) can be machined from the combustion 
surface of the cylinder head.

Use a small 51-mm (2-inch) straightedge and a 0.0254-mm (0.001-inch) 
feeler gauge to measure local flatness. Check between the cylinder bores and 
also between the coolant passages. If the 0.001-inch feeler gauge fits under 
the 51-mm (2-inch) straightedge, the cylinder head must be replaced or 
resurfaced.

[FIGURE: A18324A.gif]

If the cylinder head is machined, place the valve in the respective 
bore and check the valve depth dimension. If the depth is less than the

cylinder head is 1.09-1.62 mm (0.043-0.064 inch) for the exhaust valve and 
0.69-1.09 mm (0.027-0.043 inch) for the intake valve.

Visually inspect the valves for indications of leakage or burning.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Flywheel

 Transmission, Automatic 

Inspect the flywheel for cracks or other damage that would make it

 Transmission, Manual 

Inspect the flywheel for cracks, heat check or other damage that would

mm (0.040 inch) of stock from the original thickness, replace the flywheel.

are damaged, replace the ring gear. 

With the flywheel housing installed on the crankshaft, check the 
flywheel housing runout. Refer to Section 03-00 .

 Cleaning

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Oil Pump 

 Cleaning 

Wash all parts in a solvent and dry thoroughly with compressed air. Use 
a brush to clean the inside of the pump housing and the pressure relief valve 
chamber. Make sure all dirt and metal particles are removed. 

 Inspection 

 NOTE: Internal components are not serviced. If any component is out of 
specification, the pump assembly must be replaced. 

Check the inside of the pump housing and the inner and outer gears for 
damage or excessive wear. 

Check the mating surface of the pump cover for wear. Minor scuff marks 
are normal, but if the cover, gears or housing surfaces are excessively worn, 
scored or grooved, replace the pump. Inspect the rotor for nicks, burrs or 
score marks. Remove minor imperfections with an oil stone. 

Measure the inner to outer rotor tip clearance with feeler gauge 
inserted 13 mm (0.5 inch) minimum. Inner and outer rotor tip clearance must 
not exceed 0.1778 mm (0.007 inch).

[FIGURE: A23430A.gif]

With the rotor assembly installed in the housing, place Straight Edge 
D83L-4201-A or equivalent over the rotor assembly and the housing. 

Measure the vertical clearance (rotor end play) between the 
straightedge and both the inner rotor and the outer race. Maximum clearance 
must not exceed 0.127 mm (0.005 inch).

[FIGURE: A23431A.gif]

Measure clearance between outer rotor and housing in several areas 
around the circumference of the outer rotor. Clearance must not exceed 0.381 
mm (0.015 inch).

[FIGURE: A23432A.gif]

Measure oil pump drive gear backlash. Backlash must not exceed 0.33 mm 
(0.013 inch).

[FIGURE: A23433A.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Rocker Arms

 Cleaning

 NOTE: The rocker arm shaft supports are made from powdered metal and will

Use compressed air to dry the parts after rinsing in clean hot water.

 Inspection

 NOTE: The rocker arms do not use a bushing in the bore for the rocker arm

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Valve Tappets

 CAUTION: Any time a new camshaft is installed, new tappets must also be installed. 

Clean the valve tappets with solvent and dry with compressed air.

Inspect the socket, stem and face for excessive wear, cracks, concavity 
and other damage. Maximum allowable tappet face concavity for reuse is 0.025 
mm (0.001 inch).

[FIGURE: A17570C.gif]

Measure the valve tappet stem. Tappet stem diameter limits are 
15.925-15.98 mm (0.627-0.6291 inch).

Pit marks on the tappet face are acceptable.

The following criteria define the size of the pits allowed.

A single pit cannot be greater than 2 mm (0.078 inch).

Interconnection of pits is not allowed.

Total pits when added together must not exceed 6 mm (0.236-inch) 
diameter or a total of four percent of the tappet face.

No pitting is allowable on the edges of the wear face of the tappet.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Valves

 Cleaning 

 WARNING: WEAR PROTECTIVE EYE COVERING.

Polish the valve stem with a Scotch-Brite® pad or

worn collet grooves

worn stem tip

[FIGURE: A18327A.gif]

minor grooves on the valve sealing surface

fine pitting on the valve sealing surface

carbon or varnish buildup on the valve stem

[FIGURE: A18328A.gif]

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Cylinder Head Deck

 Cleaning 

 NOTE: Excessive deposits may be cleaned in an acid tank, but the camshaft 
bushings must first be removed to prevent damage.

Place clean lint-free rags over the pistons to prevent dirt from 
falling into the engine.

Plug or cover the coolant and oil passages in the cylinder block deck.

Use a gasket scraper to clean the cylinder block deck surface.

Use Scotch-Brite® 7448 or equivalent and solvent to 
remove any residual gasket material from the cylinder block deck surface.

 WARNING: WHEN USING COMPRESSED AIR TO CLEAN CAPSCREW HOLES, ALWAYS WEAR SAFETY 
GLASSES OR A FACE SHIELD TO PROTECT THE EYES. PERSONAL INJURY CAN RESULT. 

 NOTE: Make sure the cylinder head capscrew holes are clean.

Use compressed air to clean debris from the capscrew holes.

Inspect the coolant passages. Buildup of deposits in the coolant 
passages can cause engine overheating. A large buildup of rust and lime will 
require removal of the cylinder block for cleaning in a hot tank.

Be sure the coolant passages are clean.

[FIGURE: A18331A.gif]

 Inspection 

 CAUTION: Do not proceed with the repair if the cylinder block head deck is 
damaged or not flat. The engine will have to be removed for resurfacing the 
block. 

 NOTE: The cylinder block head deck can be resurfaced in a machine shop and a 
thicker surface head gasket installed to keep the piston-to-head clearance the 
same.

Use a straightedge and feeler gauge to measure the overall flatness of 
the cylinder head deck. The overall flatness, side to side, must not exceed 
0.075 mm (0.003 inch). The overall flatness, end-to-end, must not exceed 0.200 
mm (0.008 inch).

Use a small 51-mm (2-inch) straightedge and a 0.0254-mm (0.001-inch) 
feeler gauge to measure local flatness. Check between the cylinder bores and 
also between the coolant passages. If the 0.001-inch feeler gauge fits under 
the 51-mm (2-inch) straightedge, the cylinder head must be replaced or 
resurfaced.

Visually inspect for any localized dips or imperfections. If present, 
the cylinder head deck must be reground.

The cylinder block head deck can be resurfaced two times. The first 
resurface should be 0.25 mm (0.010 inch). If additional resurfacing is 
required, an additional 0.25 mm (0.010 inch) can be removed.

 CYLINDER BLOCK RESURFACE LIMITS

mm

Inch

0.010

The upper right corner of the rear face of the block must be stamped 
with an X when the block is resurfaced to 0.25 mm (0.010 inch). A second X 
must be stamped beside the first when the block is resurfaced to 0.50 mm 
(0.020 inch).

[FIGURE: A18332A.gif]

 NOTE: The gaskets are notched to aid in identification.

Consult the parts catalog for the correct head gasket to be used with 
resurfaced blocks to be sure of proper piston-to-valve clearance.

Use the gasket where block deck has been resurfaced 0.25 mm (0.010 
inch) (two notches).

Use the gasket where block deck has been resurfaced 0.50 mm (0.020 
inch) (three notches).

[FIGURE: A18333B.gif]

 NOTE: The liners must be checked in the "free state," without clamps.

Check the liner protrusion. Liner protrusion is the distance the liner 
protrudes above the block face. Cylinder liner protrusion limits are 
0.025-0.122 mm (0.0010-0.0048 inch). If the cylinder liner protrusion is below 
specifications, it will be necessary to machine the counterbores.

Visually inspect the cylinder liners for cracks, scuffing or scoring.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Valve Seat

 Inspection 

Inspect the valve seat inserts for cracks or burned spots. Refer to the 
following reuse guidelines for any cracks discovered. Service valve seats are 
available for seats with burned spots that will require more than 0.254 mm 
(0.010 inch) grinding to clean up.

 NOTE: The sealing surface of the valve must seat in the center of the valve 
seat insert.

Measure the width of the valve seat area of the valve seat inserts. 
Valve seat area width limits are 1.5-2.0 mm (0.059-0.079 inch).

If the valve seat area is worn wider than the maximum specified, 
replace the valve seat insert.

[FIGURE: A18334A.gif]

Install the valves in their respective bores and measure the recess in 
the cylinder head.

Make sure the seats are clean before measuring the recess. Valve recess 
in cylinder head limits is 1.09-1.62 mm (0.043-0.064 inch) for the exhaust 
valve and 0.69-1.09 mm (0.027-0.043 inch) for the intake valve. If the valve 
recess is out of limits, before replacing the valve seat, try replacing the 
old valve with a new valve. If the recess is within limits with the new valve, 
grind the old valve seat and use the new valve.

[FIGURE: A18335A.gif]

PAGE 4373
================================================================================

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Cylinder Head Cracks, Reuse Guidelines

These guidelines apply only to cracks extending from the injector bore 
to the intake valve seats. Replace cylinder heads that exhibit valve bridge 
cracks in any other location.

The reuse guidelines for a cylinder head with a crack extending from 
the injector bore to the intake seat are as follows:

If the crack does not extend into the valve seat, the head is reusable.

If the crack extends into or through the valve seat, the head must be 
repaired by installing a valve seat insert.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Valve Spring

 Inspection 

Inspect the valve springs for obvious damage (breaks, etc.).

Measure the valve spring. Valve spring free height is 65.66 mm (2.585 
inches).

[FIGURE: A18336A.gif]

Use a valve spring tester to measure the valve spring load at the 
opening height. Valve spring opening height is 37.90 mm (1.492 inch). Valve 
spring load for opening height is 960-1060 N (216-238 lbf) for new valve 
springs. Valve spring load for used valve springs is 940 N (213 lbf).

If the valve spring load for the opening height is less than the 
minimum specified, the valve spring must be replaced.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Water Thermostat

 NOTE: If the problem being investigated is insufficient heat, the thermostat 
should be checked for leakage. This can be done by holding the thermostat up 
to a lighted background. Light leakage around the thermostat valve (thermostat 
at room temperature) is unacceptable and the thermostat must be replaced. On 
some thermostats, a slight leakage of light at one or two locations on the 
perimeter of the valve may be detected. This should be considered normal.

Remove the thermostat and immerse it in boiling water. Replace the 
thermostat if it does not open more than 6.35 mm (0.25 inch) after one minute 
in water.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Cooling System

 Rust or Dirt Contamination 

If the cooling system is contaminated by residual solids such as rust 
or dirt, the system must be cleaned by using Ford Premium Cooling System Flush 
F1AZ-19A503-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESR-M14P7-A. Heavy rust 
or scale may require additional radiator cleaning service.

 Oil Contamination 

If the cooling system is contaminated by oil, perform the following 
steps:

Determine the source or cause of the contamination and eliminate it.

Drain the cooling system and fill with clean water containing two 
ounces per gallon of nonfoaming automatic dishwasher detergent.

Run the engine for 30 minutes at 1000-1200 rpm.

Drain the cooling system. Allow engine to cool.

Refill with Ford Heavy Duty Diesel Engine Cooling System Fluid 
E6HZ-19549-A or equivalent meeting Ford specification ESE-M97B18-C and Heavy 
Duty Cooling System Additive FW-15 or equivalent meeting Ford specification 
ESN-M99B169-F.

================================================================================
PAGE 4377
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 03B-01: Engine, FD-1460 Diesel

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Lubrication System 

 NOTE: Observe condition of coolant. If there is evidence of oil contamination 
in coolant, the cooling system must be cleaned.

If the engine oil has been contaminated by coolant, the engine 
lubrication system must be cleaned. 

Determine the level/severity of contamination and proceed with the 
appropriate cleaning procedure. 

 Contamination Slight to Moderate with No Sludging 

Defined as showing evidence of coolant in oil. Sludging is defined as 
evidence of gelled, slimy deposits attached to engine parts. 

 Cleaning 

Drain all oil from the engine. Also remove the oil cooler drain plug 
and drain oil. Replace drain plug. 

Remove and discard the oil filter and fit new oil filter. Remove 
crankcase breather element.

 WARNING: READ AND FOLLOW ALL STATEMENTS ON CLEANING SOLVENT CONTAINER TO ENSURE 
SAFE OPERATION. 

Mix 9.5 liters (10.0 quarts) of kerosene with 9.5 liters (10.0 quarts) 
of recommended engine oil and refill crankcase. 

Run engine for 30 minutes at 1000-1200 rpm with no load.

 CAUTION: When performing this procedure, check oil pressure frequently. Make 
sure oil pressure does not fall below 103 kPa (15 psi). 

Drain all oil from the engine. Also remove the oil cooler drain plug 
and drain oil. Replace drain plug. 

Remove and discard the oil filter and fit new oil filter. 

Repeat Steps 3, 4, 5, 6 and go to Step 8. 

Fill crankcase with recommended engine oil. 

Replace crankcase breather element. 

 Contamination Heavy with Sludging 

Defined as showing heavy concentration of coolant in oil with sludging. 
Sludging is defined as evidence of gelled, slimy deposits on parts under 
rocker cover and bottom end (oil pan area). 

 Cleaning 

Determine the source or cause of the contamination and eliminate it. 

Drain all oil from the engine. Also remove the oil cooler drain plug 
and drain oil. Replace drain plug. 

If sludge is heavy and built up, remove as much sludge deposit as 
possible from exposed engine parts, i.e., under rocker cover and lower end 
(oil pan removed) before proceeding further. 

Remove and discard the oil filter and fit new oil filter. Remove 
crankcase breather element.

 WARNING: READ AND FOLLOW ALL STATEMENTS ON CLEANING SOLVENT CONTAINER TO ENSURE 
SAFE OPERATION. 

Mix 9.5 liters (10.0 quarts) of commercially available cleaning solvent 
such as Butyl Cellosolve (Union Carbide) or Downol E-B (Dow Chemical) or 
Glycol Ether E-13 (Chem Central) or equivalent with 9.5 liters (10.0 quarts) 
recommended engine oil and refill crankcase. 

Run engine for 30 minutes at 1000-1200 rpm with no load.

 CAUTION: When performing this procedure, check oil pressure frequently. Make 
sure oil pressure does not fall below 103 kPa (15 psi). 

Drain all oil from the engine. Also remove the oil cooler drain plug 
and drain oil. Replace drain plug. 

Remove and discard the oil filter and fit new oil filter.

 WARNING: READ AND FOLLOW ALL STATEMENTS ON CLEANING SOLVENT CONTAINER TO ENSURE 
SAFE OPERATION. 

Mix 9.5 liters (10.0 quarts) of commercially available cleaning solvent 
such as Butyl Cellosolve (Union Carbide) or Downol E-B (Dow Chemical) or 
Glycol Ether E-13 (Chem Central) or equivalent with 9.5 liters (10.0 quarts) 
recommended engine oil and refill crankcase. 

Run engine for 30 minutes at 1000-1200 rpm with no load.

 CAUTION: When performing this procedure, check oil pressure frequently. Make 
sure oil pressure does not fall below 103 kPa (15 psi). 

Drain all oil from the engine. Also remove the oil cooler drain plug 
and drain oil. Replace drain plug. 

Remove and discard the oil filter and fit new oil filter. Fill the 
crankcase with the recommended engine oil. 

Run engine for 30 minutes at 1000-1200 rpm with no load.

 CAUTION: When performing this procedure, check oil pressure frequently. Make 
sure oil pressure does not fall below 103 kPa (15 psi). 

Drain all oil from the engine. Also remove the oil cooler drain plug 
and drain oil. Replace drain plug. 

Remove oil pan and inspect main and rod bearings for signs of distress. 
Replace bearings if necessary and replace oil pan. 

Remove and discard the oil filter and fit new oil filter. Fill the 
crankcase with the recommended engine oil. Install new crankcase breather 
element.

ADJUSTMENTS

Valve Adjustment, Cold

 CAUTION: Adjust the valves when the engine is cold — below 60°
C (140°F). 

 NOTE: Valve lash must be checked and adjusted at the first 32,000 km (20,000 
miles) and thereafter at 64,000-km (40,000-mile) intervals.

Use the timing pin to locate top dead center (TDC) for cylinder No. 1, 
and then remove the valve covers.

[FIGURE: A18191A.gif]

 CAUTION: To prevent damage to the timing pin, make sure to disengage the pin 
after locating top dead center (TDC). 

When the pin engages the hole in the camshaft gear, cylinder No. 1 is 
at TDC on the compression stroke.

[FIGURE: A18192B.gif]

 NOTE: The clearance is correct when slight resistance is felt as the feeler 
gauge is moved between the valve stem and rocker lever.

Adjust the valves with engine cold (below 60°C [

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Cooling System

 WARNING: NEVER REMOVE THE RADIATOR CAP UNDER ANY CONDITIONS WHILE THE ENGINE IS 
OPERATING. FAILURE TO FOLLOW THESE INSTRUCTIONS CAN RESULT IN PERSONAL INJURY 
AND DAMAGE TO THE COOLING SYSTEM AND ENGINE.

TO AVOID HAVING SCALDING HOT COOLANT OR STEAM BLOW OUT OF THE RADIATOR, 
USE EXTREME CARE WHEN REMOVING THE CAP FROM A HOT RADIATOR. IF POSSIBLE, WAIT 
UNTIL THE ENGINE HAS COOLED, THEN WRAP A THICK CLOTH AROUND THE RADIATOR CAP 
AND TURN IT SLOWLY TO THE FIRST STOP. STEP BACK WHILE THE PRESSURE IS RELEASED 
FROM THE COOLING SYSTEM. WHEN YOU ARE SURE ALL THE PRESSURE HAS BEEN RELEASED, 
PRESS DOWN ON THE CAP (STILL USING A CLOTH), TURN AND REMOVE IT. 

Refer to Section 03-03 .

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Thermostat, Water 

 CAUTION: Do not attempt to service the thermostat. It should be replaced if it 
is not operating properly. 

The poppet-type thermostat used in production is a high-temperature 
thermostat for use with a mixture of water and permanent-type antifreeze. 
Install a low temperature thermostat if a nonpermanent type antifreeze and 
water coolant solution is used (except on vehicles with automatic radiator 
shutters). 

When changing the thermostat to a higher or lower temperature range on 
vehicles equipped with automatic shutters, always change the shutterstat to a 
corresponding higher or lower range. 

 Removal 

Disconnect the battery ground cables.

Drain the engine coolant. Refer to Section 03-03 .

Remove the accessory drive belt. Refer to Section 03B-05 .

Remove retaining bolts and automatic belt tensioner.

Disconnect the upper radiator hose from the water outlet connection.

Disconnect the air duct assembly at the turbocharger inlet.

Loosen bolts retaining generator to mounting brackets.

Remove bolts securing generator upper mounting bracket and reposition 
generator assembly.

Remove water outlet connection retaining bolts.

Remove the water outlet connection and tube from the cylinder head.

Remove the thermostats.

 CAUTION: Do not let any debris fall into the thermostat cavity when cleaning 
gasket surfaces. 

Remove the gasket and any residue from the water outlet connection and 
cylinder head sealing surfaces.

[FIGURE: Q4096B.gif]

 Installation 

 NOTE: Check the thermostat before installing it. Refer to Section 03-03 . 

 CAUTION: Always install two thermostats. Failure to install two thermostats can 
cause overheating and serious damage to the engine. 

Install two thermostats. 

Position a new gasket over the thermostats.

Position the water outlet connection over the thermostats and gasket, 
making sure the gasket is aligned with the bolt holes.

Install the water outlet connection retaining bolts and hand-tighten.

 CAUTION: Do not allow any debris to fall into the water outlet connection when 
cleaning surfaces. 

Inspect the water outlet connection tube sealing surfaces. Clean any 
debris or old sealing material if necessary. Replace seal if necessary.

Install the water outlet connection tube onto the water outlet 
connection and install remaining bolts. Tighten all bolts to 21-27 Nm
 (15-20 lb-ft).

Position the generator upper mounting bracket to the water outlet 
connection and install the retaining bolts.

Tighten the bolts retaining the generator to both mounting brackets.

Install automatic belt tensioner and retaining bolts.

Install the accessory drive belt. Refer to Section 03B-05 .

Connect the upper radiator hose to the water outlet connection and

DESCRIPTION AND OPERATION

Drive Belts, Accessory 

Ford FD-1460 diesel engine is equipped with a poly-V accessory drive 
belt. The drive belt type is selected for each engine based on performance 
requirements. To ensure maximum life, a replacement belt must be of the same 
type as originally installed. The belt must be properly adjusted at all times. 
A loose belt will result in slippage, which can cause a noise complaint or 
improper accessory operation (generator will not charge, etc.). An overly 
tight belt will place severe loads on accessory bearings. 

The poly-V drive belt tension is maintained by an automatic belt 
tensioner. Regular inspection is required to check belt condition to ensure 
that excessive belt stretch does not occur.

DIAGNOSIS AND TESTING

Drive Belts, Accessory

 Inspection and Verification 

 Drive Belt Cracking/Chunking/Wear 

Under severe operating conditions (high temperatures, low humidity), 
drive belt rib cracking can occur at less than 96,000 km (60,000 miles). Drive 
belt rib cracking perpendicular to the belt ribs is not a reason for concern 
and has no detrimental effect on belt performance. Cracks parallel to ribs are 
not acceptable.

Drive belt "chunking" is the condition in which the rubber material 
actually chunks out between the cracks. The drive belt should be replaced if 
chunking occurs.

[FIGURE: Q4077C.gif]

 Drive Belt Noise 

Drive belt chirp is a regularly occurring chirping noise that occurs 
due to pulley misalignment or excessive pulley runout. It can be the result of 
a damaged pulley or an improperly replaced pulley that was not properly aligned.

To correct, determine the area the noise comes from. Then check each of 
the pulleys in that area with a straightedge to the crankshaft pulley, and 
look for the accessory pulleys to be out of position in the fore/aft direction 
or at an angle to the straightedge.

Belt squeal is an intermittent noise that occurs when the drive belt 
slips on a pulley during certain conditions, such as engine start-up or rapid 
engine acceleration.

Drive belt squeal can occur under the following conditions:

Any of the accessories are damaged, or have a worn or damaged bearing 
or internal torsional resistance above normal for any reason. All of the 
accessories should be able to be rotated by hand in the unloaded condition. If 
any are not, inspect the accessory.

Fluid gets on the drive belt. These would include power steering fluid, 
engine coolant, engine oil or air conditioning system lubricant.

If fluid does get on the drive belt during service, the best policy is 
to clean the drive belt with soap and water and thoroughly rinse with clean 
water. The drive belt does not have to be replaced if no apparent damage has 
occurred.

Drive belt is too long. A drive belt that is too long will allow the 
drive belt tensioner arm to go all the way to drive belt tensioner arm travel 
stop under certain load conditions, which will untension the drive belt. If 
the drive belt tensioner is resting on the stop, replace the drive belt.

If drive belt tensioner is worn or damaged. The drive belt tensioner 
arm should rotate freely without binding.

 Symptom Chart — Accessory Drive Belt Diagnosis 

 ACCESSORY DRIVE BELT DIAGNOSIS 

Condition

Possible Source

CHECK all accessories for free rotation and REPLACE accessory if 
necessary. REPLACE drive belt.

CHECK belt tensioner.

marks. CHECK for correct drive belt length if drive belt tensioner is out of 
operating range.

 Component Tests 

 Drive Belt Tension 

Check drive belt tension. Refer to Drive Belt Tension Adjustment in the 
Adjustments portion of this section. If tension is not within specification, 
check drive belt tensioner. Service components as required.

 Drive Belt Tensioner, Automatic 

The drive belt tensioner will maintain correct belt tension if the 
correct length drive belt is on the engine. Check drive belt tensioner as 
follows:

With the engine running, observe drive belt tensioner movement. The 
drive belt tensioner should move (respond) when the engine is accelerated 
rapidly. If the drive belt tensioner movement is constant and excessive, a 
pulley or shaft is probably bent or a pulley is out of round. In rare cases, 
excessive belt rideout (uneven depth of grooves in belt) can cause excessive 
drive belt tensioner movement. This condition can be checked by replacing the 
suspect drive belt with a known good original equipment drive belt and 
repeating the observation.

With the engine off, check for proper drive belt routing. Refer to the 
illustrations under Removal and Installation. Service as required.

Visually inspect the condition of the drive belt. Replace the drive 
belt as required.

Rotate the drive belt tensioner and check for a binding or frozen 
condition. Replace components as required.

 Drive Belt Misalignment 

 CAUTION: Incorrect drive belt installation will cause excessive drive belt wear 
and can cause the drive belt to come off the drive pulleys. 

 NOTE: Original equipment drive belts are made of a special cord construction 
and are subjected to special testing before approval for use.

 NOTE: A replacement drive belt, other than O.E.M., can track 
differently/improperly. If a replacement drive belt tracks improperly, the 
drive belt must be replaced with an O.E.M. drive belt to avoid performance 
failure or loss of drive belt during cold operation.

With the engine running, check drive belt tracking (the position of the 
drive belt on the drive belt tensioner). If the edge of the drive belt rides 
beyond the edge of the drive belt tensioner, this can cause noise and 
premature wear.

If a drive belt tracking condition exists, visually check the drive 
belt tensioner for damage, especially the mounting pad surface. If the drive 
belt tensioner is not installed correctly with the locating pins in the 
locating holes, the mounting surface pad will be out of position. This will 
result in drive belt tension and chirp and squeal noises.

If the above procedures do not correct the drive belt noise, try 
replacing the drive belt with a known good original equipment drive belt. 
However, the drive belt noise may return again (with mileage) if one of the 
above conditions still exists uncorrected.

With engine running, visually observe the grooves in the pulleys (not 
the pulley flanges) for excessive wobble. Replace components as required.

Check all accessories, mounting brackets and drive belt tensioner for 
any interference that would prevent the component from mounting properly. 
Correct any interference condition and recheck belt tracking.

Tighten all accessories mounting brackets and drive belt tensioner 
retaining hardware to specification. Recheck drive belt tracking.

Check drive belt tension. Refer to Drive Belt Tension Adjustment in the 
Adjustments portion of this section.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Drive Belt Replacement 

Conditions requiring drive belt replacement are rib chunk out, 
excessive wear, severe glazing and frayed cords. Replace any drive belt 
exhibiting any of these conditions. Minor cracks in the ribbed side of 
V-grooved portion of the drive belt are considered acceptable. 

 Drive Belt, Serpentine (Poly-V) 

 Removal 

Rotate automatic tensioner. 

Remove old belt. 

 Installation 

Install belt on crankshaft pulley. Make sure belt is completely seated 
in the pulley grooves.

Wrap the belt over the fan pulley, tensioner pulley, and the alternator 
pulleys.

Rotate the tensioner until the belt can be positioned on water pump 
pulley. Carefully release the tensioner to tighten belt.

Check again to make sure belt is seated properly in all pulleys.

Start engine and check for proper operation.

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Drive Belt Tensioner, Automatic

 Removal 

Rotate automatic belt tensioner to release drive belt tension.

With tension released, remove drive belt from water pump pulley.

Allow drive belt tensioner to slowly rotate to the relaxed position. Do 
not allow tensioner to snap back after the drive belt is removed, otherwise 
damage to the tensioner can occur.

Remove drive belt tensioner retainer bolt and tensioner. 

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Tighten drive belt tensioner bolt to 83 Nm (61 lb-ft).

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Starter Motor

 Removal 

Open battery box and disconnect battery ground cable. 

Remove starter motor upper mounting bolt. 

Disconnect starter motor and starter solenoid wires. Tag wires to 
facilitate connection at proper terminals during starter motor installation. 

Remove two remaining starter motor mounting bolts. Remove starter motor. 

 Installation 

Position starter motor on engine. Install three bolts. Tighten to 
150-200 Nm (110-148 lb-ft). 

Connect starter solenoid wire to starter terminal. 

Connect remaining starter motor wires to starter terminals. 

Connect battery ground cable and close battery box. Check starter motor 
operation.

fuel solenoid to bracket screws: 9 Nm (80 lb-in)

bracket to intake cover: 9 Nm (80 lb-in)

fuel supply lines: 10 Nm (89 lb-in)

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Glow Plug, Air Intake Heater 

 Removal 

 CAUTION: The glow plug heater can be damaged by excessive torque at the 
electrical connector terminal. Do not exceed 4 Nm (36 lb-in) 
torque when removing or installing the connector retaining nut. 

Pull back the protective boot and remove the electrical connector 
retaining nut.

 CAUTION: The glow plug contains a fine mesh filter and a small fuel metering 
orifice. Use care to prevent entry of contaminants. 

Disconnect and cap fuel line.

Loosen jam nut and remove glow plug.

 Installation 

Thread glow plug into intake cover until it bottoms. Back plug out two 
turns and align it with pointer on cover.

Connect fuel line. Tighten nut to 10 Nm (89 lb-in).

Tighten glow plug jam nut to 25 Nm (18 lb-ft).

Install wiring connector. Tighten retaining nut to 4 Nm
 (35 lb-in). Overtightening retaining nut can destroy heater element.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Starter Motor 

 Disassembly 

Thoroughly clean outside of starter motor.

Scribe an alignment mark on starter frame, lever housing and drive end 
housing for assembly reference.

Remove motor terminal retaining screw at solenoid.

Remove attaching screws and drive end housing. Tap housing with 
plastic-tipped hammer to remove from lever housing, if necessary.

Tap snap ring retainer toward drive pinion using a hammer and socket.

Remove snap ring from armature shaft and discard.

Remove snap ring retainer.

Remove lever housing retaining screws.

 NOTE: Use care when removing assembly to prevent damage to armature shaft lip 
seal located at front of lever housing.

Remove lever housing, drive pinion and solenoid as an assembly. Tap 
housing with plastic-tipped hammer to remove assembly from frame, if necessary.

Remove thrust washer from armature shaft.

Remove brush end plate retaining screws. Tap edge of end plate with 
plastic-tipped hammer to remove from starter frame.

Remove thrust washer from armature shaft.

Remove screws attaching brush terminals to brush holder.

Pry brush springs upward using screwdriver and remove brushes.

Remove armature.

Remove screws attaching field terminals to brush holder.

Remove retaining screws and brush holder.

Remove drive assembly from lever housing.

Remove lever housing plug.

Remove pinion depth adjusting screw from end of solenoid plunger shaft.

Remove retaining screws and solenoid.

Remove solenoid plunger and protective boot.

Remove snap ring and shift lever pin.

Remove shift lever from housing. Note direction of installation before 
removing.

Remove screws attaching pole shoes to frame using a pole shoe 
screwdriver and arbor press.

Remove field coils and pole shoes from frame.

Clean and inspect parts. Refer to Section 03-06 .

 Assembly 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Inspect O-ring seals on shift lever pin drive end housing, frame and 
lever housing. Replace seals if cut or otherwise damaged.

Lightly coat armature shaft seal and thrust washers with a 
multi-purpose lubricant.

Check pinion depth adjustment. Refer to Starter Drive Pinion Depth 
Adjustment in the Adjustments portion of this section.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Starter Drive

 Removal 

Thoroughly clean outside of starter motor.

Scribe alignment marks on drive end housing, lever housing and frame 
for assembly reference.

Remove motor terminal retaining screw at solenoid.

Remove retaining screws and drive end housing. Tap housing with 
plastic-tipped hammer to remove from lever housing, if necessary.

Tap snap ring retainer toward drive assembly using hammer and socket.

Remove snap ring from armature shaft and discard.

Remove snap ring retainer.

Remove lever housing retaining screws.

Remove lever housing, drive pinion and solenoid as an assembly. Tap 
housing with plastic-tipped hammer to remove assembly from frame, if necessary.

Use care when removing assembly to prevent damage to armature shaft lip 
seal located at front of lever housing. Also, note thrust washer installed on 
armature shaft.

Disengage drive assembly from shift lever and remove.

Inspect O-ring seals on drive end housing and lever housing. Replace 
seal if cut or otherwise damaged.

Inspect armature shaft lip seal in lever housing. Replace seal if worn, 
cut or otherwise damaged.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Shift lever is under solenoid spring pressure. Pry lever away from 
housing to provide clearance needed to install drive assembly.

Coat armature shaft seal with a light application of multi-purpose 
lubricant.

Make sure thrust washer is in position on armature shaft before 
installing lever housing.

Check drive pinion depth adjustment. Refer to Starter Drive Pinon Depth 
Adjustment in the Adjustments portion of this section.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Solenoid

 Removal 

Remove retaining screws and brush end plate. If necessary, tap edge of 
end plate with plastic-tipped hammer to remove from starter frame. Note thrust 
washer installed on armature shaft.

Remove screw attaching motor terminal to solenoid.

Pull solenoid away from lever housing and maneuver as necessary to

additional clearance.

installing brush end plate.

lb-ft).

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Brush

 Removal 

Thoroughly clean outside of starter.

Remove brush end plate retaining screws. Tap edge of end plate with 
plastic-tipped hammer to remove from starter frame. Note thrust washer 
installed on end of armature shaft.

Remove screws attaching brush terminals to brush holder.

Pry brush springs upward using screwdriver and remove brushes.

damaged.

Inspect armature commutator.

If commutator is contaminated, remove brush holder and clean using 00 
grade sandpaper. If commutator is excessively worn or scored, it should be 
replaced.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Make sure thrust washer is installed on end of armature shaft before 
installing brush end plate.

DISASSEMBLY AND ASSEMBLY

Armature

 Removal 

Thoroughly clean outside of starter motor.

Scribe an alignment mark on starter frame, lever housing and drive end 
housing for assembly reference.

Remove motor terminal retaining screw at solenoid.

Remove retaining screws and drive end housing. Tap housing with 
plastic-tipped hammer to remove from lever housing, if necessary.

Tap snap ring retainer toward drive pinion using hammer and socket.

Remove snap ring from armature shaft and discard.

Remove snap ring retainer.

Remove lever housing retaining screws.

 NOTE: Use care when removing assembly to prevent damage to armature shaft 
seal located at front of lever housing.

Remove lever housing, drive pinion and solenoid as an assembly. Tap 
housing with plastic-tipped hammer to remove assembly from frame, if necessary.

Remove thrust washer from armature shaft.

Remove brush end plate retaining screws. Tap edge of end plate with 
plastic-tipped hammer to remove from starter frame.

Remove thrust washer from armature shaft.

Pry brush springs upward using screwdriver and pull brushes out of 
holder until spring can be released against side of brush, holding it away 
from armature.

Remove armature.

 Installation 

Follow removal procedure in reverse order.

Inspect O-ring seal on drive end housing and frame. Replace, if cut or 
otherwise damaged.

Inspect armature shaft lip seal in lever housing. Replace if worn, cut 
or otherwise damaged.

Coat armature shaft seal with a light application of multi-purpose 
lubricant.

Make sure thrust washers are installed on armature shaft before 
installing brush end plate and lever housing.

Check drive pinion depth adjustment. Refer to Starter Drive Pinion 
Depth Adjustment in the Adjustments portion of this section.

ADJUSTMENTS

Starter Drive Pinion Depth Adjustment

Remove M-terminal attaching screw. To prevent contact between 
M-terminal and solenoid, carefully bend M-terminal away from solenoid using 
needle nose pliers.

Place an insulating material between M- terminal and solenoid.

Connect battery to S-terminal and to a clean metal ground on solenoid 
case.

[FIGURE: J35651A.gif]

 CAUTION: Keep fingers and tools away from opening in drive end housing while 
making electrical connections. The strong shifting action of the solenoid 
could cause personal injury or damage as the drive pinion moves into cranking 
position. 

Momentarily flash a jumper lead from ground to terminal M. The drive 
will now shift into cranking position and remain so until battery is 
disconnected. 

Press on overrunning clutch just enough to take up any drive assembly 
free travel.

Measure distance between pinion and snap ring retainer.

If clearance is not within specifications, adjust by removing access 
plug and turning solenoid plunger shaft nut. If shaft turns, remove solenoid 
so the shaft can be held.

[FIGURE: J3569B.gif]

DESCRIPTION

Air Induction System 

Air is pulled into the engine from an air filter. Clean air is very 
important to the life of the engine. Ingested dust and dirt can damage the 
cylinders very quickly. 

On turbocharged and aftercooled engines, the intake air flow is from 
the air cleaner to the turbocharger and then routed to the charge air cooler 
located in front of the radiator. Air leaves the charge air cooler and is 
routed to the intake manifold where it is forced into the cylinders and used 
for combustion. The cooler reduces the temperature of the air, which lowers 
combustion chamber temperatures, which in turn reduces NOx emissions. Also, 
cooling the air makes it more dense, allowing more fuel to be injected into 
the engine to increase the power-to-weight ratio. 

[FIGURE: A17849B.gif]

DESCRIPTION

Air Cleaner Element

A dry-type air cleaner is standard equipment. Air is filtered through a 
pleated, chemically-treated paper element to remove contaminants before 
entering the engine induction system.

================================================================================
PAGE 4423
================================================================================
1997 Cargo

Section 03B-12: Air Intake System, FD-1460 Diesel Engine

1997 Cargo Workshop Manual

DESCRIPTION

Air Restriction Gauge 

The air restriction gauge is connected to the air outlet tube of the 
air cleaner housing. A yellow indicator moves toward the red line on the gauge 
meter as the filter performs and nears the end of its service life. 

The yellow indicator keeps its position, even when the vehicle is not 
running. The filter must be replaced when the yellow indicator reads 6.2 kPa 
(25 inches H 2 O). The replacement condition is easily determined 
at a glance. 

The filter does not need to be replaced if the indicator has not 
reached 6.2 kPa (25 inches H 2 O). When the filter is replaced, the 
button on the air restriction gauge must be pressed in order to reset the 
indicator. 

The air cleaner restriction indicator should be checked at regular 
scheduled maintenance intervals. 

[FIGURE: V8345C.gif]

REMOVAL AND INSTALLATION

Air Cleaner Element — Radial Seal Element

 Removal 

Remove the two thumb nuts that retain the cover assembly, and remove 
the cover. 

Release the seal gently. The filter element fits tightly over the 
outlet tube, creating the critical seal on the inside diameter of the element 
end cap. Remove the element gently to reduce the amount of dust dislodged. 
There will be some initial resistance, similar to breaking the seal on a jar. 
Gently move the end of the element up and down and side to side or twist to 
break the seal.

[FIGURE: V8451A.gif]

Avoid dislodging dust from the filter element. Gently pull the filter 
element off the outlet tube and out of the housing. Avoid knocking the element 
against the housing.

[FIGURE: V8452A.gif]

 CAUTION: to minimize air leaks, use care to avoid damage to the air cleaner 
housing outlet tube. 

With a clean shop cloth, carefully clean the outlet tube where it 
extends into the housing. Inspect for possible air leaks in housing, inlet or 
outlet pipes.

[FIGURE: V8453A.gif]

Clean the inside of the outlet tube carefully. Dirt accidentally 
transferred to the inside of the outlet tube will reach the engine and cause 
wear. Use care not to damage the air cleaner element sealing area on the tube.

[FIGURE: V8454A.gif]

Check the old air cleaner element. Inspect for foreign material on the 
sealing surface that is causing leakage. A streak of dust on the clean air 
side of the air cleaner element seal is the tell-tale sign. If dust exists, 
make sure the cause is removed before installing a new air cleaner element.

 Installation 

Inspect the new element for damage. Always look for possible shipping 
or handling damage. Pay particular attention to the inside of the open end 
(the sealing area). Check for cuts, etc. Do not use a damaged element.

Insert the new element properly. The radial seal area is on the inside 
of the open end of the element. This critical sealing area will stretch 
slightly, adjust itself and distribute the sealing pressure evenly as the 
element is forced onto the outlet tube. Apply firm pressure to complete a 
tight seal. Apply pressure at the outer rim of the element, not the flexible 
center. Cover pressure is not necessary to compress the element seal.

[FIGURE: V8457A.gif]

Position the cover assembly to the housing and install the two thumb 
nuts that retain the cover assembly. Cover pressure is not necessary to 
compress the element seal. 

Press air restriction reset button, located on the restriction gauge 
(if so equipped).

[FIGURE: V8345D.gif]

Check connections and ducts for airtight fit. Make sure all clamps, 
flange connections and cleaner mounting bolts are tight. Seal any leaks in the 
clean air ducting immediately — they permit dirt to enter the 
engine directly. All ducts, from air cleaner to engine, must be tight.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Air Inlet Restriction Check 

The best method for determining dry-type air cleaner maintenance 
periods is through a periodic visual check of the air restriction indicator. 
It is recommended that the air restriction indicator be used to determine 
service intervals. A visual inspection of the air cleaner element will not 
ascertain the need for service. Overservicing is not recommended.

CLEANING AND INSPECTION

Engine Air Cleaner

Clean the air cleaner body and the cover with a mild detergent or 
compressed air. Wipe the air cleaner body and cover dry. Inspect the air 
cleaner body and cover for distortion or damage at the gasket mating surfaces. 
Replace cover or body if they are damaged beyond service.
